title: Case Coordination Caseworker
body:
**Application deadline:** Applications are accepted on an ongoing basis.

***This position is open to candidates with existing work authorization in the location where the position is advertised.***

**Job Overview:** The Caseworker provides trauma-informed services to refugees and other ORR qualified immigrants to support a positive integration experience and the achievement of client self-sufficiency. The Caseworker works closely with clients, colleagues, and external parties to develop service and/or self-sufficiency plans to meet individual client needs and preferences utilizing a broad range of financial, medical, social, vocational, and other services and resources in accordance with client eligibility and program requirements.

**Major Responsibilities:**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Conduct intake services with clients to assess needs. Develop self-sufficiency plans and timelines in partnership with each client. Provide individualized support through direct services, referrals, and advocacy.
- Receive referrals for case management for ORR-eligible and TANF-eligible clients and participate in any needed case conference meetings to assure continuity of care.
- Assess client needs, creates Family Self-Sufficiency Plans (FSSPs) and Individual Employability Plans (IEPs), focusing on removing employment barriers, stabilizing, and obtaining and retaining employment.
- Assess and monitor client progress to support their attainment of established goals, address challenges, and to ensure that available resources are utilized. Follow up with any referrals made to other programs.
- Detail each client interaction in accordance with program requirements. Input client information in database(s) and assist with tracking and reporting as needed.
- Collaborate effectively with coworkers and partner organizations. Build and maintain relationships with area service providers for the benefit of clients.
- Use personal, insured vehicle and/or public transportation (where available) to travel and transport clients and materials as needed throughout the service delivery area.
- May train and lead the activities of volunteers and interns.
- Conduct outreach to case management staff, refugee-serving agencies, ethnic community-based organizations, and others to inform service providers and refugees of programs and services.
- Complete eligibility screenings for all referral and enrollment paperwork for all eligible Program participants.
- Provide comprehensive case management services, including assisting with benefits applications as appropriate.
- Guide/assist participants to establish contact and receive support services in the community based on their service plan.
- Ensure all services are linguistically appropriate and help advocate with mainstream service providers for linguistically appropriate services.
- Complete case notes in a detailed and timely fashion.
- Ensure all family data is entered into data management system in a timely manner.
- Assist with the preparation of donor funding reports and new funding proposals.
- Participate in all program meetings, staff development activities, and fully engages as a member of the team.
- Follow all IRC policies, procedures and protocols including adherence to the IRC Way and Child Safeguarding.
- Other related duties as assigned.

**Key Working Relationships:**

**Position Reports to:**  Case Coordination Supervisor

**Indirect Reporting:** Interns/Volunteers

**Job Requirements:**

***Education:***

- Undergraduate degree Social Work or similar field strongly preferred; comparable related work experience may be substituted.

***Work Experience:***

- 2+ years of case management experience in a social services environment.
- Experience working with vulnerable or under served populations preferred

***Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:***

- Computer proficiency with an emphasis on Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Teams, Outlook).
- Strong organizational skills and detail-oriented
- Public Speaking and/or presentation experience preferred
- Ability to effectively communicate and work as a team member with collaborative partners, the community, and clients in a cross-cultural, multi-disciplinary environment.
- Ability and willingness to drive 15 passenger van.
- Strong attention to detail with the ability to prioritize and manage time effectively.
- Problem solver capable of working well independently and as a part of a team.

***Language Skills:***

- Proficiency in written and spoken English, bilingual ability preferred in Spanish, Dari, Swahili, Kinyarwanda, Arabic, French or other refugee/immigrant language used in Arizona. Cross-cultural understanding and strong communication skills, both written and verbal.

***Certificates or Licenses:***

- Must have a valid driver’s license, active insurance policy, access to reliable transportation and the ability to travel regularly throughout the service delivery area.
- In accordance with Arizona State Law, must possess or be eligible to receive a fingerprint clearance card.

**Working Environment*****:***

- A combination of standard office environment, remote work, and ‘field’ time within the service delivery area to perform the above outlined responsibilities.
- May require occasional weekend and/or evening work.
- Must be able to lift 35 to 50 pounds (furniture, household supplies, and food boxes).

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $20.97/hr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Current Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

**US Benefits effective Jan 1, 2027:** IRC offers a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-30 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $187 per month, dental starting at $7.70 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare, dependent care, and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

title: Senior Analyst for Somalia
source: Agency for Technical Cooperation and Development
body:
## **BACKGROUNG ON REACH AND IMPACT INITIATIVES**

REACH is an initiative of Acted whose purpose is to promote and facilitate the development of information products that enhance the humanitarian community’s decision making and planning capacity for emergency, reconstruction and development contexts. REACH facilitates information management for aid actors through three complementary services: (a) need and situation assessments facilitated by REACH teams; (b) situation analysis using satellite imagery; (c) provision of related database and (web)-mapping facilities and expertise.

**We are currently looking for a Senior Analyst to support our team in Somalia, based in Mogadishu.**

**Department**: REACH

**Position**: Senior Analyst

**Contract duration**: 4 months, with possibility of extension

**Location**: Mogadishu, Somalia

**Starting Date**: 1 January 2027

## **COUNTRY PROFILE**

Somalia remains within a complex and protracted crisis due to active conflict, the presence of non-state armed actors, the persistent presence of communicable diseases and climate-driven onset shocks – including droughts and flooding. Conflict and natural disasters continue to drive displacement and constrain the availability of resources, while the presence of armed groups severely impedes the level of access and support provided by humanitarian actors. The combination of restricted access to resources, drought, and flooding further exacerbates the possibility for outbreaks of communicable diseases like measles, cholera, and acute watery diarrhea (AWD).

Against this backdrop, REACH has developed a wide range of research cycles to provide an evidence base for the humanitarian community. This includes the Multi-Sectoral Needs Assessment (MSNA), the Acute Needs Analysis (ANA), the Area-Based Analysis Platform aimed at supporting Area-Based Coordination, support to the Somali Cash Consortium, among others.

## **FUNCTIONS**

Under the line management of the Deputy Country Representative, the Senior Analyst is responsible for overseeing the delivery of concise, actionable analysis on acute humanitarian needs at both national and sub-national levels, using REACH own data as well as secondary sources. At a time when the humanitarian system is facing unprecedented constraints, this role will be critical in ensuring that increasingly scarce resources are prioritised according to evidence of need.

The Senior Analyst will line manage two team members, including the Analyst who leads REACH Somalia’s Acute Needs Analysis (ANA) and the Analyst who supports the Area-Based Analysis Platform, providing them with technical oversight, quality assurance and day-to-day support. The Senior Analyst will also contribute to developing and maintaining the Area-Based Analysis Platform to support Area-Based Coordination, and help ensure that the extensive data collected by REACH in Somalia is translated into timely, decision-oriented insights.

The role offers a unique opportunity to shape analysis that directly informs humanitarian prioritisation and decision-making processes, including – but not limited to – the Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan (HNRP), the IPC, and donor resource allocation. The position is well suited to technically strong candidates who are comfortable working with large and complex datasets, while also able to situate their analysis within the broader humanitarian context to maximise operational relevance and impact. It involves close collaboration with GIS, data, and assessment colleagues to ensure that findings are communicated clearly and effectively, including through visual products where appropriate. The Senior Analyst should feel comfortable in front of a room: networking, socializing ideas, responding to questions, building and maintaining relationships, and positioning data in decision-making.

## **RESPONSIBILITIES**

The Senior Analyst’s responsibilities include:

***AREA-BASED ANALYSIS PLATFORM***

- Contribute to the continued design, development and maintenance of the Area-Based Analysis Platform to support Area-Based Coordination, including the synthesis of multiple data sources at sub-national level;
- Lead on the continued technical development of the platform’s analytical framework, including the selection, definition, calculation and validation of indicators and metrics drawn from a range of humanitarian data sources, ensuring they are methodologically sound, comparable across areas and fit for decision-making;
- Support joint analysis with Area-Based Coordination partners, ensuring outputs respond to the information needs of sub-national coordination structures.

***ACUTE NEEDS ANALYSIS***

- Oversee the delivery of the Acute Needs Analysis, ensuring that the Analyst leading it applies REACH’s global Acute Needs Analysis guidance and framework consistently;
- Review analysis, analytical outputs and products before they are submitted to HQ for validation, ensuring they are concise, high-impact and decision-oriented.

***NEEDS ANALYSIS WORKING GROUP***

- In coordination with OCHA, lead the set-up of a national-level Needs Analysis Working Group (NAWG) co-chaired by REACH, including drafting the NAWG ToR, defining its objectives, membership and workplan, and building buy-in from clusters, UN agencies, NGOs and donors;
- Lead the design of the NAWG’s analytical framework for regular intersectoral analysis, building on existing data sources such as the MSNA, the ANA, IPC analyses and cluster data, and work with Data staff to create the backend analysis system;
- Once a NAWG has been established:
- Co-chair the NAWG alongside OCHA, facilitating monthly meetings, including preparing agendas, presentations and minutes, and following up on action points with members;
- Facilitate joint analysis among NAWG members, including organising joint analysis sessions, harmonising indicators and thresholds, and consolidating inputs from clusters and partners;
- Ensure that NAWG outputs are concise, decision-oriented and timed to feed into the ICCG;
- Maintain an overview of planned and ongoing assessments and information gaps among NAWG members, promoting the coordination of assessments to avoid duplication;
- Present NAWG findings to the ICCG and other coordination fora and donors, as required.

***DATA REVIEW AND ANALYSIS***

- Review, synthesise, and assess secondary data from REACH, UN agencies, INGOs, and public sources, evaluating data quality and identifying data gaps;
- Ensure effective use of existing REACH data collected in Somalia, including the MSNA and other assessments, to produce timely, decision-oriented insights;
- Contribute to learning and methodological improvements for future analytical work in Somalia.
- Ensure that the production of analysis and outputs are aligned with key decision-making moments in the humanitarian response, including the HPC and donor allocation processes.

***STAFF MANAGEMENT***

- Line manage two team members, including the Analyst leading the Acute Needs Analysis, including setting work plans and objectives, conducting regular check-ins and appraisals, and supporting their professional development;
- Provide technical guidance, backstopping and quality assurance on analytical approaches, methods and outputs produced by the team;
- Support the capacity building of team members and the wider REACH Somalia mission in structured analysis, synthesis of multiple data sources, and drafting of decision-oriented outputs.

***DISSEMINATION MANAGEMENT***

- Ensure the drafting of timely and accurate analytical products, in collaboration with GIS, data, and assessment colleagues, which comply with REACH’s guidelines and quality standards;
- Ensure that products accurately reflect the information collected and that information is conveyed in a way that maximizes their impact for the intended audiences;
- Maintain regular communication with country management and HQ on progress and deadlines for deliverables, and ensure that all written products are validated by HQ before external release;
- After validation by the line manager, present findings to coordination fora and donors as required.

***EXTERNAL ENGAGEMENT***

- Build contextual understanding and stakeholder networks at national and sub-national levels to ensure outputs are relevant, credible, and aligned with decision-making needs;
- Contribute to the Community Engagement and Accountability Taskforce (CEATF), including by sharing relevant REACH data and analysis on community perspectives and priorities, and integrating accountability considerations into REACH’s analytical work;
- Ensure that all partner engagement and external relations are clearly documented and communicated with the line manager and relevant colleagues;
- Lead in establishing a Needs Analysis Working Group (NAWG), and provide support to other national-level needs analysis processes with OCHA and partners, including contributing to analytical framework design for regular intersectoral analysis and decision-oriented outputs for the ICCG and HPC.

***DATA CONFIDENTIALITY AND PROTECTION***

- The Senior Analyst will maintain the strictest confidentiality on all data collected and related processes, ensuring full compliance with REACH’s data protection policy and SOPs. They will actively take measures to prevent the unauthorized sharing of any information and data belonging to REACH and its partners or collected during their assignment with REACH.

## **REQUIREMENTS**

- **Academic qualifications** Excellent academic qualifications, preferably including a Master’s degree in a relevant discipline (e.g. international studies, development, humanitarian response, data science, political science, statistics, etc).
- **Years of work experience** 3 years of relevant working experience in a humanitarian setting, such as assessments, needs analysis, research design and analysis, etc.
- **Management experience** Experience managing or supervising staff, including providing technical guidance and quality assurance on analytical work.
- **Research skills** Strong quantitative and qualitative analysis skills, with experience interpreting large and complex datasets and the ability to evaluate the quality of different data sources.
- **Analytical skills** Excellent analytical and critical thinking skills, with a proven ability to identify trends, contextualise findings, and synthesise complex information into actionable insights for diverse humanitarian audiences. Very comfortable with the technical aspects of metrics and indicators across humanitarian data, including building and maintaining analytical frameworks.
- **Familiarity with the humanitarian and aid system** Understanding of the HPC and inter-agency needs analysis and assessments, and experience engaging with a variety of stakeholders (clusters, donors, UN agencies) across the humanitarian response.
- **Communication/reporting skills** Strong writing and speaking/presentation skills, with experience producing clear, concise outputs for humanitarian audiences which combine text and visuals for maximum impact.
- **Software skills** Proven knowledge of the Microsoft Office Suite, including Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. Skills in R, SPSS and/or STATA or other statistical analysis software are an advantage.
- **Multi-tasking skills** Proven ability to manage workflows and deliver high-quality outputs under tight deadlines.
- **Level of independence** Comfortable working autonomously and with limited direction, with sound judgment, emotional intelligence and the resilience to continue in difficult situations.
- **Experience in geographical region** Prior experience in Somalia would be a strong asset; past experience in the Horn of Africa region or any other emergency context where access is challenging is desirable.
- **Language skills** Fluency in English required, competency in Somali an asset.
- **Security environment** Openness to working in a high-risk security zone required. Ability to operate in a complex and challenging security environment. Ability to prioritize self-care and well-being.

### **COMPENSATION & BENEFITS**

- For this position, salary between 3’06**0 CHF** and **3’120 CHF** monthly (before income tax), as well as a monthly living allowance of **300 USD**
- NB - REACH salaries are strictly determined by our salary grid depending on the grade of the position and the level of education of staff. A location-dependent security and/or isolation adjustment is then applied as a recognition that some staff are required to work in difficult places where living and working conditions are much more difficult than elsewhere.
- Accommodation and food provided in a guesthouse. REACH is hosted by Acted in Somalia.
- Enrolment in Swiss private pension fund (Swisslife – approx. 9.975% of staff gross salary), health insurance, life insurance and repatriation assistance
- Flight tickets every 6 months & visa fees covered (in-country travel costs and professional expenses are fully covered)
- R&R after 2 months (flight ticket up to 500$ + 200$ of living allowance)
- Contribution to the luggage transportation: between 20 and 100 kgs, depending on the length of the contract (+ luggage and personal property insurance)
- Annual leave of 36 days per year. Public holidays of the country of assignment. Family/compassionate leave when applicable.
- Predeparture induction - 3 days at HQ in Geneva + one week pre-departure training in Acted HQ in Paris, including a 4-day in situ security training
- Enrolment in the Research Foundational Learning Programme within the first 3 months from the start of contract.
- REACH prioritizes the psychological safety of its staff and the health insurance provided covers, among others, up to 1000 € per year of psychosocial counselling fees.

title: Contract Manager - Youth Inclusion and Employment Project / DAPP
body:
Danish Refugee Council, one of the world’s leading humanitarian NGOs, is currently looking for a highly qualified **Contract Manager - DAPP.**

## **About the job** 

The Contract Manager provides integrated project leadership and contractual, financial and compliance oversight for the Danish Arab Partnership Programme (DAPP) Youth Inclusion and Employment Project (YIEP) in Tunisia. The role is accountable for translating the project strategy and contractual commitments into high-quality, timely and cost-effective delivery, coordinating implementing partners, and ensuring that results, budgets, risks and client obligations are actively managed throughout the project cycle.

As the project’s senior day-to-day manager and budget holder, the Contract Manager leads implementation planning, partner and stakeholder coordination, performance monitoring, reporting, forecasting, contract administration and audit readiness. The role works closely with programme and support-service colleagues and draws on technical support from DRC’s HQ Commercial Contracts team.

Your main duties and responsibilities will be:

### **1. Project leadership and delivery** 

- Lead the full project management cycle, from detailed planning to implementation, monitoring, adaptation and close-out.
- Develop, maintain and regularly review the consolidated work plan, implementation schedule, deliverables tracker and resource plan, ensuring clear sequencing, ownership and deadlines.
- Ensure timely and high-quality delivery of project activities, including entrepreneurship support, business-plan development, linkages to finance and employment opportunities, market assessments, and support to cooperatives and small businesses, implemented through a number of local partners.
- Monitor progress against outputs, outcomes, milestones and contractual deliverables; identify bottlenecks and agree corrective actions with project staff and partners.
- Lead regular project coordination and performance-review meetings and ensure decisions and action points are documented and followed through.
- Promote adaptive management by using monitoring data, market evidence, client feedback and lessons learned to adjust implementation while protecting agreed results and compliance.

### **2. Partner, subcontractor and stakeholder management** 

- Manage relationships with implementing partners and subcontractors, ensuring shared understanding of scope, deliverables, budgets, quality standards and contractual obligations.
- Provide practical implementation support, maintain regular communication, convene coordination meetings and track completion of agreed partner actions.
- Oversee the development, review and amendment of subcontractor agreements so that they align with the prime contract, approved budgets and DRC requirements.
- Lead performance and compliance reviews of partners and subcontractors, including review of narrative and financial submissions, invoices and supporting documentation.
- Maintain constructive engagement with the client, public institutions, private-sector actors and other relevant stakeholders, and ensure responsiveness to agreed requirements.

### **3. Financial management and commercial performance** 

- Act as Budget Holder, overseeing project budgets and financial systems in DRC Dynamics and ensuring expenditure is accurate, eligible, timely and aligned with implementation priorities.
- Lead financial forecasting, budget monitoring and variance analysis across DRC and subcontractors, including tracking burn rate, forecast accuracy, value for money, payment schedules and contractual milestones.
- Maintain the Contract Follow Up (CFU) and provide clear financial management information to project governance and relevant DRC stakeholders.
- Coordinate preparation and submission of compliant client invoices, with complete supporting evidence and documentation of deliverables.
- Prepare budget projections and lead budget amendments in coordination with partners, the Country Office, Regional Office and HQ.

### **4. Contractual compliance, risk and audit** 

- Serve as the principal project focal point for compliance with client terms and conditions, including cost eligibility, safeguarding, security, code of conduct, reporting and documentation requirements.
- Maintain effective compliance and quality-assurance systems, including checklists, contract files, decision logs, document-control standards and archiving.
- Maintain the internal project risk matrix, escalate material risks, assign mitigation measures and monitor their completion with programme and support-service teams.
- Ensure project systems remain audit-ready through strong internal controls, complete documentation and timely follow-up of findings from internal or external reviews and audits.
- Coordinate with Finance, HR, Supply Chain, Logistics and other support functions to resolve operational or compliance issues that could affect delivery.

### **5. Monitoring, reporting, learning and communication** 

- Ensure an effective system for monitoring activities, results, contractual milestones and data quality throughout implementation.
- Lead timely preparation of accurate, concise and evidence-based narrative, financial and operational reports, including Delivery Reporting Tools and client templates.
- Ensure reports and external communications meet contractual requirements, DRC quality standards and client expectations.
- Document case studies, good practices and lessons learned and ensure they inform project adaptation, future programming and stakeholder communication.
- Provide clear updates to project governance and act as the primary contact for operational, contractual and compliance queries.

### **6. Team coordination and management** 

- Provide clear priorities, guidance and day-to-day coordination to project staff, fostering collaboration between programme, MEAL and support service functions.
- Ensure roles, decision-making responsibilities and internal workflows are understood and applied consistently.
- Supervise the DAPP Finance Officer, ensuring timeline work planning, as well as objective setting and monitoring.
- Perform other relevant duties assigned by the line manager.

## **About you** 

To be successful in this role we expect you to have At least 7 years of progressively responsible experience in project delivery and management within the humanitarian, development or private-sector development field, including experience managing complex, multi-stakeholder projects.

Moreover, we also expect the following:

- At least 2 years of experience in contract management, commercial contracts, framework contracts or comparable donor-funded contractual arrangements.
- Demonstrated experience managing budgets of at least USD 2 million, financial forecasts, invoices, audits and partner or subcontractor agreements.
- Proven ability to lead implementation planning, monitor delivery against milestones and results, manage risks and coordinate corrective action.
- Experience in economic recovery, youth employment, entrepreneurship, market systems or private-sector engagement is strongly desirable.
- Experience working with public institutions and maintaining partnerships with private-sector, finance or entrepreneurship actors is an asset.
- Strong knowledge of donor or client compliance; experience with commercial contracting is a distinct advantage.
- Excellent planning, analytical, problem-solving, negotiation and communication skills, with the ability to work across cultures and functions.
- Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Word, Excel and PowerPoint; experience with ERP and project-management systems is desirable.
- Professional fluency in English is required. Working proficiency in French and/or Arabic is strongly desirable; fluency in both is an advantage.
- Advanced university degree in international development, business administration, economics, social sciences, project management or another relevant field. A bachelor’s degree combined with substantial relevant experience may be accepted.

In this position, you are expected to demonstrate DRC’ five core competencies:

- Striving for excellence: You focus on reaching results while ensuring an efficient process.
- Collaborating: You involve relevant parties and encourage feedback.
- Taking the lead: You take ownership and initiative while aiming for innovation.
- Communicating: You listen and speak effectively and honestly.
- Demonstrating integrity: You uphold and promote the highest standards of ethical and professional conduct in relation to our values and Code of Conduct, including safeguarding against sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment.

## **We offer** 

- Contract length: Until Dec 31, 2027
- Band: MF2
- Designation of Duty Station: Tunis
- Suggested Start date: 01 Jan 2027

Salary and conditions will be in accordance with Danish Refugee Council’s Terms of Employment for national employees; please refer to [our website](https://drc.ngo/about-drc/vacancies). For questions regarding the vacancy please contact Us.

### **Application process** 

All applicants must upload a cover letter and an updated CV (no longer than four pages) in English. Applications sent by email will not be considered.

Closing date for applications:07 December 2026

title: Humanitarian Ethical Storytelling Guidelines Consultancy
body:
**Terms of Reference IPPF Humanitarian Ethical Storytelling Guidelines**.

**Background:**

IPPF works with Member Associations (MAs) and Collaborative Partners (CPs) in almost 150 countries across the world to advance sexual and reproductive health and rights. In humanitarian settings, IPPF supports locally led action across preparedness, response and recovery, focusing on the delivery of life-saving sexual and reproductive health services to women, girls and marginalised communities.

Stories, images, audio and video can help communities influence decisions, document needs and solutions, support advocacy and fundraising, and demonstrate the impact of our humanitarian work. However, storytelling in emergencies carries heightened ethical and protection risks. IPPF works on sensitive sexual and reproductive health and rights issues, including services for survivors of sexual and gender-based violence, gynaecological care, contraception, abortion care, HIV services and support for people with diverse sexual orientations, gender identities and expressions. This work often takes place in countries affected by conflict, displacement and insecurity, including settings where sexual and reproductive health and rights are highly contested, restricted or criminalised and where communities, service users and providers may face stigma, opposition, surveillance or violence.

These conditions can affect whether consent is genuinely voluntary and whether sharing someone’s identity, experiences or location could cause harm now or later. Communications can also reinforce power imbalances by presenting people only through crisis, removing important context, privileging certain voices or exposing individuals and communities to additional risk.

IPPF is therefore commissioning a consultant to develop concise, practical Humanitarian Ethical Storytelling Guidelines for use across the Federation. The guidelines will cover the full communications process, from commissioning and collecting content to writing, editing, storing, publishing, reusing and retiring material.

The guidelines will reference existing IPPF communications materials including the Words Matter guide and consent form.

**Purpose and objectives:**

The purpose of the assignment is to create clear and usable offline guidance that helps colleagues across the Secretariat and MAs communicate and gather content about and in humanitarian contexts in ways that uphold dignity, agency, safety and accuracy. The guidelines should be suitable for communications, advocacy, fundraising, media, digital content, donor reporting and programme documentation.

The consultancy will;

- Strengthen trauma-informed, rights-based and locally led approaches to humanitarian storytelling.
- Set ethical standards for content while allowing adaptation to local context.
- Help teams identify, reduce and respond to safeguarding, protection and data risks within content gathering and usage in humanitarian settings and emergencies.
- Provide practical decision-making tools.

**Intended users and scope:**

The primary users will be the Secretariat and MA staff. The guidelines should also inform the work of photographers, filmmakers, journalists, translators, editors, designers, agencies and other suppliers commissioned by IPPF humanitarian.

The guidance should apply across a wide scope of contexts, including conflict, climate emergencies, displacement and protracted crises.

**Scope of work:**

The consultant should;

- Conduct a focused desk review of relevant IPPF policies, existing materials, consent materials, safeguarding and data protection requirements, alongside established humanitarian and ethical storytelling standards and examples.
- Consult a representative group of Federation staff and MAs to understand current practice, risks, operational constraints and examples of good practice.
- Create the structure, principles and practical tools with IPPF and selected MAs, ensuring that the guidance reflects locally led humanitarian action.
- Draft concise guidelines with realistic examples, decision-making tools and templates that can be applied by teams with different levels of communications capacity.
- Community consultation, including toolkit testing, feedback and any resulting revisions, could be incorporated at a later stage.

**Required content:**

The final structure will be agreed during inception. At a minimum, the guidelines should address the following areas.

- Foundations of storytelling in humanitarian contexts - power and representation
- Tips for pre-production for ethical content gathering
- Ethical best practice for content collection
- Informed consent in humanitarian emergencies
- Trauma informed interviewing
- Anonymisation and safeguarding (across production and post-production)
- Visual representation (photography and film)
- Accuracy and positioning in story-writing and quotes
- AI generated and digitally altered content guidance
- Data storage security
- Practical tips for co-creation in humanitarian settings

**Deliverables:**

The consultant will deliver a written toolkit.

1. An inception notes with the methodology, workplan, consultation plan, proposed structure and key ethical questions for agreement with IPPF.
2. Summary of findings from the desk review and consultations, showing how will shape the guidelines.
3. Consultation with MAs and Secretariat for contextual and technical input.
4. A draft and then finalized set of Humanitarian Ethical Storytelling Guidelines which includes practical resources and links out to existing IPPF resources

**Working arrangements:**

The consultant or consultant team will work closely with the IPPF Humanitarian Team and wider IPPF staff. The assignment is expected to be completed remotely.

**Consultant profile:**

The consultant or team should demonstrate;

- At least 10 year's experience in ethical storytelling and content production for INGOs or civil society organisations.
- Extensive practical field experience in gathering humanitarian content.
- Expertise in informed consent, safeguarding, trauma-informed practice, protection and responsible data management in humanitarian or other high-risk settings.
- A sound understanding of power, representation, gender equality, sexual and reproductive health and rights, and locally led humanitarian action.
- Experience developing concise guidelines, toolkits, training materials or editorial standards for other international organisations or civil society networks.
- Excellent English writing and facilitation skills, with the ability to turn complex ethical and operational issues into clear, practical guidance for diverse audiences.
- Experience consulting across cultures and regions and working collaboratively.

**Timeline:**

**The consultancy will run in several phases, comprising approximately 6–10 weeks of work spread over a longer period to accommodate consultations, feedback and revisions.**

**Budget:** Up to USD22,000.00.

title: ILO External Collaboration Contract
body:
Terms of Reference  
I. Background and purpose  
The ‘PROSPECTS’ Partnership for improving prospects for host communities (HCs) and forcibly displaced persons (FDPs), was launched by the Government of the Netherlands in 2019 in response to forced displacement crises, bringing together the International Finance Corporation (IFC), the International Labour Organization (ILO), the UN Refugee Agency (UNHCR), the UN Children's Fund (UNICEF) and the World Bank. The partnership spans eight countries affected by forced displacement, namely Egypt, Ethiopia, Iraq, Jordan, Kenya, Lebanon, Sudan, and Uganda.  
It employs a holistic approach whereby each partner focuses on their area of expertise to collaboratively enhance access to education, protection schemes, decent jobs and critical infrastructure for both FDPs and HCs. As of 2024, the partnership entered its Phase II, which that aims to build on the results and draw on the lessons learned from Phase I and maximize impact.  
In Iraq, the PROSPECTS partnership aims to support national efforts to strengthen systems and develop/implement policies that promote inclusion and socio-economic development of forcibly displaced and host communities, whilst working closely with local authorities, business/private sector, and communities to identify, maximize, and realize opportunities on the ground. With a geographic focus on the Kurdistan Region and Ninawa, the partnership focuses on four pillars, namely: education and learning; economic inclusion and protection; and critical infrastructure.  
Within the framework of the Education and Learning, the ILO’s focus is on supporting thousands of forcibly displaced persons and host community members to access more and better livelihoods and decent job opportunities. It is doing so through an integrated approach that support market-driven skills training; improve public employment services; implement labour intensive infrastructure projects; promote financial inclusion; and support business start-ups and micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs).  
Through the PROSPECTS partnership in Iraq, the ILO and partners aim to leverage their comparative advantages and areas of expertise to program complementary and interdependent interventions that address education, employment, and protection challenges that negatively affect the livelihoods and well-being of host communities and forcibly displaced persons. The combined efforts of the organizations will endeavour to bolster the medium- and longer-term development goals for host communities and forcibly displaced persons to access quality and market-relevant education, and decent work and enterprise opportunities.  
The partnership’s multi-agency and multidisciplined nature entail multiple levels of monitoring and evaluation to tracer its intended outcomes. Over the first year of the partnership, the ILO has invested in a robust monitoring and evaluation framework for operations in the Arab States. The framework relies on routine data collection with implementing partners, as well as a tracer study. Together these provide measures of progress against key indicators and short-term and medium-term outcomes. The current study provides a baseline analysis of ILO PROSPECTS beneficiaries’ progress towards key outcomes using the tracer study methodology.

Tracer studies1 get their name from the primary activity involved, which is to trace, find or locate a group of beneficiaries of the programme in Iraq. Tracer studies are sometimes referred to as follow-up studies because they trace individuals sometimes after an event has taken place and follow up on what has happened in their lives since then. Tracer study is an impact assessment approach and a survey methodology is developed by the ILO for assessing the PROSPECTS’ interventions in Iraq. The real challenge for the PROSPECTS programme is to produce lasting, long-term results in the lives of vulnerable hosts and forcibly displaced communities. This will be the ultimate measure of the success of PROSPECTS’ intervention. And because of this, the main reason for this tracer is to:  
1\. To provide information on key performance indicators of the PROSPECTS partnership, that will help evaluate the impact of programme interventions on the learning and employment outcomes of the project’s target population.  
2\. Able to weave a story of significant change in the lives and livelihoods of the beneficiaries of the PROSPECTS programme in Iraq  
3\. Able to identify enabling and constraining factors to achieve more success for the PROSPECTS programme.  
4\. Contribute to the betterment of PROSPECTS interventions in other parts of the country and other parts of the world.  
The frequency of application of the tracer study to the same group of sampled beneficiaries will last until the end of the project. The tracer will be done in at least three rounds over the course of the programme providing a baseline, midline, and end-line estimates of the programme impact.  
In 2027, The first-round data collection started with a number of sample telephone numbers selected from the sampling frame constructed from ILO database. This sample selected randomly among allocation across gender and nationality, aims to gather information on key performance indicators, enabling the evaluation of the program's impact on education, employment, and protection outcomes for the target population.

  
II. Scope of work  
The assignment will focus on data collection for the first round of the ILO PROSPECT Iraq tracer study. The data will be collected through phone interviews with ILO PROSPECTS Iraq beneficiaries in Kurdish and Arabic, using a pre-defined survey.  
The survey tool responds to short- and medium-term outcome indicators defined in the ILO PROSPECTS logical framework and corresponding data collection sheet. An orientation and training on the survey tool and data collection methodology will be arranged by the ILO PROSPECTS team at the outset of the assignment.  
The survey was designed to be completed in 45 minutes. Experience conducting similar surveys in ILO PROSPECTS Jordan and Lebanon indicates that a survey tool with about 50 questions is appropriate for capturing the initial impacts of PROSPECTS programming.  
The assignment will use smartphones/tablets for data collection and the Kobo toolbox2, which is an open-source suite of tools, compatible with Android and IOS.3  
A random sample of refugee, and host community beneficiaries will be selected from different ILO PROSPECTS interventions. These consist of employment and access to finance services, and skills

  
1 Source: ILO tracer study manual Book 1 http://www.ilo.org/ipecinfo/product/download.do?type=document&id=19155  
2 Kobo Toolbox | Data Collection Tools for Challenging Environments  
3 Android devices are preferred, although IOS can be used if there is stable and uninterrupted internet connectivity training programmes. Total number of sample will be 1000 beneficiaries

III. Detailed tasks  
The methods and processes for carrying out the data collection, entry, and validation, are detailed below:  
Preparation for Field Work  
1\. Induction and training on survey tools by ILO (remotely).  
2\. Revise the Survey language.  
3\. Pre-testing and adjustment of questionnaires, with clearance of changes from the ILO.

Data Collection  
1\. Data collection and validation using phone calls with project beneficiaries and implementing partners. The contact details for the assigned sample will be shared at the outset of the assignment.  
2\. Consistency checks of the questionnaire to ensure that questionnaires are fully consistent and complete.  
3\. Obtain further information for incomplete entries.  
4\. Enter data from source documents into a prescribed computer database, files, and forms (mostly by using Kobo/Excel Collect and/or Google Forms and similar kinds of Data Collection tools)  
5\. Data entry using the relevant platform and associated tools (tablets, mobile applications etc.) The ILO will detail these prior to the start of the contract.  
  
IV. Expected deliverables  
Conduct 1000 phone calls, verified by the ILO M&E Officer. The assignment will be done in four rounds, and each round 250 phone calls.  
The main deliverable shall be verified excel sheet with all phone calls conducted for each round.

  
V. Reporting arrangements  
The external collaborators will perform the assignment under the overall supervision of the PROSPECTS Project Manager in Iraq and will report directly to the PROSPECTS Regional Monitoring and Evaluation Officer.

  
VI. Detailed qualifications, experience and skills required  
• Education: An university degree in a related field, such as computer science or statistics or engineering.  
• Experience in data entry, using applications and software such as Kobo, excel, and access.  
• Exposure to work on livelihoods, employment decent work, entrepreneurship, and infrastructure would be an advantage  
• Excellent speak and write level in Arabic, Kurdish, and English.  
• Excellent attention to detail  
• Ability to work independently and meet deadlines  
• Proven excellent reporting, communication, and documentation in both English and Arabic languages.

title: ILO External Collaboration Contract
body:
Terms of Reference  
I. Background and purpose  
The ‘PROSPECTS’ Partnership for improving prospects for host communities (HCs) and forcibly displaced persons (FDPs), was launched by the Government of the Netherlands in 2019 in response to forced displacement crises, bringing together the International Finance Corporation (IFC), the International Labour Organization (ILO), the UN Refugee Agency (UNHCR), the UN Children's Fund (UNICEF) and the World Bank. The partnership spans eight countries affected by forced displacement, namely Egypt, Ethiopia, Iraq, Jordan, Kenya, Lebanon, Sudan, and Uganda.  
It employs a holistic approach whereby each partner focuses on their area of expertise to collaboratively enhance access to education, protection schemes, decent jobs and critical infrastructure for both FDPs and HCs. As of 2024, the partnership entered its Phase II, which that aims to build on the results and draw on the lessons learned from Phase I and maximize impact.  
In Iraq, the PROSPECTS partnership aims to support national efforts to strengthen systems and develop/implement policies that promote inclusion and socio-economic development of forcibly displaced and host communities, whilst working closely with local authorities, business/private sector, and communities to identify, maximize, and realize opportunities on the ground.
