title: Expression of Interest: External Evaluation of the Project "Nothing About Us Without Us: Strengthening Refugee Leadership in Diplomacy"
body:
Independent Diplomat invites qualified evaluators and agencies to submit an Expression of Interest (EOI) for the external evaluation of a multi-year project implemented across six countries in the East Africa and MENA regions. The evaluation will assess the relevance, coherence, effectiveness, efficiency and sustainability of the *“Nothing About Us Without Us: Strengthening Refugee Leadership in Diplomacy” project,* while examining the validity of the project's Theory of Change and underlying assumptions. Particular attention will be given to the extent to which the project has strengthened the capacities, autonomy and leadership of In-Country Partners (ICPs), enabled ICPs to deliver quality and contextually relevant results, and contributed to more equitable partnership practices in areas such as decision-making, funding, risk-sharing and learning. The evaluation will also generate evidence, lessons and recommendations to support accountability, organisational learning, adaptive management and future programming.

The maximum available budget for the external evaluation is EUR 25,000. Interested evaluators/agencies should take this budget ceiling into consideration when expressing their interest and assessing their capacity to undertake the assignment.

If interested, please visit the employment section of Independent Diplomat's website for a full job description: [https://www.independentdiplomat.org/about-us/employment](https://www.independentdiplomat.org/about-us/employment)

title: Shelter and WASH Specialist Lebanon
body:
**What we are looking for**

We're looking for an experienced **Shelter & WASH Specialist** to drive the technical vision and quality of our Shelter and WASH programmes in Lebanon. If you're a strategic humanitarian professional with strong technical expertise, leadership skills, and a passion for delivering innovative, people-centred solutions, this is your opportunity to shape impactful programming in a complex and evolving context.

You'll play a pivotal role in delivering high-quality humanitarian programmes that strengthen resilience, improve living conditions, and support vulnerable communities across Lebanon while leading a talented team of technical professionals.

Ready to drive lasting impact through Shelter and WASH programming? Apply today.

**What you will do**

- Lead the design, strategy, and technical quality of Shelter and WASH programmes across Lebanon.
- Provide technical guidance and capacity building to country and area office teams.
- Drive assessments, programme adaptation, learning, and evidence-based decision-making.
- Lead technical inputs for proposals, donor engagement, reporting, and programme growth.
- Strengthen partnerships with municipalities, government authorities, donors, UN agencies, and sector actors.
- Promote innovation, emergency preparedness, climate resilience, and market-based approaches.
- Represent NRC in relevant fora, working groups, and technical and sectorial coordination platforms.
- Champion safe, inclusive, and integrated programming across all interventions.

**What you will bring**

- Degree in Civil, Water, Environmental or Sanitary Engineering, Architecture, or a related field.
- Minimum 7 years' experience in Shelter and/or WASH programming, including 5 years in humanitarian settings, or related technical fields with at least 2 years in a technical advisor or specialist position.
- Experience across at least 3 contexts is highly preferred including Ukraine, and the middle east.
- Experience in technical leadership, programme design, quality assurance, and team capacity strengthening.
- Solid experience with project cycle management (PCM) and in project development; including ability to lead on assessments, design; with good skills in proposal writing/reporting.
- Strong understanding of emergency response, early recovery, cash-based programming, and market systems.
- Proven experience working with local authorities, ministries, donors, and coordination platforms.
- Excellent analytical, communication, and stakeholder engagement skills.
- Fluency in English; Arabic is an advantage.
- Experience in Lebanon, the Middle East, or similar humanitarian contexts is highly desirable.

Context related skills, knowledge and experience

- Understanding of the Lebanon context or similar contexts
- Experience in designing and implementing programming in both first line emergency response, and early recovery contexts, with a focus on household and community level infrastructure interventions.
- Technical knowledge and experience of the community engagement process in a humanitarian and early recovery contexts
- Understanding of Environment and Social Safeguarding is highly desirable.
- Skills in market analysis, sectorial cash-based interventions, and market-based programmes is required
- Experience supporting partner-led or localisation models.

Please download [the detailed job description](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:w:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQC2WZXieu4bQ7WzI5YAZdbIAUs0lNe9mdSFpJc8Zq0tMwM?e=9hIYoF) to learn more about the position.

**What we offer**

- Duty station: Beirut, Lebanon
- Fixed term contract: 12 months national contract, renewable based on performance, funding and need for the position
- Travel: 40%
- Salary/benefits: Grade 9 on NRC's national grading structure.
- NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability.
- We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative.

[Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)

Important information about the application process

- We invite applications from qualified candidates matching the profile.
- Please ensure you attach copies of your academic and professional certificates.
- To apply as an internal candidate, log in with your official email address or click on Opportunity Marketplace.
- When creating your profile, include your full name as given on your passport. Complete all the system-required fields for experience, employment history and education.
- Submit your application and CV in English, taking care to attach your latest CV.
- Applications that do not meet the minimum standards in terms of experience or qualifications will generally not be considered. Unsolicited applications not related to this specific job advertisement will not be considered.
- Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. We receive many applicants for each vacant position.

**Why NRC?**

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee. Our 15,000 staff work in crises across 40 countries, providing life-saving and long-term assistance to millions of people every year.

[Watch this short video](https://vimeo.com/736782633) to see NRC in action.

We are looking for people who are passionate about helping refugees and people forced to flee. Are you one of those people? If you are, NRC offers you the opportunity to:

- do demanding and professional work, often in challenging contexts
- join a work culture that empowers every employee to share ideas and take responsibility
- be part of a welcoming and supportive community committed to human dignity

[Learn more about NRC](https://www.nrc.no/)

[Learn more about NRC Lebanon](https://www.nrc.no/countries/middle-east/lebanon)

title: Protection Officer (National Position)
body:
TEAM PURPOSE:  
To identify, analyse and address risks affecting the safety, dignity, rights and wellbeing of individuals and communities affected by conflict, displacement and other crises, in Rural Damascus, Daraa and Assweida governorates. The team designs, implements and oversees protection interventions through direct implementation and partner-led modalities, while strengthening community capacities, local protection systems, social cohesion, and community-based protection mechanisms. The team contributes to the prevention, mitigation and response to protection risks through individual assistance, community-based protection, protection monitoring, evidence generation, advocacy, social cohesion and other protection programming in line with Oxfam Syria's strategy and humanitarian principles.

JOB PURPOSE:  
The Protection Officer in the Southern hub is responsible for the technical leadership and operational management of Oxfam's protection portfolio within the hub, ensuring that all protection activities are implemented in accordance with Oxfam Safe Programming standards and Oxfam Syria's endorsed SOPs, methodologies and guidance. This responsibility applies to both directly implemented and partner-led interventions. The Team Leader leads the identification, analysis and monitoring of protection risks affecting individuals and communities and oversees the design and implementation of appropriate protection responses, including Individual Protection Assistance (IPA), community-based protection, protection monitoring, social cohesion activities, and other protection interventions. The role is responsible for determining the most appropriate implementation modality for each intervention, including direct implementation, partner-led implementation, or phased transition approaches. This role establishes and maintains collaboration with affected communities, local authorities, community leaders, community-based organizations (CBOs), implementing partners and other humanitarian and development actors.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:  
Assessments, analysis and evidence generation  
•Lead and supervise protection staff, and/or support protection partners, in the planning and implementation of Community Gendered Protection and Social Cohesion Analyses, protection monitoring exercises, stakeholder mapping, service mapping, and other assessments required to inform programme design and advocacy priorities.  
•Ensure timely consolidation, dissemination and utilization of assessment findings to inform protection responses, programme adaptation, advocacy efforts and strategic decision-making across Oxfam sectors and external stakeholders.  
•Contribute to research, learning and evidence-generation initiatives informing protection and social cohesion programming, advocacy and policy development.  
Programme and project development  
•Contribute to the development, implementation and adaptation of Oxfam Syria's protection and social cohesion strategy and operational plans based on field evidence, protection trends, emerging risks and organizational priorities.  
•Lead the identification and design of protection and social cohesion interventions, including community-based protection, IPA, protection monitoring, social cohesion, and other protection approaches implemented through direct and/or partner-led modalities.  
•Contribute to concept notes, proposals, budgets and donor reports, ensuring technical quality and alignment with Oxfam standards, Protection and social cohesion priorities and contextual needs.  
•Identify opportunities for protection and social cohesion integration across sectors and support the design of protection-sensitive as well as conflict-sensitive interventions, in coordination with relevant technical teams.  
Programme implementation and oversight  
•Lead and supervise the implementation of protection and social cohesion activities within the hub, ensuring compliance with Oxfam standards, donor requirements and endorsed SOPs and methodologies.  
•Directly supervise Protection staff and/or support protection partner, and provide technical guidance, coaching and performance management under their responsibility.  
•Oversee the delivery of IPA, community-based protection activities, social cohesion programming, distributions, protection monitoring activities and other protection programming implemented directly by Oxfam.  
•Ensure effective collaboration with case management and other specialized strategic partners to strengthen referrals, complementarity of services and protection outcomes for individuals facing protection risks.  
•Ensure that referral pathways, service mapping mechanisms and coordination arrangements remain functional, updated and accessible to affected populations.

  
Monitoring, reporting, learning and accountability  
•Ensure interventions' outputs, outcomes and impact are monitored and evaluated, in line with methodologies and tools, and in coordination with MEAL staff at hub level.  
•Supervise programme quality, protection outcomes, risks and implementation progress through regular field visits, partner monitoring systems, data review and engagement with affected communities.  
•Ensure timely and accurate programme reporting to enable timely contribution to donor, management and sector reporting requirements, including for both direct and partner-led implementation.  
•Work closely with MEAL teams to ensure data quality and the collection and analysis of sex-, age- and diversity, including disability-disaggregated data.  
•Promote learning, adaptive management and continuous improvement based on monitoring findings, community feedback and lessons learned.

  
Representation and coordination  
• Represent Oxfam in Protection Sector and other relevant coordination platforms.  
•Coordinate with local authorities, UN agencies, NGOs, community leaders and other stakeholders to strengthen protection and social cohesion outcomes and facilitate implementation.

  
Partnership Management Responsibilities  
•Lead and oversee the planning and quality assurance, as well as support the implementation and monitoring when needed and requested, of protection and social cohesion programmes implemented through partners.  
•Manage strategic protection partnerships to ensure the timely, effective, and accountable delivery of project activities, outputs, and outcomes.  
•Provide technical guidance, mentoring, and capacity strengthening to partners, in line with partner priorities, on protection programming, including community-based protection, protection monitoring, social cohesion, individual protection assistance (IPA), referrals, safeguarding, and protection mainstreaming.  
•Support partners in developing, maintaining, and regularly updating service mapping and safe, confidential, and survivor-centred referral pathways in line with agreed protocols.  
•Ensure adequate support is provided to partners to enable the delivery of survivor-centred, timely, and quality protection services, including appropriate referrals to specialized service providers.  
•Ensure adequate support is provided to partners to enable timely and quality monitoring of the quality and effectiveness of partner-led protection interventions.  
•Support partners in identifying and designing high-quality protection and social cohesion interventions that respond to evolving humanitarian needs.  
•Promote integrated, protection-sensitive, and conflict-sensitive programming by facilitating coordination between partners and relevant technical sectors i.e. WASH and FES.  
•Together with protection partners, monitor partner-led project implementation against agreed work plans, indicators, budget& burn rates, deliverables, and implementation timelines, and support timely corrective actions where needed.  
•Conduct regular partner review meetings, field monitoring visits, and joint supervision missions to assess programme quality, identify challenges, and strengthen implementation.  
•Review partner reports and ensure timely, accurate reporting on progress, achievements, challenges, lessons learned, and best practices.  
•Identify implementation risks and operational bottlenecks and work collaboratively with partners to develop and implement corrective action plans.  
•Promote continuous learning, knowledge sharing, and partner capacity development through joint learning moments.  
•Build and maintain strong working relationships with partners, promoting accountability, mutual learning, and high-quality programme delivery.

  
ESSENTIAL:  
•Self-Awareness  
•System thinking  
•Strategic Thinking and Judgment

  
In addition:  
•Bachelor’s degree in social work, Psychology, Sociology, Human Rights, International Development, Law, Political Science, Peace and Conflict Studies, Social Sciences, or another relevant field, combined with at least five years of progressively responsible experience in protection, social cohesion, community development, governance, humanitarian, and/or early recovery programming.  
•OR in lieu of a bachelor's degree, at least eight years of demonstrated progressively responsible experience in protection, social cohesion, community development and/or governance may be accepted.  
•Demonstrated experience in at least two of the following areas: general protection specialized assistance, social cohesion or social inclusion programming, participatory governance processes.  
•Demonstrated experience in team leadership and supervision, coordination role within international NGOs, UN agencies, government institutions, or development organizations.  
•Demonstrated experience in the technical oversight, implementation and/or management of programmes delivered through both direct implementation and local partner-led modalities.  
•Proven experience in designing and delivering capacity strengthening for staff, partners, community-based organizations (CBOs), and/or community structures.  
•Proven experience in representation and coordination with local authorities, humanitarian actors, protection sector partners, UN agencies, civil society actors.  
•Strong understanding of protection principles, safe programming, survivor-centred approaches, accountability to affected populations, conflict sensitivity, social cohesion approaches, safeguarding and the humanitarian principles of humanity, neutrality, impartiality and independence.  
•Experience in proposal development, project cycle management, planning, budgeting, donor reporting and grants management.  
•Excellent analytical, facilitation, negotiation, coordination, stakeholder engagement and relationship management skills.  
•Fluency in Arabic and English, both written and spoken.  
•Strong computer literacy, including Microsoft Office applications and programme management, reporting and data management tools.  
•Managing people and developing others.  
•Building partnerships and strengthening local leadership.  
•Working effectively with communities, partners, authorities and external stakeholders.  
•Facilitating dialogue, participation and collective problem-solving processes.  
•Handling insecure, politically sensitive and rapidly changing environments.  
•Strategic thinking and evidence-based decision making.  
•Managing complexity, competing priorities and operational risks.  
•Communicating with impact, credibility and respect.  
•Commitment to diversity, inclusion, accountability, safeguarding and social justice.

  
Desirable:  
•Experience in social accountability, peacebuilding, dialogue facilitation, mediation, or related programming.  
•Experience in transitional justice, rights-based programming, civic participation, or support to local governance and community-led development processes.  
•Experience working in consortiums and managing relationships with multiple implementing partners.

title: Provision of Catering, Cleaning & Gardening Services in Dadaab Office
body:
Founded in 1956, the Danish Refugee Council (DRC) is Denmark’s largest, and a leading international NGO, supporting conflict-affected populations- refugees, internally displaced people (IDPs) and host communities in 40 countries around the world.TheDRC East Africa and Great Lakes (EAGL) Kenya office wishes to engage interested company/firm for professional *Catering, C*leaning and Gardening Services.

The successful service provider will provide Cleaning, Catering and Gardening services in accordance with the DRC Policies, Procedures and Guidelines. The main objective of this service is to ensure DRC Dadaab office gets prompt and professional cleaning, catering and gardening services round the clock whenever required.

## Requirements

The awarded service provider shall carry out the activities listed here below and provide the deliverables specified.

**Qualifications and mandatory eligibility requirements:**

## Deliverables Data Items-(Supplier)

- Provision of high-quality cleaning, catering & gardening services
- Timely replacement of the engaged reliever in case of inevitable circumstance or emergencies
- Inform DRC by letter or email of any changes in staff at least 72 hours prior to the change;
- Cleaner, caterers & Gardener to be paid no less than the minimum wage and ensure all statutory deductions (PAYE, NHIF & NSSF) are executed on behalf of the contracted employees.
- Ensure provision of full working gears and PPEs for its employees deployed at DRC premises
- Abide with DRC’s code of conduct
- Clear application of contracts as defined by the agreement (Company & its employees)
- Maintain the already existing staff for continuity and stability within the organization.

## Deliverables -(DRC)

DRC will provide

- A conducive working environment
- Working tools for the deployed employees
- DRC welfare will provide ingredients for catering services, cleaning materials, cleaning tools, toiletry required for the provision and execution of the contracted catering, cleaning and gardening service.

The Cleaning, Catering & Gardening Company shall deliver the following data items:

**Monthly billing of services**

- Statement of the billing shared quarterly clearly showing dates invoiced, payments done and pending payments. The bills should be in line with the Service contract.
- Other documents or data that may be required during the agreement period.
- Periodic report on work progress based on challenges, disputes and recommendations

**Reporting Arrangements**

- The Contractor's focal point (Supervisor) will work closely with the DRC Supply Chain Officer and the HR & Admin Officer for coordination and liaison.
- The Contractor must regularly provide updates to DRC focal point (HR/Admin Officer), according to an agreed schedule.
- Communication between the Contractor and DRC must be transparent and fluid to ensure good management of the Contractor's responsibilities. The contractor is expected register any complaints or concerns with the DRC Area Manager promptly.

**Duration of Engagement**

The engagement will be for **2 years** starting **January 1st 2027** and end without notice on **December 31st 2028** Extension will be subject to performance and availability of funds.

**Commencement:**

The Contractor must be available and ready to begin start working with effect from **January 1st 2027**

title: CONSULTANCY FOR A STRATEGIC ANALYTICAL STUDY FOCUSED ON DISPLACEMENT RESPONSE DYNAMICS AND CROSS-SECTOR IMPACTS
body: The objective of this consultancy is to develop a **Strategic Foresight and Systems Analysis Report** on the future of the displacement response in Jordan (2026–2027). The report will analyse how changes in funding, policy, service provision, and displacement dynamics interact across sectors, identify emerging risks and opportunities, and present evidence-based scenarios, systems mapping, and strategic recommendations to support decision-making by government, donors, UN agencies, and humanitarian and development partners.

title: Consortium Manager - Sudan
body:
**This position is based in Kosti, White Nile, Sudan. The position/program is funded by the Sudan Humanitarian Fund (SHF) from 1 December 2026 to 30 August 2027. Medical Teams is the prime grant holder for the HSF and will lead both International & local partners, including ACTED, HOPE, SAPA, Gonanyat, and others.**

**CONSORTIUM MANAGER - SUDAN**

The Consortium Manager - Sudan contributes to Medical Teams International’s calling by bringing together International and local partners to deliver humanitarian aid including health, nutrition, protection, WASH and MPCA for conflict-affected and displaced communities in White Nile, Sudan. This position leads the day-to-day coordination of the Sudan Humanitarian Fund (SHF) Consortium Steering Committee so all partners deliver a single, coherent program on time, on budget, and to donor and humanitarian standards. The Consortium Manager is the main link between partners, the donor, coordination bodies and authorities, and acts as a neutral convener for all members.

Medical Teams International is the lead agency and prime grant holder. The Consortium Manager heads the Consortium Management Unit (CMU) within Medical Teams, manages the prime award on behalf of the consortium, oversees sub-grants to partners and is accountable to Medical Teams and the donor for overall grant performance and compliance.

The role bearer will occasionally be required to support implementation and delivery of other SHF projects as required and guided.

**ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Partner, donor, and stakeholder management**

- Serve as the principal consortium focal point for donors, maintaining clear, timely and solutions-focused communication and coordinating formal approvals, notifications and escalation of significant issues along with key functions at Country Office level
- In coordination with the Grants and Partnership team, oversee the development, amendment and management of partner agreements and sub-awards, and ensure partner due diligence, monitoring, reporting, spot checks, verifications and corrective action plans are completed to the required standard.
- Manage partner performance through clear expectations, regular review meetings, evidence-based feedback, agreed action plans, and proportionate escalation where performance or compliance remains below standard.
- Promote equitable partnership, mutual accountability, shared learning and capacity strengthening, including harmonization of tools and systems where this improves quality and efficiency.
- Represent Medical Teams and the consortium in relevant coordination, donor, government, research, advocacy and stakeholder forums at country, regional or international level, as delegated.
- Support the identification and development of funding opportunities and contribute consortium evidence, learning and analysis to program development, strategic positioning, and advocacy.
- Lead and support structured partner capacity strengthening initiatives, including mentorship, technical coaching, compliance support, and systems strengthening, to improve implementation quality, donor compliance, and long-term institutional capacity of consortium partners.

**Consortium leadership and governance**

- Facilitate the Consortium Steering Committee and technical working groups, including agendas, minutes and follow-up on decisions.
- Maintain and update the consortium's governance documents: memorandum of understanding, terms of reference, roles and responsibilities, and decision-making procedures.
- Build trust and a culture of equal partnership among members, and mediate disagreements fairly.
- Manage consortium-wide risks, challenges, and stakeholder relationships, resolving complex operational issues, driving corrective actions, and ensuring timely communication, compliance, and implementation of agreed decisions.
- Promote meaningful participation of national and local partners in decision-making, in line with localization commitments.
- Lead the Consortium Management Unit and supervise its staff, such as MEAL, grants, and finance roles.

**Program quality, deliver, and reporting**

- Hold overall accountability for delivery of consortium results, workplans, milestones, indicators and contractual commitments across Medical Teams and all consortium partners.
- Ensure integrated planning and coordination across program, technical, MEAL, finance, awards, operations, supply chain, human resources, security, safeguarding and other enabling functions.
- Lead project start up/close out; identify and lead modifications (realignments, NCEs) in coordination with relevant internal departments and partners.
- Ensure timely procurement planning and coordination with Supply Chain during project start-up and implementation
- Ensure timely, accurate and coherent donor reporting and that narrative, indicator and financial information is reconciled across partners before submission.
- Lead development of high-quality donor reports and consortium modification requests in coordination with relevant functions and partner teams. Ensure timely reporting to all relevant cluster 5W’s, results and support participation and communication of project results and challenges in cluster meetings/updates.
- Coordinate joint work plans, targeting and geographic coverage across partners to avoid gaps and duplication.
- Track progress against the logframe, budget and work plan, and lead quarterly review meetings with partners.
- Lead an integrated, multi-sector approach so that partners' activities reinforce each other.
- Support adaptive programming as access, security and needs change, including program modifications with the donor.

**Financial stewardship, compliance, and risk management**

- Provide overall stewardship of the consortium budget, including forecasting, expenditure monitoring, burn-rate analysis, cost allocation, partner spending, and timely action on financial variances.
- Oversee timely processing of partner sub-awards, partner funding requests and disbursement of approved funds to ensure uninterrupted implementation and compliance with consortium agreements
- Ensure implementation complies with donor requirements, Medical Teams policies, consortium and partner agreements, approved budgets.
- Collaborate with HQ Global Programs and Finance teams to ensure Medical Teams International minimum standards are followed and met across the consortium, including regular compliance check-ins with partners, timely resolution of gaps, and escalation of significant issues.
- Maintain an integrated consortium risk register and ensure programmatic, financial, compliance, safeguarding, security, operational and reputational risks are actively managed and escalated.
- Promote audit readiness by ensuring complete, reliable and accessible program and partner documentation and timely closure of audit, monitoring and compliance findings.
- Oversee sub grant agreements, partner capacity and due diligence assessments, budget monitoring, spending forecasts and audits on behalf of the prime award holder.

**MEAL, accountability and learning**

- Oversee a common MEAL framework, shared indicators and data quality across partners.
- Ensure community feedback and complaints mechanisms work across the consortium, and that feedback leads to action.
- Coordinate and facilitate donor, OCHA, AIT and third-party monitoring missions, ensuring partners are prepared, documentation is available, and agreed follow-up actions are implemented in a timely manner.
- Coordinate baseline, mid-term and endline evaluations, and capture lessons learned and good practice.
- Ensure accountability is integrated into country strategies, program design, monitoring and evaluations, recruitment, staff onboarding, training and performance management, partnership agreements, and highlighted in reporting.

**Representation and external coordination**

- Represent the consortium with SHF UN agencies, humanitarian clusters and sector working groups, and relevant Sudanese authorities, consortium line ministries, including the Humanitarian Aid Commission (HAC).
- Coordinate joint advocacy and communications and make sure partner contributions are visible and credited.
- Support partners with access negotiations and travel permissions where needed.
- Ensure SHF visibility and communication requirements are implemented consistently across Medical Teams and partners’ implementation sites in line with donor and Medical Teams’ branding guidelines.

**Other Duties**

- Ensure the safeguarding of program participants and employees through promoting an environment of awareness and upholding the code of conduct provisions of Medical Teams International Protection from Sexual Exploitation, Abuse & Harassment, Child & Vulnerable Adult protection, and harassment-free workplace policies. Incumbents will remain alert and responsive to any child and adult safeguarding risks, acquire relevant knowledge and skills which will enable you to promote strong safeguarding practices, understand the child and adult safeguarding policy and procedures, and conduct yourself in a manner consistent with the Safeguarding Code of Conduct and behavior expectations across all consortium members.
- Coordinate with partners' security focal points on context monitoring and safe program delivery.
- Follow Medical Team's security management plan and contribute to consortium-wide security information sharing.
- Utilize volunteers when appropriate.
- Additional duties as assigned.

**EDUCATION, LICENSES AND CERTIFICATIONS**

**Required:**

- Bachelor’s degree in international development, humanitarian action, public policy, management or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.
- Valid passport

**Preferred:**

- Master's degree in international development, humanitarian action, public policy, management or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.
- Professional certification in Project Management, Grants Management, Monitoring & Evaluation, or Humanitarian Coordination.

**EXPERIENCE**

**Required:**

- At least 6 years of experience managing humanitarian or development programs, including at least 4 years of coordinating consortia or multi-partner programs.
- Proven experience managing sub-awards, partner oversight, compliance monitoring, and capacity strengthening of national and local NGOs
- Proven experience managing or coordinating large institutional grants, with knowledge of SHF's rules and reporting requirements.
- Experience working in insecure, conflict-affected, or fragile settings.
- A proven track record leading consortia and advancing localization with national NGOs.
- Experience with multi-sector programming in Health, Nutrition, WASH, Protection & Cash Programming.

**Preferred:**

- Experience living and communicating cross-culturally in a relief/development setting
- Working knowledge of Arabic, enough to work with partners, authorities, and communities.
- Previous experience in Sudan or the wider region.
- Lived experience of, or close community ties to, displacement-affected or conflict-affected areas, and an understanding of how this shapes program design and partnership
- Prior experience working in Sudan

title: Staff Attorney
body:
**Application deadline:** Applications are accepted on an ongoing basis.

***This position is open to candidates based in Montana who are currently authorized to work in the United States.***

***A cover letter is required for consideration. Applications submitted without one will not be reviewed.***

**IRC BACKGROUND:**

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) helps people whose lives and livelihoods are shattered by conflict and disaster to survive, recover, and gain control of their future. Founded in 1933, the IRC is at work today in more than 40 countries and in 26 U.S. cities. The IRC’s Resettlement, Asylum and Integration (RAI) department creates opportunities for refugees and other vulnerable migrants to survive and thrive in the US. RAI serves nearly 50,000 individuals each year in the US through a diverse portfolio of programs aimed at achieving outcomes in five impact areas: Health, Safety, Economic Wellbeing, Education, and Power.

In 2016, IRC re-opened its doors in Missoula and has since supported nearly 1,000 individuals building a new life in Montana. Over nine years, the IRC in Montana has served refugees and immigrants from Syria, Afghanistan, Ukraine, Iraq, Yemen, Burma, the Democratic Republic of Congo, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Haiti, Venezuela, Central America, and Mexico.

**JOB OVERVIEW:**

IRC seeks a Staff Attorney to join the Montana Legal team to represent refugees and other individuals with petitions before US Citizenship & Immigration Services (USCIS). The Staff Attorney will also conduct community-based Know Your Rights workshops. The position will be part of the IRC Immigration Legal Services Network led by IRC’s Immigration Technical Unit (TU) at IRC’s headquarters, which supports IRC’s 24 legal service programs across the US. The role will collaborate closely with the IRC team in Missoula, Montana, but the position may be based in another high-needs service area outside of Missoula. The position will require some travel within Montana.

**MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES:**

*Direct Legal Representation and Program Management*

- Conduct intakes and consultations with IRC clients and community members, and provide direct legal representation to individuals before USCIS, DOS, and possibly other governmental agencies.
- Coordinate closely within IRC’s multidisciplinary teams to identify needs and facilitate referrals to services offered in-house and through partnerships with external providers.
- Ensure client and program data is collected consistently, managed appropriately, and reported accurately in accordance with program reporting requirements set by IRC.
- Position may supervise legal assistants and/or interns.
- Maintain up-to-date knowledge and expertise of changing immigration policies through independent research and analysis, regular trainings, and peer-to-peer consultation.
- Participate in community-based coalitions related to immigrant rights.
- Serve as a strong advocate for humanitarian immigrants.

*Community Partnerships and Workshops*

- Create and maintain a viable outreach strategy to cultivate and maintain strong relationships with community-based organizations, local immigration attorneys, and nonprofit legal providers.
- Collaborate with other IRC departments and partners to offer community-based workshops or information sessions when demand exceeds capacity to provide direct legal representation. This may include pro se workshops to complete requests under the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) among others.

**JOB REQUIREMENTS:**

- Law degree (JD or LLM) from an ABA-accredited U.S. institution and membership in good standing with any state bar;
- Ideally at least 1-3 years of experience providing direct representation in immigration court and/or before USCIS to asylum applicants and other immigrants seeking humanitarian relief; law school graduates with clinical legal experience may be considered;
- Excellent legal research, writing, analytical, and organizational skills;
- Ability to communicate clearly and effectively, both orally in a courtroom setting and in writing;
- Bilingual in one or more commonly spoken languages among IRC Montana’s client population preferred (eg, Spanish, Arabic, Swahili, Dari, Pashto);
- Deep commitment to immigrant rights and working with humanitarian immigrants;
- Trauma-informed and sensitive listening and communication skills; respect for diverse perspectives;
- Evidence of capacity to be a strong team member in a highly collaborative and fast-paced multidisciplinary environment;
- Must have ability to travel in and around the service area to engage with clients and community partners and attend USCIS interviews.

**Working Environment*****:***

- Standard office environment with occasional participation in community outreach and legal assistance events.
- Depending on location, remote work from within the state of Montana may be a possibility.
- May require occasional weekend and/or evening work.

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $65,000-$86,000/yr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Current Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

**US Benefits effective Jan 1, 2027:** IRC offers a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-30 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $187 per month, dental starting at $7.70 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare, dependent care, and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

title: Head of Support Services Mozambique
body:
**Position:** Head of Support Services Mozambique

**Reports to**: Country Representative

**Location**: Maputo, Mozambique (with field visits to operational areas)

**Application deadline**: 19/12/2026

**Starting date**: ASAP

**Family duty station**: YES

**R&R**: NO

**Type of contract**: Expatriate (International)

**Working context**

WeWorld has been active in Mozambique since 2000, implementing programmes focused on education, food security, climate resilience, disaster risk reduction (DRR), and humanitarian assistance, particularly in response to natural disasters and conflict-induced displacement.

The Head of Support Services (HoSS) is part of the mission’s management structure and oversees the main support functions, including Finance, HR, Logistics and Procurement. The role works closely with the Country Representative and programme teams to ensure that the mission has the appropriate systems, resources and support in place to effectively deliver its programmes.

**Purpose of the Role**

The **Head of Support Services** provides strategic and operational leadership to the mission’s support functions, ensuring efficiency, compliance, accountability and effective risk management across Finance, HR, Logistics and Procurement.

The HoSS ensures that projects are adequately resourced and implemented in line with donor and internal requirements, while strengthening internal systems and staff capacity. The role also contributes to country strategy, budget planning and donor engagement on compliance and financial matters, supporting the mission’s overall sustainability and enabling programme teams to deliver quality interventions.

**Main tasks and ResponsIbilities**

**Strategic Leadership**

- Lead, manage and coordinate the Finance, HR, and Logistics & Procurement departments
- Ensure support services are aligned with WeWorld’s country strategy and donor requirements
- Actively contribute to country-level strategic planning, risk management, and institutional strengthening
- Support managers to coordinate activities of teams, ensuring workload is prioritized appropriately
- Supervise and verify that deliverables and timelines related to grants, contracts, vendors, partners, and internal procedures are respected
- Collaborate with Regional Managers to set goals and objectives, identify strategic activities, and design development plans for support services
- Supervise and coordinate archiving of HR, Finance, and Logistics/Procurement documents according to WeWorld guidelines
- Ensure high-level collaboration with relevant stakeholders (technical working groups, partner forums, authorities, communities, vendors, donors)

**Financial Management**

- Ensure timely and accurate accounting, financial reporting, and expenditure monitoring in line with WeWorld and donor regulations
- Oversee preparation, consolidation, and monitoring of country and project budgets, ensuring proper cost allocation and updates of cost allocation tables
- Maintain and update the country financial plan, ensuring sufficient cash flow and financial coverage for operations
- Ensure financial coverage to implement activities, pay salaries, suppliers, and running costs
- Supervise external and internal audits, ensuring timely follow-up on recommendations

**Human Resources (HR)**

- Supervise the HR team, ensuring effective recruitment, induction, performance management, and staff development
- Ensure all support services staff receive training according to identified needs and training plans
- Monitor staffing adequacy and structure across Finance, HR, and Logistics & Procurement
- Analyze staffing needs & costs, compensation & benefits, and performance review practices
- Promote staff well-being, safeguarding, and inclusive work environment practices
- Ensure compliance with national labor law, WeWorld policies, and donor requirements
- Supervise compliance with payroll, health insurance, work insurance, and employee benefits

**Logistics & Procurement**

- Oversee procurement processes in line with WeWorld’s Global Procurement Manual and donor guidelines, from planning to completion
- Supervises operations of logistics and correct application in accordance with WeWorld’s Logistics Manual and Donor Guidelines, in particular assets management, fleet management, warehouse and stock management and Base management
- Strengthen supply chain management to ensure timely and cost-effective procurement and logistics
- Monitor and mitigate procurement risks, ensuring transparency and accountability
- Supervise preparation of procurement and logistics reports in required formats
- Ensure all the Procurement and Logistics tools are in place and correctly used

**Systems, Compliance & Risk Management**

- Develop, adapt, and enforce Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) across support departments
- Design systems and routines that strengthen efficiency and collaboration between Finance, HR, and Logistics & Procurement
- Conduct regular reviews and audits to identify inefficiencies or risks
- Ensure strong internal controls and anti-fraud/corruption measures are in place
- Ensure recommendations for improvements are implemented in a timely manner
- Maintain compliance with donor requirements across contracts, grants, and procurement

**Safety & Security**

- Support the Country Representative in implementation of safety and security measures in line with mission SOPs and global guidelines
- Ensure logistics and administrative systems contribute to staff safety, including base management, fleet tracking, and communication systems

**Coordination & Representation**

- Ensure effective coordination between support and programme departments
- Represent WeWorld on operational and compliance matters with partners, vendors, auditors, and relevant external stakeholders
- Liaise with HQ/regional finance, HR, and logistics units for technical guidance and alignment

Duties and responsibilities above are not exhaustive and may be adjusted as required by the Country Representative. The role holder may be required to perform any other tasks requested by the Line Manager in line with the position, mission needs, and organizational priorities.

Proper handover must be ensured before the end of the assignment.

**ESSENTIAL REQUIREMENTS**

**Qualifications and Knowledge**

- Degree in Economics, Political Science or related fields
- Good knowledge of main donors’ administrative rules and procurement procedures (ECHO, UE, UN, AICS)
- Full professional competency in Microsoft Office Suite, especially Word, Excel and Outlook
- Knowledge of written and spoken Portuguese
- Knowledge of written and spoken English

**Professional experience**

- At least 5-10 year of previous professional experience in similar roles
- Experience in managing donor funded budgets and/or working in project management in development and/or humanitarian aid
- Working experience with AICS/Italian Cooperation and/or EU grants is desirable
- Experience in managing teams, also remotely
- Experience in developing and updating country budgets for donor funded organizations
- Experience in managing operations of (inter-) national NGOS

**Skills and Abilities**

- Planning, reporting, monitoring and evaluation skills
- Organization and teamwork skills
- Ability to support and train staff to enhance skills
- Proactive and dynamic attitude
- Ability to adapt and work under constraint, under pressure and in complex and multicultural contexts
- Good listening and communication skills
- Positive attitude to work, self-reflective, motivated, inspired, collegial
- Strong commitment to the Mission of WeWorld
- Demonstrates integrity with regards to NGO values and ethical standards
- Displays cultural, gender, religion, nationality and age sensitivity and adaptability
- Treats all people fairly without favoritism

**DESIRABLE REQUIREMENTS**

- Previous professional experience in Mozambique and/or Eastern and Southern Africa
- Knowledge of written and spoken Italian
- Given the timing and operational requirements of the role, priority will be given to candidates who can ensure their availability to work in Mozambique within the required timeframe

**WHAT WE OFFER**

**Type of contract**: a first 6 (six) month collaboration contract subject to verification of the achievement of specific objectives (these objectives will be agreed together with the Line Manager upon arrival on assignment); a second collaboration contract of 6 (six) months renewable, following the positive evaluation of the first three months of contract

**Economic conditions**: according to WeWorld Expatriates Compensation Policy Base Salary (3.190€ - 3.790€ monthly) + Contributions reflecting role complexity and hardship level of the duty station + Housing contribution

**Flight ticket**: One round-trip air ticket every 12 months of service (between country of residence and duty station)

**Health insurance**: covered

**Family duty Station**: Yes

**R&R**: NO

**Wellbeing & Inclusion**: One day of paid menstrual leave per month. We promote a positive and inclusive work environment based on psychological safety, respect, and team empowerment.

**Flight ticket:** One round-trip air ticket every 12 months of service (between country of residence and duty station)

**Equal Opportunities**

We are dedicated to fostering an inclusive and respectful workplace where everyone has equal access to opportunities. Employment decisions are based on merit, qualifications, and organizational needs, without regard to gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, ethnicity, nationality, religion or belief, age, family or parental status, disability or any other status protected by applicable law.

We are committed to building talented teams and welcome applications from individuals of all backgrounds.

title: Senior Core Services Caseworker
body:
***This position is represented by the OPEIU union and subject to the terms and conditions of a collective bargaining agreement.***

***This position is open to candidates with existing work authorization in the location where the position is advertised.***

**Job Overview:** The Senior Core Services Caseworker delivers trauma-informed support to refugee clients during their resettlement and post-resettlement periods, as well as to other eligible immigrant populations, including Cuban, Haitian, and Ukrainian clients. The Caseworker is responsible for promoting a positive resettlement experience and helping clients achieve self-sufficiency. This role involves close collaboration with clients, internal teams, and external partners to create individualized service and self-sufficiency plans. The Caseworker connects clients with a range of financial, medical, social, and vocational resources in alignment with program guidelines and client eligibility criteria.

**Major Responsibilities:**  
The Senior Core Services Caseworker plays a critical role in ensuring that clients successfully transition to life in their new community and achieve self-sufficiency. Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

**Client Intake, Assessment & Planning**

- Conduct comprehensive intake services to assess individual and family needs, including housing, health, education, employment, and social services.
- Develop tailored self-sufficiency plans in collaboration with clients, outlining specific goals, timelines, and action steps to achieve self-reliance.
- Identify immediate needs and prioritize services such as securing housing, enrolling in benefits, and accessing medical services.

**Pre- and Post-Arrival Coordination**

- Ensure clients receive essential services upon arrival, including temporary or permanent housing, access to nutritious food, healthcare, and transportation support.
- Coordinate with internal departments and external service providers to facilitate timely delivery of services and resources.
- Provide ongoing orientation to clients on accessing services in their new community, including healthcare systems, public benefits, financial literacy, and transportation.

**Direct Support, Advocacy & Case Management**

- Offer individualized support to clients, ensuring they receive appropriate referrals to community resources such as schools, legal services, and mental health providers.
- Advocate on behalf of clients to help them overcome barriers in accessing services and exercising their rights.
- Monitor and assess client progress regularly, addressing challenges and updating self-sufficiency plans as needed to ensure successful outcomes.
- Facilitate connection to employment services in coordination with the employment team to support clients in gaining job readiness skills and securing suitable employment.
- Assist clients in completing critical documents, including benefit renewals, address change notifications (AR-11 forms), and other legal documentation.

**Home Visits & Community Integration**

- Conduct home visits to assess living conditions, provide follow-up services, and ensure clients are safe and stable.
- Help clients build community connections by facilitating their engagement with local services, cultural events, and educational workshops.

**Financial Assistance & Budgeting**

- Plan, request, and track direct assistance funds, ensuring expenditures are aligned with program requirements and client needs.
- Assist clients with financial planning, helping them budget for rent, utilities, and other essential expenses.
- Manage Matching Grant Program client finances, ensuring compliance with program guidelines and accurate reporting of funds disbursed.

**Documentation & Reporting**

- Maintain detailed case files and documentation for each client interaction, ensuring accuracy and compliance with program standards.
- Enter data into client databases and assist with program tracking and reporting requirements.
- Prepare reports as required by internal leadership and external funders.

**Collaboration & Relationship Building**

- Collaborate with internal teams such as Employment, Health, and Youth Services to ensure seamless service delivery.
- Build and maintain relationships with external service providers, such as healthcare organizations, schools, and community groups, to expand the support network for clients.
- Participate in cross-departmental meetings and community coalitions to strengthen partnerships and identify additional resources for clients.

**Client Education & Workshops**

- Develop and facilitate educational workshops for clients on topics such as navigating healthcare, job readiness, budgeting, tenant rights, and U.S. culture.
- Encourage and support client participation in group activities that promote learning, self-advocacy, and social integration.

**Supervision & Volunteer Engagement**

- Train, supervise, and coordinate the activities of interns and volunteers, ensuring they understand program goals and the needs of clients.
- Provide ongoing feedback and support to volunteers to maximize their contribution to client success.

**Compliance, Ethical Standards & Safety**

- Ensure compliance with all organizational policies, program guidelines, and ethical standards in the delivery of services.
- Maintain confidentiality and uphold the highest professional standards in all client interactions.
- Participate in ongoing training and professional development to stay current on best practices and program regulations.

**Transportation & Logistics**

- Use a personal, insured vehicle or public transportation to transport clients and materials as needed throughout the service delivery area.
- Assist clients in learning how to use public transportation to access essential services independently.

**Other Responsibilities**

- Support special projects and initiatives that enhance client services and improve program outcomes.
- Perform other duties as assigned to meet the evolving needs of clients and the organization.

**Job Requirements:**

**Preference:** Bilingual or multilingual candidates are strongly preferred. Proficiency in additional languages relevant to the client population is a plus.

**Education:** Bachelor’s degree in social work or related field of study preferred.

**Work Experience:**

- **Required:** Minimum of 2 years of professional experience in the human services field.
- **Preferred:** Experience working with refugee and/or immigrant communities.

**Demonstrated Skills & Competencies:**

- **Relationship Building & Networking:** Proven ability to build and maintain effective internal and external relationships through strong diplomacy, communication, and collaboration skills.
- **Cross-Cultural Communication:** Demonstrated success in working and communicating in a multicultural environment.
- **Initiative & Problem-Solving:** Self-motivated with excellent problem-solving abilities, capable of managing multiple tasks, setting priorities, and meeting deadlines efficiently.
- **Detail-Oriented:** Strong attention to detail and a commitment to producing accurate, high-quality work.
- **Digital & Technical Skills:** Proficient in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Outlook) and skilled in using the internet and digital tools for data entry, research, and problem-solving.
- **Transportation:** Must have a valid driver’s license and access to a personal, insured vehicle.

**Working Environment:**

- A combination of standard office environment, remote work, and ‘field’ time within the service delivery area to perform the above outlined responsibilities.
- May require occasional weekend and/or evening work.

Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.
