title: Consultoría Veterinaria para apoyar en Acciones Anticipatorias de El Niño en el Sur del Lago, estado Zulia– DRC Venezuela
body:
**1. Antecedentes**

El Danish Refugee Council (DRC) es una organización humanitaria internacional que trabaja en más de 40 países. Brinda protección y asistencia a personas refugiadas, desplazadas internas, retornadas, migrantes y comunidades de acogida, siguiendo los principios humanitarios de humanidad, neutralidad, imparcialidad e independencia.

DRC Venezuela opera desde Caracas y cinco bases: Maracaibo, Guasdualito, Carúpano, Sur del Lago y La Guaira. En el estado Zulia, DRC implementa acciones de preparación frente a los efectos del fenómeno de El Niño en los municipios de Colón, Catatumbo y La Guajira, donde la agricultura y la ganadería constituyen medios de vida fundamentales. Los análisis climáticos y las consultas comunitarias realizadas en 2026 evidencian una disminución de las fuentes de agua, el deterioro de los pastizales, el aumento de la salinidad (Guajira) y mayores dificultades para mantener la producción agropecuaria, generando riesgos para la seguridad alimentaria y los ingresos de los hogares rurales.

Las comunidades identificaron una afectación creciente sobre los rebaños bovinos, ovinos y caprinos, reflejada en pérdida de condición corporal, reducción de la producción y mayor vulnerabilidad a enfermedades asociadas al estrés hídrico y nutricional. En respuesta, DRC desarrollará acciones anticipatorias para fortalecer la salud animal mediante campañas de vacunación y desparasitación, suplementación vitamínica y mineral, evaluación sanitaria de rebaños y capacitación para reducir los efectos negativos del niño sobre sus ganados y animales traspatio, con el fin de proteger los activos productivos y la resiliencia de las familias más expuestas a los efectos de la sequía.

**2. Objetivos**

**Objetivo general:**

Fortalecer las capacidades de los hogares productores de los municipios Colón y Catatumbo del estado Zulia para la protección y manejo adecuado de sus activos pecuarios, mediante acciones de asistencia técnica, formación e implementación de medidas preventivas de sanidad animal que contribuyan a la sostenibilidad de sus medios de vida frente a los efectos de la sequía.

**Objetivos específicos:**

1. **Realizar la evaluación y selección técnica de los potenciales beneficiarios del componente pecuario**, mediante diagnósticos de campo que permitan determinar la elegibilidad de los hogares y el estado sanitario de sus animales, de acuerdo con los criterios establecidos por DRC.
2. **Diseñar e impartir un programa de formación en manejo y sanidad animal preventiva**, dirigido a pequeños productores u hogares que poseen cría de animales para la subsistencia (auto-consumo), abordando temas relacionados con alimentación animal en condiciones de sequía, suplementación nutricional, vacunación, desparasitación, bioseguridad y otras medidas para la protección de los medios de vida pecuarios.
3. **Implementar jornadas veterinarias preventivas para bovinos, caprinos, porcinos y aves de traspatio**, incluyendo actividades de evaluación sanitaria, vacunación, desparasitación y orientación técnica a productores, contribuyendo a mejorar la salud animal y la capacidad de recuperación de los hogares frente a los impactos de la sequía.
4. **Desarrollar una evaluación final de los beneficiarios y elaborar un informe técnico de resultados**, que documente la implementación de las actividades, los principales logros alcanzados, las mejoras observadas en las capacidades de los hogares participantes y las recomendaciones para el fortalecimiento de la resiliencia de los medios de vida pecuarios frente a eventos climáticos adversos.

**3. Alcance del trabajo**

La consultoría cubre los siguientes componentes:

1. **Realizar la evaluación y selección técnica de los potenciales beneficiarios del componente pecuario.** Meta: Evaluar al menos a 110 hogares, para seleccionar 90 hogares que cumplan con los criterios (línea de base). Zonas de implementación: Comunidades del Municipio Colón y Catatumbo.
2. **Diseñar e impartir un programa de formación en manejo y sanidad animal preventiva.** Meta: 1. Diseñar un programa formativo de 4 sesiones, para un total de 16 horas formativas por cada grupo. 2. Brindar formación a al menos 3 grupos de 30 personas, para un total de 90 personas formadas. Zonas de implementación: Comunidades del Municipio Colón y Catatumbo: Espacios comunitarios ubicados por DRC para realizar la formación
3. **Implementar jornadas veterinarias preventivas para bovinos, caprinos, porcinos y aves de traspatio.** Metas: Brindar jornadas veterinarias a los 90 participantes seleccionados en el programa. Zonas de implementación: Comunidades del Municipio Colón y Catatumbo: Espacio puede ser mediante visitas domiciliarias o acordando con la comunidad un espacio céntrico para la formación de los participantes.
4. **Desarrollar una evaluación final de los beneficiarios y elaborar un informe técnico de resultados**.Metas: 1. Aplicar una línea de salida a los participantes (74 encuestas) 2. Elaborar 1 informe técnico de resultados. Zonas de implementación: Comunidades del Municipio Colón y Catatumbo: Espacio para realizar línea de salida puede ser mediante visitas domiciliarias o acordando con la comunidad un espacio céntrico para los participantes

Nota: la persona consultora no tendrá que cubrir los costos de traslados a las comunidades ni la adquisición de materiales formativos, toda vez que serán cubiertos por DRC.

A su vez, la lista de personas pre-identificadas a diagnosticar será proporcionada por el equipo de Recuperación Económica de DRC.

**4. Productos esperados**

Los productos se entregan de forma progresiva durante el contrato, según las prioridades que fije el Líder de recuperación económica con el Gerente de base. Los plazos y productos son indicativos y se cuentan desde la firma del contrato.

1. Diagnóstico inicial y plan de trabajo con estimación de horas por componente. Semana 1.
2. Realizar la evaluación y selección técnica de los potenciales beneficiarios del componente pecuario. Semanas 2-4.
3. Diseñar un programa de formación en manejo y sanidad animal preventiva de forma general y con énfasis en situaciones de altas temperaturas a fenómenos asociados (El Niño). Semanas 5-6.
4. Implementar jornadas veterinarias preventivas para bovinos, caprinos, porcinos y aves de traspatio. Semanas 6-8.
5. Impartir un programa de formación en manejo y sanidad animal preventiva. Semanas 9-12.
6. Desarrollar una evaluación final de los beneficiarios y elaborar un informe técnico de resultados. emanas 13-16.

**5. Dedicación, modalidad y supervisión**

- **Período:** desde la firma del contrato, prevista para noviembre de 2026, hasta febrero de 2027. Puede extenderse por enmienda según necesidades y presupuesto.
- **Dedicación:** por horas, según las necesidades del Gerente de base y Líder de Recuperación Económica. El total no puede superar **640 horas**, DRC no garantiza un mínimo de horas.
- **Modalidad:** Presencial. El consultor deberá trasladarse con el equipo de DRC a las comunidades de intervención del proyecto, en el cronograma acordado con la oficina de la base de DRC.
- **Supervisión:** Gerente de base. La coordinación diaria es con la Líder de equipo de Recuperación Económica. También habrá coordinación con Supply cuando aplique\*\*.\*\*
- **Recursos que aporta DRC:** acceso a la documentación interna necesaria, costos de traslado a comunidades y material didáctico requerido. La persona consultora usa su propio equipo y conexión, así como la propiedad intelectual del desarrollo de las formaciones.

**6. Perfil requerido**

Requisitos obligatorios

- Profesional universitario en Medicina Veterinaria, Zootecnia, Ingeniería en Producción Animal, Biología o carreras afines relacionadas con la producción pecuaria y la sanidad animal.
- Mínimo dos (2) años de experiencia profesional comprobable en el diseño, implementación o acompañamiento de proyectos vinculados a la sanidad animal, producción pecuaria, extensión rural o fortalecimiento de medios de vida agropecuarios.
- Experiencia en la ejecución de jornadas veterinarias preventivas, incluyendo vacunación, desparasitación, evaluación sanitaria y manejo de especies pecuarias como bovinos, caprinos, porcinos, ovinos y aves de traspatio.
- Experiencia en el desarrollo e implementación de procesos de formación y asistencia técnica dirigidos a productores agropecuarios, organizaciones comunitarias o promotores locales.
- Conocimiento y experiencia en enfoques de adaptación al cambio climático y gestión de riesgos en sistemas productivos agropecuarios, incluyendo medidas orientadas a fortalecer la resiliencia de los medios de vida rurales frente a eventos climáticos extremos.
- Experiencia de trabajo de campo con comunidades rurales, poblaciones vulnerables, personas desplazadas, migrantes, refugiadas y/o comunidades de acogida.
- Capacidad demostrada para facilitar procesos participativos, relacionarse con diversos actores comunitarios e institucionales, coordinar actividades en terreno y trabajar de manera efectiva con equipos multidisciplinarios.
- Habilidades para la elaboración de informes técnicos, sistematización de resultados y presentación de recomendaciones derivadas de procesos de diagnóstico, capacitación y asistencia técnica.
- Disponibilidad para iniciar en noviembre de 2026 y trasladarse a las comunidades de los municipios indicados, de preferencia en horarios de la mañana.

Requisitos deseables

- Experiencia previa de trabajo con organizaciones humanitarias, agencias de cooperación internacional o programas de recuperación temprana y resiliencia.
- Conocimiento de los sistemas productivos pecuarios predominantes en el estado Zulia o en otras zonas rurales de Venezuela.

**7. Contenido y presentación de la oferta**

Las ofertas deben incluir:

1. **CV** de la persona consultora, con tres referencias profesionales verificables.
2. Propuesta de contenido formativo (preliminar), detallando la siguiente información: - Número de módulo, - Nombre de la sesión, - Contenido a abordar propuesto, - Horas requeridas, - Total horas, -Material didáctico requerido.
3. **Oferta financiera:** tarifa diaria en USD, **todo incluido** (honorarios, impuestos, equipo, conexión y cualquier otro costo), por una jornada de 8 horas. La tarifa horaria se calcula como la tarifa diaria dividida entre 8. El consultor deberá proveer de cuenta internacional para el pago del servicio a contratar o en su defecto pago en Bs.
4. **Documentos administrativos:** RIF vigente, documento de identidad o registro mercantil, y formulario de registro de proveedor de DRC.
5. Declaración firmada de ausencia de conflicto de interés y aceptación del Código de Conducta de Proveedores de DRC.
    
    No se solicita propuesta técnica.

**8. Criterios de evaluación**

Las ofertas que cumplan los requisitos administrativos y obligatorios se evalúan con una ponderación de 70 % técnica y 30 % financiera. La evaluación técnica se basa en el CV y las referencias. Solo pasan a la evaluación financiera las ofertas con al menos 49 de 70 puntos técnicos. DRC puede entrevistar a las personas mejor puntuadas.

- Formación académica en Medicina Veterinaria, Zootecnia, Ingeniería de Producción Animal o áreas afines. **20** puntos.
- Experiencia en sanidad animal, producción pecuaria y ejecución de campañas de vacunación, desparasitación o atención veterinaria preventiva. **20** puntos.
- Experiencia demostrable en el diseño e implementación de intervenciones para el fortalecimiento de medios de vida pecuarios, incluyendo diagnósticos técnicos, capacitación de productores, asistencia veterinaria preventiva y acciones de resiliencia frente a riesgos climáticos en comunidades rurales. **15** puntos.
- Calidad de la propuesta metodológica para la ejecución de la consultoría. **15** puntos.
    
    **Total técnico: 70 puntos.**
- Oferta financiera: tarifa diaria más baja / tarifa evaluada × 30. **30** puntos.
    
    **Total: 100 puntos.**

**9. Condiciones contractuales**

- **Contrato:** Contrato de Servicios de Consultoría de DRC, con las Condiciones Generales de Contrato y el Código de Conducta de Proveedores de DRC como anexos obligatorios.
- **Pagos:** mensuales, por transferencia, según las horas efectivamente trabajadas, a la tarifa horaria derivada de la tarifa diaria ofertada. Cada pago requiere factura válida y timesheet aprobado por el Gerente de base. Se aplican las retenciones de ley. El monto total no puede superar el equivalente a 640 horas. El consultor deberá proveer de cuenta internacional para el pago del servicio a contratar o en su defecto pago en Bs. •
- **Confidencialidad:** toda la información de DRC, de sus donantes, de su personal y de las personas participantes es confidencial. Los productos de la consultoría son propiedad de DRC.
- **Protección de datos:** el tratamiento de datos personales, incluidos los de personas beneficiarias de CVA, sigue las políticas de protección de datos de DRC.
- **Conducta:** la persona consultora firma y cumple el Código de Conducta de DRC, incluida la tolerancia cero frente a la explotación y el abuso sexual, el fraude y la corrupción.
- **Conflicto de interés:** no pueden participar personas de DRC Venezuela ni que tengan vínculos con personal involucrado en esta contratación.
- **Derecho de DRC:** DRC puede aceptar o rechazar cualquier oferta, total o parcialmente, sin obligación de justificar su decisión.

title: Communications Adviser IDMC (Maternity Cover)
body:
**What we’re looking for:**

Are you a strategic communications professional passionate about using storytelling, media engagement and digital platforms to drive awareness and influence change?

IDMC-JIPS is seeking an experienced **Communications Adviser (Maternity Cover)** to lead the strategic direction, development and delivery of external communications, amplifying the organisation’s mission to raise awareness and drive action on internal displacement. In this role, you will work collaboratively across teams and with external partners to shape compelling narratives, strengthen the organisation’s visibility and ensure consistent messaging across key audiences. You will oversee the organisation’s primary communication channels, including media relations, website, email campaigns and social media.

You will also play a pivotal role in shaping the communications landscape of the newly merged IDMC-JIPS organisation, leading the evaluation, development and rollout of a shared brand identity while coordinating communications throughout the transition. Working closely with the Global Insights Manager, Director, colleagues and external service providers, you will help build a coherent organisational voice and strengthen the reach and impact of its work.

If you thrive at the intersection of strategic communications, brand development and social impact, this could be your next opportunity!

*Applications close on 6 December 2026. Interviews may take place on a rolling basis, so we encourage early applications.*

**What You Will Do:**

Here are some of your generic responsibilities:

## Strategic Direction and Planning

- Develop and adapt the organisation’s communications strategy in alignment with evolving organisational priorities and capacity, ensuring consistent messaging and audience engagement.
- Lead and coordinate strategic direction of IDMC’s communications outputs, in close alignment with the Global Insights Manager and Director, ensuring messaging supports institutional priorities and is evidence-based.
- Support the Director with the development of key organisational messaging, speeches, and public statements.
- Establish and use performance analytics to refine content strategies and improve communications impact across platforms.
- Work closely with the Insights and Policy teams to align communication outputs with IDMC’s analytical agenda and flagship products.
- Coordinate the evaluation, review and development of the organisation’s brand identity, working with management and external service providers as needed.
- Coordinate the review, alignment and integration of communications platforms and digital tools to support the merger transition and maintain continuity of audience engagement.

## Content Development and Editorial Oversight

- Oversee writing and editing and refinement a wide range of communication materials including website content, newsletters, social media content, and press releases.
- Collaborate with internal teams to identify compelling content from IDMC’s global monitoring, insights, capacity strengthening and policy for dissemination.
- Maintain an editorial calendar and coordinate content input from across the organisation.

## Digital Content and Channel Management

- Design and produce basic visual assets, such as quote cards, infographics, and animations using internal tools or free software.
- Manage IDMC’s social media accounts in line with the overall communications strategy and brand guidelines.
- Produce and distribute email newsletters, optimising performance through testing and analytics.
- Manage media engagement, including drafting press releases, responding to media enquiries, preparing spokespeople, and identifying reactive media opportunities.

## Coordination and Stakeholder Engagement

- Work with colleagues across teams to ensure communications outputs reflect the relevance and accessibility of IDMC’s work.
- Coordinate with NRC communications teams to align messaging and amplify shared content.
- Supervise consultants involved in content creation, knowledge dissemination, uploads, technical website maintenance, and data visualisation design.
- Ensure website content is regularly updated and aligned with best practice in architecture and accessibility.

Please download a more detailed[**JOB DESCRIPTION**](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:w:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQB4iEgg6uXLTJOUPW6YoKwuAU1AB5njGMMEnx7xhfysiAg?e=mgx0q3) for more specific duties and responsibilities.

**What you will bring:**

- At least 7 years’ professional experience in communications, journalism, public affairs, or related field.
- Proven track record in strategic communication and digital media management.
- Strong writing and editorial skills, with the ability to translate complex issues into accessible content.
- Familiarity with performance analytics, media monitoring tools, and content management systems.
- Fluency in English; working knowledge of another UN language is an asset.
- Experience in humanitarian, development, or policy-focused organisations is highly desirable.
- Ability to manage multiple projects and coordinate across diverse teams and stakeholders.
- Demonstrated ability to distil complex research and data into engaging communications for diverse audiences.
- Experience in managing social media, media relations, and visual content production.
- Proficiency in using design tools (e.g. Canva, Adobe Creative Suite) and CMS platforms (e.g. Drupal or similar).
- Knowledge of international displacement, humanitarian issues, or development policy is an asset.
- Excellent interpersonal skills, with a collaborative and proactive approach to team coordination and stakeholder engagement.
- Experience coordinating brand development or organisational rebranding, including working with external agencies or consultants, is an asset.
- Ability to plan and manage communications during organisational change, build agreement across teams, and translate strategic decisions into practical communication materials and guidance.

**What we offer:**

- Duty station: NRC offices in Geneva, Oslo, Brussels, Berlin, London, or any other country where NRC has an established office, provided the duty station is within ±3 hours of CET. The successful candidate must have the legal right to live and work in their chosen country of residence.
- Contract: 6 - 12 months.
- Travel: Up to 10%.
- Salary/benefits: grade 8 on NRC’s Resident salary scale, with accompanying terms and conditions.
- NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability.
- We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative.

[Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)

Important information about the application process

- For Internal candidates: To apply as an internal candidate, log in with your official email or click on Opportunity Market Place.
- When creating your profile, include your full name as given on your passport. Complete all the system-required fields for experience, employment history and education.
- Submit your application and CV in English, taking care to attach your latest CV.
- Applications that do not meet the minimum standards in terms of experience or qualifications will generally not be considered. Unsolicited applications not related to this specific job advertisement will not be considered.
- We receive many applications for each vacant position and so only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

If you have any questions about this role, please email **ho.recruitment@nrc.no**with the job title as the subject line.

**Why NRC?**

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee. Our 15,000 staff work in crises across 40 countries, providing life-saving and long-term assistance to millions of people every year.

[Watch this short video](https://vimeo.com/736782633) to see NRC in action.

We are looking for people who are passionate about helping refugees and people forced to flee. Are you one of those people? If you are, NRC offers you the opportunity to:

- do demanding and professional work, often in challenging contexts.
- join a work culture that empowers every employee to share ideas and take responsibility.
- be part of a welcoming and supportive community committed to human dignity.

## About Us

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is a global humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee.

Join us in assisting millions of people in areas where others cannot, tackling some of the world's most dangerous and difficult crises. Bring your skills and dedication to an organisation recognised for providing high quality aid and for defending the rights of refugees and internally displaced people.

At NRC, we give responsibility to employees at all levels and foster professional growth and innovative teams. You can expect a supportive culture and an open dialogue with management. We are committed to diversity, equity and inclusion.

Together, we save lives and rebuild futures.

Safeguarding is central to NRC’s work. We expect all employees to:

• treat everyone with respect and dignity

• contribute to building a safe environment for all

• never engage in any form of exploitation, harassment and specifically sexual exploitation, abuse and sexual harassment (SEAH)

• always report. NRC has a zero-tolerance approach to inaction against exploitation, abuse and SEAH

title: Survivors of Violence Mobile Implementation Referent (f/m/x) – Brussels, Abidjan or Nairobi – MSF Belgium
body:
## **CONTEXT**

The medical department of MSF Belgium (OCB - Operational Centre Brussels) plays a key strategic role by defining the modalities of implementation of MSF’s medical strategy so that both coherence and quality can be safeguarded. It also has an overarching normative role and provides technical and strategic support for project implementation and follow-up throughout the project cycle. It ensures knowledge transfer to the medical workforce and stimulates research and innovation by challenging current medical practices and scanning for new approaches.

It comprises multiple specialists across a network of units worldwide (Belgium, Brazil, Ivory Coast, Kenya, Luxembourg, and South Africa) and works in close collaboration with operations, other OCB departments and the MSF movement. It also provides specific partial support to the projects of MSF WACA and Ubuntu.

MSF works predominantly in contexts where violence and exposure to potentially traumatic events are important determinants of health, wellbeing and access to care. Patients may have experienced conflict-related violence, sexual and gender-based violence, child maltreatment, intimate partner and family violence, torture and ill-treatment, trafficking and exploitation, violence associated with migration or detention, and other forms of violence and coercion. These experiences may have significant physical, psychological and social consequences and may also create barriers to accessing safe and appropriate healthcare.

OCB aims to strengthen the translation of its technical guidance on Survivors of Violence (SoV) into safe, functioning and context-adapted models of care at project level. Initial implementation priorities will include embedding trauma-informed responses and approaches in projects with emergency or surgical activities and strengthening the integration of Sexual Violence (SV) and Child Maltreatment (CM) care across OCB projects.

As a **SoV Mobile Implementation Referent**, you will provide direct implementation support to project teams, supported by, and in close collaboration with, the SoV Circle, relevant technical advisors, and the Deputy Medical Director. The role complements, rather than replaces, existing SRH/SV, paediatric, MHPSS, social work, safeguarding, health promotion, and other technical functions.

The role focuses on implementation accompaniment rather than creating a parallel SoV service, supporting projects to translate technical standards into operational practice, identify and address implementation barriers, establish functioning processes, and strengthen multidisciplinary working.

## **MAIN RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Direct technical project support**

Through short- and medium-term project visits, you will support projects in translating OCB guidance into a context-adapted approach to identifying and caring for survivors of violence, addressing the medical and psychological consequences of violence, and reducing the risk of further harm to patients within our operational contexts. You can support projects to:

- Facilitate the use of the Trauma-Informed Responses and Approaches (TIRA) diagnostic tool to help project teams identify and prioritise areas where implementation support would be most useful.
- Accompany project teams in addressing selected implementation priorities related to the organisation and quality of care for survivors of violence, including access, confidentiality, barriers to care, referral and follow-up
- Support project teams to adapt and implement SV and Child Maltreatment protocols and pathways within existing services, according to their context and priorities
- Accompany the establishment or strengthening of specific patient pathways, where identified as a priority, including recognition, care, documentation, multidisciplinary support, referral and follow-up
- Support project teams to strengthen specific gaps in readiness and continuity of care, including the SV minimum package, out-of-hours arrangements and internal or external referral pathways
- Facilitate multidisciplinary working and case review in order to help teams address identified gaps, including clarification of roles and responsibilities
- Work with teams to review selected case vignettes and identify practical changes that can reduce access barriers and risks to patients
- Provide targeted training, on-the-job mentoring and case-based learning in response to identified project needs and as part of implementation support
- Support project teams to strengthen clinical documentation, use of service data, case review or survivor/team feedback where relevant to their priorities
- Support Health Promotion and community teams in addressing identified barriers to safe access and care
- Support project teams in implementing relevant transversal SoV priorities identified by the Medical Department

**Indirect project support, dissemination of lessons learned**

- Produce reports following project visits, documenting clear objectives, findings, agreed priorities, activities completed, challenges encountered, implementation progress, remaining gaps, and recommendations, and discuss relevant points with the relevant Medical Department Advisers and Operations
- Provide implementation-based input into technical and strategic discussions on SoV, particularly SV and CM, together with other relevant technical referents
- Capitalise on lessons learned from different projects, including implementation barriers, enabling factors, and practical solutions, and disseminate them within the Medical Department, Operations, and other projects
- Contribute to the development and refinement of practical implementation tools based on recurrent project needs, including the TIRA diagnostic, patient pathways, job aids, training materials and implementation-monitoring approaches
- Responsible for updating and disseminating information through the intranet and inventory and working in close collaboration with the IKM team

## **REQUIREMENTS**

**Education & experience**

- Degree in Medicine, Nursing, Midwifery, Psychology, Social Work, or another relevant health, social-care, or humanitarian discipline or humanitarian discipline.
- A medical degree or a master’s in public health is an asset
- Minimum 3 years of relevant humanitarian experience, preferably in conflict, displacement, migration or other settings with significant exposure to violence, with MSF or with a comparable humanitarian organisation
- Minimum 6 months of experience in the direct care of survivors of violence, with substantial experience in at least one of the following areas: Sexual Violence, Child Maltreatment/child safeguarding, MHPSS, torture and ill-treatment, or violence affecting people on the move
- Experience of working within and supporting multidisciplinary models of care is essential
- Demonstrated experience translating technical guidance into operational practice, including the development or implementation of clinical/service pathways, SOPs, or referral mechanisms
- Experience in training, mentoring and/or supportive supervision
- Experience in quality improvement, service assessment or implementation monitoring is an asset

**Competencies**

- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to identify and prioritise implementation barriers and support practical, context-adapted solutions
- Ability to work across disciplines and facilitate multidisciplinary collaboration
- Strong communication and facilitation skills, including active listening and diplomacy
- Ability to work sensitively with complex issues involving violence, confidentiality, consent, safeguarding and protection
- Survivor-centred, trauma-informed and person-centred approach
- Ability to work effectively in multicultural and multi-stakeholder environments
- Ability to recognise the limits of one’s expertise and mobilise appropriate technical support
- Strong organisational and prioritisation skills
- Adaptability to changing circumstances, emergency environments and insecure contexts
- Awareness of risks related to staff distress, moral distress and vicarious trauma, and appropriate approaches to mitigating these risks

**Languages**

- Fluency in spoken **French** and **English** is mandatory. Excellent writing skills in one of these languages are also required
- Arabic, Portuguese, Spanish or other languages relevant to OCB operational contexts are an asset

## **CONDITIONS**

- Expected starting date: **As soon as possible**
- Location\*\*: Brussels\*, Nairobi or Abidjan

*\*Due to legal administrative constraints, given the duration of the contract, candidates must already have the permanent right as Belgian or EU national, and/or valid work permit with mention of "Unlimited access to the labor market" to work in Belgium*

*\*\*Other location/s where there is an MSF entity could be discussed on an exceptional basis. The final outcome depends on the residency of the candidate, the local legal limitations (residency, work permit, etc.) and on agreement with the hosting MSF entity of these locations*

- Mobility: approximately 70% of time spent on project visits
- Contract type: fixed-term contract, full-time
- Contract duration: 1 year with possible extension
- Salary according to MSF mobile staff salary grid
- High mobility allowance
- The contractual terms, conditions and salary will be established according to the official residence of the selected candidate and in respect of MSF standard function and salary grid for mobile staff
- Medical insurance 100% covered as per international package; 45 days annual paid leave
- Unaccompanied position
- **Adhere to the MSF principles and to our managerial values: Respect, Transparency, Integrity, Accountability, Trust and Empowerment**
- **Adhere to the MSF Behavioural Commitments**

**Deadline for applications: 14th of December 2026**

title: Climate/Multi-Hazard Early Warning System /Hazard Advisory Expert MoEDM Damascus, Syria (Arabic Speaker)
body:
**Introduction**

NORCAP works to improve aid to better protect and empower people affected by crisis and climate change. We do this by providing expertise and solutions to humanitarian, development and peacebuilding partners, because we believe working together is the best way to reduce needs, risks and vulnerability over time. We seek and promote more effective ways of working at the global level and in the field. NORCAP’s aim is not only to reduce needs, but also to create choice and opportunity for vulnerable people. NORCAP works with and through our partners to improve aid in two complementary ways:

- We provide targeted expertise to strengthen our partners’ response.
- We collaborate with partners to develop solutions to un-met gaps and challenges.

This role directly contributes to NORCAP’s commitment to strengthening risk-informed decision-making, preparedness, and anticipatory action in contexts affected by crisis and climate-related hazards.

The position is hosted by the Ministry of Emergency and Disaster Management (MoEDM) in Syria and supports the development of a government-led Multi-Hazard Early Warning System aligned with global Early Warnings for All principles. Syria faces multiple interconnected risks, including drought, flooding, conflict-related shocks, and displacement, making effective hazard monitoring, forecasting, and early warning systems essential to national preparedness and response efforts.

**The Role**

The Climate/MHEWS/Hazard Advisory Expert will provide technical leadership and specialist expertise to support the design, development, and operationalisation of a Multi-Hazard Early Warning System in Syria. The role focuses on ensuring that risk analysis, hazard monitoring, forecasting systems, and anticipatory action mechanisms are technically robust, integrated, and directly linked to decision-making processes. Success in this role means strengthening national capacities to anticipate risks and enabling timely, evidence-based action before hazards escalate into crises.

The position is based in Damascus, Syria, on a 12-month fixed-term contract with the possibility of extension. The successful candidate will report to the MoEDM line manager, NORCAP Localisation Thematic Manager, and NRC Head of Programmes.

**As the Climate/MHEWS/Hazard Advisory Expert, you will take on the following responsibilities:**

**Role and Responsibilities**

- Lead the development and validation of national and sub-national multi-hazard risk profiles and identify priority hazards and indicators.
- Support the design and refinement of hazard monitoring frameworks, forecasting methodologies, and analytical approaches.
- Integrate climate, hydrometeorological, food security, mobility, and other relevant datasets into risk analysis processes.
- Develop, test, and validate trigger thresholds and forecasting logic for early warning and anticipatory action systems.
- Support the integration of triggers and risk information into standard operating procedures and decision-making mechanisms.
- Contribute technical expertise to the architecture and operationalisation of the Multi-Hazard Early Warning System.
- Develop analytical workflows, technical guidance, and documentation to support system implementation and sustainability.
- Deliver training, mentoring, and capacity-strengthening support to government counterparts and relevant stakeholders.

**Qualifications and Experience**

*To excel in this role, candidates should possess the following qualifications and skills:*

- Advanced university degree (Master's degree or equivalent) in climate science, disaster risk reduction, public policy, governance, international development, humanitarian affairs, or another relevant field.
- At least 8-10 years of professional experience in climate science, disaster risk reduction, early warning systems, hazard analysis, or closely related technical fields.
- Demonstrated experience designing or applying multi-hazard risk assessments, forecasting systems, early warning systems, and anticipatory action frameworks.
- Strong technical expertise in hazard analysis, forecasting, risk modelling, trigger development, and translating complex analysis into operational decision-making tools.
- Experience working with climate, hydrometeorological, food security, mobility, or related datasets, and familiarity with geospatial tools, remote sensing, or analytical platforms.
- Fluency in English and Arabic is required.
    
    Please read [the attached terms of reference](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:b:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQB7_Gh10UsmTpr11RW3XbkPAUaHYT9LU5HRj-3Er1hZ2Cs?e=4mp3ng) for more details before applying.

**Competencies**

**The main competencies of a NORCAP Expert are:**

- Building working relationships
- Planning and organising
- Adaptability
- Resilience

**What We Offer**

*In recognition of your expertise and contributions, we provide the following benefits and opportunities:*

- Rewarding work for a renowned global organisation
- Access to a network of humanitarian, peace, and development professionals
- A dedicated Staff Care Unit
- Eligible for consideration for NORCAP membership and future assignments, subject to a successful performance review.

**How to Apply**

Based on what you have read so far, do you think you could be a good fit? If so, please follow these steps and apply!

- When submitting your application, kindly register in English your full employment history and education. Please include your full name as written in your passport. Uploaded CVs alone will not be reviewed.
- NORCAP reserves the right to conduct a full background check on shortlisted candidates.
- Approved Health Certificate will be required prior to contract commencement and assignment.
- Feedback will be given to all applicants within four weeks after the closing of this advertisement.
- Apply before the 30th of November at 23:59 (Oslo time).

We look forward to receiving your application!

**Our Values & Commitment**

**NORCAP is part of the Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC).**

All NRC employees are expected to act in accordance with the **organisation’s values**.

Being **dedicated, innovative, inclusive, and accountable** are behaviours and beliefs that guide how we work and how we build relationships. We are committed to creating a safe, respectful, and inclusive workplace where everyone feels valued, empowered, supported, and a genuine sense of belonging.

NORCAP values **diversity, equity, and inclusion** and welcomes applications from all qualified candidates. We believe that a diverse workforce strengthens our ability to respond effectively to the needs of people affected by crisis.

NRC has **a zero-tolerance stance toward any form of exploitation or abuse, including sexual exploitation, abuse, and harassment (SEAH)**, and we do not tolerate inaction when concerns arise.

All offers are subject to reference and background checks conducted in line with our safeguarding standards, and NORCAP reserves the right to conduct a full background check on shortlisted candidates.

title: Global Protection Coordinator
body:
Danish Refugee Council, one of the world’s leading humanitarian NGOs, is seeking a highly qualified and experienced global protection coordinator to join the dynamic and ambitious global protection team (GPT).

  
**About the job**

The Global Protection Coordinator will be part of the global protection team and contribute to and enable DRC to continue developing and advancing its expertise, competencies, and role as a leading protection actor. The position is responsible for delivering technical advice and support to country offices in East Africa, Myanmar and Bangladesh to ensure high-quality protection programming, and will lead DRC’s component on Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS). Your main duties and responsibilities will be:

Support to Project Delivery and Programme Quality

- Contextualize DRC’s global protection sectoral standards, policies, and guidance, and provide technical support to country offices to ensure their effective application and adherence to quality protection programme standards.
- Provide strategic direction to country operations to ensure protection sectoral programming and approaches align with DRC’s mandate, align with donor priorities and the sectors comparative advantage
- Provide technical support and capacity building to country offices and DRC partners to ensure quality analysis, strategies, and measurement of responses, in adherence with DRC's global standards and principles.
- Support country offices in protection sectoral preparedness planning, including analysis, scenario planning, and technical input into contingency plans.
- Support quality assurance and learning in line with the Protection Program Quality Framework, including technical capacity assessments, technical quality assurance and capacity building efforts through in person and remote methods.

Support to Project and proposal development

- Provide protection sectoral technical review and/or support the development of proposals at the country level to ensure technical capacities and resources are appropriately planned, and donors’ requirements are met.
- Where relevant, promote integrated and innovative programmatic approaches through coordination with other sectors, incorporating climate resilience and environmental considerations, and advancing DRC’s localization commitments.

Support to global efforts and advocacy

- Contribute to the development and enhancement of DRC’s program approaches and guidelines, tools and standards based on evidence and learning from country offices.
- Promote the piloting, documentation, and scale-up of innovative sectoral approaches and tools, based on field experience and emerging trends.
- Engage with and represent DRC, where relevant, in fora and meetings with donors and external stakeholders with evidence-based learning in close collaboration with PAER.

  
**About you**

To be successful in this role we expect we expect you to have a minimum of 7 years of significant, progressively responsible experience in protection programming in the context of conflict and forced displacement, with a technical background in Mental health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS). Moreover, we also expect the following:

**Required**

- Proven experience of working with international organisation(s) in the field of protection at both the field and global levels
- Significant and demonstrable experience in providing high quality, in person and remote protection technical and strategic advice and support to country operations, across the project cycle.
- Demonstratable capacity building skills, including the design and facilitation of trainings / workshops
- Demonstrable problem-solving skills and ability to adopt flexible, creative, innovative approaches
- Significant experience with effectively coordinating with national partners, local/government authorities, NGO partners, UN and other relevant stakeholders.
- English proficiency is a requirement while ability to work in French is desirable.

All employees are expected to demonstrate DRC’s five core competencies:

**Striving for excellence:** You focus on reaching results while ensuring an efficient process.

**Collaborating:** You involve relevant parties and encourage feedback.

**Taking the lead:** You take ownership and initiative while aiming for innovation.

**Communicating:** You listen and speak effectively and honestly.

**Demonstrating integrity:** You uphold and promote the highest standards of ethical and professional conduct in relation to our values and Code of Conduct, including safeguarding against sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment.

**We offer**

Contract length: Minimum 12 months, but depending on the country and contract terms, the duration might be longer.

Work location: Nairobi, Kampala, Tunis or Copenhagen

Start date: February 2026 or as soon as possible thereafter

Salary and conditions will be in accordance with DRC’s terms of employment.

We welcome all nationalities to apply for the role. If you do not have the existing right to work in Denmark, DRC will support with applying and paying for a work permit.

**Further information**

For questions regarding the vacancy please contact Brennan Webert, Global Lead for Protection. We will do our best to respond to as many inquiries as possible.

For more information about the Danish Refugee Council, please visit our website [**drc.ngo**](https://drc.ngo/).

Danish Refugee Council is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to creating an inclusive and positive work environment based on mutual respect for all employees. All applicants are considered for employment regardless of personal characteristics or attributes.

title: Global Protection Advisor – Gender-Based Violence in Emergencies (GBViE)
body:
Danish Refugee Council, one of the world’s leading humanitarian NGOs, is seeking a highly qualified and experienced global GBViE advisor to join the dynamic and ambitious global protection team (GPT).

**About the job**

The Global GBViE Advisor will be part of the global protection team and contribute to and enable DRC to continue developing and advancing its expertise, competencies, and role as a leading protection actor. The position is responsible for providing technical advisory services, including: 1) development of technical resources in the area of GBViE; 2) technical support to country offices implementing GBViE; 3) support to project and proposal development; and 4) support to global efforts and advocacy. Your main duties and responsibilities will be:

Provision of high-level technical protection sectoral oversight and advisory support in GBV in Emergencies to ensure quality, consistency, and compliance across DRC programming.

**Protection Sectoral Technical Responsibility**

Technically responsible for the development and roll-out of global guidance, tools and capacity development on GBV in Emergencies. This may include, but is not limited to:

- Map and assess DRC’s existing GBViE interventions, technical capacities and gaps within protection programming. Identify good practices, priorities for strengthening specialized GBV prevention and response, and opportunities for integration with DRC’s core sectors.
- Develop and roll out a priortised GBViE training package and training of trainers approach for DRC staff and local partners, including resources on GBV case management, survivor-centered approach and GBV risk mitigation across sectors.
- In collaboration with protection and other sectoral colleagues identify and develop practical entry points for integrated GBViE programming across, Economic Recovery, Humanitarian Disarmament and Peacebuilding (HDP), and Shelter, WASH & Infrastructure (SWI).
- In collaboration with MHPSS colleagues, strengthen the integration of appropriate psychosocial support within GBViE, including through the adaptation of existing resources and development of structured MHPSS curricula.
- Provide technical support to country operations and HQ in the analysis, design and proposal development of medium- and large-scale emergency responses. Support the identification of GBV risks, response priorities and appropriate interventions, and their inclusion in response strategies, proposals and budgets, including those supported through the Global Emergency Response Fund (GERF).
- Assess how DRC’s GBViE programming currently addresses protection risks associated with climate-related hazards and disasters. Synthesize country experience, relevant evidence and learning to identify gaps and opportunities, and develop practical recommendations for strengthening GBV prevention and response within emergency preparedness, anticipatory action, and disaster response.
- Develop and support the use of a capacity assessment approach and a supervision, mentoring and coaching framework, to strengthen the quality and sustainability of GBViE programming.
- Develop practical recommendations and resources for the supervision, wellbeing and support of staff and partner personnel working on GBViE, including measures to address work-related stress and vicarious trauma.

title: PIR Caseworker
body:
**Application deadline:** Applications are accepted on an ongoing basis.

**Job Overview:**   
The Caseworker provides trauma-informed, client-centered services to recently arrived refugees and other qualified immigrants to meet immediate needs and support progress toward self-sufficiency. The role works closely with clients, internal teams, and external partners to develop and implement individualized service and self-sufficiency plans. The Caseworker connects clients to appropriate financial, medical, social, vocational, and community resources in alignment with program requirements, eligibility guidelines, and IRC standards.

**Major Responsibilities:**  
Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Coordinate timely pre- and post-arrival services to ensure clients have access to housing, food, medical care, transportation, and community orientation.
- Conduct housing set-ups, airport pick-ups, home visits, grocery and public transportation orientation, and other field-based services to address immediate client needs.
- Purchase and transport program-related items; lift, move, and deliver materials necessary for service delivery.
- Conduct client intake assessments and develop individualized self-sufficiency plans and timelines in partnership with clients.
- Provide ongoing case management through direct services, referrals, advocacy, and coordination with internal and external service providers.
- Monitor client progress toward established goals, identify barriers, and adjust service plans as needed.
- Document all client interactions accurately and in compliance with program requirements; enter and maintain client data in required databases and tracking tools.
- Support Preferred Communities programming and intensive case management services, as assigned.
- Collaborate with colleagues across programs and grants to ensure clients access all eligible services.
- Build and maintain effective working relationships with community partners and service providers.
- Participate in program quality assurance activities to ensure appropriate use of funds and compliance with grant requirements.
- Use a personal, insured vehicle and/or public transportation to travel within the service delivery area as needed.
- Perform other duties as assigned.

**Job Requirements**

**Education**

- Bachelor’s degree in social work or a related field preferred.

**Work Experience**

- Prior experience working with refugee and/or immigrant populations required.
- Experience providing casework, pre-arrival, or intensive case management services preferred.
- Demonstrated experience navigating program eligibility requirements and ensuring accurate service documentation.

**Language Skills:**

- Proficiency in English required; bilingual ability in Spanish, Dari, Swahili, Kinyarwanda, Arabic, French, or other refugee/immigrant language preferred.

**Certificates or Licenses:**

- Valid driver’s license, active insurance policy, and access to reliable transportation.
- Must possess or be eligible for a fingerprint clearance card per Arizona state law.

**Demonstrated Skills and Competencies**

- Strong relationship-building, diplomacy, and networking skills.
- Ability to work effectively in a multicultural environment.
- Proven problem-solving skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines.
- High attention to detail and accuracy.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Outlook) and ability to use digital tools for data entry, research, and reporting.
- Ability to lift and carry items weighing 50+ pounds, including furniture and household goods.
- Ability to drive a large van or passenger vehicle, as required for program delivery.

**Compensation:** ($20.97). Compensation is based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements

**Working Environment**

This position operates in a hybrid environment that includes office-based work, remote work, and fieldwork within the service delivery area. Typically, the role is based in the office four days per week and remotely one day per week, with field responsibilities possible on all workdays. Schedule flexibility is required, including occasional evenings and weekends for activities such as airport pick-ups.

**This position is open to candidates with existing work authorization in the location where the position is advertised.**

At the IRC, we seek to build a welcoming, inclusive environment not only for our refugee clients, but for all of our employees. As an equal opportunity employer, we value the strength found in the diversity of voices, experiences, and backgrounds who join us in our work. Fostering an inclusive culture with equitable practices is everyone's responsibility, and we regularly offer trainings and opportunities to learn more and find ways to do better. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, gender, gender expression, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, socioeconomic status, or disability status. We are dedicated to ensuring that disabled individuals are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment. Please contact us to request accommodation. In your application, please feel free to indicate your preferred pronouns.

We recognize that few applicants may "check all the boxes," but that each person has their own unique strengths that they would bring to the table. In our commitment to building a diverse and authentic work culture, we invite you to apply anyway. You belong here.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

title: Consultancy for ECW FER Drought Response Project Baseline & Endline Evaluation
body:
**TERMS OF REFERENCE**

Baseline and Endline Survey

## 1. Background and Project Context

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organization helping people forced to flee. We protect displaced people and support them as they build a new future. NRC has been operating in Somalia since 2004, providing critical aid for internally displaced persons (IDPs) and returnees. NRC works in the hard-to-reach areas – helping families get the food, water, shelter and support they urgently need1.

NRC is implementing the ECW-funded project “***Education in Emergencies for Flood-Affected Boys and Girls in Jubaland, Hirshabelle, Puntland, Northeastern and South-West States and Anticipatory Action Pilot Programme for Somalia.”***

The project responds to the compounding impacts of drought and flooding, which have severely disrupted access to education, contributed to school closures and increased dropout rates, weakened teacher retention, and heightened protection risks for children. Prolonged climate shocks have left many schools unable to operate effectively, resulting in widespread learning disruptions and reduced participation in education

The project builds on the achievements of Phase 1, which expanded access to education through the provision of temporary learning spaces, rehabilitation of education facilities, and support to teachers. The current phase will further strengthen access to safe, inclusive, and quality learning opportunities for crisis-affected children through learning materials, teacher support, psychosocial services, safeguarding measures, community engagement, cash assistance, and enhanced education preparedness.

NRC therefore seeks a qualified consultant or firm to undertake a baseline and endline survey. The two survey rounds will establish pre-intervention values, measure change over the implementation period, assess progress against the revised project results framework, and generate evidence for programme adaptation, accountability and final reporting.

The project will deliver a comprehensive package of interventions to achieve the following outcomes:

**Outcome 1**: Increased access to safe and equitable education

**Outcome 2:** Improved quality of teaching and learning

**Outcome 3:** Strengthened government and community capacity for education in emergencies

**Outcome 4:** Children and communities benefit from timely, well-coordinated, and effective responses to drought and emerging hazards, including floods, reducing disruption and enhancing resilience

## 2. Purpose, objectives and scope of the evaluation

**2.1 Purpose**

The purpose of the assignment is to design and implement comparable baseline and endline surveys for the project. The baseline will establish credible starting values for relevant outcome and output indicators and document the initial conditions of targeted learners, households, teachers, schools and education systems. The endline will repeat the core measurements using a consistent methodology to assess change, contribution and achievement against project targets.

## 2.2 Objectives

The overall objective of the baseline survey is to establish the initial conditions against which project performance will be measured, with particular emphasis on outcome-level changes. This survey will provide reference data for assessing the extent to which the project achieves its intended objectives. These include:

- Establish baseline values for all relevant indicators in the project results framework for which primary data are required.
- Assess education access, attendance, retention, participation and barriers to enrolment among targeted girls and boys, including internally displaced and host-community learners and children with disabilities.
- Assess learning-environment conditions, safety, WASH facilities, availability of teaching and learning materials, and school preparedness for drought, flood and displacement.
- Document the starting status of learner well-being, psychosocial support, safeguarding, referral awareness and community accountability mechanisms.
- Assess teacher capacity, motivation, well-being, training exposure and support needs.
- Assess household-level economic and protection barriers to education, including the relevance of cash support and flexible learning pathways.
- Provide disaggregated evidence to refine targeting, implementation priorities and monitoring arrangements.

### 3.2 Endline objectives

- Measure endline values for the same core indicators and assess changes from baseline.
- Assess the extent to which the project improved equitable access, participation, retention, learning continuity, safety and learner well-being.
- Examine the effectiveness and perceived relevance of project support, including learning spaces, materials, teacher support, psychosocial services, cash assistance, community engagement and preparedness actions.
- Assess differential results by sex, age, disability, displacement status, location and education pathway, where sample sizes permit.
- Identify unintended effects, remaining gaps, operational lessons and recommendations for future Education in Emergencies programming.
- Produce defensible evidence for ECW reporting, programme accountability and learning.

## 4. Scope of Work

The consultant or firm will be responsible for the full survey cycle for both rounds, from design through dissemination. The assignment will cover the following tasks:

- Review the ECW project document, revision request, results framework, indicator definitions, monitoring data, Phase 1 reports, safeguarding protocols and relevant assessment tools.
- Develop an inception report and detailed survey protocol, including an indicator measurement matrix, evaluation questions, sampling strategy, field plan, analysis plan, quality-assurance plan and risk-mitigation measures.
- Design or adapt quantitative and qualitative tools for learners, caregivers or households, teachers, head teachers, Community Education Committees, education authorities and relevant project stakeholders.
- Ensure that tools are age-appropriate, gender- and disability-sensitive, conflict-sensitive and suitable for formal and non-formal education settings.
- Translate tools into relevant local languages, back-check translations, program digital forms and conduct field testing and piloting.
- Recruit or support the selection of enumerators, deliver training, test enumerator competency and establish clear supervision and safeguarding arrangements.
- Undertake baseline and endline data collection using comparable tools, sampling procedures and quality controls.
- Clean, label and analyse quantitative and qualitative data; calculate indicator values; and compare baseline and endline findings.
- Facilitate validation sessions and produce concise, practical reports and presentations for NRC, implementing partners and relevant authorities.
- Submit all approved tools, anonymised datasets, syntax, codebooks, transcripts or structured notes, consent materials and supporting documentation.
