title: Senior Officer, Research & Innovation Partnerships
body:
***This position is open to candidates with existing work authorization in the location where the position is advertised.***

**Job Background/Overview:**

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) helps people affected by humanitarian crises to survive, recover and rebuild their lives. The Airbel Impact Lab is the research and innovation arm of the IRC. Airbel designs, tests, and scales cost-effective solutions for people affected by conflict and disaster, from new tools and technologies to cost analysis and rigorous research on what works. To keep innovating and deliver on its annual operating budget of about $25 million, Airbel relies on flexible private funding as well as project funding for impact and cost evidence generation in areas such as nutrition and immunization.

We are seeking a Senior Officer, Research & Innovation Partnerships to help raise this funding. This role supports the IRC’s high-value fundraising teams, who work with major individual donors, corporate partners, and foundations, to secure funding for research and innovation (R&I). It also helps Airbel put its work in front of the right donors without pulling the Airbel team away from their core work. You will turn technical findings into compelling, accurate donor-facing material, guide each opportunity from first lead to proposal submission, and keep both sides informed as awards are delivered.

**Major Responsibilities:**

You will work alongside the IRC’s high-value fundraisers, Airbel innovation project leads and researchers, program and technical experts, and finance and support teams to raise the profile of, and increase private funding for, the IRC’s research and innovation work. This role coordinates and connects technical expertise from Airbel’s experts with donor strategy and relationships led by fundraisers. Your job is to make sure both teams have what they need, when they need it, and to own the quality of what is produced along the way.

The major responsibilities will include:

**Turn research and innovation into donor-ready content (30%)**

- Draft donor-facing materials in partnership with Airbel teams, including pitch decks, one-pagers, briefing notes, and proposal narratives, tailored to each audience (individual philanthropists, corporate partners, foundations and trusts) so that what reaches reviewers is close to final rather than a blank template.
- Get involved at the start of each product, helping decide whether the audience needs a punchy high-level pitch or deeper technical content and shaping a clear outline, and at the end, rewriting dense technical content for external readers and polishing the final format.
- Build clear, evidence-based arguments that read as both visionary and grounded, using facts and figures accurately and without losing what is actually true about the work.
- Help fundraisers and Airbel leaders position Airbel’s funding priorities (core funding, pooled funds, and project funding) with the donors most likely to care about each, and shape project ideas and funding pitches that are ready for donor conversations.

**Share knowledge and build the pipeline (20%)**

- Be the fundraisers’ go-to source for what is happening in R&I right now: innovation opportunities, evidence generation priorities, project milestones, funding needs, and results worth sharing. Give fundraisers a heads-up on wins or risks before important donor conversations.
- Maintain and regularly update the tracker of private funding opportunities and awards for R&I, and flag new opportunities as soon as they are identified.
- Pass donor interest, feedback, and trends back to Airbel so teams know where to focus their pitch and proposal effort next.
- Support donor mapping, targeting, and briefings for R&I prospects, and help fundraisers track donor activity and progress toward revenue goals, including linkages with the organizations Impact at Scale funding priorities and other strategic initiatives.
- Work with Airbel leaders and fundraisers on strategy and pipeline development for priority areas, such as cost analysis, evidence generation, and innovative approaches that are ready to scale.
- Stay current on developments in humanitarian research and innovation, and on trends in private philanthropy, to inform fundraising efforts.

**Manage opportunities and proposals from first lead to submission (30%)**

- Run the go/no-go process (the decision on whether to pursue an opportunity) for R&I-linked funding opportunities: gather what the fundraiser knows about the gift, such as its value, timeline, donor restrictions, and likelihood; present it to Airbel in a format that supports a quick, clear decision; and start the internal approval workflow once a decision is made.
- Project-manage private donor proposals and reports from start to finish, including timelines, reviewers, and inputs from program, finance, and technical teams. Take ownership of content quality and the overall outcome, not just the workplan and reminders.
- Check draft proposals, budgets, and agreements against donor and IRC requirements before they go to the fundraiser, and confirm that internal approvals, waivers, and sign-offs happen at each stage so nothing stalls further down the line.
- Coordinate answers to donor questions and any revisions after a proposal is submitted. As needed, join donor meetings to provide technical expertise and strategy support.
- Ensure strong coordination with other Program Services team members and program units for decision-making and shared workflows on complex cross-departmental or multisectoral proposals

**Connect teams, improve how we work, and support active grants (20%)**

- Connect the right people at the right time. When a donor question, pitch, or site visit comes up, quickly route fundraisers to the right Airbel colleague, and route Airbel colleagues to the right fundraiser, setting up direct conversations between program leads and account managers rather than acting as a go-between. Help prepare Airbel colleagues for donor meetings.
- Help develop and document simple, clear ways of working between fundraising and Airbel teams, such as when each side should expect to hear from or update the other, and coordinate effective cross-team meetings with timely follow-up on decisions.
- For active awards, work with Airbel teams and fundraisers to track implementation and spending, and flag risks, delays, or amendment needs early. Coordinate reporting inputs and amendment documentation so donor reports are timely and high quality.
- Contribute to long-term donor relationships by ensuring donor requirements and compliance obligations are met throughout the life of a grant.
- Work closely with other Program Services team members to ensure ways of working for R&I fundraising are aligned with those of other departments such as Crisis Response, Recovery, and Development (CRRD), Resettlement, Asylum and Integration (RAI), et al.

**Essential Qualifications:**

- 6-7 years of related work experience in fundraising, partnerships, program development, or communications, preferably with a mission-driven organization
- Experience contributing directly to securing multi-million-dollar funding for evidence generation, innovation, or other technical programming, including with private philanthropy, such as major donors, corporate partners, or foundations,
- Outstanding writing skills, with a demonstrated ability to quickly get up to speed on technical content and turn highly technical or research content into clear, compelling material for non-expert audiences (a writing sample may be requested).
- Experience managing complex proposals, grants, or similar projects from start to finish, with a track record of delivering high-quality results under tight deadlines
- Experience with fundraising and grants management processes, including budgets, donor requirements, and reporting
- Excellent relationship management and communication skills, including the ability to build trust and influence senior colleagues without direct authority over them
- Experience working across diverse contexts with global, cross-cultural teams, including collaborating remotely

**Desired Qualifications:**

- Familiarity with how social innovation, evidence generation, or cost-effectiveness analysis is used in humanitarian or global development work
- Experience with customer relationship management (CRM) or pipeline tracking tools
- Knowledge of other IRC languages (Spanish, French, Arabic) would be an asset
- We strongly encourage applications from candidates who have lived experience in the contexts where the IRC operates

**Working Environment:**

This role may require working remotely, and occasional travel. If remote, applicants must have a home or alternate workspace they can effectively complete their work from during regularly scheduled hours.

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $93,000-$106,000/yr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

title: Head of Mission - Yemen
body:
INTERSOS is an independent humanitarian organization that assists the victims of natural disasters, armed conflicts and exclusion. Its activities are based on the principles of solidarity, justice, human dignity, equality of rights and opportunities, respect for diversity and coexistence, paying special attention to the most vulnerable people.

## **Terms of reference**

**Job Title:** Head of Mission

**Code:** SR-35-10204

**Duty station:** Aden / Sanaa with visits to the projects' sites

**Starting date:** 15/12/2026

**Contract duration:** 6 months (renewable)

**Reporting to:** Regional Director MENA

**Functional Supervisor:**

**Supervision of:** Senior Management Team

**Type of Duty Station:** Non-family duty station

## **General context of the project**

While the armed conflict entered its 12th year, Yemen remains one of the largest humanitarian crisis. The country’s deteriorating economy, the protracted conflict and crumbling basic services are exacerbating humanitarian needs across the country. Meanwhile, climate shocks, increased regional tensions and chronic underfunding of critical humanitarian sectors are further worsening people’s vulnerability and suffering.

Four years since the UN- brokered truce, international non-governmental organizations (INGOs) operating in Yemen warn that humanitarian conditions are more fragile than at any point since the peak years of the response. Over 22.2 million people 1 continue to face dire humanitarian conditions, struggling to meet basic needs and access essential services amid protracted crisis, economic deterioration, aid cuts, displacement and climate-related shocks. Furthermore, the escalating conflict in the Middle East and the wider region threatens to exacerbate the dire economic situation and could trigger a resumption of large-scale armed conflict within Yemen. These regional shifts risk disrupting vital humanitarian and commercial supply chains and inflating the cost of essential goods.

INTERSOS, in collaboration with local partners, has been providing essential health, nutrition, protection, water and sanitation, as well as livelihoods support for the vulnerable people across Yemen since 2008.  
While INTERSOS operational presence has been impacted by the signficant funding downsize in the last few years, the integrated programming serving the most vulnerable communities (IDPs, migrants, people at hightened protection risks) continues providing essential lifesaving aid.

## **General purpose of the position**

The Head of Mission represents INTERSOS in the country and acts on behalf of the Director General, leading the organization’s response, including strategy design, planning resources, management and implementation of programs.

## **Main responsibilities and tasks**

**Strategy and vision**

- Is responsible for monitoring and analysing the political and humanitarian situation across the country and surrounding countries through established contacts and carrying out exploratory missions to identify potential fields of intervention. Design, propose, elaborate and develop new strategy of interventions in line with INTERSOS values and principles.
- Explore and present funding opportunities that integrate initiatives and leverage impact for the communities; support and direct fund-raising activities with institutional and private donors.
- Monitor donor’s priorities and intervention strategies in the country. Guarantee the strict observance and adherence to INTERSOS and donors’ procedures.
- Overview the development and implementation of projects and programs and through periodic visits to the areas of intervention, evaluate their evolution and quality as per internal and external standards and requirements, final results and achievements to ensure that organization’s technical and ethical standards are respected and objectives are achieved.
- Greenlight project proposals and response to emergencies to be submitted to HQ for approval. Evaluate potential emergency responses in the country and lead on developing additional programs in line with review and assessment results.
- Lead the detailed country strategy planning process and prioritising of actions and resources to achieve program objectives.

**Representation and advocacy**

- Represent the organisation and manage relations with the authorities ensuring smooth and timely implementation of planned interventions and safeguarding impartiality and independence.
- Follow up, guarantee and monitor government recognition procedures for the organisation in compliance with the host country formalities.
- Maintain a productive communication with donors and ensure that the assessed needs are communicated to impact on donors’ priorities.
- Represent INTERSOS in relevant fora.

**People management**

- Ensure that the senior management team is effective, mutually supporting and sufficiently involved in key decision-making processes.
- In coordination with the HR Coordinator, guide and supervise the staff performance process for international and national staff.
- Ensure the respect organisational values, Code of Ethics, Organization Management and Control Model, and INTERSOS procedures.
- Maintain high ethical standards and promote teamwork and ensure a productive working environment.
- Empower staff to meet organizational goals and work as a highly functioning and cooperative team.

**Finance, logistics and supply**

- Together with the Finance Coordinator, define and oversee the overall financial management of the mission, striving towards financial sustainability and assume responsibility for the mission funds management (NGO budget).
- Ensure that allocated resources are managed effectively and transparently.
- Together with the Logistics and Supply Coordinator, ensure that required and efficient supply services and processes are in place.

**Safety and security**

- Hold final accountability for security, including development and validation of country security plan and ensuring adherence to procedures, monitoring of the context development, analysis and provision of recommendations.
- Regularly interact with the Regional Office and the Security Advisor on security issues.
- Hold final responsibility for any decision concerning security in the country.

**Accountability and quality control**

- In collaboration with the SMT is responsible to produce and submit the mission monthly activity reports.
- Continuously assess, analyse and evaluate the impact of the country program and operations, also through periodic visits to the areas of intervention, in collaboration with the Program Coordinator and MEAL.
- Ensure all the policies within INTERSOS Safeguarding Framework are respected by the staff
- Together with MEAL Department, supervise the effectiveness of a complaint feedback mechanism
- Oversee program quality and impact in line with established strategic objectives and related indicators.
- Oversee program reporting, ensuring compliance with INTERSOS policies and procedures, donor regulations and national requirements.

## **Required profile and experience**

**Education**

- University degree Project management, International Affairs, Development, International Political Economy or other relevant field

**Professional experience**

- At minimum eight years experience in management positions in humanitarian contexts
- Previous experience working in Yemen and/or other countries in the Middle East is considered a strong asset

**Professional requirements**

- Experience with NGOs in humanitarian response contexts
- Experience with major grants and international donors (e.g., ECHO, etc)
- Experience of working within an insecure environment with responsibility for security planning, monitoring and management
- Experience in managing humanitarian access in complex contexts
- Essential computer literacy (word, excel and internet)

**Languages**

- Full fluency in English language
- Arabic language is considered an asset

**Personal requirements**

- Strategic vision
- Good organizational and planning skills
- Leadership, team management and cooperation
- Behavioral flexibility
- Networking, negotiation skills and decision-making skills
- Diplomatic, interpersonal and good communication skills
- Ability to take initiative and work independently
- Strong analytical and practical problem-solving skills
- Commitment to INTERSOS principles.

## **General conditions and benefits**

- **Salary range:** 14 - 4.505€ - 5.182€ monthly gross
- **Accommodation:** Shared Guesthouse
- **R&R:** 7 days of psycho-physical recovery every 8 weeks + 1000€ allowance.
- **Annual Leave:** 2.5 days per month
- **Medical insurance** for the staff
- **Transportation and visa:** Round-trip flights. For missions lasting at *least 9 months,* an additional flight ticket to the Country of residence and return to the mission will also be provided.
- **Induction:** one week of online induction before the deployment

title: Human Resources and Administration Assistant
body:
Danish Refugee Council, one of the world’s leading humanitarian NGOs, is currently looking for a highly qualified **Human Resources and Administration Assistant**.

## **About the job** 

Responsible for performing general Human Resources and Administration functions, playing a key role in the overall HR functions including participating and organizing staff recruitment processes, contracts preparations and review, guesthouse management, visa preparation tracking etc.

Your main duties and responsibilities will be:

**Human Resources**

- Supervise and assist in ensuring staff compliance with human resources polices, as per DRC’s Operations Handbook and local HR Handbook.
- Ensure that leave, recruitment, contract, and training trackers are updated on a regular basis.
- Assist in communicating with interview candidates and scheduling for tests and interviews.
- Review employee contracts and ensure completion of contracts requirements, in coordination with HR Team at ALT office
- Work closely with the finance department to ensure all contracts are reflected in the organization Master Budget.
- Responsible for ensuring the following are accurate, complete and up to date: -personnel files, administration of health insurance scheme, social security,

- Ensure new staff receive an appropriate orientation and induction with different departments, schedule timetables, and receive work related tools.

- Ensure that DRC staff have Identification cards (ID) and supervise a record of handover and clearance

## **About you** 

To be successful in this role we expect you to have At least 2 year's relevant work experience in similar field such as Administration, Human Resources, etc.

Moreover, we also expect the following:

- Proven experience in HR and administrative tasks
- Good communication skills and team spirit
- Proficient in spoken and written English and Arabic.

In this position, you are expected to demonstrate DRC’ five core competencies:

- Striving for excellence: You focus on reaching results while ensuring an efficient process.

## **We offer** 

- Contract length: Until Jun 30, 2027
- Band: NMI
- Designation of Duty Station: Tripoli
- Suggested Start date: 15 Dec 2026

Salary and conditions will be in accordance with Danish Refugee Council’s Terms of Employment for national employees; please refer to [our website](https://drc.ngo/about-drc/vacancies). For questions regarding the vacancy please contact Us.

## **Application process** 

All applicants must upload a cover letter and an updated CV (no longer than four pages) in English. Applications sent by email will not be considered.

Closing date for applications: 30 November 2026

For further information about the Danish Refugee Council, please consult our website [drc.ngo](https://drc.ngo/).

title: RFP JOR-FWA-0039 – Framework Agreement for Evaluation Consultants
body:
**RFP JOR-FWA-0039 – Framework Agreement for Evaluation Consultants**

**About CARE Jordan**  
CARE International in Jordan implements multi-year protection, livelihoods, gender and resilience projects for refugees and vulnerable Jordanians in urban, camp and non-camp settings, funded by institutional donors such as ADA and ECHO. Each project requires an independent evaluation, often within short timelines.

**Purpose**  
CARE Jordan is establishing a framework agreement with a pool of pre-qualified local and international evaluators (individual consultants and firms), so that evaluations can start on time under consistent quality, ethics and safeguarding standards.

**Scope of services**  
Final (endline) evaluations of CARE Jordan projects and, depending on the assignment, midterm reviews, baseline and endline studies, and outcome-focused reviews. Tasks include designing the evaluation, collecting data through mixed methods, analysing results, writing the report and presenting findings. Routine monitoring and audits are not covered.

**Expertise areas**  
Protection, GBV and MHPSS; cash assistance, livelihoods and economic empowerment; gender equality and inclusion; humanitarian-development-peace nexus and resilience; quantitative survey design and analysis; qualitative and theory-based methods.

**Minimum requirements**

- At least 7 years of experience in evaluating humanitarian or development programmes, and at least 3 completed evaluations in the last 5 years.
- A master’s degree or equivalent experience in a relevant field.
- Demonstrated experience with GBV-sensitive and safeguarding-aware data collection.
- Local applicants: fluent Arabic and English. International applicants: experience in the Middle East or comparable refugee contexts and access to Arabic speakers.
- Independence: no conflict of interest with the CARE projects to be evaluated.

Consortia are accepted, with one lead applicant. Experience with institutional donors such as ADA and ECHO is an advantage.

Full details, application requirements and the selection process are in the RFP and Terms of Reference: [RFP JOR-FWA-0039 – FWA for Evaluation Consultants](https://careinternational-my.sharepoint.com/:f:/g/personal/rajaa_abumohammad_care_org/IgCJOJntGdR_SYO1DfOr3qHAAU3MKcKD6kJx24BKguMrGa0?e=OvrNRG)

title: Area Manager Maradi Niger
body:
**Background**

The humanitarian crisis in the Central Sahel remains severe, complex and fast evolving, driven by conflict, displacement, climate shocks, food insecurity and shrinking operational space. In Niger and Burkina Faso, millions of people continue to require humanitarian assistance; while underfunding, insecurity and access constraints place sustained pressure on principled humanitarian action and programme quality.

Niger continues to face a protracted humanitarian crisis driven by insecurity, climate-related events, and chronic poverty, disrupting livelihoods for families and communities. Nearly one million displaced people, including refugees and internally displaced persons, are living in Niger, many of them in the regions of Tillabéri, Tahoua and Diffa.

NRC is currently working in Niger, with staff dedicated to assisting people affected by conflict. Its humanitarian interventions are based on programming expertise in core competencies including Education, WASH, Information Counselling and Legal Assistance (ICLA), Protection from Violence, and Shelter to vulnerable displaced people.

Within the Central Sahel Multi-Country Office (MCO) model, Burkina Faso and Niger are managed under a unified structure led by the Central Sahel MCO Country Director, while maintaining strong Area Office delivery hubs.

The Area Manager – Maradi is responsible for leading NRC’s area operations in the Maradi / Tillabéri / Dosso / Tahoua area, ensures high standard of project delivery and contributes to multi-country coherence through participation in the Multi-Country Management Group (MCMG).

Find out more about NRC [https://www.nrc.no/](https://www.nrc.no/%22%20/t%20%22_blank) and Watch this short video to see NRC in action [https://vimeo.com/736782633](https://vimeo.com/736782633%22%20/t%20%22_blank)

**What we are looking for**

The purpose of the Area Manager position is to ensure high quality and cost-effective programme/project implementation in the Maradi, Tillabéri, and Tahoua Regions of Niger. The Area Manager supervises several field offices/antennas – Tillabéri, Tahoua, Dosso (non-exhaustive).

**What you will do**

- Overall responsibility of managing the Maradi / Tillabéri Area Office including potential sub offices, with close supervision of the Field Manager in Tillabéri
- Responsible for overall staff security, including completing security risk assessments for the area and possible new areas of intervention
- Support needs assessment in the region, ensure the implementation of all projects active in the area in line with the agreed standards and donors’ requirements; this includes ensuring that NRC’s data collection systems are in place and information is properly stored and analyzed
- Support the team in identifying the gaps for further programming and development, and participate in assessments for new areas of operation, possible areas of intervention, aiding the development of program strategy for implementation.
- Lead on access strategy and its implementation in hard-to-reach areas, in close collaboration with CD and relevant colleagues at the country level. This includes contextualizing, adapting, and implementing SOPs and procedures to ensure effective provision of assistance to hard-to-reach areas
- In conjunction with Country Office, liaise with donors on new funding and operational areas of programming, liaise regularly with local authorities (political and security), donors and humanitarian actors in the operational area. This includes support in the development of concept notes, project proposals, and budgets for scale-up of post emergency activities
- Represent NRC at coordination platforms at area level and provide regular feedback and input to advocacy initiatives
- Overall responsibility for staff management. Recruitment of qualified staff for the area office, in close collaboration with HR and support team in the Country Office, lead by example the teams on the ground on NRC’s core values (dedication, innovation, inclusion and accountability). Ensuring training is provided to all staff and capacity building initiatives are in place, work and development plans are completed by all staff in the operational area, and performance feedback sessions are conducted on a minimum quarterly basis
- Ensure sound financial management, including the Master Budget is covered and up to date, reflecting cost-efficient use of the available funding

Please download the detailed job description to learn more about the [JD Area Manager Maradi-Tillabéri Niger .pdf](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:b:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQBHy7h6uVMuQ6WNdVjh2jUiAXcbCfRs-sXSEBD6a1lIVN4?e=3ZheyZ)

**What you will bring**

**1.Professional Competencies**

- Minimum 3-5 years of experience working as a Senior Project Manager / field manager in a humanitarian and recovery context
- Previous experience working in complex and volatile contexts
- Documented results related to the position’s responsibilities
- Knowledge about own leadership skills/profile
- Fluency in French and proficiency in English, both written and verbal

***Context related skills, knowledge and experience***

- Knowledge of the context in West Africa and Niger in particular
- Experience working in insecure / hard to reach locations
- Experience managing safety and security
- Competencies in humanitarian and access negotiations

**2. Behavioural competencies**

- Handling insecure environments
- Strategic thinking
- Empowering and building trust
- Managing performance and development
- Managing resources to optimise results
- Coping with change

***Leadership profile***

- Building meaningful relations
- Acting with integrity
- Empowering people
- Delivering results

**What we offer**

- **Duty station**: Maradi,Niger
- **Contract**: Fixed term for 12 months with possibility of extension
- **Salary&Benefits**: Grade 10 on NRC’s National salary scale
- NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability.
- We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative.
- Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC [https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)
- Kindly send any questions about the application process to: ***cwa.recruitment@nrc.no***. *Applications sent via email will not be accepted. Please check your application status on your NRC application profile.*

**Female Applicants are Highly encouraged to Apply**

title: Protection from Violence Programme Development Manager Ethiopia Addis Ababa
body:
**What we’re looking for:**

NRC Ethiopia is looking for a dynamic and strategic **Protection from Violence (PFV) Programme Development Manager (PDM)** to provide technical leadership and drive the growth, quality and impact of its Protection from Violence programming.

In this role, you will lead the technical development and strategic direction of the PFV Core Competency, spearhead programme development and fundraising initiatives, and ensure high-quality programme delivery across the operation. You will also strengthen technical capacity through staff mentoring, training and coaching, while providing oversight of programme quality, MEAL, budget management and procurement to ensure effective implementation and accountability.

We are looking for a leader who can translate protection priorities into impactful programmes, build strong technical teams and drive sustainable programming that responds to the needs of people affected by displacement and violence.

*Please note: This opportunity is open exclusively to Ethiopian nationals.*

**What You Will Do:**

Here are some of your generic responsibilities:

- Develop and implement the Protection from Violence strategy for NRC Ethiopia including Macro Log frames that are aligned with country and global strategies priorities.
- Develop technical standards, SOPs, guidance documents for PFV across NRC Ethiopia, under the guidance of NRC’s PFV Global Advisers
- Promote the rights of conflict- and displacement-affected people in line with the advocacy strategy. Undertake Protection Advocacy initiatives.
- Contribute to fundraising, develop and revise funding proposal, budgets and donor reports.
- Overall technical management and mentorship of project staff across NRC Ethiopia
- Provide systematic training and build capacity of technical staff, in approaches including cash-based interventions and market-based programme
- Oversee PFV project(s) implementation across NRC Ethiopia, including development and oversight of Community Feedback Mechanism
- Lead the localization agenda of NRC Ethiopia for PFV. Identify meaningful partners for strategic cooperation aiming to advance PFV portfolio across Ethiopia.
- Follow up on compliance with contractual commitments within PFV, ensure high technical quality products
- Ensure that key learnings are extracted from Protection from Violence implementation, and incorporate them in Protection from Violence and staff development processes
- Represent NRC in relevant forums/clusters, including with national authorities and donors

Please download a more detailed[**JOB DESCRIPTION**](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:w:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQAt92z8Iv4rSqzgkeTdghASAZNyyCLKN07CJRmwR94cBx8?e=poxnT3) for more specific duties and responsibilities.

**What you will bring:**

- Graduate degree with minimum 5 years of relevant experience from a senior level project implementation position in a humanitarian/recovery context.
- Excellent understanding of protection issues in emergency and displacement situations
- Detailed knowledge of humanitarian and protection principles and guidelines for humanitarian assistance
- Good understanding of Protection Cluster coordination mechanisms
- Strong coordination, representation skills and inter-personal skills, working well both in teams and independently
- Self-motivated and excellent observer of protection issues
- Able to work under pressure and good at timely decision making
- Excellent written and spoken English
- Knowledge of international legal and policy processes and instruments relating to displacement, protection, peace/conflict, and humanitarian action
- Cogent communication skills, both written and verbal
- Aptitude to think creatively and boldly, to engage (potentially hostile) protection and access advocacy targets
- Strong experience in programme development and management
- Experience in training facilitation and capacity-building
- Experience in Ethiopia mandatory
- Willingness to spend a significant period of time at NRC’s Area Offices
- This position is open to Ethiopian nationals only.

**What we offer:**

- Duty station: Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.
- Contract: 12 months.
- Travel: Up to 40%.
- Salary/benefits: grade 9 on NRC’s Resident salary scale, with accompanying terms and conditions.
- NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability.
- We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative.

[Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)

Important information about the application process

- For Internal candidates: To apply as an internal candidate, log in with your official email or click on Opportunity Market Place.
- When creating your profile, include your full name as given on your passport. Complete all the system-required fields for experience, employment history and education.
- Submit your application and CV in English, taking care to attach your latest CV.
- Applications that do not meet the minimum standards in terms of experience or qualifications will generally not be considered. Unsolicited applications not related to this specific job advertisement will not be considered.
- We receive many applications for each vacant position and so only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

If you have any questions about this role, please email **ho.recruitment@nrc.no**with the job title as the subject line.

**Why NRC?**

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee. Our 15,000 staff work in crises across 40 countries, providing life-saving and long-term assistance to millions of people every year.

[Watch this short video](https://vimeo.com/736782633) to see NRC in action.

We are looking for people who are passionate about helping refugees and people forced to flee. Are you one of those people? If you are, NRC offers you the opportunity to:

- do demanding and professional work, often in challenging contexts.
- join a work culture that empowers every employee to share ideas and take responsibility.
- be part of a welcoming and supportive community committed to human dignity.

## About Us

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is a global humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee.

Join us in assisting millions of people in areas where others cannot, tackling some of the world's most dangerous and difficult crises. Bring your skills and dedication to an organisation recognised for providing high quality aid and for defending the rights of refugees and internally displaced people.

At NRC, we give responsibility to employees at all levels and foster professional growth and innovative teams. You can expect a supportive culture and an open dialogue with management. We are committed to diversity, equity and inclusion.

Together, we save lives and rebuild futures.

Safeguarding is central to NRC’s work. We expect all employees to:

• treat everyone with respect and dignity

• contribute to building a safe environment for all

• never engage in any form of exploitation, harassment and specifically sexual exploitation, abuse and sexual harassment (SEAH)

• always report. NRC has a zero-tolerance approach to inaction against exploitation, abuse and SEAH

title: Protection Officer - Hasaka
body:
**About World Vision**

For more than 75 years, World Vision has been committed to making a positive and lasting difference in the world. We have become a global leader in improving and transforming the lives of children, their families, and their communities. We help children, families, and communities overcome poverty and injustice, irrespective of religion, race, ethnicity, or gender. Every child deserves a life rich in meaning and purpose. We work with the most vulnerable children in the world so they can experience life in all its fullness.

**Job purpose:**

The Protection Officer is responsible for the technical and day-to-day implementation of protection activities within the project, ensuring that interventions are relevant, inclusive, safe, conflict-sensitive, and aligned with approved project objectives, protection standards, workplans, and donor requirements. The position supports the planning, monitoring, quality assurance, and reporting of protection interventions, while providing technical guidance to protection facilitators, volunteers, partners, and other relevant field staff. The Protection Officer also works closely with relevant protection stakeholders, communities, authorities, and other project sectors to identify and respond to protection risks and promote safe, dignified, and inclusive support to children, adults, and vulnerable groups.

Activities will address relevant hygiene priorities, including handwashing with soap at critical times, safe drinking water handling and storage, household cleanliness, environmental hygiene, sanitation practices, menstrual hygiene management where relevant and appropriate, and prevention of waterborne diseases. The Hygiene Promoter will adapt communication approaches according to age, gender, disability, literacy level, cultural context, and the specific needs of the target population.

The Hygiene Promoter will work closely with the WASH team, community mobilizers, local authorities, community leaders, health actors, and other relevant stakeholders to ensure that hygiene promotion activities are inclusive, safe, culturally appropriate, and aligned with approved project objectives and technical guidance. The position will also support the identification of hygiene-related concerns and barriers within communities and communicate relevant findings to the supervisor for appropriate follow-up

**Major Responsibilities:**

**Protection Programme Implementation and Technical Support 30%**

- Support the planning and implementation of protection activities in line with the approved project design, DIP, performance framework, protection standards, and relevant humanitarian principles.
- Provide technical guidance to protection facilitators, volunteers, partner staff, and other field teams involved in protection activities.
- Ensure protection interventions respond to identified protection risks, needs, vulnerabilities, and barriers to accessing services.
- Support the adaptation of protection activities to the local context and the specific needs of children, women, persons with disabilities, displaced populations, and other vulnerable or marginalized groups.
- Promote safe, inclusive, gender-sensitive, child-sensitive, and conflict-sensitive approaches throughout protection programming.
- Ensure that activities are implemented according to the principles of Do No Harm, confidentiality, informed consent, dignity, participation, and non-discrimination.

**Protection Monitoring, Risk Identification and Referrals 20%**

- Support the identification and monitoring of protection risks, concerns, trends, and barriers affecting children, adults, and vulnerable groups.
- Conduct or support protection assessments, community consultations, focus group discussions, key informant interviews, and other relevant data collection activities.
- Identify individuals or groups requiring additional or specialized protection support and facilitate referrals through established referral pathways.
- Maintain updated information on available protection and other relevant services and referral mechanisms.
- Ensure referrals are conducted safely, confidentially, and in accordance with established procedures.
- Monitor emerging protection concerns and communicate significant risks or trends to the Project Coordinator/Protection Manager and relevant programme teams.
- Support protection risk mitigation measures and follow up on identified protection concerns within the scope of the position.

**Monitoring, Quality Assurance and Capacity Building 20%**

- Develop and follow up on protection activity plans, schedules, and field implementation plans.
- Monitor participation, coverage, quality, and progress against agreed protection indicators and targets.
- Conduct regular field visits and provide technical feedback and recommendations to improve protection activities.
- Support the collection, review, verification, and analysis of protection-related data and ensure that information is accurate and timely.
- Identify implementation gaps, protection risks, and emerging needs and propose appropriate corrective actions.
- Identify capacity-building needs among protection staff, volunteers, partners, and community structures.
- Support the delivery of training, coaching, mentoring, and awareness sessions on relevant protection topics, including protection principles, safeguarding, PSEA, referral mechanisms, and safe programming.

**Coordination and Stakeholder Engagement 15%**

- Coordinate with relevant Protection Sector/Sub-Sector actors, authorities, partners, community representatives, service providers, and other stakeholders as required.
    - Participate in relevant protection coordination meetings, working groups, technical discussions, and inter-agency coordination mechanisms.
    - Engage with communities to understand protection concerns, priorities, barriers, and feedback and ensure that programme responses are appropriate and context-sensitive.
    - Support community-based protection mechanisms and promote meaningful participation of women, men, girls, boys, persons with disabilities, and other potentially marginalized groups.
    - Coordinate with other project sectors to ensure protection is appropriately mainstreamed across programme interventions, including Education, WASH, FSL, PSS, and other relevant sectors.
    - Promote safe, dignified, accessible, and inclusive programme approaches and support teams to identify and mitigate protection risks.
    - Support the identification and strengthening of referral pathways and linkages with specialized services.

**Reporting, Documentation and Learning 15%**

- Prepare regular protection activity updates and contribute to project reports, donor reports, situation updates, and other programme documentation.
    - Maintain comprehensive and secure records of protection activities, including attendance, training, monitoring, assessments, community consultations, referrals, and field visits, in accordance with data protection requirements.
    - Document protection trends, challenges, achievements, good practices, lessons learned, and success stories while ensuring confidentiality and protection of sensitive information.
    - Support the implementation of community feedback and response mechanisms and ensure relevant protection-related feedback is appropriately followed up.
    - Support the preparation and review of protection-related proposals, budgets, activity plans, indicators, and project documents as required.
    - Coordinate with MEAL colleagues to support data quality, monitoring, accountability, and learning processes.
    - Ensure protection documentation is maintained in accordance with organizational, donor, safeguarding, and data protection requirements.

**Knowledge/Qualifications for the Role**.

1. **Required Professional Experience**

- At least 2–3 years of relevant experience in protection, humanitarian, development, or community-based programming, preferably with an NGO or humanitarian organization.
- Experience implementing or monitoring protection, child protection, community-based protection, protection monitoring, awareness-raising, or referral activities is desirable.
- Experience working with children, families, displaced populations, vulnerable groups, and communities affected by conflict or displacement.
- Experience providing technical support, coaching, mentoring, or capacity building to staff, volunteers, community structures, or partner organizations.
- Experience working with Protection Sector/Sub-Sector coordination mechanisms, referral networks, local authorities, service providers, or other humanitarian actors is an advantage..

1. **Required Education, training, license, registration, and certification:**

- Bachelor's degree in Social Work, Psychology, Sociology, Human Rights, Law, International Development, Social Sciences, or another relevant field.
- Additional qualifications or training in Protection, Child Protection, GBV, PSEA, Safeguarding, Humanitarian Action, Human Rights, or related areas are an advantage.

1. **Preferred Knowledge and Qualifications**

- Good knowledge of Protection programming principles and approaches relevant to humanitarian and/or development contexts.
- Understanding of barriers to protection access and participation, particularly for vulnerable and marginalized children.
- Knowledge of child safeguarding, child participation, inclusion, gender, and conflict-sensitive programming.
- Good monitoring, data collection, analysis, and reporting skills.
- Strong communication, facilitation, interpersonal, and coordination skills.
- Ability to work effectively with partners, community representatives, education

1. **Travel and/or Work Environment Requirement**

Non

1. **Physical Requirements**

Non

1. **Language Requirements**

- Good in English and Fluent in Arabic

title: National Non-Technical Survey/ Explosive Ordnance Risk Education Manager
body:
**Who are we?**

The Danish Refugee Council assists refugees and internally displaced persons across the globe: we provide emergency aid, fight for their rights, and strengthen their opportunities for a brighter future. We work in conflict-affected areas, along the displacement routes, and in the countries where refugees settle. In cooperation with local communities, we strive for responsible and sustainable solutions. We work toward successful integration and – whenever possible – for the fulfillment of the wish to return home. The Danish Refugee Council was founded in Denmark in 1956 and has since grown to become an international humanitarian organization with more than 7,000 staff and 8,000 volunteers. Our vision is a dignified life for all displaced. All of our efforts are based on our value compass: humanity, respect, independence and neutrality, participation, and honesty and transparency.

**DRC Syria**

DRC has been operating in Syria since 2008, initially responding to the Iraqi refugee crisis before pivoting to a full-scale response to the Syria crisis from 2011 onwards. Our work encompasses the full cycle of displacement—responding to life-saving humanitarian needs and supporting community recovery until durable solutions can be achieved. DRC Syria takes an area-based approach to supporting internally displaced persons (IDPs), returnees, and host communities across our key sectors: Economic Recovery and Resilience, Protection, WASH, Shelter and Infrastructure, and Humanitarian Disarmament and Peacebuilding (including Humanitarian Mine Action). With an established rapid response mechanism, DRC can rapidly respond to emerging crises and shocks to meet acute emergency needs. Recognizing the significant need for early recovery and resilience programming to ensure dignified, sustainable, and cost-effective solutions for fragile communities, DRC’s programmes foster resilience for individuals and communities in situations of protracted displacement and during the initial stages of post-conflict recovery, towards a durable solution of their choice. With active portfolios in the neighboring countries of Jordan, Lebanon, Türkiye and Iraq, DRC offers a cross-border, regional response to the Syria crisis, through cross-border protection monitoring, advocacy, and trends analysis.

**Overall purpose of the role**: The NTS/EORE Manager leads and oversees DRC’s Non-Technical Survey (NTS), Community Liaison (CL), and Explosive Ordnance Risk Education (EORE) activities in Syria, ensuring full compliance with International Mine Action Standards (IMAS), national standards, and DRC Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs).

The role is responsible for the planning, implementation, quality management, and continuous improvement of NTS/EORE operations, while contributing to the strategic development of DRC’s Humanitarian Mine Action (HMA) programme. This includes developing and adapting SOPs, tools, and methodologies in line with the evolving operational context.

A key function of the role is to ensure strong integration of NTS/EORE with DRC’s broader recovery portfolio, including HLP, livelihoods, shelter, WASH, and protection, so that mine action activities directly enable safe, sustainable, and area-based recovery outcomes.

The NTS/EORE Manager ensures that DRC effectively maps EO contamination through systematic identification, recording, and analysis of hazardous areas, while delivering targeted EORE to reduce risk-taking behavior among affected populations.

This is a twelve-month, country-wide role designed to support the scale-up, consolidation, and standardization of NTS/EORE operations across Syria. The position offers a unique opportunity to shape operational approaches, systems, and tools during a critical phase of programme expansion.

**Key Responsibilities and Accountabilities:**

**Technical Management and Implementation**

- Lead the planning, implementation, and oversight of NTS, CL, and EORE activities in assigned areas
- Ensure activities are conducted safely, efficiently, and in line with IMAS, national standards, and DRC SOPs
- Oversee tasking, deployment, and daily management of NTS/EORE teams
- Ensure systematic integration of NTS/EORE outputs into clearance prioritization and broader HMA programming
- Ensure that NTS/EORE activities are aligned with and support DRC’s recovery interventions, including livelihoods, shelter, infrastructure, WASH, and protection
- Lead the development, revision, and contextualization of SOPs, guidelines, and tools for NTS, CL, and EORE
- Develop and refine data collection tools, prioritization tools, and methodologies
- Ensure alignment of operational tools with IMAS and evolving national standards
- Promote continuous improvement and adaptation of approaches based on operational learning
- Develop monthly team workplans linked to project targets, locations and available resources; coordinate implementation with Technical Field Managers and Area Managers and escalate delivery gaps to the HMA Operations Manager.
- Ensure deployment readiness in accordance with approved safety, communications and medical procedures; suspend unsafe activities and immediately report concerns to the HMA Operations Manager.
- Lead EORE needs assessments, adapt and pre-test messages and materials for different at-risk groups, and work with MEAL to assess understanding and safer behavior.

**Strategy and Programme Development**

- Contribute to the strategic development and expansion of DRC’s HMA programme in Syria
- Provide technical inputs to proposal development, concept notes, and donor engagement
- Actively promote area-based and nexus approaches, ensuring mine action enables and is integrated with recovery and development outcomes
- Identify operational gaps and opportunities for scale-up and cross-sector collaboration

**Staff Management & Capacity Development**

- Line manage and supervise NTS/EORE team leaders and field teams
- Design and deliver initial and refresher training in NTS, CL, and EORE
- Lead capacity development of national staff, including substantial training, mentoring and on-the-job training
- Lead EORE/ NTS capacity development of national authorities (e.g. NMAC) and relevant stakeholders

**Quality Management, Monitoring & IM**

- Ensure strong quality assurance (QA) and quality control (QC) of all NTS/EORE activities
- Oversee data collection, verification, and analysis related to EO contamination
- Track progress against targets and indicators
- Ensure data is accurately captured, stored, and shared with relevant stakeholders (e.g. SNMAC, MA AoR)
- Strengthen linkages between operations and Information Management (IM)
- Document QA findings and non-conformities, assign corrective actions and deadlines, and verify closure.
- Coordinate with IM and MEAL on indicator definitions, disaggregated beneficiary reporting and prevention of double counting; protect personal and sensitive information and share it only through approved procedures.

**Coordination & External Liaison**

- Liaise with Mine Action AoR, relevant working groups and other operators to ensure alignment and avoid duplication
- Engage with local authorities, community leaders, and civil society actors
- Represent DRC in relevant coordination forums as required
- Support coordination on tasking, prioritization, and information sharing

**Budget Management, Reporting & Compliance**

- Manage EORE/NTS budgets and track expenditures against targets as well as progress
- Prepare and oversee high-quality internal and donor reporting (weekly, monthly, and ad hoc)
- Ensure timely submission of field reports and data
- Contribute to donor reports with technical inputs and analysis
- Exercise budget responsibilities within delegated authority, coordinating expenditure forecasts and procurement planning with the HMA Operations Manager and the Head of HDP

**Integrated Programming and Housing, Land and Property (HLP)**

- Strengthen operational linkages between NTS/EORE and DRC's Protection, HLP, Economic Recovery, Shelter and WASH programmes, ensuring that contamination data and risk assessments inform integrated, area-based interventions.
- Facilitate joint assessments, operational planning and referral pathways with other DRC sectors, enabling mine action to support safe access to land, infrastructure, essential services and livelihoods.
- Act as the HMA technical focal point for a HLP consultancy, supporting the development, field-testing and operationalization of harmonized HLP due diligence guidance, tools and procedures for Syria's mine action sector.
- Ensure HLP considerations, including land ownership, tenure, access, competing claims and potential land-related disputes, are systematically integrated into NTS, community liaison, prioritization and land release planning.
- Coordinate with DRC's HLP specialists, the HLP Technical Working Group, Mine Action AoR and relevant national stakeholders to support the adoption of harmonized HLP approaches and their potential integration into National Mine Action Standards.
- Promote conflict-sensitive approaches to survey and land release, ensuring that HMA interventions do not inadvertently exacerbate land disputes, exclusion or community tensions.
- Refer land disputes and legal questions to qualified HLP specialists; provide operational input to HLP processes within the manager’s technical competence and delegated authority.

**Safeguarding, Inclusion and Accountability**

- Ensure compliance with DRC’s Code of Conduct, safeguarding and prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse requirements; report concerns through designated channels.
- Ensure inclusive participation and accessible community complaints and feedback channels, and coordinate appropriate referrals with Protection and Accountability colleagues.
- Undertake any other tasks as required by HMA Operations Manager and Head of HDP.

**Experience and technical competencies:**

- Minimum 5 years of experience in EORE and NTS within humanitarian mine action (HMA) programmes
- At least two years of experience supervising teams or managing EORE/NTS activities.
- NTS and EORE qualified
- QMS qualified (is an asset)
- Demonstrated experience in managing and training NTS, Community Liaison (CL), and EORE teams, including capacity development of national staff and authorities
- Strong knowledge of IMAS and SOPs applicable to NTS, CL, and EORE, including quality management (QA/QC)
- Proven experience in developing, adapting, and implementing SOPs, tools, and methodologies
- Solid understanding of EO contamination patterns and operational context in Syria or similar environments, including familiarity with military tactics and their impact on contamination
- Knowledge of land release processes, including NTS–TS–clearance linkages, and familiarity with clearance methodologies and equipment
- Experience integrating HMA with other humanitarian and recovery sectors, particularly HLP, including an understanding of land tenure risks, conflict sensitivity and the role of NTS in supporting integrated, area-based programming (desirable).
- Experience with information management and data analysis, including IMSMA and GIS tools (e.g. QGIS, ArcGIS, Garmin/BaseCamp or similar)
- Experience contributing to programme development, reporting, and donor engagement
- Strong coordination and representation skills, including engagement with national authorities, UN agencies, and other operators.

**Education**:

- Relevant university degree or technical qualification, or substantial directly relevant professional experience in lieu of a formal academic qualification.
- Documented NTS and EORE training and demonstrated technical competence remain essential.

**Languages:**

- Strong working English, both spoken and written.
- Fluent in Arabic, both spoken and written.

*In this position, you are expected to demonstrate DRC’ five core competencies:*

- **Striving for excellence**: You focus on reaching results while ensuring an efficient process.
- **Collaborating**: You involve relevant parties and encourage feedback.
- **Taking the lead**: You take ownership and initiative while aiming for innovation.
- **Communicating**: You listen and speak effectively and honestly.
- **Demonstrating integrity**: You act in line with our vision and values.

**We offer:**

- **Contract length**: 12 months (Extension based on performance and funds)
- **Salary Level**: MF2 (in accordance with the DRC's salary scale)
- **Location**: Rural Damascus
- **Expected Start Date:** As soon as possible

title: Country Director
body:
**This position is open to candidates with existing work authorization in the location where the position is advertised.**

**BACKGROUND**

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world’s worst humanitarian crises and helps people to survive and rebuild their lives. Founded in 1933 at the request of Albert Einstein, the IRC offers lifesaving care and life-changing assistance to refugees forced to flee from war or disaster. At work today in over 40 countries, we restore safety, dignity and hope to millions who are uprooted and struggling to endure. The mission of the IRC is to help people whose lives and livelihoods are shattered by conflict and disaster to survive, recover and gain control of their future.

**IRC Chad strategy**

The IRC began operations in Chad in 2004 in response to the humanitarian crisis caused by the influx of Darfur refugees into eastern Chad, starting with the Ouré Cassoni refugee camp. Today, the IRC supports Sudanese refugees and host communities in 14 camps and host villages in the east, and since April 2023 has expanded its response to assist refugees fleeing the conflict in Sudan. Services in the east include health, nutrition, water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH), economic recovery and development, women’s empowerment and protection. The IRC also works in Guéra province to address malnutrition and in the Lac region to respond to the Boko Haram crisis, with projects in health, nutrition, protection and response to gender-based violence. Across the country, IRC Chad combines humanitarian, nexus and development responses to help the most affected populations exercise their rights with dignity and access quality basic social services that meet their needs.

IRC Chad’s strategy focuses on three outcome areas: health (nutrition, child health, sexual and reproductive health and rights, and climate-resilient WASH), safety (high-impact targeted individual assistance) and economic wellbeing (food security, basic needs, early recovery and resilience). It is underpinned by commitments to gender equality, diversity and inclusion, cash and voucher assistance, and investment in partnerships with relevant ministries and local partners.

**SCOPE OF WORK**

The Country Director will provide the strategic vision and leadership for the country program with the primary focus on ensuring IRC Chad’s programs meet the expressed needs of the beneficiaries we serve. S/he is responsible for ensuring the delivery of quality programs, maintaining/expanding donor and government relations, engaging strategic local organizations, fundraising and budget management, security and operations management, and developing a motivated and professional team.

Success in this position requires an individual with exemplary leadership abilities who deploys strong communications and interpersonal skills effectively, both internally and externally. The successful candidate will enjoy developing networks to build partnerships and diversify program resources. Given the operating environment, the Country Director is expected to be attentive to risk management. S/he will be directly responsible for the overall coordination and strategic direction of the country program; providing oversight and coaching for directly supervised senior managers; leading country program teams to identify, design and deliver responsive, high-quality programs; ensuring efficient management of public grants and private funds for results, compliance and focused, timely reporting; and oversight of financial management and compliance systems.

Reporting to the Regional Vice President, this position receives support from regional and headquarters staff in the areas of program quality, new business development, safety and security management, finance, operations management, and external affairs. The Country Director is additionally expected to actively participate in defining the IRC’s public advocacy positions.

**SPECIFIC RESPONSIBILITIES**

***Leadership and Representation***

- Provide exemplary leadership by fostering a strong team spirit, open communication, and an inclusive and empowering work environment.
- Develop and maintain strategic relationships with: Chad Government authorities at various levels; donors (including institutional, non-institutional and private); UN and other international organizations; international and local NGOs; and networks such as INGO coordination mechanisms and appropriate working groups.
- Position IRC as a key partner for major international donors and seize opportunities to promote IRC’s work.
- Develop and maintain a high level of understanding of donor priorities and planned funding.
- Initiate and sustain strong, mutually beneficial, and authentic partnerships with Chadian organizations.
- Seek out and pursue opportunities to raise the profile of the work of the IRC and its partners in Chad, as well as the lives and the needs of the people the IRC seeks to serve.

***Strategic Direction, Program Quality and Development***

- Ensure that the country program’s strategic vision and direction are aligned with the IRC’s strategy to serve populations through responsive, high-quality, and accountable programming, and secure the necessary resources for its implementation.
- Ensure the country program’s alignment with the IRC strategy and the implementation of the strategic action plan.
- Ensure program quality through rigorous design, M&E, and accountability processes, and investments in staff development and partner capacity sharing.
- Remain current on national and regional issues impacting the country program and partners and develop responsive strategies to ensure the IRC mission can be carried out appropriately in case of contextual changes.
- Ensure country program alignment with and involvement in meeting regional objectives.
- Identify opportunities to expand programming and ensure continuous contextual monitoring.
- Oversee the development and submission of competitive, high-quality proposals; lead partnerships with local civil society organizations in line with PEERS standards, lead negotiations with donors; and build relationships with Chad Ministries.

***Safety Security and Access Management***

- Take primary responsibility for overall management of safety and security for the country program.
- Oversee the management of all security issues, including appropriate response to emergency situations as they arise.
- Create and maintain a culture of safety and security awareness throughout the country program, including trainings and briefings that prepare all country program staff for security incident prevention and response.
- Keep security, evacuation and contingency plans up to date and accessible to country program staff.
- Maintain close coordination and communication with the Regional Safety & Security Director on safety security concerns and evolving issues that could adversely affect IRC staff or operations.

***Staff Performance Management and Development***

- Supervise and mentor direct-report staff, including communicating clear expectations, setting performance objectives, providing regular and timely performance feedback, and leading documented semi-annual performance reviews.
- Provide constructive feedback and counsel on appropriate career paths and professional development for IRC staff.
- Oversee the management, coaching and development of all staff to build a cadre of skilled, committed and motivated personnel.
- Pursue nationalization of senior management positions.
- Promote and monitor staff care and well-being. Model healthy work-life balance practices. Support appropriate interventions in response to identified staff care needs of both national and international staff.
- Undertake regular reviews of labor laws, and salary markets in Chad for the purpose of enhancing the competitiveness of the IRC’s overall compensation package for team members.

***Stewardship and Operational Management***

- Drive operational excellence to achieve optimal efficiency and cost-effectiveness in all functions and operations of the country program.
- Oversee the development, deployment and utilization of financial and operational policies, procedures, and systems to comply with IRC and donor requirements.
- Ensure appropriate support for all departments (HR, Finance, Supply Chain) and the consistent implementation of the IRC Way.
- Provide timely and effective oversight of the Chad country program’s financial position.
- Ensure rigorous budget monitoring of grants and discretionary funds and identify opportunities for operational optimization

***Communications***

- Model and encourage active practice of the principles of the “IRC Way – Global Standards for Professional Conduct” throughout the Chad country program.
- Maintain a healthy and empowering office environment that encourages open, honest and productive communication among IRC staff and with partner organizations.
- Maintain open communication with regional management staff, regional technical advisors, and HQ departmental staff.

**KEY REPORTING RESPONSIBILITIES:**

**The position reports to**: Regional Vice President, WACAR

**The position directly supervises:** Deputy Director Programs, the Deputy Director of Finance, the Deputy Director Field Management, the People and Culture Coordinator, Humanitarian Access and Security Coordinator, Communication and media coordinator, Safeguarding and Compliance Coordinator.

**JOB REQUIREMENTS**

- Graduate degree in a relevant field or equivalent experience
- At least seven years of progressively responsible international work experience, including at least three years in a leadership role at the Country Director level of multi-site, multi-sectoral operations in a complex operating environment.
- Experience of building personal networks at a senior level, resulting in securing new opportunities for the organization
- Demonstrated successful leadership and management experience with a multi-disciplinary team in a cross-cultural setting, including active mentoring and coaching.
- Proven experience delivering appropriate levels oversight of a portfolio consisting of a variety of complex, high-value donor-funded projects.
- Extensive representation and fundraising success, including prior experience with European, US and international development donors.
- Experience of managing security in a fluid environment
- Proven ability to negotiate and work with partner organizations. Experience with organizational capacity strengthening and partnership building helpful.
- Strong budget and fiscal oversight capacities
- Established capacity to deal with ambiguity in stressful situations.
- French and English fluency
- Ability to respond to multiple priorities in a timely manner, producing high-quality outcomes.
- Previous experience working in Chad or in the West and Central Africa region preferred.

This position is based in N’djamena and is fully accompanied with an estimated 33% of the Country Director’s time spent in other locations in Chad and the region.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**CONTEXTE**

L’International Rescue Committee (IRC) répond aux pires crises humanitaires du monde et aide les populations à survivre et à reconstruire leur vie. Fondé en 1933 à la demande d’Albert Einstein, l’IRC apporte des soins vitaux et une aide qui transforme des vies, notamment auprès des réfugiés contraints de fuir la guerre ou les catastrophes. Présente aujourd’hui dans plus de 40 pays, l’IRC rétablit la sécurité, la dignité et l’espoir pour des millions de personnes qui luttent pour leur survie. Sa mission est d’aider les personnes dont la vie et les moyens de subsistance ont été brisés par les conflits et les catastrophes à survivre, à se relever et à reprendre le contrôle de leur avenir.

**Stratégie de l’IRC au Tchad**

L’IRC a lancé ses opérations au Tchad en 2004 pour répondre à la crise humanitaire provoquée par l’afflux de réfugiés du Darfour dans l’est du pays, en commençant par le camp de réfugiés d’Ouré Cassoni. Aujourd’hui, l’IRC soutient les réfugiés soudanais et les communautés d’accueil dans 14 camps et villages d’accueil de l’Est et, depuis avril 2023, a élargi son intervention pour venir en aide aux réfugiés fuyant le conflit au Soudan. Les services fournis dans l’Est comprennent la santé, la nutrition, l’eau, l’hygiène et l’assainissement (EHA), le relèvement et le développement économiques, l’autonomisation des femmes et la protection. L’IRC intervient également dans la province du Guéra pour lutter contre la malnutrition, et dans la région du Lac pour répondre à la crise liée à Boko Haram, avec des projets en santé, nutrition, protection et réponse aux violences basées sur le genre (VBG). Dans l’ensemble du pays, l’IRC Tchad combine réponses humanitaires, approches de nexus et actions de développement afin d’aider les populations les plus touchées à exercer leurs droits dans la dignité et à accéder à des services sociaux de base de qualité répondant à leurs besoins.

La stratégie de l’IRC Tchad s’articule autour de trois domaines de résultats : la santé (nutrition, santé de l’enfant, santé et droits sexuels et reproductifs, et EHA résilient face au changement climatique), la sûreté (assistance individuelle ciblée à fort impact) et le bien-être économique (sécurité alimentaire, besoins de base, relèvement précoce et résilience). Elle repose sur des engagements en faveur de l’égalité de genre, de la diversité et de l’inclusion, de l’assistance en espèces et par coupons, ainsi que sur l’investissement dans des partenariats avec les ministères concernés et les partenaires locaux.

**PÉRIMÈTRE DU POSTE**

Le/la Directeur(trice) Pays assure la vision stratégique et le leadership du programme pays, avec pour priorité de garantir que les programmes de l’IRC Tchad répondent aux besoins exprimés par les bénéficiaires que nous servons. Il/elle est chargé(e) de veiller à la qualité des programmes, d’entretenir et d’élargir les relations avec les bailleurs et le gouvernement, de mobiliser des organisations locales stratégiques, d’assurer la levée de fonds et la gestion budgétaire, de superviser la sécurité et les opérations, ainsi que de constituer une équipe motivée et professionnelle.

La réussite à ce poste exige une personne dotée d’un leadership exemplaire, capable de mobiliser efficacement de solides compétences en communication et en relations interpersonnelles, tant en interne qu’en externe. Le/la candidat(e) retenu(e) devra développer des réseaux afin de bâtir des partenariats et de diversifier les ressources des programmes. Compte tenu du contexte d’intervention, le/la Directeur(trice) Pays doit porter une attention particulière à la gestion des risques. Il/elle est directement responsable de la coordination d’ensemble et de l’orientation stratégique du programme pays ; assure la supervision et le coaching des cadres supérieurs qu’il/elle encadre directement ; dirige les équipes du programme pays dans l’identification, la conception et la mise en œuvre de programmes réactifs et de grande qualité ; veille à une gestion efficiente des subventions publiques et des fonds privés, axée sur les résultats, la conformité et la remise de rapports ciblés dans les délais ; et supervise les systèmes de gestion financière et de conformité.

Le/la Directeur(trice) Pays, placé(e) sous l’autorité du/de la Vice-Président(e) régional(e), bénéficie de l’appui du personnel régional et du siège en matière de qualité des programmes, de développement de nouvelles opportunités de financement, de gestion de la sûreté et de la sécurité, de finances, de gestion des opérations et d’affaires extérieures. Il/elle est en outre appelé(e) à participer activement à la définition des positions de plaidoyer public de l’IRC.

**RESPONSABILITÉS SPÉCIFIQUES**

***Leadership et Représentation***

- Faire preuve d’un leadership exemplaire en favorisant un fort esprit d’équipe, une communication ouverte et un environnement de travail inclusif et valorisant.
- Développer et entretenir des relations stratégiques avec : les autorités gouvernementales tchadiennes à différents niveaux ; les bailleurs de fonds (institutionnels, non institutionnels et privés), dont l’Union européenne ; les Nations Unies et les autres organisations internationales ; les ONG internationales et locales ; ainsi que les réseaux tels que les mécanismes de coordination des ONG internationales et les groupes de travail pertinents.
- Positionner l’IRC comme un partenaire clé des grands bailleurs de fonds internationaux et saisir les occasions de promouvoir son action.
- Acquérir et maintenir une connaissance approfondie des priorités des bailleurs et des financements qu’ils prévoient.
