- Nouer et entretenir des partenariats solides, authentiques et mutuellement bénéfiques avec des organisations tchadiennes.
- Rechercher et saisir les occasions de mieux faire connaître le travail de l’IRC et de ses partenaires au Tchad, ainsi que les conditions de vie et les besoins des personnes que l’IRC s’efforce de servir.

***Orientation Stratégique, Qualité et Développement des programmes***

- Veiller à ce que la vision et l’orientation stratégiques du programme pays soient alignées sur la stratégie de l’IRC afin de servir les populations à travers des programmes réactifs, de grande qualité et redevables, et mobiliser les ressources nécessaires à leur mise en œuvre.
- Veiller à l’alignement du programme pays sur la stratégie de l’IRC et à la mise en œuvre du plan d’action stratégique.
- Garantir la qualité des programmes grâce à une conception rigoureuse, à des processus de suivi-évaluation et de redevabilité, ainsi qu’à des investissements dans le développement du personnel et le renforcement des capacités des partenaires.
- Se tenir informé(e) des enjeux nationaux et régionaux qui touchent le programme pays et les partenaires, et élaborer des stratégies adaptées afin de pouvoir poursuivre la mission de l’IRC de manière appropriée en cas d’évolution du contexte.
- Veiller à ce que le programme pays soit aligné sur les objectifs régionaux et contribue à leur réalisation.
- Identifier les possibilités d’extension de la programmation et suivre en continu l’évolution du contexte.
- Superviser l’élaboration et la soumission de propositions compétitives et de grande qualité ; piloter les partenariats avec les organisations locales de la société civile conformément aux standards PEERS ; mener les négociations avec les bailleurs ; et nouer des relations avec les ministères tchadiens.

***Gestion de la sûreté, de la sécurité et de l’accès***

- Assumer la responsabilité principale de la gestion globale de la sûreté et de la sécurité du programme pays.
- Superviser la gestion de toutes les questions de sécurité, y compris la réponse adaptée aux situations d’urgence au fur et à mesure qu’elles surviennent.
- Créer et entretenir, au sein du programme pays, une culture de sensibilisation à la sûreté et à la sécurité, notamment par des formations et des séances d’information qui préparent l’ensemble du personnel à prévenir les incidents de sécurité et à y répondre.
- Tenir à jour les plans de sécurité, d’évacuation et de contingence, et les rendre accessibles au personnel du programme pays.
- Maintenir une coordination et une communication étroites avec le/la Directeur(trice) régional(e) de la sûreté et de la sécurité au sujet des préoccupations en la matière et des évolutions susceptibles de nuire au personnel ou aux opérations de l’IRC.

***Gestion de la performance et développement du personnel***

- Encadrer et accompagner les collaborateurs placés sous sa responsabilité directe, notamment en communiquant des attentes claires, en fixant des objectifs de performance, en leur donnant régulièrement et en temps utile un retour sur leur performance, et en conduisant des évaluations semestrielles documentées.
- Donner au personnel de l’IRC des retours constructifs et des conseils sur son parcours de carrière et son développement professionnel.
- Superviser la gestion, le coaching et le développement de l’ensemble du personnel afin de constituer un vivier de collaborateurs compétents, engagés et motivés.
- Poursuivre la nationalisation des postes d’encadrement supérieur.
- Promouvoir et suivre la prise en charge et le bien-être du personnel. Montrer l’exemple en matière d’équilibre entre vie professionnelle et vie privée. Soutenir les interventions adaptées aux besoins de bien-être identifiés, tant pour le personnel national que pour le personnel international.
- Examiner régulièrement la législation du travail et les niveaux de salaire pratiqués sur le marché au Tchad afin de renforcer la compétitivité de l’ensemble du dispositif de rémunération de l’IRC pour les membres de l’équipe.

***Gestion responsable des ressources et des opérations***

- Promouvoir l’excellence opérationnelle afin d’atteindre une efficience et un rapport coût-efficacité optimaux dans l’ensemble des fonctions et opérations du programme pays.
- Superviser l’élaboration, le déploiement et l’utilisation de politiques, procédures et systèmes financiers et opérationnels conformes aux exigences de l’IRC et des bailleurs.
- Assurer un appui adéquat à l’ensemble des départements (RH, Finance, Chaîne d’approvisionnement) et veiller à la mise en œuvre cohérente de l’IRC Way.
- Assurer une supervision rapide et efficace de la situation financière du programme pays du Tchad.
- Assurer un suivi budgétaire rigoureux des subventions et des fonds discrétionnaires et identifier les possibilités d’optimisation opérationnelle.

***Communication***

- Incarner les principes de « l’IRC Way – Normes globales de conduite professionnelle », et en encourager activement l’application dans l’ensemble du programme pays du Tchad.
- Maintenir un environnement de travail sain et valorisant, qui favorise une communication ouverte, honnête et productive entre les membres du personnel de l’IRC et avec les organisations partenaires.
- Maintenir une communication ouverte avec l’équipe de direction régionale, les conseillers techniques régionaux et le personnel des départements du siège.

**PRINCIPALES RELATIONS HIÉRARCHIQUES ET FONCTIONNELLES :**

**Le poste est rattaché à** : Vice-Président(e) régional(e), WACAR

**Le poste encadre directement :**le/la Directeur(trice) adjoint(e) Programmes, le/la Directeur(trice) adjoint(e) Finances, le/la Directeur(trice) adjoint(e) Gestion du terrain, le/la Coordinateur(trice) Personnes et Culture, le/la Coordinateur(trice) Acces Humanitaire et Sécurité, le/la Coordinateur(trice) Communication et médias, le/la Coordinateur(trice) Sauvegarde et Conformité

**Principaux contacts internes :** Équipe régionale WACAR ; Gestion des subventions, Opérations et Stratégie, Finance, Qualité des programmes, Plaidoyer, Département juridique, Éthique et Conformité ; autres Directeurs(trices) Pays de la région WACAR ; personnel des départements du siège, selon les besoins.

**Principaux contacts externes :** Organisations partenaires, représentants du gouvernement du pays d’accueil, agences de bailleurs publics et privés, ONG internationales et nationales, agences des Nations Unies, gouvernements étrangers.

**EXIGENCES DU POSTE**

- Diplôme de niveau master (bac+5) dans un domaine pertinent ou expérience équivalente.
- Au moins sept ans d’expérience internationale à des postes de responsabilité croissante, dont au moins trois ans à un poste de direction de niveau Directeur(trice) Pays, à la tête d’opérations multisites et multisectorielles dans un environnement d’intervention complexe.
- Expérience dans la constitution de réseaux personnels de haut niveau, ayant permis d’ouvrir de nouvelles perspectives à l’organisation.
- Expérience avérée de leadership et de gestion d’une équipe pluridisciplinaire en contexte interculturel, avec un mentorat et un coaching actifs.
- Expérience avérée de supervision, à un niveau approprié, d’un portefeuille de projets complexes de grande envergure financés par des bailleurs.
- Solide expérience de représentation et de levée de fonds, y compris auprès de bailleurs européens, américains et d’autres bailleurs internationaux du développement.
- Expérience en gestion de la sécurité dans un environnement instable.
- Capacité avérée à négocier et à collaborer avec des organisations partenaires. Une expérience en renforcement des capacités organisationnelles et en développement de partenariats est un atout.
- Solides compétences en supervision budgétaire et financière.
- Capacité confirmée à gérer l’ambiguïté en situation de stress.
- Maîtrise du français et de l’anglais.
- Capacité à gérer plusieurs priorités dans les délais impartis, tout en produisant des résultats de grande qualité.
- Une expérience préalable au Tchad ou en Afrique de l’Ouest et du Centre est souhaitée.

Ce poste est basé à N’Djamena, en statut accompagné. Le/la Directeur(trice) Pays consacrera environ 33 % de son temps à des déplacements dans d’autres localités du Tchad et de la région.

**Employeur garantissant l'égalité des chances** : L'IRC est un employeur garantissant l'égalité des chances. L'IRC évalue tous les candidats sur la base du mérite, sans distinction de race, de sexe, de couleur de peau, d'origine nationale, de religion, d'orientation sexuelle, d'âge, de situation matrimoniale, de statut d'ancien combattant, de handicap ou de toute autre caractéristique protégée par la législation en vigueur.

**Normes professionnelles** : Tous les collaborateurs de l’International Rescue Committee (IRC) doivent adhérer aux valeurs et principes fondamentaux énoncés dans le document « IRC Way – Normes de conduite professionnelle ». Nos normes sont l’intégrité, le service, l’égalité et la responsabilité. Conformément à ces valeurs, l’IRC met en œuvre et applique des politiques relatives à la protection des personnes, aux conflits d’intérêts, à l’intégrité financière, au signalement des irrégularités et à la protection contre les représailles. L’IRC s’engage à prendre toutes les mesures préventives nécessaires et à créer un environnement où chacun se sent en sécurité, ainsi qu’à prendre toutes les mesures nécessaires et correctives en cas de préjudice. L’IRC constitue des équipes de professionnels qui favorisent la réflexion critique, le partage des responsabilités, le débat et l’objectivité afin d’offrir les meilleurs services possibles à nos bénéficiaires.

title: Grants, Partnerships and Communication Coordinator
body:
***This position is open to candidates with existing work authorization in the location where the position is advertised.***

***Fluency in both English & Spanish required***.

***Funding until September 30, 2027, potential to extend***.

**BACKGROUND**

Venezuela continues to face a protracted humanitarian crisis. Inside the country, millions of people have limited access to food, health care, safe water and other essential services, and needs are most acute among people on the move and returnees, Indigenous communities, women and girls at risk of gender-based violence, and children at risk of acute malnutrition. In 2026, an earthquake affecting La Guaira, Miranda and Caracas added new humanitarian needs. At the same time, more than 7 million refugees and migrants have left Venezuela, making this one of the largest external displacement crises in the world, with Colombia hosting the largest number of them.

In Colombia, the escalation of the internal armed conflict has deepened humanitarian needs. Disputes between non-state armed groups over territorial control are driving forced displacement, confinement, movement restrictions, the recruitment of children and adolescents, and gender-based violence, particularly in border and Pacific regions such as Norte de Santander and Nariño. The crisis in Catatumbo alone, which began in January 2025, has displaced more than 100,000 people. Mixed migration flows continue in several directions, including Venezuelans in transit and pendular movements across the border, as well as reverse flows of people returning south from Central and North America and returns to Venezuela, which add complexity to the response.

The IRC is addressing these needs through an integrated, population-based response in Colombia and Venezuela, covering health (including sexual and reproductive health and mental health), protection and women’s protection and empowerment, child protection, multipurpose cash and economic recovery, nutrition, water, sanitation and hygiene, and education. The IRC employs a mixed modality, providing lifesaving services directly and with local partners, and in Venezuela a significant share of funds is channeled through local organizations. Activities are financed by a diverse portfolio of donors, including ECHO, Sida, GFFO, OCHA-managed pooled funds (such as the Venezuela Humanitarian Fund and the Regional Humanitarian Pooled Fund for Latin America and the Caribbean), the Disasters Emergency Committee, UN agencies and private foundations, among others.

**Purpose of the role:** IRC Colombia and Venezuela is seeking an experienced business development, grants, and partnerships professional for the role of Grants, Partnerships and Communications Coordinator. This role is responsible for leading resource mobilization and the timely production of high-quality funding proposals, modification requests and donor reports; playing a lead role in the full award management cycle, including compliance; facilitating partnership development and management processes; leading the communications strategy that positions the IRC’s work with donors, partners and the public and protects the organization’s reputation; and coordinating grants management-related capacity building efforts among IRC staff and partners. The Grants, and Partnerships Coordinator ensures the quality of and efficient processes for proposal development and grants management, and manages the delivery of the IRC’s partnership ambitions while supporting program coordinators and country leadership to ensure that IRC Colombia and Venezuela lives up to the partnership principles of responsibility, results-oriented approaches, equality, transparency, and complementarity.

The postholder will need to work under tight deadlines and deal with competing and changing priorities. The postholder will need to gather inputs by influencing other functions and roles while submitting quality and timely deliverables, will work with diverse country, region and headquarters-based teams, and will need to ensure adherence to organizational and donor compliance requirements. The position will be based in Bogota with frequent visits to field sites in Colombia and Venezuela.

**Scope and authority:** The Grants, Partnerships and Communications Coordinator will lead a team of 15 members (both direct and indirect) divided in three sub-teams: grants, partnerships, and communications. The postholder will line manage 6 direct reports.

**Key Accountabilities & responsibilities:**

***Business Development and Resource Mobilization:***

- Lead the development and annual update of a resource mobilization strategy for IRC Colombia and Venezuela, aligned with the country Strategy Action Plan, with clear targets by donor, sector and geography.
- Manage the funding pipeline: investigate and track funding opportunities, maintain an up-to-date pipeline tracker, and regularly report on its status to country leadership.
- Lead the Go/No-Go analysis for each opportunity, assessing strategic fit, competitiveness, implementation capacity, risks, cost recovery and compliance requirements, and facilitate timely decisions with country leadership.
- Drive donor diversification and positioning beyond traditional institutional donors, including pooled funds (such as the Venezuela Humanitarian Fund and the Regional Humanitarian Pooled Fund), multilateral agencies and development banks, the private sector and foundations, and funding dedicated to localization and to partnerships with local organizations.
- Lead program design workshops for new business development opportunities with relevant IRC staff, and partners’ staff where applicable.
- Develop, lead, and track proposal development processes, including consortium proposals, directly coordinating and managing the development of proposals and concept notes in collaboration with multiple departments and stakeholders; write sections of proposals and conduct final reviews, editing, and polishing of proposal documents for accuracy and quality control.
- Assist in compiling and editing proposal budgets and ensure communication and coordination between all departments (finance, programs, and operations) in drafting of budgets, bringing a strategic and competitive lens to the process.

***Grants/Sub-Grants Management:***

- Ensure that IRC awards and sub-awards in Colombia and Venezuela are well-administered and implemented in compliance with the relevant donor regulations and IRC procedures throughout the full award cycle.
- Lead award start-up, including grant summaries and kick-off meetings (pre-award and opening meetings) with programs, finance, operations and partners, so that all teams understand donor requirements from the outset.
- Lead the review and negotiation of grant and sub-grant agreements, in coordination with the Awards Management Unit, finance and other relevant departments.
- Coordinate award modifications, including cost and no-cost extensions, budget realignments and changes in scope, ensuring timely submission and donor approval.
- Take the lead on internal and external reporting in coordination with programs, MEAL, and finance, ensuring high-quality, well-written and timely reports meeting donor and IRC requirements. Maintain close collaboration with all relevant departments in preparation of donor reports.
- Maintain award tracking systems, including the grants tracker, reporting and deadline calendars and award dashboards, ensuring that information is accurate and available to budget holders and senior management.
- Supervise the GPU in the coordination and facilitation of project cycle meetings.
- Lead award close-out processes, ensuring that final reports, financial reconciliation, asset disposition and documentation are completed on time.
- Coordinate the preparation for and follow-up of donor audits, verifications and monitoring visits, including the implementation of their recommendations.
- Play a significant role in efforts to strengthen and maintain country program project management capacities.
- Ensure that sub-grantees are being monitored for donor compliance and progress against objectives, and that key compliance monitoring information and learning are documented.
- Assist program technical leads, operations staff, and partners with understanding the reporting and other compliance requirements on their grants and sub-grants.
- Proactively identify compliance risks throughout the portfolio and advise programs, operations, finance and senior management on necessary actions.

***Partnerships Management:***

- Play a lead role in stakeholder analysis and potential partner mapping and vetting.
- Working closely with other senior staff, play a lead role in identifying, liaising on, and negotiating teaming arrangements with potential partners; collaborate with other departments as needed to verify and issue various types of partnership agreements.
- Ensure and coordinate adherence to IRC’s Partnership Excellence for Equality and Results System (PEERS) in the selection and management of IRC Colombia and Venezuela’s partnerships.
- Co-lead the review of the performance of different partnerships, including successes, challenges and lessons learned.
- Support country leadership in promoting an enabling environment for effective work in partnership.
- Provide a quarterly Partnership Management Report to the CD, incorporating input from technical coordinators and operational leads as appropriate.

***Staff management and capacity building***

- Maintain a broad and deep understanding of donor policies, regulations, and procedures and build this knowledge among grants team members.
- Build grant management capacity of field staff, and provide supportive supervision in report writing, budget management, indicator tracking, IRC-specific tools, and other topics as/if needed.
- Maintain open and professional relations with team members, promoting a strong team spirit and providing oversight and guidance to enable staff to successfully perform in their positions.
- Maintain documentation of institutional knowledge and program activities in coordination with relevant sector coordinators and department leads.

***Communications***

- **Communications strategy:** Lead the development and implementation of a communications strategy for IRC Colombia and Venezuela, aligned with the country strategy, resource mobilization priorities and IRC regional and global communications.
- **Brand management and visibility:** Ensure consistent and appropriate use of the IRC brand across materials, events, field sites and partner activities; provide advice on donor visibility requirements and proactively engage with program teams to ensure appropriate IRC and donor visibility.
- **Creation of communication materials:** Lead Colombia and Venezuela’s efforts in designing, writing and editing key communication materials (factsheets, capacity statements, stories from the field, digital content or special reports on IRC’s activities) in coordination with DDPs, program leads, and sector and field coordinators.
- **Crisis communications and reputational risk:** Develop and maintain protocols for crisis communications and reputational risk management, and advise the CD and senior management on sensitive issues, including security, data protection and the political context in Colombia and Venezuela.
- **Internal communications:** Promote clear and timely internal communication across offices and teams in Colombia and Venezuela, so that staff are informed about the country program’s priorities, results and key decisions.
- **Media:** Support media and communications activities in coordination with IRC regional and global communications teams, ensuring the safety, dignity and informed consent of clients.
- **Advocacy:** Support the CD and DDPs as needed.

**Key Working Relationships:**

**Position Reports to:** Country Director, Colombia and Venezuela

**Position directly supervises:** Grants, Partnerships and Communications Unit staff

**Other Internal and/or external contacts:**

**Internal:** Venezuela Country Manager and Venezuela senior management team, with whom the postholder works closely on the Venezuela portfolio; Colombia/Venezuela Deputy Directors of Programs and leads of programs, Finance and Operations, Budget Officers/Managers, HR Lead, Access & Security Department; MEAL Unit; Awards Management Unit (Regional), regional partnerships advisor, regional and global communications teams, and Technical Advisors.

**External:** Donors and pooled fund managers, consortium partners, local partner organizations, UN agencies and humanitarian coordination mechanisms, other NGO counterparts and media, as needed and indicated by Country Director, Country Manager or Deputy Director of Programs.

**Qualifications**

- Bachelor’s degree in relevant discipline, Master’s degree desired.
- At least five years international work experience in humanitarian and development programs; experience in a similar position/role is desired.
- Demonstrated, successful experience in program design and writing proposals for public and private donors.
- Solid knowledge of donor rules and regulations, including ECHO, Sida, GFFO, UN agencies and OCHA-managed pooled funds; knowledge of other European, multilateral and private donor requirements is an asset.
- Demonstrated experience managing the full award cycle, including compliance, modifications, audits and close-out, and in managing partnerships with local organizations.
- Experience in communications, brand management or external relations in a humanitarian or development organization is desirable.
- Demonstrable understanding of project planning and management cycles.
- Highly organized, close attention to detail, and ability to effectively prioritize tasks in a fluid environment.
- Demonstrable high-level performance management and team-working skills, and well developed negotiation skills.
- Highly developed interpersonal, communication and relationship skills, with the ability to influence and represent the organization with external organizations and stakeholders.
- Effective people- and program-management skills in acute emergency contexts: can train and lead staff productively under stressful circumstances.
- Flexible, focused and reliable, with the ability to work well under administrative and programmatic pressures in an environment of changing demands.
- Experience in the region is an asset; knowledge of the Colombian and Venezuelan contexts is strongly desired.
- Digital literacy and strong computer skills: MS Word, Excel & email applications required.

**Language Preference**

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English and Spanish, with high quality copywriting and editing skills in both languages.

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate around: 10,051,500 COP/monthly). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

title: Director of Finance
body:
PATHWAYS INTERNATIONAL

**Director of Finance**

**About us – what do we do?**

At a time of unprecedented forced displacement and system disruption, we are reforming the global system of safe and legal routes to protection. Our world-class team works closely with leaders and innovators from across sectors in over 20 countries. Together we design, launch, and expand safe and legal routes for displaced people. Together we pilot bold new ideas aimed at making the entire global system of safe and legal routes stronger and more sustainable.

**How we do it**

- We build and lead powerful partnerships and networks.
- We provide trusted advice.
- We accelerate operational delivery.
- We generate and share insights.
- We inspire change.

**About the role – what will you do?**

The Director of Finance manages Pathways International’s day-to-day finance operations across our entities, making sure they are accurate, compliant and on time. Over time, the role will also oversee our HR and IT operations.

This is a senior role in a small team, and a hands-on one. You’ll set direction and supervise, but you’ll also do the work yourself when needed, whether that’s reconciling an account, posting journal entries, running a payroll cycle or rebuilding a grant report. We’re looking for someone who genuinely enjoys both.

The role is designed to expand in time. In the first months you’ll learn our entities, funders and systems alongside the CFO, then take ownership of core processes step by step. As Pathways International evolves, the scope of the role will evolve with it.

**Key responsibilities**

- **Financial operations:** Lead the monthly close, reconciliations and consolidated reporting across our entities and currencies, and keep the general ledger accurate and well-structured.
- **Grant finance:** Partner with programme teams on grant budgets, monitor spending, and prepare funder financial reports.
- **Payroll and compliance:** Oversee payroll and statutory compliance across multiple jurisdictions, including provider and employer-of-record relationships.
- **Audit and tax:** Manage the statutory, tax and audit calendar, and act as day-to-day contact for external auditors.
- **Planning and reporting:** Contribute to budgets and forecasts, and prepare financial information for leadership and Boards.
- **Controls and systems:** Maintain strong internal controls and documented procedures, and keep improving our systems and processes.
- **Administration:** Over time, oversee HR operations and IT, coordinating specialist support, contract and onboarding processes, and systems and access across the organization.
- **Team:** Supervise and develop a small finance and administration team.

**About you – who are we looking for?**

You are a highly organized, detail-oriented finance professional who enjoys both leading and rolling up your sleeves to do the work. You are comfortable building and running processes with limited direction. You are able to work across a varied and evolving portfolio of entities, currencies and jurisdictions. You are comfortable in a fast-paced environment with recurring deadlines, while keeping sensitive financial and personnel information fully confidential. You also bring a high degree of professionalism, discretion, sound judgement and responsibility.

- You have a bachelor’s degree or equivalent in accounting, finance, business administration or a related field.
- A professional accounting designation (e.g. CPA or equivalent).
- You have at least eight years of relevant work experience, including senior responsibility for the month-end close, financial reporting and audit. Experience in a non-profit or grant-funded organization is a strong asset.
- You have a strong command of accounting fundamentals, including consolidation, multi-currency transactions and fund or grant accounting.
- You have experience managing restricted funding: budgets, spending oversight and financial reporting to institutional and private funders.
- You have a working knowledge of payroll, tax and statutory compliance in more than one country. Experience with employer-of-record providers or international payroll is an asset.
- You are hands-on and comfortable working directly in the books, the payroll and the spreadsheets, with strong attention to detail.
- You have a sound understanding of internal controls, segregation of duties and documentation, and you build processes that others can follow.
- You have experience supervising and developing staff.
- You learn new entities, systems and regulatory environments quickly, and you are comfortable in a role whose scope will grow and change over time.
- You have excellent written and verbal communication skills in English and can explain financial information clearly to non-finance colleagues, leadership and Boards. Proficiency in other languages, in particular Spanish, Italian, or Portuguese, is an asset.
- You have excellent interpersonal skills and have experience collaborating with people from different backgrounds, countries, cultures and languages.
- You are proficient with cloud accounting systems (e.g. QuickBooks Online) and advanced Excel, and comfortable using Zoom, MS Teams and SharePoint. You are open to using new tools, including AI, to improve how the team works.

**Location:** This is a full-time remote position within the range of Eastern Time (ET) to Central European Time (CET). The candidate must be available for flexible working hours, including meetings in CET and ET.

Applicants contacted for evaluation will be asked to provide proof that they have the legal right to work in their country of residence. Maintaining such legal right to work in their country of residence is a condition of employment.

**Salary**

Competitive, commensurate with experience.

**Contract**

- One-year term contract (renewable)

**How to apply**

Please submit in English:

- Cover letter
- CV

Please apply through BambooHR at [https://pathways.bamboohr.com/careers/62 ](https://pathways.bamboohr.com/careers/62)by November 30, 2026, at 11:59 pm EST to be considered for this position.

**Equal opportunity employer**

Pathways International is an equal opportunity employer, committed to diversity and inclusion. We encourage applications from qualified candidates of all genders and from all national, religious, and ethnic backgrounds, including persons with disabilities and those with lived experience of forced displacement. We will provide accommodation upon request during the recruitment, selection, and assessment process.

title: Democratic Republic of Congo Program Officer
body:
FGHR is seeking a consultant to support its DRC grantmaking and grantee partner engagement. FGHR supports grassroots activists and communities who respond to immediate needs, generate and use knowledge about the systems and power relations driving injustice, build solidarity, and organize while laying the groundwork for longer-term change, peace, justice, and accountability.

This twelve-month consultancy reports to the East Africa Program Director, who is based in Burundi. The consultant should be based in East Africa and available to communicate with partners across the DRC. The role is envisioned as full-time. The work calls for someone who combines deep, trusted relationships within the DRC’s human rights movement with sound judgment about security and the discretion to handle sensitive information responsibly.

## Essential Functions and Responsibilities

This is where you will make the most impact. Responsibilities fall across three connected areas of work.

### Ecosystem engagement and Partner Relationships

- Build and Maintain regular, trusted relationships across the wider human rights ecosystem in the DRC, including current and prospective grantee partners, community-led and Indigenous organizations, movements, networks, collaborative structures, and other relevant actors.
- Assess security risks facing partners and their communities, and help the team understand how those risks are evolving.
- Provide advice and accompaniment to partners on security and risk management, drawing on established relationships and contextual knowledge.
- Help identify and engage new partners as the DRC portfolio evolves, drawing on knowledge of civil society, community-led and Indigenous organizing, and collaborative structures to match ecosystem needs with diverse positions, knowledge, skills, and capacities.
- Identify and engage emerging or underrepresented actors, perspectives and areas of expertise that could contribute to a more diverse and strategically complementary portfolio, while strengthening FGHR's understanding of the ecosystem.
- Gather and verify information about the operating context, with attention to the safety of those who share it.

### Political and Contextual Analysis

- Collect, process, and synthesize information from prospective and current grantees and other sources inside the DRC.
- Track sectors and dynamics of particular concern— such as mining and other natural-resource sectors, areas affected by land disputes and extractive projects, sites of civic mobilization and human rights violations, and territories affected by armed conflict, displacement and competing forms of authority. —and provide the team with regular, timely updates.
- Contribute analysis and on-the-ground insight to FGHR’s strategy and planning for the DRC and the wider region.

### Grantmaking

- Conduct due diligence on prospective and current grantees.
- Write clear, well-reasoned grant recommendation memos.
- Monitor grantee performance and support partners throughout the life of their grants.

### Qualifications

- Deep familiarity with the human rights movement in the DRC, including organized civil society and communities directly confronting injustice.
- Established trust across a broad cross-section of the DRC’s human rights movement, especially in ethnic areas.
- Demonstrated understanding of security and risk in the DRC context, and sound judgment in handling sensitive information.
- Fluency in French and English, with strong communication skills.
- Based in East Africa and able to work across the DRC and Burundi time zones.
- Experience with a donor agency or in grantmaking is preferred.
- A proven commitment to human rights in all its dimensions.

## What We Offer

FGHR aims to provide competitive compensation and a supportive working environment. Benefits available to eligible staff and consultants include:

- 20 days of annual leave in the first year, with incremental increases over time.
- Statutory bank holidays plus up to 14 personal leave days.
- “Refreshing Fridays”—non-working wellbeing days every other Friday from June through August.
- 12 paid sick days per year.
- 20 days of parental leave, where applicable.
- Up to three months of paid sabbatical after seven years of service.
- Retirement plan.
- A professional development plan with dedicated funding.
- Employee Assistance Program (via INOVA).

title: Venezuela : Country Finance Manager – Caracas
source: Agency for Technical Cooperation and Development
body:
**Fixed term | 6 months | ASAP**

## **Acted**

***Who we are***

Acted works with 19 million people across 43 countries at the intersection of humanitarian, development, climate and environmental programming. We draw on deep contextual knowledge and embrace emerging technologies to save lives, alleviate suffering, and protect and restore our planet. Working in collaboration with a growing ecosystem of local, national and international partners, we pursue one shared objective: a 3Zero World – Zero Exclusion, Zero Carbon and Zero Poverty.

***Who we are looking for***

You bring the core competencies required for classical humanitarian and development work, alongside an active climate and environmental conscience, and you can navigate the challenges that arise when human and environmental suffering intersect. You have an entrepreneurial mindset: you see opportunities, connect dots, adapt your approach to different environments, and take measured risks in pursuit of results. You balance principles with pragmatism, and ambition with humility.

## **Acted Colombia - Venezuela**

Colombia continues being affected by a complex humanitarian crisis, characterized by multidimensional factors such as protracted armed conflict, natural disasters, and mixed movement/displacement dynamics (both internal and external displacement). Moreover, the crisis is exacerbated by the limited presence of state actors in several zones of the country, especially in hard-to-reach and rural areas combined with high poverty rates (36.6%) and food insecurity levels (30%) resulting in approximately 9.1 million people estimated in need of humanitarian assistance.

In parallel, Venezuela continues facing a severe humanitarian crisis, with nearly 8 million people having migrated since 2014, marking the largest exodus in Latin America. 7.9 million people are in need of humanitarian assistance due to the deterioration of basic public services and a deep economic crisis characterized by high inflation rates and lack of purchase power, resulting in an estimated 56% of its population living in extreme poverty. Moreover, according to the OECD, Venezuela also ranks among the top 3 countries with the highest increase in human fragility, while 40% of the population experience moderate to severe food insecurity and 62% face restriction on access to drinking water. Highly vulnerable communities, living in rural and border areas are affected the most, and 1.4 million children are estimated in need of protections assistance.

## **You will be in charge of**

The Country Finance Manager (CFM) is a key member of the Management Team at country level. He/she will be responsible for Acted financial management in-country under the authority of the Country Director and Finance & Administrative Director in HQ. The CFM ensures that national legislation is adhered to, and that Acted’s financial standards are applied in terms of accounting, financial control systems, internal / external reporting processes, in order to ensure an efficient use of resources. He/She leads, provides technical support and capacity building to the country finance and administrative staff. The CFM shall alert the Country Director and Finance Director in case some major problems arise with a potential financial impact on the mission.

***Main duties***

1\. Accounting and treasury Management

- *Accounting management – supervise the accounting cycle for the mission*
- *Treasury management – ensure a controlled and smooth cash management*

2\. Commitment of expenditures, budget control, & Financial Management

- *Commitment of expenditure – guaranty budget availability and compliance to Acted and donor’s procedures before releasing payments*
- *Project budget follow-up, mission’s cost control, internal & external audits – anticipate and mitigate financial risks ensuring operations are run in a compliant and cost-efficient manner*

3\. Project financial cycle management

- *Develop project budgets and reports – ensure the financial feasibility of projects, respecting Acted and donors’ rules and deadlines*

4\. Team leadership & other tasks

## **Expected skills and qualifications**

- Msc in Finance, Audit, Business Management, Economics or equivalent;
- 3+ years of solid experience in financial & budget management;
- Excellent financial and analytical skills;
- Excellent communication and drafting skills for effective reporting on programme financial performance;
- Ability to manage a financial team and demonstrate leadership;
- Ability to monitor and evaluate financial skills of teams through capacity-building efforts;
- Ability to undertake serious responsibilities and to manage stress efficiently;
- Ability to operate in a cross-cultural environment requiring flexibility;
- Prior knowledge of the region an asset.

## **Conditions**

- Salary between 3300 and 3500€ monthly (before income tax), depending on the level of education, security level, etc as well as a monthly living allowance of $300
- Accommodation and food provided in Acted guesthouse
- Pension, health insurance, life insurance and repatriation assistance (& unemployment insurance for EU citizens)
- Flight tickets every 6 months & visa fees covered
- Contribution to the luggage transportation: up to 100 kgs, depending on the length of the contract
- R&R every 3 months, flight tickets covered up to $500 and allowance of $200
- Annual leave of 25 to 43 days per year
- One week pre-departure training in Acted HQ, including a 4-days in situ security training
- Tax advice (free 30-minute call with a tax consultant)
- Psychological assistance
- This position is classified as an **international staff position** under Acted’s recruitment framework. Eligibility for an international contract is therefore required.

title: SOUTH SUDAN - COUNTRY DIRECTOR (M/F) - JUBA
body:
## About us

**Desired start date:** 15/02/27  
**Duration of the mission:** 12 months  
**Location:** Juba, South Sudan

**SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL (SI)** is an international humanitarian aid association which, since more than 40 years, has been providing assistance to populations affected by armed conflicts and natural disasters by meeting their basic needs for food, water and shelter. Particularly committed to the fight against diseases linked to unsafe water, the leading cause of death in the world, SI's interventions provide expertise in the field of access to drinking water, sanitation and hygiene promotion, but also in the essential area of food security and livelihoods. Present in 26 countries, the SI teams – 3200 people in total, made up of expatriates, national staff, permanent staff at HQ, and a few volunteers - intervene with professionalism and commitment while respecting cultural norms.

## About the mission

SOLIDARITÉS INTERNATIONAL (SI) has been operating in South Sudan since 2006, conducting activities in emergency and post emergency context, particularly in rural and semi-urban areas, including IDP camp settings. Its expertise in running emergency WaSH intervention is highly acknowledged by all WaSH actors and donors. Furthermore, SI is implementing longer term WASH and FSL activities in multiple locations.  
Since the onset of the crisis in 2013, hundreds of thousands of people have been fleeing the conflict in South Sudan and an estimated 8.4 million are in need of humanitarian assistance as of 2023. Severity of food insecurity continues to grow due to compounding shocks amplified by intensified sub-national violence, three consecutive years of widespread flooding, localized dry spells, and an ongoing protracted macro-economic crisis with heightened poverty and vulnerability (more than 80% of the population is reportedly below the poverty line).   
In April 2023, fighting broke out in Khartoum, Sudan, spreading to other parts of the country in the following days and weeks, and resulting in mass displacement from Sudan to Egypt, Chad, Ethiopia, Libya, the Central African Republic, and South Sudan. By end of 2023, more than 480 000 people had reportedly displaced to South Sudan, the vast majority of entering through the Joda/ Wunthow border point in Renk County, Upper Nile State, the northernmost border crossing in South Sudan. Of those crossing, 82% were South Sudanese returnees, many of whom fled war in then-southern Sudan prior the Comprehensive Peace Agreement (CPA) in 2005, or war in South Sudan between 2013 and 2018.

  
Following the influx of displaced people to Upper Nile and Unity States, Solidarités International mobilized an emergency response. SI emergency teams - responding to natural disasters, epidemics, and population displacement - were deployed early on to participate in the coordination and organization of the response. In Upper Nile, SI already had an office in Malakal (where one of the deployable team is based) and a field-office in Kodok and Melut. Renk is the second coordination office in UPPEr Nile have been set-up to support the ongoing response to the Sudan Crisis and to ensure constant monitoring and rapid access to affected communities. SI's long term presence in Upper Nile enables the organization to ensure proper coordination with other key players on the ground in order to provide a high-quality response and avoid duplication of efforts. SI is currently working to scale-up its response in both Upper Nile and Unity by recruiting additional team members to reinforce its capacities over the coming months.  
The activities implemented are in the sectors of WASH, FSL, Shelter, RRM and Emergency Preparedness Response.   
In 2026, the mission’s estimated budget is around USD 8+ million, and there are 200+ employees.

## About the job

GENERAL OBJECTIVES :

The Country Director is Solidarités International’s official representative in a country. He / She oversees the smooth running of the mission. He / She proposes mission strategy, according to the geopolitical and humanitarian context, and ensures its implementation once it has been validated. He / She monitors projects, ensuring that they are progressing in accordance with the Solidarités International charter and complying with internal and contractual procedures. He / She mobilizes the material and financial resources necessary for the programs to run effectively and supervises the administration of these resources. He / She coordinates the teams in place and ensures their security on the mission. He / She is the direct liaison for Solidarités International’s HQ.

PRIORITIES ON THE 2-3 FIRST MONTHS :

\- Oversee the implementation of the annual strategy 2027

\- Reinforce the security management / contingency planning of the mission

\- Dynamic analysis of the context to identify new potential needs / relevant areas of intervention

\- Consolidate the recent scale-up of the mission to ensure programmatic quality and process compliance

\- Sustain and further develop SI’s funding strategy in South Sudan and identify new donors to diversify the funding portfolio.

\- Support the Senior Management Team in their coordination roles.

\- Regularly represent SI with donors, local authorities, NGOs J17and Coordination forum.

PRIORITIES ON THE 2-3 FIRST MONTHS :

\- Oversee the implementation of the annual strategy 2027

\- Reinforce the security management / contingency planning of the mission

\- Dynamic analysis of the context to identify new potential needs / relevant areas of intervention

\- Consolidate the recent scale-up of the mission to ensure programmatic quality and process compliance

\- Sustain and further develop SI’s funding strategy in South Sudan and identify new donors to diversify the funding portfolio.

\- Support the Senior Management Team in their coordination roles.

\- Regularly represent SI with donors, local authorities, NGOs and Coordination forum.

SECURITY CONSTRAINTS :

There is an internal curfew at night for international staffs - different zones are set (6-8-10PM). Curfew can be reduced based on security updates.  
The situation in South Sudan is volatile. SI is adapting the set up in real time as context evolves  
There is one driver available on evenings and 2 on weekends for movements out of office hours.  
Access to activities is possible for all (and encouraged!).  
In coordination, movements outside of Juba town (besides intervention location) for leisure are limited

## Your profile

DIPLOMAS : Master Degree in humanitarian/development studies, social sciences, management or other related discipline.

EXPERIMENT IN THE HUMANITARIAN SECTOR : more the 5 years

EXPERIMENT ON SIMILAR POSITIONS : 3 - 4 years

TECHNICAL SKILLS :

1\. Excellent communication, organizational and prioritization skills and the ability to multi-task and support and/or fill multiple positions at one time.

2\. High management abilities, and particularly team management skills and capacities to provide distance technical support.

3\. Significant knowledge and experience of grant writing and management for major institutional donors, including EU, BHA/USAID, ECHO, UN Agencies (UNHCR, UNICEF, etc.) and pooled funding mechanisms, such as SSHF.

4\. Ability, acquired through experience, to represent the organization and negotiate and defend SI’s interests with a diverse range of government officials, departments and ministries, civil society organizations, and other international organizations professionally and appropriately.

5\. Demonstrated attention to detail and ability to follow procedures, meet deadlines and work both independently and cooperatively with team members.

6\. Proven ability to deal with donors and operational partners.

7\. Technical knowledge in SI sectors of expertise (WASH, FSL, Shelter) is an asset

TRANSVERSAL SKILLS :

1\. Significant experience of building and supervising large and culturally diverse teams of expatriate and national staff, and interest in capacity building of people.

## SI will offer you

SI will offer you:

**A salaried position:** According to experience, starting from EUR 3740 gross per month (3400 EUR base salary + 10% annual leave allowance paid monthly) and a monthly Per Diem of USD 700.

SI also covers accommodation costs and travel expenses between the expatriate's country of origin and the place of assignment.

**Breaks:** During the assignment, a system of alternation between work and time off is implemented at the rate of 7 working days every three months (with a USD 850 break allowance, allocated by Sl). To these breaks periods, SI grants one (1) additional rest day per month worked.

**Insurance package:** Expatriates benefit from an insurance package which refunds all healthcare expenses (including medical and surgical expenses, dental care and ophthalmological expenses, repatriation) and a welfare system including war risks. Essential vaccination and antimalarial treatment costs are refunded.

**Living conditions :**

Housing package possible. In Juba (level 2), situation is relatively quiet after the tensions of last year. Curfew between 6 and 10 PM depending on areas. Limited walking capacity but movements with cars rather free in the center. Juba, as the capital of South Sudan offers a good variety of markets, supermarkets, restaurants, and bars.

title: Housing Counseling Program Manager
body:
***This position is open to candidates with existing work authorization in the location where the position is advertised.***

**JOB OVERVIEW**

The Program Manager, Housing Counseling provides technical and administrative support for the development of network-wide Housing Counseling toolkits, curricula, guidelines, and Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) that build IRC’s capacity to deliver and sustain housing counseling services under IRC’s Housing and Urban Development (HUD) Housing Counseling Multi-State Organization (MSO). The role will support local offices in expanding housing counseling activities that strengthen client housing stabilization and homelessness prevention. This role will also support IRC’s housing programs and services in collaboration with the HQ Resettlement Team, Economic Empowerment Team, and other teams across RAI US. The position sits within the HQ Resettlement Housing Team and reports to the Director, Initial Resettlement.

**MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES**

- Draft and update Housing Counseling curricula, toolkits, and SOPs aligned with HUD regulations and guidance (e.g., Handbook 7610.1 and 24 CFR part 214) and IRC’s Strategy 100, for use by housing counseling staff across IRC’s U.S. network and those preparing to take the HUD Housing Counselor Certification exam.
- Prepare client-facing housing counseling curriculum materials for in-person counseling and workshop, plus online LMS platforms.
- Maintain and update Resource Navigation tools that map available local, state, and federal housing stabilization, homelessness prevention, and rental assistance resources across the network.
- Help plan and facilitate Housing Counseling and counselor certification training, as well as other IRC housing training, peer learning, and knowledge-sharing opportunities across the network, including through the Monthly Housing Call, Communities of Practice, Switchboard, and similar forums.
- Serve as a first point of contact for day-to-day operational questions, providing technical assistance to support offices in launching, expanding, and sustaining housing counseling programming and other IRC housing programs and their requirements.
- Respond to office requests for guidance on housing counseling program design, documentation, and compliance, applying established HUD requirements and IRC guidance, and escalating complex or ambiguous cases as needed.
- Collaborate with the HQ Housing Team, HQ Economic Empowerment Team, Resettlement colleagues, and other HQ departments (e.g., Preferred Communities and Policy) to support the alignment of housing counseling programming with IRC’s broader housing and resettlement strategy.
- Support data collection, outcome tracking, and HUD-required reporting (e.g., HUD Form 9902), compile and summarize program data to flag trends and gaps for program improvements, and contribute to housing related grant proposals, donor reports and applications, including mapping local funding opportunities in collaboration with field offices and HQ staff.
- Draft standardized practices and quality assurance protocols (e.g., case file review guidance, supervisory monitoring templates) that align affiliate housing counseling practice with HUD Housing Counseling Program requirements, for review and approval.
- Monitor changes to HUD Housing Counseling Program regulations and guidance, flag their implications for the network, and update network tools, curricula, and training materials as directed.
- Attend HUD, intermediary, and national housing counseling meetings or forums, as assigned, and share key updates with the team.
- Other duties as assigned.

**REQUIREMENTS**

- Bachelor’s degree required; Master’s degree in Social Work, Urban Planning, Public Policy and Administration, or a related field preferred.
- HUD Housing Counselor Certification strongly preferred, or ability to obtain within 90 days of hire; demonstrated working knowledge of HUD Housing Counseling Program requirements (24 CFR part 214, HUD Handbook 7610.1) required. Experience supporting HUD-approved housing counseling agency in compliance, technical assistance and capacity-building support preferred.
- Minimum of 2–3 years of relevant professional experience in housing counseling, affordable housing programs, or housing case management, including experience contributing to curricula, SOPs, or training materials.
- Demonstrated ability to draft, adapt, and facilitate curricula, toolkits, and training materials for adult learners across diverse organizational contexts.
- Excellent project management and organizational skills, with experience supporting multi-site or multi-state initiatives, and the ability to manage competing priorities and meet deadlines.
- Experience working with refugee, immigrant, or other underserved populations preferred.
- Demonstrated ability to promote an organizational culture that reflects IRC’s core values of integrity, service, equality, and accountability.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office required; familiarity with types of AI solutions for operational productivity and accuracy required; experience with the HUD Housing Counseling System (HCS), client management systems (CMS), reporting, and other software used for counseling and IRC housing services is a plus.
- Ability to travel up to 25% of the time to visit IRC field offices and affiliates as required. Preference for candidates living within reasonable proximity of an IRC Housing Counseling location, to perform housing counseling activities as needed.

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $60,000-75,000/yr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

title: Consortium Project Manager Colombia Bogota
body:
All NRC employees are expected to work in accordance with the organization’s core values: dedication, innovation, inclusivity, and accountability. These attitudes and beliefs shall guide our actions and relationships.

## What we are looking for

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is seeking a **highly qualified,** **resilient, and dynamic professional** to take up the role of **Consortium Manager – Emergency Response** for Colombia. The purpose of the position is to **ensure MIRE+ emergency and early recovery responses are implemented with quality, in a coordinated and timely manner, in compliance with donors and partners’ strategies and policies and in accordance to target populations’ needs in a rapidly evolving context. The Consortium Manager should strive to maintain MIRE+ positive reputation as Colombia’s largest rapid response mechanism, always seeking to improve technical and operational processes to achieve optimal efficiency and quality in the response. He/She should show leadership and adaptability as well as strong problem-solving skills and positive, assertive communication capacities.**

## What you will do

1. Provide overall direction and leadership of the Consortium to ensure seamless operations, leveraging complementarity among multi-disciplinary partners.
2. Ensure day-to-day strategic and operational coordination with NRC management leadership as leader of the consortium.
3. Oversee day-to-day management of the project, including planning, implementation, monitoring and evaluation and budget spending, ensuring the project is always on scope and schedule.
4. Represent the Consortium towards relevant stakeholders, including national authorities, donors, humanitarian country team and counterparts, promoting the best interests of the Consortium.
5. Line manager and supervise the work of the Consortium Management Unit; carry out any needed recruitment, including consultants.
6. Lead the consultations, design and preparation of the next strategic cycle of the Consortium based on evidenced needs, donor expectations and drawing from partners’ diverse expertise.
7. Contribute to fundraising initiatives to diversify the Consortium’s portfolio, actively seeking new relationships with donors and developing funding proposals.

Please download the [detailed job description](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:b:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQCGbGBJjy3XS5T_HgandSoAAewHPGz5AdIi2R2sH6YMgYs?e=rWpSar)to learn more about the position.

What you will bring

- Minimum 5-7 years of experience in the sector, with progressively increasing responsibilities in humanitarian crises’ contexts.
- At least three of those years in a leadership position involving the management and coordination of similarly sized, international donor supported programmes.
- Proven ability to communicate a common vision among diverse partners and the ability to lead multi-disciplinary teams.
- Experience in complex and volatile settings.
- Full professional proficiency in English and Spanish.
- Knowledge and experience of working in Latin America is strongly preferred. Specific knowledge and experience of the context in Colombia is desirable.
- Demonstrated experience in emergency response management and international best practice.
- Well-versed in humanitarian architecture in the region.
- Knowledge of the particular dynamics of ethnic communities and regulatory frameworks.
- University Degree in International Development, Social or Human Sciences, Project Management, Emergency Response or related field.

## What we offer

- **Duty station: Bogotá, Colombia** (with extensive travel within the country)
- **Contract: national or international contract**
- Travel: up to 30%
- Salary/benefits**: grade 9 on NRC’s salary scale**, with accompanying terms and conditions
- NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability.
- We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative.

[Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)

## Important information about the application process

- *Internal candidates only: please click on the suitcase icon labelled “I am an employee” to be redirected to NRC’s internal careers site.*
- When creating your profile, include your full name as given on your passport. Complete all the system-required fields for experience, employment history and education.
- Submit your application and CV in English, taking care to attach your latest CV.
- Applications that do not meet the minimum standards in terms of experience or qualifications will generally not be considered. Unsolicited applications not related to this specific job advertisement will not be considered.
- Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. We receive many applicants for each vacant position.
- If you have any questions about this role, please email aela.recruitment@nrc.no with the job title as the subject line.

## Why NRC?

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee. Our 15,000 staff work in crises across 40 countries, providing life-saving and long-term assistance to millions of people every year.

[Watch this short video](https://vimeo.com/736782633) to see NRC in action.

We contribute to the development of policy aiming to protect the rights of the displaced and we call for increased humanitarian funding and engagement on processes that will generate structural changes in protection and assistance in the region.

NRC implements a multi-country Colombia-Panama-Ecuador strategy to respond to the complex crises and emergencies across the sub-continent. In Colombia, we provide assistance to IDPs and victims of the armed conflict in hard-to-reach areas where authorities struggle to protect civilians and provide help. We also help Colombians in need of international protection in Ecuador and Panama, as well as Venezuelans who were triggered to flee their country as a result of the growing political instability and humanitarian crisis. We provide protection, legal assistance, education, livelihoods and food security, WASH and shelter services to affected populations.

Within this context, NRC leads an intersectoral Rapid Response Mechanism (MIRE+ consortium) together with Action Against Hunger (ACF), Médecins du Monde (MdM) and Pastoral Social - Cáritas Colombia funded by EU Humanitarian Aid (ECHO), the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA), the Spanish Agency for International Development (AECID) and Swiss Development Cooperation (COSUDE/SDC). Under a triple nexus framework, the consortium delivers multi-sectoral humanitarian assistance responding rapidly to emergencies resulting from the armed conflict in Colombia, natural hazards and early recovery activities. MIRE+ operates across all the country, prioritizing response in hard-to-reach areas and bringing support to people that have been affected by multiple compounding crises. The consortium has just entered a new two-year strategic cycle. We are therefore searching for an experienced and dynamic Chief of Party to lead the multi-donor emergency and early recovery Consortium. Whilst this position is hosted by NRC, the Consortium Manager will represent the MIRE+.

We are looking for people who are passionate about helping refugees and people forced to flee. Are you one of those people? If you are, NRC offers you the opportunity to:

- do demanding and professional work, often in challenging contexts.
- join a work culture that empowers every employee to share ideas and take responsibility.
- be part of a welcoming and supportive community committed to human dignity.

[Learn more about NRC](https://www.nrc.no/)

### About Us

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is a global humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee.

Join us in assisting millions of people in areas where others cannot, tackling some of the world's most dangerous and difficult crises. Bring your skills and dedication to an organisation recognised for providing high quality aid and for defending the rights of refugees and internally displaced people.

At NRC, we give responsibility to employees at all levels and foster professional growth and innovative teams. You can expect a supportive culture and an open dialogue with management. We are committed to diversity, equity and inclusion.

Together, we save lives and rebuild futures.

Safeguarding is central to NRC’s work. We expect all employees to:

• treat everyone with respect and dignity

• contribute to building a safe environment for all

• never engage in any form of exploitation, harassment and specifically sexual exploitation, abuse and sexual harassment (SEAH)

• always report. NRC has a zero-tolerance approach to inaction against exploitation, abuse and SEAH

title: External Auditor for JRS Project
Director of Advocacy
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Background:**

The External Relations (ER) Department mobilizes external audiences to raise the requisite funds, influence policies and achieve practice changes to improve outcomes for our clients, while growing and protecting our global brand. The Global Policy & Advocacy team is a dynamic part of the ER Department that leverages the power of IRC’s ideas to solve the biggest challenges facing IRC’s clients across the “arc of crisis” and influence external stakeholders, in particular governments and multi-lateral institutions, to enact these solutions to ultimately make meaningful change for our clients. From addressing the drivers of conflict to meeting the needs of displaced people, the team partners with innovative thinkers, experts and those with lived experience to identify solutions and bring them to life. We take pride in being solutions-oriented and creative. We are precise in our goals, tactics, and messages. We drive change year over year, knowing that system change takes dedicated focus while maintaining the flexibility to respond to emerging needs across the globe. Finally, we are collaborative, constantly seeking new ideas and perspectives from others in our sector and beyond as we work side by side with programs, strategy, communications and research and innovation teams across the IRC.

**Job Overview:**   
As the Director of Advocacy, you will lead development of the IRC’s advocacy efforts to support key priorities across crisis and solutions-driven global influence priorities for the International Rescue Committee. You are responsible for crafting our influence strategies using IRC’s programmatic and research evidence, surgical policy and practice solutions, and trusted brand to inspire collective action. You are the expert for understanding current federal legislative and policy trends in the US and how our policies cut across political agendas. You will engage key stakeholders across government and civil society. You will work across the IRC to develop advocacy campaigns and build relationships including with Congressional representatives, U.S. and other government officials in D.C. as well as foundations, think tanks, multilateral organizations, and other humanitarian organizations. You will also look across IRC’s global priorities, engaging relevant embassies and crafting specific advocacy messages for donor governments.

**Major Responsibilities:**

- **Advocacy Strategy:** Lead advocacy strategies for specific policy goals, including thought leadership objectives relevant to the U.S. market, collaborating with policy leads to advance IRCs key influence priorities and maximize the opportunity for IRC to advance our influence objectives. Engage across the IRC with all relevant stakeholders. Craft advocacy strategies, drawing on IRC’s policy expertise, that are suited to global donor government priorities.
- **Influence Analysis:** Develop U.S. power maps for key policy issues to identify influence priorities. Cultivate relationships across the U.S. Government and lead Congressional engagement. Work with team to support development and execution of creative influence strategies, including with nontraditional partners. Look across IRC’s global priorities and ensure they are integrated into advocacy and influence strategies.
- **Advocacy:** Support efforts to build IRC’s credibility, profile and relationships by engaging with key policy stakeholders and supporting opportunities to raise IRC’s profile at key meetings and fora. Collaborate closely with other U.S. market staff and global policy and advocacy staff, contributing to efforts designed to build IRC’s credibility, profile and relationships in Washington.
- Legislative and Policy Tracking. Expand IRC’s legislative reach by tracking and analyzing shifting Congressional and Executive branch positions, individuals engaging on our issues, and the politics around our issues. Translate policy asks into legislative asks. Engage U.S. Government stakeholders relevant to the IRC’s work in the U.S. Track U.S. legislative and executive processes.
- **Policy Engagement:** Contribute to policy generation by providing U.S.-specific analysis that increases the credibility and efficacy of our solutions through constant collaboration. Support IRC’s policy team in identifying and developing policy priorities that are impactful and achievable in the U.S. as well as in global markets.
- **Communications:** Provide market and audience expertise to communications team to shape policy communications specific to the U.S.Support the team in developing communications strategy and develop materials for advocacy targets. Support planning and implementation of strategic activities including events. Facilitate development and editing of internal and external advocacy products to ensure resonance in U.S. market and adherence to high standards of quality.
- **Steward Gender Equality, Diversity and Inclusion:** both in the culture of IRC, as well as in the policy solutions we develop and the ways we wield influence.
- **Spokesperson:** Act as an IRC influence spokespersonon focused advocacy areas. Act as key interlocutor with legislative and governmental staffers**.**
- **Board and Advisors:** Support relationships with IRC's Board and Advisors by identifying points of mutual interest and opportunities around our priority issues.
- **Teamwork:** Support a positive team culture by acting openly and collaboratively, supporting colleagues in their work and sharing credit with others where appropriate. Potential supervision of Senior Advisor or other staff.

**Key Working Relationships:**

- **Position reports to:** Senior Director, Advocacy & Influence and Vice President of Policy and Advocacy
- **Internal contacts:** Policy and Advocacy colleagues across the globe; Technical Excellence leads; International Programs leads; Crisis Response, Recovery and Development Department; Communications; Awards Management; President’s Office, External Relations Department
- **External contacts:** Key Opinion Formers and policy makers in the U.S. Government and U.S. Congress, other humanitarian leaders and thinktanks, relevant embassies, multilateral institutions

**Job Requirements:**

***Education:***

- Degree in relevant field such as Public Policy, Law or International Relations

***Work experience:***

- Demonstrated experience in advocacy and advocacy strategy development with a focus on creativity and strategic thinking
- 10-12 years of experience working on complex humanitarian and/or development issues
- Knowledge of U.S. Government functioning and prior work the U.S. Government or Congress are a plus.
- Understanding of global issues, multilateral engagement experience.

***Demonstrated skills and competencies:***

- Examples of influence/impact on legislative and executive policy. Strong network of influencers and policy makers
- Deep understanding of global issues related to the humanitarian field.
- Ability to think strategically and creatively, being solutions-oriented
- Extensive knowledge of humanitarian aid and refugee issues, particularly around the complex drivers of humanitarian need
- Demonstrated ability to communicate and collaborate successfully with experts, high level decision and policy makers, and colleagues in the humanitarian and development fields. Good public speaking skills.
- Excellent writing skills and the ability to translate complex material and data into coherent narratives that resonate with policymakers
- Fluency with key parts of the IRC’s strategy and existing policy strategy
- Ability to work on tight deadlines and juggle competing demands
- Self-motivated

**Working Environment:** Remote

**Compensation:** ***($130,000 - $156,000 - annually).*** Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

title: Head of Programmes CARE Ukraine
body:
## **Is this you?**

**Contract Start Date**: early 2027, no later than 1 March, 2027  
**Contract Duration:** 1 year  
**Duty Station:** Kyiv (Ukraine)
