Salary and conditions will be in accordance with Danish Refugee Council’s Terms of Employment for employees on national or expatriate contract.

title: Employment Specialist
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Job Overview:**

The Employment Specialist helps newly arrived refugee clients achieve self-sufficiency through employment. This role delivers job readiness services, career coaching, and employer connections while supporting clients through the application and placement process. The Specialist maintains strong relationships with local employers, coordinates with other IRC staff, and ensures compliance with donor and program requirements.

**Major Responsibilities:**

- Responsibilities may include, but are not limited to:
- Conduct intake and assessment for employment-eligible clients and develop individualized employment plans.
- Deliver job readiness orientations in both group and one-on-one settings, focusing on essential skills for employability.
- Cultivate and maintain relationships with area employers to identify appropriate opportunities for clients.
- Match clients to employment opportunities and guide them through applications, interviews, and hiring processes.
- Monitor job placements, wages, and satisfaction of both clients and employers, providing post-placement support.
- Assist clients with Unemployment Insurance applications and weekly claims when applicable.
- Maintain accurate case notes and data entry in required systems; prepare employment vouchers and other documentation.
- Participate in program meetings, trainings, and professional development activities; follow all IRC policies including safeguarding and confidentiality standards.
- Perform other related duties as assigned

**Job Requirements:**

**Education:**

- Bachelor’s degree in Social Work, workforce development, or related field strongly preferred; equivalent work experience may be considered.

**Work Experience:**

- At least 2 years of case management, employment, job placement, or business experience in a social services setting.
- Experience working with vulnerable or underserved populations strongly preferred.

**Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:**

- Knowledge of U.S. job search process and ability to coach clients through securing employment.
- Strong organizational and time-management skills; detail-oriented.
- Computer proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Outlook, Teams).
- Excellent verbal and written communication skills; public speaking/presentation skills preferred.
- Proven ability to problem-solve, prioritize tasks, and meet goals independently or as part of a team.

**Language Skills:**

- Proficiency in English required; bilingual ability in Spanish, Dari, Swahili, Kinyarwanda, Arabic, French, or other refugee/immigrant language preferred.

 **Certificates or Licenses:**

- Valid driver’s license, active insurance policy, and access to reliable transportation.
- Must possess or be eligible for a fingerprint clearance card per Arizona state law.

**Working Environment*****:***

- A combination of standard office environment, remote work, and ‘field’ time within the service delivery area to perform the above outlined responsibilities.
- May require occasional weekend and/or evening work.
- Must be able to lift 35 to 50 pounds (furniture, household supplies, and food boxes).

**Compensation:** ($20.97/hour). Compensation is based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements

At the IRC, we seek to build a welcoming, inclusive environment not only for our refugee clients, but for all of our employees. As an equal opportunity employer, we value the strength found in the diversity of voices, experiences, and backgrounds who join us in our work. Fostering an inclusive culture with equitable practices is everyone's responsibility, and we regularly offer trainings and opportunities to learn more and find ways to do better. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, gender, gender expression, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, socioeconomic status, or disability status. We are dedicated to ensuring that disabled individuals are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment. Please contact us to request accommodation. In your application, please feel free to indicate your preferred pronouns.

We recognize that few applicants may "check all the boxes," but that each person has their own unique strengths that they would bring to the table. In our commitment to building a diverse and authentic work culture, we invite you to apply anyway. You belong here.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

title: Nutrition Specialist
body:
***This position is open to candidates with existing work authorization in the location where the position is advertised.***

**IRC Background:**

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world’s worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is at work in over 40 countries and 26 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. IRC reaches over 50,000 clients annually across the US through programs for resettled refugees, asylum seekers, unaccompanied children, survivors of torture and trafficking, and individuals from local communities welcoming newcomers.

**Scope of work:**

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. title: Human Capability Transformation ‎Advisor
source: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies
body:
**Organizational context**

The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) is the world’s largest humanitarian network, with 191 member National Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies. IFRC uses the Triple R – response, resilience and respect – to deliver on Strategy 2030. IFRC responds to disasters and crises, ensuring timely, coordinated and locally led humanitarian action. IFRC supports its members in building community resilience in the areas of climate and environment, health and wellbeing, and migration and displacement. IFRC promotes respect for our fundamental principles of humanity, impartiality, neutrality, independence, voluntary service, unity, and universality, including in our work on values, power and inclusion. The IFRC focuses throughout on our core mandate – our raison d’être – of strategic and operational coordination, humanitarian diplomacy, National Society development, and accountability.

IFRC is led by its Secretary General and has its Headquarters in Geneva and five regional offices in Africa (Nairobi); the Americas (Panama); Asia Pacific (Kuala Lumpur); Europe (Budapest); and MENA (Beirut) as well as representation offices, service centres and delegations across the globe.

IFRC has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment and other forms of harassment, abuse of authority, discrimination, and lack of integrity (including but not limited to financial misconduct). IFRC also adheres to strict child safeguarding principles.

The Ukrainian Red Cross Society (URCS) is implementing a comprehensive institutional transformation agenda under the URCS Strategy 2026-2030 and the Institutional Capabilities Programme. As part of this transformation, URCS intends to evolve its current Human Resources Department into a strategic Human Capability Function, moving beyond traditional HR administration towards a model that enables workforce capability, leadership development, talent management, organizational culture, employee and volunteer experience, succession planning, and organizational effectiveness.

To support this transition, URCS has invited technical assistance from IFRC through the recruitment and deployment of an experienced HR professional. The position will be recruited and contracted by IFRC and seconded to URCS for an extended period to provide dedicated technical leadership and implementation support throughout the transformation process.

The role is intended to serve as a trusted advisor and technical expert, working alongside a newly hired HR Director and URCS leadership to design, guide and support the implementation of the Human Capability Transformation Programme that focuses on strengthening workforce planning, talent and leadership development, organizational culture, performance management, employee and volunteer experience, people analytics and digital people systems. Through institutional capacity building, change management and knowledge transfer, the Programme aims to create a resilient, high-performing and future-ready organization capable of delivering its humanitarian mission and strategic objectives through 2030 and beyond.

The position is intended as seconded technical backstop supporting both strategic development and practical implementation of the transition.

**Job purpose**

The Human Capability Transformation Advisor will serve as a trusted technical expert and change leader, supporting URCS in the design and institutionalization of a comprehensive Human Capability Transformation Programme aligned with the URCS Strategy 2026–2030 and the Institutional Capabilities Development Programme.

The Advisor will support the transition of the traditional Human Resources function into a modern, strategic Human Capability function that strengthens organizational performance, leadership, workforce sustainability and effectiveness. This will include strategic workforce planning, talent and performance management, leadership and capability development, organizational culture, succession planning, and employee and volunteer experience.

Working closely with the Deputy Director General Organization and Human Capability Development, HR Director and other key stakeholders, the role holder will provide strategic advice and hands-on implementation support to strengthen operating models, systems, governance and ways of working. A key focus will be coaching, mentoring and knowledge transfer to build internal capability and ensure that new approaches are effectively embedded and can be sustained and continuously developed by URCS.

**Key Areas of Responsibility**

**Strategic Human Capability Transformation**

- Provide strategic leadership and technical advice for the implementation of the Human Capability Programme.
- Support the establishment of the future Human Capability operating model, ensuring alignment with the URCS Strategy 2026-2030 and Institutional Capabilities (NSD) Programme.
- Introduce and embed good international practices, systems and methodologies that strengthen organizational capability and workforce effectiveness.

**Organizational Development and Effectiveness**

- Strengthen organizational effectiveness through improved organizational design, workforce structures and capability management.
- Support the identification and closure of critical organizational capability gaps and succession risks.
- Promote accountability, organizational resilience and effective people management practices across the URCS.

**Strategic Workforce Planning**

- Establish strategic workforce planning processes that align people capabilities with current and future organizational needs.
- Strengthen workforce analysis, capability mapping and succession planning to support sustainable organizational growth.

**Leadership Development and Talent Management**

- Support the development of a leadership system that strengthens leadership capability at all levels of the organization.
- Establish sustainable approaches to talent management, leadership development and succession planning.
- Coach and mentor leaders in people management, organizational effectiveness and change leadership.

**Learning and Organizational Capability Development**

- Support the establishment of an integrated learning and capability development system aligned with organizational priorities.
- Promote a culture of continuous learning, knowledge sharing and professional development across URCS.

**Performance Management and Rewards**

- Support the development of performance management and reward systems that promote accountability, engagement and high performance.
- Strengthen the use of performance data to inform talent, workforce and organizational decisions.

**Organizational Culture and Employee Experience**

- Support the development of a unified organizational culture aligned with URCS values and strategic objectives.
- Strengthening employee engagement, wellbeing and employee experience practices to improve retention and organizational commitment.

**HR Business Partner Capability Development**

- Establish the HR Business Partner model as a strategic partner to managers and leaders across URCS.
- Strengthen the advisory, workforce planning and organizational development capabilities of Human Capability staff.

**People Analytics and Digital Human Capability Systems**

- Promote data-driven decision-making through workforce analytics, people metrics and management reporting.
- Support the development of digital systems and tools that improve workforce management and organizational effectiveness.

**Change Management and Transformation Support**

- Lead and support change management efforts that enable the successful adoption of new systems, structures and ways of working.
- Strengthen stakeholder engagement, organizational readiness and leadership alignment throughout the transformation process.

**Capacity Strengthening and Knowledge Transfer**

- Act as a strategic adviser and mentor to the HR Director and Human Capability Programme leadership team that is managed by the HR Director.
- Build sustainable institutional capability through coaching, knowledge transfer and implementation support.

Ensure the long-term sustainability of the transformation through structured handover and institutionalization of systems and practice

Duties applicable to all staff  
‎1.‎ Work actively towards the achievement of IFRC’s goals. ‎  
‎2.‎ Abide by and work in accordance with the Red Cross and Red Crescent principles.‎  
‎3.‎ Perform any other work-related duties and responsibilities that may be assigned by the line manager.‎

**Education**

- Advanced university degree/ postgraduate qualification in one or more of the ‎following fields: Organizational Development, Management and Leadership, Human ‎Resources Management, Human Capital Management, Organizational Psychology, ‎Business Administration (MBA), Human Capital Strategy or Change Management or ‎other relevant fields. ‎
- Professional certifications in HR and organizational development/change management ‎would be considered an asset

**Experience**

- Minimum 7 years of progressively responsible professional experience in senior HR, ‎Human Capital, Organizational Development or Human Capability leadership roles.‎
- Demonstrated experience leading large-scale HR transformation or organizational ‎transformation programmes, including organizational development, change ‎management and culture transformation. ‎
- Experience developing and implementing workforce planning, talent management, ‎succession, performance and leadership/capability development systems.‎
- Proven experience providing strategic advice to executive leadership and leading ‎capacity strengthening, institutional development and knowledge transfer initiatives.‎
- Experience working in humanitarian, international development, NGO or public sector ‎environments, including organizations operating through decentralized networks and ‎branch structures.‎
- Experience working in complex emergencies, recovery or transition contexts; previous ‎experience within the Red Cross Red Crescent Movement is an asset.‎

**Knowledge and Skills**

- Strong knowledge and practical experience in: Human Capability Strategy, HR ‎Transformation, Organizational Development and Organizational Design
- Knowledge and experience in Workforce Planning, Leadership Development, Talent ‎Management and Succession Planning
- Strong programme/project management skills, with the ability to translate ‎transformation strategies and roadmaps into prioritized, practical and measurable ‎implementation plans.‎
- Strong stakeholder management and influencing skills, with the ability to build ‎alignment and drive organizational change across diverse functions and seniority ‎levels.‎
- Experience and knowledge of Learning and Development processes, Performance ‎Management, Managing Employee Experience and Enriching Organizational Culture. ‎
- Knowledge and experience in executing Change Management, Conducting People ‎Analytics
- Knowledge and experience of HRIS and Digital HR Systems ‎
- Proven experience in Coaching and Mentoring Facilitation and Capacity Development
- Demonstrated core proficiency in (a) digital communication & collaboration, (b) basic ‎digital content creation, (c) digital safety & security, (d) data literacy, and (e) problem ‎solving with technology (including responsible use of AI assistants.‎
- Understanding of and commitment to IFRC’s mission and values. ‎
- Fluent spoken and written English

**Values:** Respect for diversity; Integrity; Professionalism; Accountability  
**Core competencies:** Communication; Collaboration and teamwork; Judgement and decision making; National society ‎and customer relations; Creativity and innovation; Building trust

title: Protection Officer
body:
**Job Title:** Protection Officer

**Function**: Programme Implementation

**Job Group**: Programme

**Duty Station**: Ukraine (Kherson)

**Administrative Line Manager**: Team Leader

**Technical Line Manager:** Team Leader

**Position Type**: Full-time

**ABOUT US**

NP (Nonviolent Peaceforce) reimagines security and civilian protection in areas most impacted by conflict by working alongside communities to interrupt and prevent violence. NP is a global civil society organization that works with people affected by violent conflicts to enhance their security and dignity through Unarmed Civilian Protection (UCP) and by helping to transform the world’s response to conflict situations.

NP first established a presence in Ukraine in 2014 working on peacebuilding and conflict mediation. NP has had sustained presence in Ukraine since April 2022, documenting civilian protection challenges, providing protection advocacy, and engaging with a variety of local and international stakeholders and responding to identified civilian protection needs. NP has a holistic and forward leaning approach to civilian protection in Ukraine with a particular focus on increasing the safety and security of civilians, including internally displaced persons (IDPs), as they move across the country, with a focus on population groups exposed to vulnerabilities.

**JOB PURPOSE**

The role of the Protection Officer (PO) is to support the implementation of civilian protection and violence-prevention programming for those affected by conflict.

**KEY OBJECTIVES/RESPONSIBILITIES:**

**Project implementation**

- Provide support for the day-to-day implementation of project activities in accordance with the agreed work plans and log-frames.
- Support and assist the Team Leader (TL) in the engagement and relationship building with relevant stakeholders, including local humanitarian NGOs, community-based organizations, and local authorities.
- Support in identifying protection needs in Kherson by conducting site assessments, context monitoring, and community outreach
- Conduct and facilitate community meetings and dialogues in the project areas.
- Support and assist the TL and team in conducting and facilitating training and seminars for community and project partners, for example, Civilian Protection – Early Warning and Early Response (CP-EWER), International Humanitarian Law (IHL), Human Rights Law (HRL), Child Protection (CP), Gender Based Violence (GBV).
- Support in providing protective accompaniment to civilians exposed to vulnerabilities, particularly the elderly and people with special needs.
- Support and assist, monitor, verify and report incidents of violence and civilian displacement.
- Regularly monitor provision and the availability of humanitarian services to civilians in need, conduct referrals, when necessary.
- Write and submit activity reports documenting the completion of protection activities and their impact.

**Duties Applicable to All Staff**

- Actively work towards the achievement of the goals and mandate of NP.
- Abide by and work in accordance with NP values and principles as provided in the Global Employee Handbook and existing policies.
- Perform any other work-related duties and responsibilities that may be assigned by the line manager.

**QUALIFICATIONS AND COMPETENCIES:**

**Education**

*Required*

- University degree in a related field (Social Science, Development Studies, etc.).
- Interest in peacebuilding, conflict transformation, and civilian protection and human rights. Practical experience in these fields is highly desirable.

*Preferred*

- Qualifications or commensurate practical experience in peacebuilding, conflict transformation or nonviolent peacekeeping.

**Work Experience**

*Required*

- 1-2 years relevant work experience in civilian/humanitarian/child protection and human rights.

*Preferred*

- NGO/ humanitarian work.
- Post-conflict/conflict area experience.
- Experience in community organizing/mobilization.
- Experience leading or coordinating trainings.

**Knowledge and Skills**

*Required*

- Understanding on civil protection and human rights frameworks
- Understanding of conflict dynamics in Ukraine
- Understanding of the humanitarian and **DO NO HARM** principles
- Knowledge and understanding in peace making, peacekeeping and peace building and social cohesion concepts
- Report writing skills
- Able to communicate in oral and written English, as well as Ukrainian and/or Russian

title: Protection from Violence Manager Ethiopia North Afar
body:
**What we’re looking for:**

Are you passionate about advancing protection and making a tangible difference in the lives of people affected by violence and displacement?

NRC Ethiopia is looking for a **Protection from Violence (PfV) Project Manager** to lead its project portfolio in the North Area Office. This is an opportunity to provide strategic and operational leadership, drive high-quality protection programming, strengthen accountability and ensure effective project delivery in line with NRC standards, strategies and donor requirements.

As NRC continues to strengthen and expand its PfV programming across Ethiopia, you will play a pivotal role in shaping and delivering integrated protection interventions across Amhara, Afar and Wolkait Tegede Setit Humera, while contributing to the wider programme's ambitions across the country.

*Please note: This opportunity is open exclusively to Ethiopian nationals. Female candidates are encouraged to apply.*

**What You Will Do:**

Here are some of your specific responsibilities:

- Train, mentor and coach staff delivering specialised protection services, including protection case management and Individual Protection Assistance (IPA), in line with NRC modalities, tools and guidance.
- Promote consistency and alignment of specialised protection activities across field teams and support the development or adaptation of common guidelines, tools and standard operating procedures (SOPs) where required.
- Ensure that tools and SOPs align with NRC approaches to specialised protection services and that appropriate transition or capacity-development plans are in place where needed.
- Lead or coordinate area-based, conflict-sensitive analysis and monitoring of protection risks to inform programme design, implementation and adaptation.
- Ensure that an appropriate case-management tracking system is maintained or established, with due attention to confidentiality, informed consent and data protection.
- Monitor trends in protection risks emerging from specialised protection services and engage with NRC teams and other protection actors to address risks at community level.
- Coordinate with the Monitoring and Evaluation team to ensure appropriate monitoring approaches and tools and promote safe monitoring of specialised protection activities.
- Capture and share lessons learned on project methodology and implementation, and use findings to improve programme quality.
- Provide technical and managerial support for implementation of specialised protection work plans.
- Contribute to regional donor reporting, including narrative and financial inputs.
- Lead the development and design of Civilian Self-Protection (CSP) activities, ensuring that interventions are contextually appropriate and informed by protection analysis.
- Ensure that learning from CSP implementation is documented and incorporated into programme adaptation and staff development.

Please download a more detailed[**JOB DESCRIPTION**](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:w:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQBZxn6Fs8NTRYp9ytigCMdvAWezj2k686m80DaIw4drkbo?e=zUcUnn) for more specific duties and responsibilities.

**What you will bring:**

- Minimum five years of experience in a senior project implementation or management position in a humanitarian or recovery context.
- Experience working in complex and volatile contexts.
- Technical expertise in Protection programming.
- Demonstrated results relevant to the responsibilities of the position.
- Knowledge of own leadership skills and profile.
- Fluency in written and spoken English.
- Technical expertise and field experience in general protection case management in operation area.
- Field experience conducting case management and referrals in low-resource settings.
- Strong interpersonal skills and knowledge of the North Area operational context.
- Knowledge of local language
- Experience managing teams and working with IDPs, returnees, refugees and host communities.

**What we offer:**

- Duty station: Afar, Asyita.
- Contract: 12 months.
- Travel: Up to 40%.
- Salary/benefits: grade 8 on NRC’s Resident salary scale, with accompanying terms and conditions.
- NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability.
- We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative.

[Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)

Important information about the application process

- For Internal candidates: To apply as an internal candidate, log in with your official email or click on Opportunity Market Place.
- When creating your profile, include your full name as given on your passport. Complete all the system-required fields for experience, employment history and education.
- Submit your application and CV in English, taking care to attach your latest CV.
- Applications that do not meet the minimum standards in terms of experience or qualifications will generally not be considered. Unsolicited applications not related to this specific job advertisement will not be considered.
- We receive many applications for each vacant position and so only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

If you have any questions about this role, please email **ho.recruitment@nrc.no**with the job title as the subject line.

**Why NRC?**

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee. Our 15,000 staff work in crises across 40 countries, providing life-saving and long-term assistance to millions of people every year.

[Watch this short video](https://vimeo.com/736782633) to see NRC in action.

We are looking for people who are passionate about helping refugees and people forced to flee. Are you one of those people? If you are, NRC offers you the opportunity to:

- do demanding and professional work, often in challenging contexts.
- join a work culture that empowers every employee to share ideas and take responsibility.
- be part of a welcoming and supportive community committed to human dignity.

## About Us

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is a global humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee.

Join us in assisting millions of people in areas where others cannot, tackling some of the world's most dangerous and difficult crises. Bring your skills and dedication to an organisation recognised for providing high quality aid and for defending the rights of refugees and internally displaced people.

At NRC, we give responsibility to employees at all levels and foster professional growth and innovative teams. You can expect a supportive culture and an open dialogue with management. We are committed to diversity, equity and inclusion.

Together, we save lives and rebuild futures.

Safeguarding is central to NRC’s work. We expect all employees to:

• treat everyone with respect and dignity

• contribute to building a safe environment for all

• never engage in any form of exploitation, harassment and specifically sexual exploitation, abuse and sexual harassment (SEAH)

• always report. NRC has a zero-tolerance approach to inaction against exploitation, abuse and SEAH

title: Secretary General
body:
The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is seeking a new Secretary General to succeed Jan Egeland. Under his leadership, NRC has strengthened its international standing and become a prominent voice for people forced to flee. The next Secretary General will build on these achievements and lead NRC into the future.

This is an opportunity to lead one of the world's most respected humanitarian organisations, influence the international humanitarian agenda and make a real difference to people affected by conflict and displacement.

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee. Our 14,000 staff work in crises across 39 countries, providing life-saving and long-term assistance to millions of people every year. NRC includes the two brands NORCAP – global provider of aid expertise and solutions ([https://www.nrc.no/norcap](https://www.nrc.no/norcap)) and the displacement monitoring centre IDMC-JIPS ([https://www.internal-displacement.org/](https://www.internal-displacement.org/)).

## Responsibilities

**The opportunity:**

As Secretary General, you will lead a large and complex global organisation, set its strategic direction and ensure that NRC delivers on its humanitarian mission.

Working closely with the NRC Board and senior management group, you will be responsible for the organisation's continued development, its people and resources, and the strategic choices needed to remain effective and efficient in a changing world.

You will be NRC's leading international representative and public voice, engaging with governments, international institutions, donors and humanitarian partners. You will advocate for the rights of displaced people, influence humanitarian policy and mobilise support for NRC's work, including when this means challenging those in power.

The role requires someone who can combine a strong international presence with the ability to lead and develop a major global organisation.

## Qualifications

**The person we are looking for:**

We are seeking an accomplished international leader with strong humanitarian values, international credibility and the ability to take NRC forward.

A deep personal commitment to humanitarian principles, human dignity and the rights of people forced to flee is essential.

You bring substantial leadership experience from a complex international organisation or sector, with a track record of setting direction, making difficult decisions and leading change. You have a strong understanding of international affairs and geopolitical dynamics, and the judgement to navigate complex political and organisational challenges.

You are an effective communicator who can engage and influence senior decision-makers internationally. As a leader, you build trust, empower others and bring people together around a shared purpose.

We welcome candidates from different backgrounds who share NRC's humanitarian values and have the leadership experience and commitment needed for the role.

Your experience may come from humanitarian or international development organisations, government, diplomacy, multilateral institutions or other international sectors.

Fluency in English and proficiency in Norwegian or another Scandinavian language are required.

source: International Centre for Migration Policy Development
body:
MRAPP funded by the Government of the Netherlands, aims to strengthen migration prevention efforts and improve access to migration-related information, counselling, referral and reintegration services in Iraq. The project is implemented by ICMPD in close coordination with the Ministry of Migration and Displacement and other relevant governmental and local stakeholders, with a focus on strengthening and expanding the Migrant Resource Centre (MRC) model.

The position will be based within the MRAPP project team and will report to the Project Manager, while working closely with relevant ICMPD colleagues, MRC staff, government counterparts and project stakeholders to support the effective delivery of project activities and results.

## Functional Overview

Working closely with the respective Migration Resource Centre (MRC) Coordinator, the MRC Counsellor assists with the implementation of MRC activities and workplans, in support of effective communication, information and service delivery. They contribute to the organisation of events and outreach activities organised by the MRC. They work collaboratively with the MRC Coordinator and other Counsellors, administrative support staff, project teams, relevant local counterparts, and Units at Headquarters, ensuring the effective and timely delivery of MRC activities and services, in accordance with ICMPD rules and procedures.

## Key Results

***Support to MRC Activities:*** Via various means and platforms such as face-to-face, phone and online, counselling, guidance, referral and information provided to a variety of clients (prospective or returning migrants, migrants, families of migrants, etc.) who visit or attend MRC activities, initiating and following up on referrals, linking them with relevant agencies depending on their needs, e.g. technical and vocational institutes to upgrade their skills or with the relevant authorities for the processing of their documents for overseas employment. Outreach activities supported via the use of media and social media and participation in online discussions, forums or symposiums, conferences, and other related events. In collaboration with the MRC Coordinator the MRC website and database, Facebook page and other social media accounts regularly updated.

***Support to Outreach Activities:*** In cooperation with relevant agencies both in the public and private sector, networks and contacts effectively established. Community events and outreach activities organised such as briefings in academic and training institutions, symposia with civil society, training of education or emigration consultancies, and the setting-up of booths, kiosks, or similar structures in public places to disseminate information and materials on safe, orderly, and regular migration, including on return and reintegration.

***Preparation of Information Materials:*** In collaboration with the ICMPD team and whenever applicable, with consultants or experts, research or mapping undertaken of available migration-related programmes, services, and activities of various stakeholders. Knowledge materials compiled on migration that are helpful in the full operation and functioning of the MRC. Additional knowledge products andinformation materials revised, prepared, or further developed, as necessary, such as brochures, handbooks, audio-visual products, web-based information documents, etc. Online discussions relevant to migration, regularly maintained and populated, initiating regular and timely responses to issues raised and information requested.

***Support to the MRC Coordination Activities:*** Assistance provided to the respective MRC Coordinator to ensure the timely, efficient, and effective implementation of MRC activities, and with the monitoring and updating of the workplans, as necessary, ensuring that outputs and outcomes are aligned and integrated with the national priorities and strategies of government partners, and of the projects. Substantive contributions provided to the preparation of relevant reports, responses to client feedback and monitoring and reporting to relevant agencies on any policy or programmatic recommendations. Information materials compiled and prepared for dissemination. The MRC database regularly updated recording relevant activities, events and outreach activities undertaken. Effective support provided to the MRC Coordinator in preparing weekly, quarterly and annual progress reports, work plans and budget, meeting agendas and minutes, activity andmission reports, expenditure plans and advance budget requests on agreed formats, and other documentary requirements.

## Required Expertise

- ​Solid organizational, planning and prioritizing skills and abilities.
- Upon consultation with the supervisor, ability to make decisions in full compliance with ICMPD’soperational regulations and rules.
- Analytical thinking to gather, analyse and compile information, identifying critical relationships and patterns among data and proposing workable solutions.
- An understanding of migration dynamics in the country.
- Experience in the area of migration in the country.
- High sense of initiative and good judgement to be able to work independently with minimum supervision.
- Strong sense of client orientation and good understanding of effective service delivery, community engagement, outreach, and social work.
- Ability to work effectively with people of different nationalities and cultural backgrounds.
- Capability to establish effective relationships across the organisation at all levels.

## Qualifications, Experience and Language Skills

- Bachelor’s degree or equivalent in a relevant field. High school diploma or equivalent with two additional years of relevant work experience may be accepted in lieu of the bachelor’s degree.
- Minimum of 2 years of position-specific experience.
- Working experience with international organisations is an asset.
- Experience in office administration and management.
- Experience working with local authorities and businesses.
- Solid organizational skills.
- Proficiency in English, Kurdish and Arabic (verbal/written) is required.
- Proficiency in the use of standard IT tools.

title: Operations Manager
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
body:
## About Refugee-Led Research Hub (RLRH)

The Refugee-Led Research Hub (RLRH) supports individuals with lived experience of displacement to become leaders in fields related to human rights, forced migration, humanitarian response and development, politics, and law, among other areas. We do so by delivering academic and professional development programming to a global cohort of students who have been affected by displacement—as refugees, asylum seekers, IDPs, stateless, and beyond—supporting access to graduate degrees and advanced career opportunities. RLRH also creates opportunities for researchers with displacement backgrounds to lead primary and secondary research studies, from start to finish.

RLRH’s team is composed of colleagues who are deeply committed to advancing refugee leadership, the majority of whom have lived experience of displacement. Our network of staff, researchers, students, and other affiliates is made up of 1,400+ individuals across 80+ countries. RLRH has five active offices: our first was established in Nairobi in 2020, we have had an office at the University of Oxford since 2021, and we have since developed physical hubs in Kakuma refugee camp (Kenya), Kuala Lumpur (Malaysia), Kampala (Uganda), and in the Oxfordshire community (UK).

From October 2025 RLRH is funded to serve as a technical partner for the Mastercard Foundation’s Scholars Program network, advancing an ambitious global agenda to support displacement-affected learners to access 1,000+ graduate-level scholarships at partner universities around the world. RLRH provides expert guidance and implements specialised programmes to help these learners enter university, thrive on course, and pursue meaningful and enduring careers on completion of their degrees. A complementary, refugee-led research agenda designed by RLRH colleagues produces insights to help Scholars Program partner universities and other stakeholders accelerate positive, long-lasting systems change.

## Job Description

### About the Operations and Strategy Pillar

The Operations and Strategy Pillar provides the organisational infrastructure that enables RLRH to deliver high-quality programmes and advance its mission at scale. Working across finance, operations, people, organisational systems, planning, governance, and institutional partnerships, the Pillar ensures colleagues have the support and systems required to deliver meaningful work across multiple countries, institutional contexts, and funding streams.

As a globally distributed organisation operating across the University of Oxford, the British Institute in Eastern Africa (BIEA), and a growing network of international offices, RLRH works within a complex operating environment that requires careful coordination, strong financial stewardship, and adaptable ways of working. The Operations and Strategy Pillar helps bring these different contexts together, building consistent organisational approaches while responding to local operational needs.

Beyond supporting day-to-day operations, the Pillar plays a central role in shaping how RLRH works and develops as an organisation. Through the continuous improvement of policies, systems, and ways of working that strengthen organisational effectiveness, improve organisational decision-making, support compliance, and enables the organisation to respond to new opportunities and challenges

RLRH is entering a significant period of growth, with new regional hubs, expanding programmes, and a diversifying portfolio of funding and institutional partnerships. The Operations and Strategy Pillar helps turn this ambition into reality, building the foundations for sustainable growth while ensuring RLRH remains resilient, effective , and true to its mission.

### Overview of the Role

As RLRH continues to expand globally, the Operations Manager will report to and work in close partnership with the Director of Operations and Strategy to provide operational leadership across the organisation's finance and operational support functions, ensuring systems, processes, and resources effectively enable the delivery of RLRH's programmes.

As an organisation hosted by the University of Oxford and operating through international host institutions, RLRH works within established finance and grants management structures rather than operating as an independent finance function. The Operations Manager will also work closely with the Oxford Department of International Development (ODID) finance team, Research Support, Post-Award, and other professional services across the University of Oxford, as well as colleagues within partner host institutions such as BIEA in Kenya and Ideas Academy in Malaysia. While these partnered teams provide institutional operations and financial administration oversight, this role is responsible for coordinating RLRH’s internal financial planning, operations management, grant oversight, and organisational systems, ensuring financial and operational processes effectively support programme delivery, organisational priorities, sustainable growth, and compliance with institutional and donor requirements.

The role has responsibility for providing line management to the Finance Officer and Administrative Assistant based at the University of Oxford. The postholder will oversee finance, administration, procurement, travel, contracts, and operational support activities, ensuring these services operate efficiently,and maintain compliance,

Success in the role will depend not only on strong technical and operational expertise, but also on the ability to navigate complex institutional environments, build trusted relationships, and ensure colleagues have the systems, guidance and operational support they need to deliver RLRH's programmes and mission successfully.

### Responsibilities

**Financial Systems, Analysis, and Reporting (25%)**

- Lead the preparation of regular financial reports and analyses to support organisational decision-making by providing RLRH senior leadership with clear oversight of financial performance, available resources, grant expenditure, financial risks, and opportunities.
- Coordinate the preparation, consolidation, and review of project budgets, financial forecasts, and expenditure reports across multiple funding streams.
- Maintain oversight over organisational financial commitments and advise on financial viability of new contracts and supplier agreements based on available and eligible grant balances.
- Manage cashflow forecasting and liquidity, ensuring RLRH can meet its ambitious global commitments and calling attention to fundraising risks.
- Lead the continuous development and improvement of financial systems, reporting tools, and workflows, ensuring information from host institutions and accounting systems is integrated effectively to support accurate financial management and reporting.

**Financial Controls and Expenditure Tracking (20%)**

- Provide oversight and quality assurance to the RLRH Finance Officer to ensure transaction-level tagging is accurate.
- Establish, implement, and monitor financial standards for how RLRH tracks expenses, ensuring alignment with Oxford, BIEA, and other emergent institutional compliance requirements.
- Coordinate and support internal and external audits, ensuring appropriate records, documentation, and controls are maintained.
- Build effective working relationships with host institutions to ensure compliance with responsibilities set out in collaboration agreements and financial reporting requirements.
- Work closely with the RLRH Finance Officer and Departmental Finance team to ensure month-end financial transactions, including journals and cost transfers, are completed accurately and in a timely manner, with expenditure correctly allocated to the appropriate funding streams, projects and cost centres.

**Operational Policy, Governance, and Training (15%)**

- Lead the development, implementation, and improvement of RLRH-specific financial and operational policies, SOPs, and guidance within the frameworks established by host institutions. Work with relevant institutional teams to ensure RLRH procedures complement and consistently apply wider organisational processes, while also meeting donor requirements and responding to RLRH's operational needs.
- Strengthen financial capability across RLRH by providing training and guidance on budgeting, monitoring, expenditure, and financial procedures.
- Identify and implement opportunities to improve operational processes, reduce administrative burden, and embed scalable ways of working across RLRH.

**Donor Management and Compliance (15%)**

- Lead the preparation of budgets and financial information for funding proposals, renewals, and organisational growth initiatives, working closely with senior leadership, programme teams, and host institutions.
- Maintain detailed knowledge of donor budgets and expenditure restrictions ensuring organisational spending remains compliant with approved budgets and funder requirements.
- Support the development of collaboration agreements and MOUs with host institutions and programme partners, ensuring appropriate financial and operational arrangements are in place for programme delivery.
- Act as the principal operations and finance liaison for funders working closely with the University Post-Award focal point to coordinate financial reporting, budget amendments, funder approvals, and other grant management requirements.
- Review donor financial reports prepared by the Finance Officer and lead re-budgeting exercises as per organisational priorities and donor requirements and deadlines (e.g. quarterly, bi-annually, annually).
- Provide strategic financial advice and guidance to programme teams on budgeting, expenditure, donor requirements and financial planning throughout the grant lifecycle.

**Organisational Planning and Budgeting (15%)**

- Lead the delivery of RLRH’s annual budgeting and budget revisions, working closely with the Director of Operations and Strategy, senior leadership and the MEL team.
- Develop and maintain a multi-dimensional budgeting framework that supports organisational planning, resource allocation and budget management across departments, donors, programmes, and cost categories.
- Work closely with the Department Finance Manager to coordinate the quarterly forecasting process, reviewing financial performance against budget, and updating forecasts.
- Work closely with senior leadership and programme leads to ensure organisational planning is rooted in financial reality and that data collection informs future budget allocations.

**People Management and Team Support (10%)**

- Provide day-today leadership, coaching, workload planning, and quality assurance to the Finance Officer and Administrative Assistant, fostering their professional growth and technical proficiency.
- Maintain a dotted-line relationship with the East Africa Operations Coordinator, the SEA Programme Manager, and other future hubs to ensure regional financial workflows support global RLRH standards.

### **Selection criteria**

**Essential**

- Educated to a degree-level in finance, accounting, business, economics, or a related subject, or equivalent relevant professional experience.
- Significant professional experience in finance and/or operations within the charity sector, higher education, international development, research or another complex multi-stakeholder environment.
- Experience developing, improving or overseeing financial systems, processes and reporting tools, including working with multiple financial platforms and institutional stakeholders.
- Strong analytical skills and advanced proficiency in spreadsheets and financial data analysis, with the ability to interpret and communicate complex financial information effectively.
- Expertise in complex multi-dimensional budgeting (by donor/programme) and managing the financial complexities of large-scale grants (e.g., Mastercard Foundation).
- Proven ability to set standards, audit regional teams, and develop SOPs that balance rigor with the needs of international development contexts.
- Proven experience managing donor-funded grants and ensuring compliance with funder requirements.
- Experience leading, managing, and developing finance/administrative staff in a high-growth environment.
- Experience preparing and reviewing grant budgets, supporting funding proposals, and contributing to donor financial reporting processes.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to manage up to executive leadership and liaise effectively with University administrators.
- Experience using a range of digital systems to support finance and operations, including accounting software, budgeting and reporting tools, collaboration platforms (e.g. Slack), HR, or CRM systems.
- Experience working across teams, organisations, and institutional environments and managing competing requirements and priorities.
- Demonstrated commitment to working inclusively and effectively within diverse, multicultural, and international teams.

**Desirable**

- Familiarity with University of Oxford financial procedures and higher education administration.
- Experience working in financial operations in Low and Middle Income Countries (LMIC), East Africa, and/or with fiscal sponsors like the BIEA.
- Professional accounting qualification (e.g., ACCA, CIMA) or equivalent.
- Knowledge of international development, higher education, research, migration, refugee studies, or related sectors.
- Fluency in another language spoken by RLRH learners and affiliates, for example, Arabic, Farsi, French, or Swahili.

title: Senior Core Services Caseworker
body:
**This position is represented by the OPEIU union and subject to the terms and conditions of a collective bargaining agreement.**

**This position is open to candidates with existing work authorization in the location where the position is advertised.**

**Job Overview:** The Senior Core Services Caseworker delivers trauma-informed support to refugee clients during their resettlement and post-resettlement periods, as well as to other eligible immigrant populations, including Cuban, Haitian, and Ukrainian clients. The Caseworker is responsible for promoting a positive resettlement experience and helping clients achieve self-sufficiency. This role involves close collaboration with clients, internal teams, and external partners to create individualized service and self-sufficiency plans. The Caseworker connects clients with a range of financial, medical, social, and vocational resources in alignment with program guidelines and client eligibility criteria.

**Major Responsibilities:**  
The Senior Core Services Caseworker plays a critical role in ensuring that clients successfully transition to life in their new community and achieve self-sufficiency. Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

**Client Intake, Assessment & Planning**

- Conduct comprehensive intake services to assess individual and family needs, including housing, health, education, employment, and social services.
- Develop tailored self-sufficiency plans in collaboration with clients, outlining specific goals, timelines, and action steps to achieve self-reliance.
- Identify immediate needs and prioritize services such as securing housing, enrolling in benefits, and accessing medical services.

**Pre- and Post-Arrival Coordination**

- Ensure clients receive essential services upon arrival, including temporary or permanent housing, access to nutritious food, healthcare, and transportation support.
- Coordinate with internal departments and external service providers to facilitate timely delivery of services and resources.
- Provide ongoing orientation to clients on accessing services in their new community, including healthcare systems, public benefits, financial literacy, and transportation.

**Direct Support, Advocacy & Case Management**

- Offer individualized support to clients, ensuring they receive appropriate referrals to community resources such as schools, legal services, and mental health providers.
- Advocate on behalf of clients to help them overcome barriers in accessing services and exercising their rights.
- Monitor and assess client progress regularly, addressing challenges and updating self-sufficiency plans as needed to ensure successful outcomes.
- Facilitate connection to employment services in coordination with the employment team to support clients in gaining job readiness skills and securing suitable employment.
- Assist clients in completing critical documents, including benefit renewals, address change notifications (AR-11 forms), and other legal documentation.

**Home Visits & Community Integration**

- Conduct home visits to assess living conditions, provide follow-up services, and ensure clients are safe and stable.
- Help clients build community connections by facilitating their engagement with local services, cultural events, and educational workshops.

**Financial Assistance & Budgeting**

- Plan, request, and track direct assistance funds, ensuring expenditures are aligned with program requirements and client needs.
- Assist clients with financial planning, helping them budget for rent, utilities, and other essential expenses.
- Manage Matching Grant Program client finances, ensuring compliance with program guidelines and accurate reporting of funds disbursed.

**Documentation & Reporting**

- Maintain detailed case files and documentation for each client interaction, ensuring accuracy and compliance with program standards.
- Enter data into client databases and assist with program tracking and reporting requirements.
- Prepare reports as required by internal leadership and external funders.

**Collaboration & Relationship Building**

- Collaborate with internal teams such as Employment, Health, and Youth Services to ensure seamless service delivery.
- Build and maintain relationships with external service providers, such as healthcare organizations, schools, and community groups, to expand the support network for clients.
- Participate in cross-departmental meetings and community coalitions to strengthen partnerships and identify additional resources for clients.

**Client Education & Workshops**

- Develop and facilitate educational workshops for clients on topics such as navigating healthcare, job readiness, budgeting, tenant rights, and U.S. culture.
- Encourage and support client participation in group activities that promote learning, self-advocacy, and social integration.

**Supervision & Volunteer Engagement**

- Train, supervise, and coordinate the activities of interns and volunteers, ensuring they understand program goals and the needs of clients.
- Provide ongoing feedback and support to volunteers to maximize their contribution to client success.

**Compliance, Ethical Standards & Safety**

- Ensure compliance with all organizational policies, program guidelines, and ethical standards in the delivery of services.
- Maintain confidentiality and uphold the highest professional standards in all client interactions.
- Participate in ongoing training and professional development to stay current on best practices and program regulations.

**Transportation & Logistics**

- Use a personal, insured vehicle or public transportation to transport clients and materials as needed throughout the service delivery area.
- Assist clients in learning how to use public transportation to access essential services independently.

**Other Responsibilities**

- Support special projects and initiatives that enhance client services and improve program outcomes.
- Perform other duties as assigned to meet the evolving needs of clients and the organization.

**Job Requirements:**

**Preference:** Bilingual or multilingual candidates are strongly preferred. Proficiency in additional languages relevant to the client population is a plus.

**Education:** Bachelor’s degree in social work or related field of study preferred.

**Work Experience:**

- **Required:** Minimum of 2 years of professional experience in the human services field.
- **Preferred:** Experience working with refugee and/or immigrant communities.

**Demonstrated Skills & Competencies:**

- **Relationship Building & Networking:** Proven ability to build and maintain effective internal and external relationships through strong diplomacy, communication, and collaboration skills.
- **Cross-Cultural Communication:** Demonstrated success in working and communicating in a multicultural environment.
- **Initiative & Problem-Solving:** Self-motivated with excellent problem-solving abilities, capable of managing multiple tasks, setting priorities, and meeting deadlines efficiently.
- **Detail-Oriented:** Strong attention to detail and a commitment to producing accurate, high-quality work.
- **Digital & Technical Skills:** Proficient in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Outlook) and skilled in using the internet and digital tools for data entry, research, and problem-solving.
- **Transportation:** Must have a valid driver’s license and access to a personal, insured vehicle.

**Working Environment:**

- A combination of standard office environment, remote work, and ‘field’ time within the service delivery area to perform the above outlined responsibilities.
- May require occasional weekend and/or evening work.

***This position is expected to end on January 30, 2027.***

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $24.10 - $25.37/hr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer the following benefits to short term employees in the US: 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, sick leave, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

**TERMS OF REFERENCE FOR FISCAL SPACE ANALYSIS FOR SOMALIA/SOMALILAND**
