CONCEPT NOTE  
Fiscal Space Analysis for Somalia/Somaliland (2026-2027)  
Strengthening Domestic Resource Mobilization and Sector Financing for Sustainable Development

The fiscal systems in Somalia remain structurally constrained, fragmented, and highly dependent on external financing. Despite gradual improvements in public financial management (PFM) reforms and modest gains in domestic revenue mobilization, fiscal space remains limited by narrow tax bases, weak institutional capacity, high expenditure rigidity, and persistent political economy constraints. These structural weaknesses directly affect the State’s ability to progressively realize children’s rights through adequate financing of essential services.  
At a macro-fiscal level, Somalia/land’s aggregate domestic revenue remains below 15% of GDP, significantly underperforming compared to the Sub-Saharan African average of 18–20%. This reflects a structurally weak revenue system characterized by heavy reliance on customs duties, limited inland taxation capacity, and an informal economy estimated at 60–80% of total economic activity. At subnational level, fiscal disparities are significant. Across Somalia, fiscal capacity remains constrained and uneven, with Somalia and Somaliland experiencing low and volatile own-source revenue performance. Annual revenues across FMS typically range between approximately USD 20–120 million, influenced by differences in port and trade activity, administrative capacity, economic conditions, and security dynamics. Revenue systems remain heavily dependent on a narrow range of tax and non-tax sources, while weaknesses in revenue forecasting continue to affect budget credibility, expenditure planning, and predictability of budget execution.  
Expenditure structures across all governance systems are highly rigid, with wage bills and security expenditures consuming between 50% and 75% of total recurrent spending. This has resulted in chronic underinvestment in child-focused development sectors, particularly education, health, nutrition, and child protection systems. Education spending remains at 2–6% of total public expenditure, far below international benchmarks of 15–20%, constraining access to quality learning and widening equity gaps for vulnerable children, particularly in rural and displaced populations. Health systems similarly remain predominantly donor-financed and structurally underfunded from domestic sources, limiting sustainable access to essential maternal and child health services.  
A defining feature of Somalia/land’s fiscal architecture is the high degree of aid dependency and fragmentation. A substantial portion of service delivery financing is off-budget and donor-managed, particularly in health, nutrition, education, and humanitarian response sectors. While external financing plays a critical role in sustaining essential child survival and protection services, it creates parallel systems of planning and execution that weaken fiscal coordination, reduce accountability, and limit the progressive transition toward sustainable, nationally owned financing of child rights obligations.  
Beyond technical constraints, Somalia/land’s fiscal space is shaped by complex political economy dynamics. Customs points and trade corridors remain the primary revenue generation nodes, making fiscal systems highly sensitive to political control, security conditions, and intergovernmental relations. Weak fiscal decentralization frameworks, overlapping mandates between federal and state authorities, and limited taxpayer trust further constrain revenue expansion and compliance. These structural dynamics reinforce uneven fiscal capacity across regions and limit the predictability and adequacy of financing for child-centered public services.  
In this context, fiscal space is not only a function of resource scarcity but also of institutional fragmentation, weak revenue governance, and inefficient expenditure prioritization. These constraints have direct implications for the realization of children’s rights, as fiscal limitations translate into insufficient and inequitable investment in education, health, nutrition, and social protection systems.  
A comprehensive and comparative fiscal space analysis is therefore essential to identify realistic pathways for expanding domestic resource mobilization, improving expenditure efficiency, and enhancing alignment between fiscal policy and child rights commitments across Somalia/land,  
Overall Objectives  
To assess fiscal space, domestic resource mobilization potential, and public expenditure efficiency across Somalia/land’ to translate the findings into actionable policy and advocacy pathways that strengthen sustainable domestic financing for child rights and essential social services.  
Specific Objectives.  
• Assess fiscal space and public financing trends, including revenue performance, expenditure patterns, debt and fiscal sustainability, and financing constraints.  
• Map revenue systematically (by source, collecting institution and level of government) and identify and quantify DRM opportunities through tax policy and administration reforms, non-tax revenues and other fiscal space measures.  
• Analyse intergovernmental fiscal relations, including revenue assignment, sharing and transfer arrangements between Somalia and Somaliland, and their effect on financing for child-focused services.  
• Review the share, trend and equity of public expenditure on child-sensitive sectors (education, health, nutrition and social protection), including disparities by region, gender, displacement status and disability, as the entry point for later sector-specific expenditure and fiscal space analyses.  
• Assess the alignment between public financing and child rights priorities, identify financing gaps, inequities, and barriers that limit investment in children and essential social services.  
• Map domestic and external financing flows, including on-budget and off-budget ODA, and assess their contribution to child-focused sectors and long-term sustainability.  
• Map and analyse domestic and external financing flows, including on-budget and off-budget development assistance, to determine their contribution to child-focused sectors and long-term financing sustainability.  
• Develop fiscal reform scenarios and investment cases showing how DRM and expenditure-efficiency reforms can translate into increased and predictable allocations to child-focused sectors, including through earmarking, soft ring-fencing and performance-based transfers.  
• Identify political, institutional and policy entry points for reform through stakeholder, political economy and budget process analysis.  
• Design advocacy pathways and policy engagement strategies that enable governments, parliamentarians, civil society, and development partners to advance fiscal reforms and increase sustainable domestic financing for child rights and essential social services.  
Outcomes  
• Governments and stakeholders have access to harmonized and comparative evidence based on fiscal space, domestic resource mobilization opportunities, public financing trends, and expenditure efficiency across Somalia/land.  
• Government institutions utilize fiscal space and financing evidence to inform budget planning, fiscal policy reforms, and resource allocation decisions in priority child-sensitive sectors.  
• Evidence-based fiscal reform options and financing scenarios are identified and promoted to expand domestic resource mobilization and increase fiscal space for investments in children and essential social services.  
• Civil society, development partners, parliamentarians, and government actors are equipped with actionable advocacy pathways and policy recommendations to influence fiscal and budget decisions in Favor of children.  
• Policy dialogue and reform efforts are informed by evidence on expenditure efficiency, equity, and financing gaps, contributing to more effective and equitable allocation of public resources for child rights.  
• Children benefit from increased, equitable, efficient, and sustainable public investments in education, health, nutrition, social protection  
Intended use and users.  
• The study is a macro-level, whole-of-government analysis and the necessary first step before sector-specific work. Ministries of finance and planning in each jurisdiction are their primary users, for setting realistic budget ceilings, planning revenue reforms and negotiating on-budget aid.  
• Sector ministries (education, health, social affairs) will use it to understand the size and predictability of the resource envelope available to their sectors and the reforms that could expand it, strengthening their budget submissions.  
• Parliamentarians, civil society and development partners will use it as a shared evidence base for budget advocacy. Sector-specific fiscal space and expenditure analyses can then build on its findings.  
Methodology  
The study will use mixed-methods, comparative design that combines fiscal space analysis, domestic resource mobilization (DRM) diagnostics, public expenditure analysis, climate-fiscal risk assessment, and advocacy pathway development. It will integrate quantitative fiscal analysis with qualitative stakeholder perspectives to give a comprehensive picture of the opportunities and constraints for financing children’s rights across the Somalia/Somaliland.  
The analytical framework rests on the standard fiscal space expansion model, which has five drivers: (a) economic growth, (ii) domestic revenue mobilization, (iii) expenditure reprioritization and efficiency gains, (iv) deficit financing and debt sustainability, and (v) external grants and transfers. A child-focused public finance analysis complements it to assess the adequacy, equity, efficiency, and sustainability of spending in priority social sectors.  
6.1 Inception and Analytical Framework  
During inception, the consultant will refine the analytical framework, theory of change, stakeholder mapping, data collection tools, and validation process. The study will be guided by internationally recognized fiscal space and public finance approaches:  
• Fiscal Space Frameworks for Children- including UNICEF’S Framework  
• IMF Fiscal Space Assessment Approaches  
• Public Expenditure and Financial Accountability (PEFA) principles  
• Public Expenditure Reviews (PERs)  
• Domestic Resource Mobilization Assessment Frameworks  
• Child-responsive Budgeting and Public Finance for Children methodologies  
6.2 Desk Review and Secondary Data Analysis  
The study will begin with a comprehensive desk review of fiscal, economic, and sectoral documentation to establish the fiscal, institutional, and policy context. Sources will include, but are not limited to:  
• national and subnational budgets and budget execution reports  
• Public Financial Management (PFM) assessments  
• revenue and tax administration reports and revenue performance data  
• IMF Article IV consultations and World Bank Public Expenditure Reviews  
• National Development Plans and sector financing strategies  
• existing public expenditure and child rights financing studies  
The review will identify historical financing trends, policy reforms, expenditure patterns, institutional bottlenecks, and evidence gaps that require primary data collection.  
6.3 Harmonized Fiscal and Financing Database  
FGS, the FMS, and Somaliland use different fiscal and reporting cycles. A data normalization exercise will therefore harmonize them into a single fiscal and financing database. This will allow consistent cross-jurisdictional comparison of revenues, expenditures, fiscal balances, and external financing flows. Quantitative analysis will assess trends in DRM, expenditure allocation, fiscal sustainability, and sector financing efficiency, with a focus on opportunities to expand fiscal space for child-focused investment.  
6.4 Key Informant Interviews (KIIs) and Stakeholder Consultations  
Semi-structured KIIs will complement the desk review. They will be held with Ministries of Finance, Ministries of Planning, revenue authorities, sector ministries, development partners, and civil society organizations across all study jurisdictions. They will gather perspectives on fiscal constraints, resource mobilization opportunities, expenditure prioritization, and the political feasibility of reforms.  
6.5 Domestic Resource Mobilization (DRM) Diagnostic  
The study will conduct a systematic DRM diagnostic comprising revenue mapping and a revenue potential assessment. it will also examine shadow economy and informal sector contributions to estimate unrealized fiscal potential.  
6.6 Public Expenditure and Child Financing Analysis  
The consultant will undertake a child-sensitive public finance analysis covering both the volume and the equity of public spending in the key social sectors (education, health, nutrition, social protection, and child protection). The analysis will cover:  
• Spending levels  
• Spending trends over the last 5–10 years  
• Spending composition  
• Equity of expenditure patterns  
Results will be benchmarked against international standards and comparable fragile-state contexts where feasible. The analysis will identify financing gaps, allocation bottlenecks, and opportunities to improve resource prioritization for children. It will also develop human capital return-on-investment (ROI) scenarios to show the economic returns of investing in child-sensitive sectors.  
6.7 Intergovernmental Fiscal Relations Analysis  
• Given Somalia’s federal dynamics, the consultant will conduct a dedicated assessment of intergovernmental fiscal relations, including revenue sharing, transfers, and expenditure responsibilities between FGS and the FMS.  
6.8 Scenario Modelling and Fiscal Reform Options  
• Drawing on the combined fiscal and institutional analysis, the study will develop evidence-based financing scenarios. These will estimate the fiscal gains achievable under different reform pathways and set out DRM options aimed at increasing sustainable public financing for children. The scenarios will feed into sector-specific investment cases that set out the financing gap, the cost of the proposed interventions, the expected returns, and the priority reforms for each key social sector.  
6.9 Climate-Fiscal Risk Assessment  
Given Somalia’s recurrent droughts, floods, and climate shocks, the study will examine how climate-related risks affect:  
• revenue generation  
• expenditure pressures  
• humanitarian financing needs  
• social sector budget  
• It will also explore opportunities to integrate resilience and climate-sensitive financing into fiscal planning.  
6.10 Political Economy and Feasibility Analysis  
The study will not conduct a standalone Political Economy Analysis. It will integrate political economy considerations throughout by drawing on existing Save the Children PEAs, other recent and relevant PEA findings where needed, recent governance studies, and stakeholder consultations. These inputs will inform the identification of realistic fiscal reform entry points, stakeholder incentives, and feasible advocacy pathways. This ensures that recommendations are technically sound and politically feasible in Somalia’s context.  
6.11 Validation and Quality Assurance  
Findings will be validated through technical review workshops, stakeholder validation meetings, peer review by fiscal and PFM experts, and triangulation of quantitative and qualitative evidence. Validation workshops will be held in Mogadishu, Garowe, and Hargeisa to ensure accuracy, policy relevance, ownership, and contextual fit.  
6.12 Advocacy Pathway Development  
Based on the findings, the study will develop practical advocacy pathways targeting all key stakeholders, including but not limited to Ministries of Finance, Parliamentarians, Development Partners, Civil Society Organizations, and Sector Ministries.  
6.13 Expected Outputs/Deliverables  
• Inception Report  
• Harmonized Fiscal and Financing Database  
• Comparative Fiscal Space Analysis Report  
• DRM for Child Rights Analysis Report  
• Three Child Rights Public Expenditure Analysis Reports on Federal, Somaliland and Puntland  
• Financing Gap and Scenario Modelling Report, including sector investment cases covering Federal, Somaliland and Puntland  
• Policy Briefs (3–5)  
• Advocacy and Policy Influence Toolkit  
• Stakeholder Validation Workshop Report  
• Final Consolidated Report, integrating the fiscal space analysis, DRM findings, child rights financing assessment, and advocacy pathways.

Scope of the Study  
• Coverage: national fiscal systems and subnational implementation realities, focusing on ministries of finance, planning institutions, revenue authorities, and key sector ministries.  
• Period: approximately 5–10 years of fiscal data, depending on availability.  
• Financing flows: The study will assess domestic and external financing, on-budget and off-budget, to give a comprehensive picture of total public financing for child-focused services. It will also identify key gaps in fiscal transparency, alignment, and sustainability. Sectors: education, health, nutrition, social protection, and child protection.  
• Institutions: The study will focus on public financial systems at the federal and regional levels, including ministries of finance, planning institutions, revenue authorities, and key sector ministries. It will also examine the flow of resources to the priority child-sensitive sectors of education, health, nutrition, and social protection.  
• Geographically, the study will be conducted in key administrative and fiscal hubs, including Somalia/Somaliland (Mogadishu), Hargeisa (Somaliland), Garowe (Puntland). These locations are selected due to their central role in budget formulation, revenue administration, and public financial management decision-making processes.  
• Excluded: a standalone political economy analysis. The consultant will draw on existing Save the Children PEAs and other recent studies

Stakeholders  
The study will engage key stakeholders in line with its objectives on fiscal space analysis, domestic resource mobilization (DRM), child rights financing, and advocacy pathway development of Somalia/land.  
• Government Institutions- Ministries of Finance, Planning, and Economic Development will be central to the study, particularly in relation to assessing fiscal space, identifying domestic resource mobilization opportunities, and informing fiscal reform scenarios. Sector ministries (Education, Health, and social affairs will be engaged to support analysis of public expenditure adequacy, efficiency, and alignment with child rights priorities.

• Revenue authorities and tax administrations will contribute to the assessment of domestic revenue performance and identification of revenue enhancement opportunities under the DRM objectives.

• Legislative Institutions- Parliamentary budget and finance committees will be engaged to support understanding of budget approval processes and to identify entry points for influencing fiscal allocations toward child-focused sectors. Their role will be central in translating fiscal evidence into budget advocacy and reform actions.

• Development Partners will be engaged to support analysis of external financing flows, alignment with domestic fiscal systems, and identification of opportunities to improve financing efficiency and sustainability. Their engagement will also support validation of findings and alignment with ongoing fiscal and sector reforms.

• Civil Society and Advocacy Actors- including child rights and budget advocacy groups, will be key stakeholders in validating findings on child-focused expenditure and in translating evidence into advocacy actions. They will play a central role in advancing the study’s objective on developing advocacy pathways for increased domestic financing for children.

• Research and Technical Institutions-Local research institutions and technical experts will support data validation, methodological review, and contextual interpretation of fiscal, sectoral, and financing data to strengthen the credibility and robustness of findings.

• Indirect Beneficiaries- Children and vulnerable populations are the ultimate beneficiaries of the study. Although not directly engaged in primary data collection, their needs and outcomes will be reflected through secondary data analysis and sector financing assessments, particularly in relation to education, health, nutrition, social protection, and child protection services.  
Data Sources  
• The study will rely on a combination of primary and secondary data sources to ensure comprehensive and comparable fiscal and financing analysis of the Somalia/land.

• Primary data will be collected through key informant interviews and consultations with Ministries of Finance, Planning and Economic Development, sector ministries, revenue authorities, and relevant parliamentary committees. Additional insights will be obtained from development partners, civil society organizations, and technical experts involved in public financial management and child rights financing.

• Secondary data will include national budget documents, budget execution reports, medium-term fiscal frameworks, public expenditure reviews, revenue performance reports, and audit reports where available. The study will also utilize macroeconomic datasets, sector financing reports, and publicly available donor aid data, including on-budget and off-budget external financing flows.

• Where possible, the study will draw on existing databases and statistical sources from government institutions and international financial datasets to support trend analysis and cross-country comparability

Duration and Timeline of the Assignment  
Duration  
The assignment will be completed within three months  
Data Sources  
• The study will combine primary and secondary data to ensure a comprehensive and comparable fiscal and financing analysis of Somalia and Somaliland.  
• Primary data will come from key informant interviews and consultations with Ministries of Finance, Planning and Economic Development, sector ministries, revenue authorities, and relevant parliamentary committees. Further insights will come from development partners, civil society organizations, and technical experts in public financial management and child rights financing.  
• Secondary data will include national budget documents, budget execution reports, medium-term fiscal frameworks, public expenditure reviews, revenue performance reports, and audit reports where available. It will also include macroeconomic datasets, sector financing reports, and publicly available donor aid data, covering on-budget and off-budget external financing flows.  
• Where possible, the study will draw on existing government databases and international financial datasets to support trend analysis and cross-country comparability.  
4\. Tasks, Activities, and Timeline  
The assignment will be 3 months.  
Phase 1: Inception and Design.  
• Inception meetings and detailed desk review  
• Finalization of the methodology and data collection tools  
• Development of the analytical framework and stakeholder mapping  
Phase 2: Data Collection and Harmonization.  
• Collect fiscal, revenue, and expenditure data from Ministries of Finance, Planning, and revenue authorities in Mogadishu, Hargeisa, and Garowe  
• Conduct KIIs with government, donors, and sector actors.  
• Compile domestic revenue and external financing datasets.  
• Harmonize fiscal data across regions and develop the integrated fiscal and financing database.  
• Conduct an overview-level child-sensitive public finance analysis of trends in the share and equity of spending on education, health, nutrition, and social protection, across geography, gender, displacement, and disability. This will be the basis for the later sector-specific analyses.  
• Conduct data quality review and validation checks.  
Phase 3: Analysis and Drafting.  
• Fiscal space analysis, DRM assessment, and child-focused public expenditure analysis  
• Scenario modelling and sector investment cases  
• Development of policy and advocacy outputs  
Phase 4: Validation and Finalization.  
• Validation workshops and consultations in Hargeisa, Garowe, and Mogadishu, covering Somalia/Somaliland.  
• Incorporation of feedback from government, development partners, and civil society  
• Finalization of the DRM analysis, the child rights financing assessment, and all research products  
The consultancy will also produce all final knowledge products: the comparative fiscal space report, the DRM analysis, the child rights financing assessment, factsheets on the research findings, PowerPoint presentations of the findings, policy briefs, and advocacy materials ready for dissemination and policy engagement.  
Consultant Qualifications and Experience.  
Education  
• Master’s degree in economics, public finance, development economics, public policy, or a related field. A PhD is an advantage.  
Professional experience  
• At least 10 years of experience in fiscal analysis, public financial management (PFM), or public finance research, including fiscal space analysis and domestic resource mobilization (DRM).  
• Proven experience conducting public expenditure analysis or public expenditure reviews, ideally in education, health, nutrition, or social protection.  
• Demonstrated experience with child-responsive budgeting or public finance for children, preferably using the UNICEF Fiscal Space for Children framework.  
• Experience in fiscal scenario modelling, including financing gap analysis and return-on-investment or investment case development.  
• Experience building and harmonizing fiscal datasets from sources with different reporting cycles.  
• Experience in fragile, conflict-affected, or federal contexts, preferably in Somalia/Somaliland. Familiarity with the fiscal systems of the Somalia/Somaliland is a strong advantage.  
• Experience engaging ministries of finance, planning institutions, revenue authorities, and parliamentary committees, and conducting KIIs and validation workshops with them.  
• Experience developing policy briefs and advocacy materials for government and development partner audiences.  
• At least 3 comparable studies completed in the last 5-7 years, with references or samples.

title: Senior Youth Program Specialist
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

***This position has an end date of August 31, 2027.***

**IRC Background:** IRC opened an office in Spokane in 2022 and provides a continuum of services including intensive case management, employment and economic empowerment services, immigration assistance, health and wellness programming, and education support to refugee and immigrant families in Washington State. IRC Spokane is committed to providing trauma-informed, equitable, and accessible services and maintaining and evolving a diverse, inclusive, and supportive workplace.

**Job Overview:** The vision of the IRC Washington Youth Program is that youth from refugee and immigrant backgrounds will have the skills and resources necessary to pursue a future of opportunity. The Youth and Education Program works towards this vision by providing educational and enrichment opportunities to help school-aged youth from refugee and immigrant backgrounds catch up on missed education, adjust to a new school, accelerate English language development, and build positive relationships in the school and community. This program supports school-age youth and their families, and also provides support to teachers and school administration to better connect and serve these students.

The Sr. Youth Program Specialist is responsible for teaching and implementation of IRC’s Youth and Education Programs in Spokane, WA.

The Virtual Ready to Read (VR2R) program promotes enjoyment of reading, literacy skills, language acquisition, social and emotional asset development, and positive cultural identity for students in grades 3–8. Upon enrollment, students receive a device, a learning kit with craft materials and art supplies, a workbook, and a set of books. Parents and students attend an orientation to ensure they know how to use their device and the video call platform. Each student attends one-hour online classes twice a week from January through May. Students read a book as a group and engage in themed lessons with vocabulary and grammar content, discussion questions, and activities. Students also take part in virtual field trips to institutions such as the Pacific Science Center, Woodland Park Zoo, and Seattle Aquarium. Two consecutive 1-hour classes are led by an IRC teacher on Tuesdays and Thursdays from 4:00 pm – 6:00 pm (a slightly later start at 4:15 pm can be accommodated if your schedule does not allow an earlier start). The program runs from January to May. Classes are small with typically under 15 students in attendance for each class.

The Individualized Tutoring Program matches K-12 students and families with an IRC-screened, trained, and supervised tutor who supports English language acquisition, literacy and fluency, math skills, general homework, and social-emotional learning. Tutors meet with students in their homes once a week after school for 1–2 hours over a period of 3–6 months. Tutoring is one of IRC’s long-standing programs, and IRC is committed to providing high-quality tutoring in alignment with the standards of Stanford University’s National Student Success Accelerator. Tutoring appointments are typically scheduled on weekdays between 4:00 pm – 7:00 pm or weekends.

**Major Responsibilities:**

**Virtual Reading Program**

title: Senior Youth Program Specialist

Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

***This position has an end date of August 31, 2027.***

**IRC Background:** IRC opened an office in Spokane in 2022 and provides a continuum of services including intensive case management, employment and economic empowerment services, immigration assistance, health and wellness programming, and education support to refugee and immigrant families in Washington State. IRC Spokane is committed to providing trauma-informed, equitable, and accessible services and maintaining and evolving a diverse, inclusive, and supportive workplace.

**Job Overview:** The vision of the IRC Washington Youth Program is that youth from refugee and immigrant backgrounds will have the skills and resources necessary to pursue a future of opportunity. The Youth and Education Program works towards this vision by providing educational and enrichment opportunities to help school-aged youth from refugee and immigrant backgrounds catch up on missed education, adjust to a new school, accelerate English language development, and build positive relationships in the school and community. This program supports school-age youth and their families, and also provides support to teachers and school administration to better connect and serve these students.

The Sr. Youth Program Specialist is responsible for teaching and implementation of IRC’s Youth and Education Programs in Spokane, WA.

The Virtual Ready to Read (VR2R) program promotes enjoyment of reading, literacy skills, language acquisition, social and emotional asset development, and positive cultural identity for students in grades 3–8. Parents and students attend an orientation to ensure they know how to use their device and the video call platform. Each student attends one-hour online classes twice a week from January through May. title: Haiti-Based Sectoral and Technical Experts and Trainers
body:
**Position:** Sectoral Technical Experts / Trainers - Haiti  
**Type:** Consultancy / Project-based / Roster  
**Location:** Haiti  
**Organization:** STOOS Consulting

**STOOS Consulting** is inviting qualified **sectoral technical experts, trainers, facilitators, researchers, and consultants in Haiti** to join its roster for upcoming humanitarian, development, research, assessment, capacity building, monitoring, evaluation, and third-party monitoring opportunities across the country.

This call is open to experienced professionals from different technical backgrounds who are interested in supporting future assignments with **UN agencies, INGOs, NGOs, donors, development partners, local organizations, and community-based actors**.

**About STOOS Consulting**

**STOOS Consulting** is an international consulting firm specialized in **Third-Party Monitoring, MEAL, research and assessments, evaluations, data collection, capacity building, conflict and gender analysis, market systems research, and economic empowerment studies**. STOOS works in complex humanitarian and development contexts to produce practical, field-based, and evidence-driven findings that support programme quality, accountability, learning, and decision-making.

Through its network of national and international experts, STOOS supports assignments in areas such as **needs assessments, baseline and endline studies, final evaluations, outcome monitoring, technical training, capacity building, qualitative and quantitative research, community consultations, and field monitoring**.

**Profile of Experts Sought**

STOOS is looking to expand its Haiti roster with qualified experts and trainers in a wide range of sectors, including but not limited to **WASH, health, nutrition, protection, GBV, child protection, education, food security and livelihoods, climate resilience, disaster risk reduction, shelter, social protection, TVET, economic empowerment, migration, gender, disability inclusion, peacebuilding, conflict sensitivity, and MEAL**.

STOOS also welcomes applications from experts with experience in **research design, qualitative and quantitative data collection, training facilitation, curriculum development, institutional capacity building, market assessments, youth employment, entrepreneurship, community engagement, safeguarding, accountability to affected populations, and humanitarian/development programme quality**.

**Main Areas of Work**

Selected experts may be contacted for future assignments involving **technical training, capacity building, sectoral assessments, programme evaluations, field research, tool development, data collection supervision, contextual analysis, report writing, quality assurance, and technical advisory support**.

Depending on the opportunity, experts may support **KIIs, FGDs, surveys, community consultations, workshops, technical reviews, training delivery, data analysis, and preparation of practical recommendations** tailored to the Haiti context.

**Haiti Context and Relevant Experience**

Candidates with strong knowledge of Haiti's humanitarian and development context are encouraged to apply, especially those with experience related to **humanitarian response, disaster preparedness and response, earthquakes, hurricanes, flooding, climate resilience, displacement, protection risks, public health, nutrition, WASH, education, food security and livelihoods, social protection, gender equality, disability inclusion, migration, and community resilience**.

Experience working with communities in **urban, rural, coastal, earthquake-affected, hurricane-affected, displacement-affected, insecurity-affected, or hard-to-reach areas** is highly valued. STOOS particularly welcomes experts who can work respectfully with **women, youth, children, persons with disabilities, internally displaced people, migrants, returnees, farmers, fisherfolk, low-income households, and other vulnerable groups**.

**Key Skills and Qualifications**

Candidates should have relevant professional experience in one or more technical sectors and a strong understanding of the **Haiti context**, including local institutions, community structures, civil society actors, access and security dynamics, disaster risk management systems, and humanitarian/development priorities.

Applicants are encouraged to apply if they have worked with **UN agencies, INGOs, NGOs, local organizations, government partners, donor-funded programmes, academic institutions, consulting firms, or community-based initiatives**.

Strong candidates will demonstrate practical experience in **training, facilitation, technical advisory work, assessments, monitoring and evaluation, field research, community engagement, or programme implementation**.

Knowledge of **Do No Harm, safeguarding, PSEA, child protection, gender sensitivity, disability inclusion, ethical research, confidentiality, conflict sensitivity, and accountability to affected populations** is highly desirable.

Experience using digital tools such as **KoboToolbox, ODK, SurveyCTO, Excel, SPSS, Power BI, NVivo, or similar platforms** is considered an asset, depending on the assignment.

**Language Skills**

Fluency in **Haitian Creole** is required for most field-based and community-level assignments.

Good working knowledge of **French** is strongly preferred, especially for assignments involving technical reports, donor documentation, training materials, data analysis, and communication with international teams.

Knowledge of **English and/or Spanish** is a strong advantage, particularly for assignments requiring communication with regional or international stakeholders.

title: Research Manager
source: Agency for Technical Cooperation and Development
body:
## **BACKGROUND ON REACH**

REACH is an initiative of Acted whose purpose is to promote and facilitate the development of information products that enhance the humanitarian community’s decision making and planning capacity for emergency, reconstruction and development contexts. REACH facilitates information management for aid actors through three complementary services: (a) need and situation assessments facilitated by REACH teams; (b) situation analysis using satellite imagery; (c) provision of related database and (web)-mapping facilities and expertise.

**We are currently looking for a Research Manager to lead our research team in Somalia, based in Mogadishu.**

**Department**: REACH

**Position**: Research Manager

**Contract duration**: 1 year, with possibility of extension

**Location**: Mogadishu, Somalia

**Starting Date**: 1 January 2027.

## **Country profile**

Somalia remains within a complex and protracted crisis due to active conflict, the presence of non-state armed actors, the persistent presence of communicable diseases and climate-driven onset shocks – including droughts and flooding. Conflict and natural disasters continue to drive displacement and constrain the availability of resources, while the presence of armed groups severely impedes the level of access and support provided by humanitarian actors. The combination of restricted access to resources, drought, and flooding further exacerbates the possibility for outbreaks of communicable diseases like measles, cholera, and acute watery diarrhea.

Against this backdrop, REACH has developed a wide range of research cycles to provide an evidence base for the humanitarian community in Somalia. Data collected and disseminated by REACH aims to directly inform humanitarian response planning, as well as highlight areas of highest need and concern as crises emerge. Key areas of focus include:

**Multi-Sector Needs Assessment (MSNA):** REACH conducts the annual MSNA, whose findings feed into the Joint Intersectoral Analysis Framework (JIAF) workshop and, through it, the annual Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan (HNRP).

**Food Security and Nutrition:** REACH conducts food security and nutrition assessments that feed into Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) Acute Food Insecurity and Acute Malnutrition analyses.

**Cash and Markets:** REACH provides research and analytical support to the Somali Cash Consortium and conducts market monitoring analysis as part of a harmonised approach, led by the Cash Working Group.

**Ad-hoc Research:** REACH conducts ad-hoc assessments as needs arise, including rapid needs assessments following sudden-onset shocks such as flooding, drought and conflict-induced displacement.

To ensure that research findings meaningfully inform humanitarian response planning, REACH shares data through formal coordination platforms, including the Inter-Cluster Coordination Group (ICCG), needs analysis and planning processes, the IPC Technical Working Group and the Cash Working Group, among others. Partner feedback is actively integrated to validate and triangulate findings, as well as to guide research design and geographic targeting.

## **FUNCTIONS**

REACH is seeking an experienced candidate who has previously managed teams and implemented projects in a complex humanitarian setting. Under the line management of the Deputy Country Representative, and in close coordination with the Country Representative and HQ, the Research Manager will be responsible for overseeing the implementation, development, and strategy of the research portfolio of the REACH Somalia mission. This includes managing the teams responsible for the MSNA, food security and nutrition assessments, the Somali Cash Consortium, market monitoring, and ad-hoc assessments such as rapid needs assessments.

The candidate should be comfortable representing REACH with donors and be able to coordinate and liaise with a range of senior external partners, including OCHA, cluster coordinators, UN agencies and NGOs. This position requires a profile that can be both analytical and managerial, as the Research Manager’s job can range from coordinating with external partners (whether data actor, humanitarian cluster, or donor) to analytical oversight of research products.

## **RESPONSIBILITIES**

The Research Manager’s responsibilities include the following:

***STAFF MANAGEMENT***

- Direct management of international and national research staff across the MSNA, food security and nutrition, cash and markets, and ad-hoc assessment workstreams, including recruitment, appraisals, and capacity building;
- Day-to-day management of the research team, including the development of work plans and performance indicators, and development and implementation of capacity training plans to improve efficiency and performance;
- Conduct regular check-ins with staff within the unit, and promote team building, productivity and staff welfare as the main pastoral focal point for research staff;
- Provide regular support and technical backstopping;
- Take on additional work streams and management responsibilities as well as advise in strategic mission decision-making as a member of the Senior Management Team (SMT), as required.

***RESEARCH CYCLE MANAGEMENT***

- Ensure that all research cycles are planned in line with the country strategy, relevant project and programme objectives, and REACH’s research cycle guidelines;
- Ensure that all (Senior) Research Officers are comprehensively briefed on objectives and expected outputs of research cycles, and that the overall implementation strategy of any given activity is clearly understood;
- Ensure that required secondary data review and/or analysis has been conducted in preparation for an assessment;
- For each research cycle, review ToRs before they are sent to HQ for validation and ensure that ToRs are validated before data collection begins;
- Ensure relevant stakeholders and partners are engaged in assessment design and planning, data collection, and management;
- Monitor data collection, ensuring correct implementation in line with agreed ToRs, and keep track of progress and delays of all assessments throughout the research cycle;
- Work closely with the Field Manager and Ops teams to ensure logistics, finance, administration, security and HR processes directly related to REACH are appropriately implemented, alongside the relevant Acted departments.

***PORTFOLIO OVERSIGHT***

- Oversee the timely delivery of the annual MSNA, ensuring that findings are available in time to feed into the JIAF workshop and the HNRP, and support the team in preparing for and participating in the JIAF process;
- Oversee food security and nutrition assessments, ensuring that methodologies, timelines and outputs are aligned with IPC requirements and that data is made available to IPC analyses as planned;
- Oversee REACH’s research support to the Somali Cash Consortium, ensuring that deliverables meet consortium and donor requirements and timelines;
- Oversee market monitoring analysis, ensuring consistent, timely outputs that are used by Cash Working Group partners;
- Lead the planning and rapid deployment of ad-hoc assessments, such as rapid needs assessments, in response to emerging crises and partner information needs, in coordination with OCHA and the clusters.

***ANALYSIS AND DISSEMINATION MANAGEMENT***

- Ensure research staff maintain regular communication with HQ on progress and deadlines for written products;
- Ensure the drafting of timely and accurate outputs (i.e. reports, factsheets, briefs, presentations, etc.), complying with REACH’s guidelines and quality standards;
- Review all research products before they are sent to HQ for validation and ensure that all written products are validated by HQ before external release;
- Under supervision of HQ, ensure that research products are uploaded to relevant data portals, as specified in research ToRs;
- Under the direction of the Country Representative and Deputy Country Representative, engage in the dissemination of research products, including emails, presentations to coordination bodies, and bilateral meetings, such as with donors;
- Support the Country Representative and Deputy Country Representative in conducting monitoring and evaluation as specified in the research ToRs and in line with REACH guidelines.

***STRATEGY DEVELOPMENT AND IMPLEMENTATION***

- With the Country Representative and Deputy Country Representative, identify information gaps in line with humanitarian priorities in Somalia, and identify advocacy and dissemination strategies to strengthen the impact of REACH’s work;
- Lead on formalising synergies with other assessment and knowledge management actors, as well as strategic partnerships with key humanitarian stakeholders and decision makers;
- As a member of the Senior Management Team (SMT), contribute to the development and implementation of the REACH Somalia country strategy.

***EXTERNAL ENGAGEMENT***

- Represent REACH at the Inter-Cluster Coordination Group (ICCG) and in other inter-agency coordination forums, and act as a key REACH focal point for OCHA on needs analysis and humanitarian programme cycle processes;
- Represent REACH in cluster and multi-sector meetings and technical working groups, including the IPC Technical Working Group and the Cash Working Group, and follow up on technical issues identified in these forums;
- In coordination with the Country Representative and Deputy Country Representative, present research findings to relevant partners to enhance their use and impact;
- Ensure that external communications with partners and key stakeholders, including UN agencies, local and national authorities, and NGOs, are conducted and documented as appropriate;
- Support the Country Representative and Deputy Country Representative in external engagement on REACH strategy and, when requested, in fundraising and grants management.

***DATA CONFIDENTIALITY AND PROTECTION***

- The Research Manager will maintain the strictest confidentiality on all data collected and related processes, ensuring full compliance with REACH’s data protection policy and SOPs, and will ensure that the research team does the same. They will actively take measures to prevent the unauthorized sharing of any information and data belonging to REACH and its partners or collected during their assignment with REACH.

The Research Manager is also responsible for ensuring that all interactions with crisis-affected populations are conducted in a respectful and consultative manner, and that communities are adequately consulted and informed about REACH programme objectives, activities and methodologies.

## **REQUIREMEnTS**

- **Academic qualifications** Excellent academic qualifications, including a Master’s degree in a relevant discipline (e.g. international relations, development, humanitarian response, data science, political science, statistics, social research, or similar).
- **Years of work experience** At least 3-5 years of relevant working experience in a humanitarian setting, such as assessments, monitoring and evaluation, research design and analysis.
- **Management experience** Previous experience in a management role in an INGO at field level. Track record in successful management of international and national teams in humanitarian contexts.
- **Research skills** Strong quantitative and qualitative research experience, including sampling, methodology design and analysis. Ability to provide technical oversight of research products to a high standard.
- **Familiarity with the humanitarian and aid system** Good understanding of the aid system and the research community. Experience with the humanitarian programme cycle (HNRP/JIAF) and with humanitarian coordination forums (e.g. ICCG, clusters) is strongly preferred.
- **Thematic experience** Prior experience with MSNA-type research, food security and nutrition assessments and/or IPC processes, and cash and markets research is highly desirable.
- **Communication/reporting skills** Excellent communication and drafting skills for effective reporting, including proven experience in contributing to high-level presentations and briefings to senior external audiences.
- **Software skills** Proven knowledge of the Microsoft Office Suite, including Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. Skills in R, SPSS and/or STATA or other statistical analysis software are an advantage.
- **Multi-tasking skills** Ability to manage multiple research cycles in parallel with tight deadlines in a complex environment.
- **Level of independence** A self-starter with a proven ability to work independently.
- **Cross-cultural work environment** Ability to operate in a cross-cultural environment.
- **Experience in geographical region** Past experience in the Horn of Africa region is desirable, or in any other emergency context where access is challenging.
- **Language skills** Fluency in English required, competency in Somali an asset.
- **Security environment** Openness to working in a high-risk security zone required. Ability to operate in a complex and challenging security environment. Ability to prioritize self-care and well-being.

## **COMPENSATION & BENEFITS**

- For this position, salary between 3’660 **CHF** and 3’720 **CHF** monthly (before income tax), as well as a monthly living allowance of 300 **USD**
- NB - REACH salaries are strictly determined by our salary grid depending on the grade of the position and the level of education of staff. A location-dependent security and/or isolation adjustment is then applied as a recognition that some staff are required to work in difficult places where living and working conditions are much more difficult than elsewhere.
- Accommodation and food provided in a guesthouse. REACH is hosted by Acted in Somalia.
- Enrolment in Swiss private pension fund (Swisslife – approx. 9.975% of staff gross salary), health insurance, life insurance and repatriation assistance
- Flight tickets every 6 months & visa fees covered (in-country travel costs and professional expenses are fully covered)
- R&R after 2-3 months (flight ticket up to 500$ + 200$ of living allowance)
- Contribution to the luggage transportation: between 20 and 100 kgs, depending on the length of the contract (+ luggage and personal property insurance)
- Annual leave of 36 days per year. Public holidays of the country of assignment. Family/compassionate leave when applicable.
- Predeparture induction - 3 days at HQ in Geneva + one week pre-departure training in Acted HQ in Paris, including a 4-day in situ security training
- Enrolment in the Research Foundational Learning Programme within the first 3 months from the start of contract.
- REACH prioritizes the psychological safety of its staff and the health insurance provided covers, among others, up to 1000 € per year of psychosocial counselling fees

title: Senior Research Officer
source: Agency for Technical Cooperation and Development
body:
## **BACKGROUND ON IMPACT AND REACH**

REACH was born in 2010 as a joint initiative of two International NGOs ([IMPACT Initiatives](http://www.impact-initiatives.org/) and [ACTED](http://www.acted.org/)) and the United Nations Operational Satellite Applications Programme ([UNOSAT](http://www.unitar.org/unosat/)). REACH’s **purpose** is to promote and facilitate the development of information products that enhance the humanitarian community’s decision making and planning capacity for emergency, reconstruction and development contexts. REACH facilitates information management for aid actors through three complementary services: (a) need and situation assessments facilitated by REACH teams; (b) situation analysis using satellite imagery; (c) provision of related database and (web)-mapping facilities and expertise.

IMPACT Initiatives is a humanitarian NGO, based in Geneva, Switzerland. The organisation manages several initiatives, including the REACH Initiative. The IMPACT team comprises specialists in data collection, management and analysis and GIS. IMPACT was launched at the initiative of ACTED, an international NGO whose headquarter is based in Paris and is present in thirty countries. The two organizations have a strong complementarity formalized in a global partnership, enabling IMPACT to benefit from ACTED’s operational support on its fields of intervention.

**We are currently looking for a Senior Research Officer to support our team in Somalia.**

**Department**:REACH

**Position**:Senior Research Officer

**Contract duration**:4 months, with high likelihood of extension

**Location**: Mogadishu

**Starting Date**: 7 September 2026

## **COUNTRY PROFILE**

Somalia remains within a complex and protracted crisis due to active conflict, the presence of non-state armed actors, the persistent presence of communicable diseases and climate-driven onset shocks – including droughts and flooding. Conflict and natural disasters continue to drive displacement and constrain the availability of resources, while the presence of armed groups severely impedes the level of access and support provided by humanitarian actors. The combination of restricted access to resources, drought, and flooding further exacerbates the possibility for outbreaks of communicable diseases like measles, cholera, and acute watery diarrhea (AWD).

Against this backdrop, IMPACT Initiatives has developed a wide range of research cycles to provide an evidence-base for the humanitarian community. This includes the Multi-Sectoral Needs Assessment (MSNA), the Area-Based Analysis Platform aimed at supporting Area-Based Coordination, support to the Somali Cash Consortium, among others.

## **FUNCTIONS**

Under the line management of the Research Manager, the Senior Research Officer is responsible for the implementation of IMPACT’s MSNA research cycle in Somalia, including the preparation, data collection, analysis, drafting, dissemination, and evaluation stages. Throughout the MSNA, the Senior Research Officer engages with partners and stakeholders to promote their participation and maximize their impact. They also ensure an efficient and transparent use of resources required for project implementation.

This position requires strong research skills (particularly in quantitative and mixed methodology sampling), willingness to work in hardship location, an analytical mind, creativity, independence, and an interest in the national and regional context. Candidates should have strong writing and presentation skills and be able to clearly think through and articulate implications of research findings, as well as engage with external stakeholders in the design and dissemination of the research cycle. The position will regularly require interpreting data, highlighting relevant findings, writing engaging briefs and factsheets, presenting findings to external audiences with varying amounts of data literacy, and guiding colleagues in how to think more analytically about their own research.

BACKGROUND OF MULTI SECTORAL NEEDS ASSESSMENT

IMPACT HQ in Geneva support the work of Multi-Sector Needs Assessments (MSNAs) in more than 20 countries. As a result of the World Humanitarian Summit and the Grand Bargain, a commitment was made to “impartial, unbiased, comprehensive, context sensitive, timely and up to date” joint needs assessments that can serve as “a sound evidence base for humanitarian response plans”. These exercises have been informing consolidated humanitarian appeals since 2016. Since 2016, the number of MSNAs supported by REACH has more than quadrupled; MSNA data continues to influence flagship humanitarian response processes such as Humanitarian Needs and Response Plans (HNRPs). This indicates that evidence-based decision making is increasingly becoming a cornerstone of effective humanitarian action.

## **RESPONSIBILITIES**

The Senior Research Officer is responsibilities include:

***Research CYCLE MANAGEMENT***

- Anticipate knowledge gaps prior to the execution of a Research Cycle through strong understanding of the Somali context.
- Ensure that required secondary data review and/or analysis has been conducted in preparation of an assessment.
- Ensure that all research cycles are planned in line with the country strategy, relevant research and project objectives and with IMPACT’s research cycle and other relevant guidelines.
- Design research approaches and methodologies according to IMPACT’s requirements and principles as well as partners’ information needs.
- Compose and construct, in close coordination with GIS and data teams, qualitative and quantitative data collection tool.
- Ensure relevant stakeholders and partners are engaged in research design and planning.

***STAFF MANAGEMENT AND TRAINING***

- Line manage the MSNA Research Officer directly and lead the MSNA team throughout the research cycle
- In close liaison with the Field Manager and Ops teams (field officer and logistics team), manage assessment logistics, including with partner organizations, identifying assessment areas, facilitating design workshops, managing joint data collection processes, and facilitating joint analysis workshops.
- In close liaison the Ops teams, ensure logistics, financial, administration, security and HR processes directly related to ongoing and upcoming assessments are appropriately planned, implemented and coordinated with the relevant Acted departments.
- In close liaison with data colleagues, provide quantitative, qualitative, and spatial data analysis on primary and/or secondary data as per ToRs, ensuring that meaningful techniques are used to analyze the data collected.
- Promoting capacity building across the IMPACT Somalia mission related to deepening analytical capacities using existing research (capacity building portfolio will depend on level of experience)
- Providing day-to-day direct and indirect management of the research team within their unit/workstream, and field team during data collection.
    
    ***Internal Coordination***
- Interacting autonomously with HQ departments and serve as mission focal point for HQ’s corresponding unit and specialists in particular themes or technical areas.
- Engage in the development and implementation of IMPACT’s strategy in Somalia
- Conduct regular meetings with relevant national and international assessment staff members to assess progress in relevant research cycles and to review work plan.
- For all activities, ensure that all assessment and field teams are comprehensively briefed on objectives, expected outputs and that the overall implementation strategy is clearly understood.
- Ensure that project/field staff are given required training and resources to achieve their tasks in line with IMPACT and project requirements. Support to the line managers and specialists in the development and implementation of capacity training plans for team members.
- Be available to provide regular support and technical backstopping; regularly debrief team members to receive feedback on the progress of an activity.
- In coordination with line manager, contribute to conduct induction for new staff members, including training in basic technical competencies for research design, implementation and analysis.

***DISSEMINATION MANAGEMENT***

- Ensure the drafting of timely and accurate outputs that consolidate the analyses from each research cycle into relevant products such as factsheets, reports, briefs, presentations, etc which comply with IMPACT’s guidelines and quality standards.
- Ensure that products accurately reflect the information collected and that information is conveyed in a way that maximizes their impact in line with their intended use for the relevant audiences.
- Follow the designated timeline of reports to be submitted to project partners and donors. Ensure that delays or identified challenges for specific assessments are reported in writing and orally in a timely manner.
- Maintain regular communication with country Management and IMPACT HQ on progress and deadlines for deliverables
- Ensure that all written products are validated by IMPACT HQ before external release.

***External Engagement***

- Ensure that relevant partners are consulted and involved at all stages of research cycle: assessment preparation; data collection; data analysis; review of research products; product dissemination; and lessons learnt.
- After validation by the line manager, represent IMPACT in relevant external meetings/ working groups.
- Follow up on issues identified by partners or during meetings / working groups.
- Promote an active use of datasets and research findings by partners and the broader humanitarian community for their decision making.
- After validation by line manager, disseminate research findings to relevant third parties in order to enhance their use and impact.
- Ensure that all partner engagement and all external relations are clearly documented and communicated with the line manager and relevant colleagues.
- More generally, contribute to the creation of a positive image and overall credibility of the organization, notably through the application of IMPACT’s mandate, ethics, values and stand-point with regard to other actors.

***Data Confidentiality and Protection***

- The Senior Research Officer will maintain the strictest confidentiality on all data collected and related processes, ensuring full compliance with IMPACT’s data protection policy and SOPs. He/she will actively take measures to prevent the unauthorized sharing of any information and data belonging to IMPACT and its partners or collected during his/her assignment with IMPACT.

## **REQUIREMENTS**

- **Years of work experience** 3 years of relevant working experience in a humanitarian setting, such as assessments, monitoring and evaluation, research design and analysis, etc.
- **Research skills** Excellent quantitative and qualitative research data analysis experience required. Ability to adapt, implement and interpret methodology, sampling and analysis to a high standard
- **Familiarity with the humanitarian and aid system** Good understanding of the aid system and the research community. Prior experience with humanitarian coordination forums preferred
- **Thematic experience** Prior experience with MSNA type of research and humanitarian assessments is an asset. Prior experience working with components of FSL/public health is highly desirable
- **Communication/reporting skills** Excellent verbal and written communication and drafting skills for effective and accurate reporting required
- **Academic** **qualifications** Excellent academic qualifications, preferably including a Master’s degree in relevant discipline (e.g. international studies, development, humanitarian response, data science, political science, statistics, etc)
- **Software skills** Proven knowledge of the Microsoft Office Suite, to include Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. Advanced skills in R, SPSS and/or STATA or other statistical analysis software are an advantage; Experience with InDesign an asset.
- **Level of independence** Proven ability to work independently.
- **Experience in geographical region** Past experience in the HoA region is desirable; or any other emergency context where access is challenging.
- **Language skills** Fluency in English required, competency in Somali an asset.
- **Security environment** Openness to working in a high-risk security zone required. Ability to operate in a complex and challenging security environment. Ability to prioritize self-care and well-being.

## **COMPENSATION & BENEFITS**

- For this position, salary between **3’000 CHF** and **3’120 CHF** monthly (before income tax), etc as well as a monthly living allowance of **300 USD**
- NB - IMPACT salaries are strictly determined by our salary grid depending on the grade of the position and the level of education of staff. A location-dependent security and/or isolation adjustment is then applied as a recognition that some staff are required to work in difficult places where living and working conditions are much more difficult than elsewhere.
- Accommodation and food provided in a guesthouse. IMPACT is hosted by Acted in this country \[to be adjusted depending on the country\]
- Enrolment in Swiss private pension fund (Swisslife – approx. 9.975% of staff gross salary), health insurance, life insurance and repatriation assistance
- Flight tickets every 6 months & visa fees covered (in-country travel costs and professional expenses are fully covered)
- R&R after 2-3 months (flight ticket up to 500$ + 200$ of living allowance)
- Contribution to the luggage transportation: between 20 and 100 kgs, depending on the length of the contract (+ luggage and personal property insurance)
- Annual leave of 36 days per year. Public holidays of the country of assignment. Family/compassionate leave when applicable.

title: IT Business Relationship Director, Americas
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Job Overview**

We are hiring an IT Business Relationship Director to ensure IT service delivery meets the operational needs of program offices across the Americas geography (US and LATAM), translating business needs into IT priorities and IT technical capability into business value. The role sits at the intersection of IT and program operations — building trust with leadership, diagnosing where IT processes break down, and brokering the cross-office knowledge and escalation paths that don't currently exist structurally.

 This role will operate as the connective layer between IT and Resettlement, Asylum and Integration (RAI) and Crisis, Response, Recovery and Development (CRRD) leadership across the US and LATAM, working alongside the Global IT Solutions team, the Americas IT Service Desk (POD) and RAI Operations staff. They will build a regular engagement cadence with RAI office and CRRD program leadership, develop enough programmatic fluency to judge whether an IT solution will work in the field, own escalations, knowing when an issue needs IT leadership, a vendor, or executive attention. The role embeds proactive communication and cross-office knowledge-sharing into how IT and program operations work together, so that consistency across offices is structural rather than dependent on individual relationships.

 The ideal candidate has direct experience in complex, distributed program operations, and brings credibility with program leadership as a result — not just IT service management experience. They are equal parts relationship manager, translator, and escalation owner: able to build trust with operations staff, assess whether a proposed IT solution will hold up in the field, and judge when to resolve something directly versus route it structurally. They have a bias for proactive communication, a high bar for consistency across offices, and a clear instinct for equipping program and office staff with the tools, access, and know-how to handle their own work.

 This role reports to the Senior Director, IT Business Relationship Management and partners closely with RAI and CRRD leadership through an agreed engagement model. The role will also work closely with the Global IT Solutions Team, including the Service Delivery Center of Excellence, Helpdesk team, Enterprise Applications and Infrastructure.

 **Key Responsibilities:**

**Relationship Management and Engagement**

- Serve as the senior IT partner to RAI office and CRRD program leadership, providing strategic guidance and thought partnership on IT service delivery performance, planned initiatives, and emerging risks across the US and LATAM
- Maintain a regular engagement cadence with RAI operations directors and senior CRRD leadership, ensuring IT priorities are aligned with program needs and that leadership has visibility of service delivery against commitments
- Act as the accountable IT point of contact for escalations from office and program leadership — owning the response, not just the routing
- Build sufficient familiarity with the programmatic context of each cluster to advise credibly on whether IT solutions will work in practice, and to represent office needs accurately to HQ IT
- Own cross-office knowledge brokering — surfacing what's working in one office to others, and serving as the connective point for "what are other offices doing on this?" questions that currently have no structural answer
- Act as the strategic focal point for IT initiative rollouts across RAI offices and CRRD programs in the Americas – shaping appropriate timing, delivery and relaying infrastructure, application, and programmatic IT needs from offices to HQ IT teams and vice versa.
- Support IT budget planning for the Americas region and ensure asset documentation, audit readiness, and regulatory compliance obligations are maintained

**Escalation, Risk Management and Service Performance**

- Own escalation pathways for issues that fall between the helpdesk and engineering teams, knowing when to involve specific IT leads, vendors, or procurement and following through to resolution
- Monitor service delivery performance and key performance indicators across the Americas region, identifying patterns and recurring issues that should trigger problem management review; escalate trending patterns as they emerge for either immediate action, system enhancement, or larger risk management
- Partner with the Global Service Desk Manager on T1/T2 technician performance, ensuring ticket priority logic and SLA adherence

**Job Requirements:**

**Knowledge & Experience**

- 6-8 years in a relationship management, business partnering, or program/operations role bridging technical and non-technical stakeholders — direct experience with humanitarian, nonprofit, or similarly complex distributed-operations environments strongly preferred
- Working knowledge of the IT service and technology lifecycle, from planning and delivery through operations and continuous improvement, sufficient to engage credibly with technical teams and evaluate whether a proposed solution is fit for purpose
- Familiarity with IT best-practice frameworks and delivery models (e.g., ITIL, Agile/Scrum, or equivalent project delivery methodologies) and how they apply to service management and technology rollouts; ITIL Foundation certification preferred, not required
- Demonstrated experience translating operational needs into technical priorities and representing technical capability back to non-technical leadership
- Experience defining and tracking performance metrics (KPIs, SLAs, or equivalent) and running a recurring review cadence with stakeholders

**Personal Attributes**

- Spanish language proficiency
- Builds credibility quickly with leadership
- Comfortable holding ambiguity and structuring it
- Strong written and verbal communication; able to translate fluently between technical and program audiences

**Working Environment*****:***

This position is based in the US – Hybrid. The role may require travel to US and LATAM Offices as necessary.

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $132,000/yr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.
