They regularly visit field offices to ensure the harmonisation and application of these procedures across the entire Country Office.

They are the point of contact within the Country Office for all matters relating to human resources, and acts as the liaison between headquarters and the Country Office on these matters.

**The main challenges:**

- Manage a team that needs support
- Complex and demandind labor aurhorities with different specificities depending on the location
- Growing teams in all bases that need follow up on HR procedures
- Creation of Policies on missing procedures
- Communication with other NGOs in the country
- Strong collaboration with other departments for various issues
- Follow up with a high number of expats on their documentation and off-boardings when needed

**Priorities for the 2/3 first months:**

- Stabilize the Private Insurance payments and follow ups
- Stabilize the Shared Cost processes to be on time
- Follow up on revised DW Policy, updated function grid & salary grid
- Visit the bases and introduce himself/herself to the teams and to authorities

**Security constraints:**

There is an internal curfew at night for international staffs - different zones are set (6-8-10PM). Curfew can be reduced based on security updates.

The situation in South Sudan is volatile, please document yourself before applying. SI is adapting the set up in real time as context evolves

There is one driver available on evenings and 2 on weekends for movements out of office hours.

Access to activities is possible for all (and encouraged!).

In coordination, movements outside of Juba town (besides intervention location) for leisure are limited

## Your profile

**DIPLOMAS AND EXPERIENCE**

Diploma : BA in Psychology, Business Administration or similar, MA in HR preferable

Experience in the humanitarian sector : More than 5 years

Experience on a similar position : 3/4 years

**SKILLS**

TECHNICAL SKILLS

1. HOMERE user and familiarity with SI HR tools preferable
2. Good and comfortable to use Excel
3. HR Policies: Applying them consistently, be rigorous on identifying needs for new policies and create them
4. Able to handle sensitive cases with outmost professionalism and confidentiality

TRANSVERSAL SKILLS

1. Clear, effective, sensitive communication
2. Build positive relations
3. Confidentiality and Discretion
4. Cultural Awareness within the country
5. Rigor and attention to details

**LANGUAGES**

1. English necessary
2. Arabic is a bonus

## SI will offer you

**A salaried position:**  
**According to experience,** starting from EUR 2860 gross per month (2600 base salary + 10% annual leave allowance paid monthly) and a monthly Per Diem of USD 700.

SI also covers accommodation costs and travel expenses between the expatriate's country of origin and the place of assignment.

**Breaks:** During the assignment, a system of alternation between work and time off is implemented at the rate of 7 working days every three months (with a USD 850 break allowance, allocated by Sl). To these breaks periods, SI grants one (1) additional rest day per month worked.

**Insurance package:** Expatriates benefit from an insurance package which refunds all healthcare expenses (including medical and surgical expenses, dental care and ophthalmological expenses, repatriation) and a welfare system including war risks. Essential vaccination and antimalarial treatment costs are refunded.

**LIVING CONDITIONS:**

The HR Head of Department will be living in a shared guesthouse with the other international staffs. With the scale up, different options are being considered and

some staffs may also be hosted at another NGO nearby.

Individual room in the guesthouse, with electricity 24/7 and generator during specific time. NB: During field visits, living conditions are much more basic.

Juba, as the capital of South Sudan offers a good variety of markets, supermarkets, restaurants, and bars.

title: PIR Caseworker
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Job Overview:** The Caseworker provides trauma-informed, client-centered services to recently arrived refugees and other qualified immigrants to meet immediate needs and support progress toward self-sufficiency. The role works closely with clients, internal teams, and external partners to develop and implement individualized service and self-sufficiency plans. The Caseworker connects clients to appropriate financial, medical, social, vocational, and community resources in alignment with program requirements, eligibility guidelines, and IRC standards.

**Major Responsibilities:**  
**Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:**

- Coordinate timely pre- and post-arrival services to ensure clients have access to housing, food, medical care, transportation, and community orientation.
- Conduct housing set-ups, airport pick-ups, home visits, grocery and public transportation orientation, and other field-based services to address immediate client needs.
- Purchase and transport program-related items; lift, move, and deliver materials necessary for service delivery.
- Conduct client intake assessments and develop individualized self-sufficiency plans and timelines in partnership with clients.
- Provide ongoing case management through direct services, referrals, advocacy, and coordination with internal and external service providers.
- Monitor client progress toward established goals, identify barriers, and adjust service plans as needed.
- Document all client interactions accurately and in compliance with program requirements; enter and maintain client data in required databases and tracking tools.
- Support Preferred Communities programming and intensive case management services, as assigned.
- Collaborate with colleagues across programs and grants to ensure clients access all eligible services.
- Build and maintain effective working relationships with community partners and service providers.
- Participate in program quality assurance activities to ensure appropriate use of funds and compliance with grant requirements.
- Use a personal, insured vehicle and/or public transportation to travel within the service delivery area as needed.
- Perform other duties as assigned.

**Job Requirements**

**Education**

- Bachelor’s degree in social work or a related field preferred.

**Work Experience**

- Prior experience working with refugee and/or immigrant populations required.
- Experience providing casework, pre-arrival, or intensive case management services preferred.
- Demonstrated experience navigating program eligibility requirements and ensuring accurate service documentation.

**Language Skills:**

- Proficiency in English required; bilingual ability in Spanish, Dari, Swahili, Kinyarwanda, Arabic, French, or other refugee/immigrant language preferred.

**Certificates or Licenses:**

- Valid driver’s license, active insurance policy, and access to reliable transportation.
- Must possess or be eligible for a fingerprint clearance card per Arizona state law.

**Demonstrated Skills and Competencies**

- Strong relationship-building, diplomacy, and networking skills.
- Ability to work effectively in a multicultural environment.
- Proven problem-solving skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines.
- High attention to detail and accuracy.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Outlook) and ability to use digital tools for data entry, research, and reporting.
- Ability to lift and carry items weighing 50+ pounds, including furniture and household goods.
- Ability to drive a large van or passenger vehicle, as required for program delivery.

**Working Environment**

**This position operates in a hybrid environment that includes office-based work, remote work, and fieldwork within the service delivery area. Typically, the role is based in the office four days per week and remotely one day per week, with field responsibilities possible on all workdays. Schedule flexibility is required, including occasional evenings and weekends for activities such as airport pick-ups.**

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $120 per month, dental starting at $7 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

**Compensation:( 20.97$/hourly**): Compensation is based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

title: Associate Director, Global CRM (Salesforce)
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world’s worst humanitarian crises and helps people to survive and rebuild their lives. Founded in 1933 at the request of Albert Einstein, the IRC offers lifesaving care and life-changing assistance to refugees made to flee from war or disaster. At work today in over 40 countries and 28 U.S. cities, we restore safety, dignity and hope to millions who are uprooted and struggling to endure. The IRC leads the way from harm to home.

This position sits within Marketing Technology, the team that builds and runs the systems IRC uses to raise funds, engage supporters and advocate for the people we serve. These include the enterprise Salesforce CRM, our donation platforms, the global Rescue.org website and our email communications platforms. Together they underpin the fundraising, communications and advocacy work of External Relations around the world.

**Job Overview / Summary (What and Why):**

IRC’s Salesforce platform sits at the heart of how we raise funds and stay in touch with supporters. It manages a multi-million dollar fundraising operation, is used by around 500 staff, and runs as a single global, GDPR-compliant org built on a heavily customised Nonprofit Success Pack (NPSP). We are now evaluating a potential move to Salesforce Nonprofit Cloud, and exploring how AI, including Agentforce and integrations with models such as Anthropic’s Claude, can work responsibly inside the platform.

The Associate Director will lead that next chapter. Reporting to the Senior Director, Marketing Technology, the postholder owns the platform’s strategy, roadmap and architecture, and plays a central role in how Salesforce evolves at the IRC in the future.

The role brings together three things that rarely sit in one job: architect-level Salesforce judgement, leadership of a technical team, and a real understanding of how a global nonprofit raises and manages income. The postholder leads and develops the CRM team, holds contractors and delivery partners to clear standards of quality, security and supportability, and explains technical choices and trade-offs in plain language to senior leaders.

This is a team leadership role that stays close to the technology. We expect the postholder to spend most of their time on strategy, architecture and leading the team, while remaining hands-on where it matters: designing solutions, reviewing the team’s work and building when the situation calls for it.

**In their first year, the postholder will:**

- Get to know the current NPSP org in depth, including its customisations, integrations and technical debt, and the teams who depend on it.
- Agree a clear platform roadmap and the governance to deliver it with stakeholders across External Relations, Finance and programme teams.
- Identify where AI tools such as Agentforce can add real value, safely and in line with IRC’s data protection and AI governance requirements.
- Shape the team structure, ways of working and partner model the platform needs for its next phase.

**Major Responsibilities:**

**Platform strategy and product ownership**

- Act as global product and platform owner for IRC’s Salesforce ecosystem, setting its direction and making the case for investment.
- Develop and maintain a prioritised CRM roadmap aligned with IRC’s fundraising, supporter engagement, finance and programme objectives, and run a fair, transparent process for managing demand.
- Lead IRC’s evaluation of Salesforce Nonprofit Cloud, including the business case, options appraisal and, if approved, the migration strategy and plan.
- Lead the responsible evaluation and adoption of AI within the CRM ecosystem, including Agentforce and integrations with external AI models, identifying worthwhile use cases while meeting IRC’s data protection, security, ethical AI and governance requirements.
- Assess AppExchange and other third-party products and recommend what IRC should adopt, keep or retire.

**Architecture and technical leadership**

- Own the solution architecture of the platform: data model, automation, security model, integrations and managed packages, including NPSP, Account Engagement (Pardot), Outlook integration, Blackthorn and Apsona.
- Set design and build standards for declarative and programmatic development (Flow, Apex, Lightning Web Components, APIs), and review the work of the team and partners against them.
- Reduce technical debt in a heavily customised org, and make sure new work is simpler to support and ready for future platform changes.
- Oversee integrations with donation platforms, finance systems, the data warehouse and reporting tools, so that data flows are reliable and well documented.
- Stay hands-on: prototype, configure and build when that is the fastest way to unblock the team or prove an approach.

**Team and partner leadership**

- Lead, coach and develop a team of Salesforce administrators, developers and a business analyst, including recruitment, performance management, career development and workload planning.
- Build a team culture of good engineering practice, clear documentation and service to the people who use the platform.
- Manage contractors, implementation partners and suppliers, holding them to account for quality, cost and delivery, and contribute to procurement, licensing and budgeting.

**Governance, security and operations**

- Own platform governance: access management, security, audit controls, data quality, business continuity, and compliance with GDPR and other data protection requirements across countries.
- Oversee incident, problem, change and release management, including readiness for Salesforce’s three annual releases and managed-package updates.
- Oversee user support, testing and defect resolution delivered by the team and partners.
- Make sure reports and dashboards give leaders accurate, trusted information.

**Stakeholders and business context**

- Build strong relationships with fundraising, finance, data and programme leaders, and understand how IRC raises, processes and stewards income in different countries.
- Explain technical options, risks and trade-offs in plain language so that senior, non-technical stakeholders can make good decisions.

**Key Working Relationships:**

**Position Reports to:** Senior Director, Marketing Technology

**Position directly supervises:** Team of Salesforce Admins/Developers/Business Analyst

**Other Internal and/or external contacts**:

**Internal***:* Close collaboration with global and regional stakeholders across External Relations, Resettlement, Asylum and Integration, Information Technology, Communications, Finance, Data and Analytics and other teams that rely on the CRM platform.

**External**: Technology suppliers, implementation partners, consultants, contractors and other service providers.

**Job Qualifications:**

**Education:**

**Minimum:**

Bachelor’s degree in information technology, computer science, business systems or a related discipline or equivalent professional experience.

**Preferred:** Salesforce Architect-track certifications (e.g. Application Architect, System Architect), Nonprofit Cloud Consultant, Advanced Administrator, Platform App Builder or Platform Developer I/II.

**Work Experience:**

**Minimum:**

- Significant experience leading an enterprise Salesforce platform in a complex, multi-country organisation, with the architectural judgement to design and govern a large, heavily customised org.
- Experience acting as a product or platform owner, including developing roadmaps, governing demand and prioritising investment.
- Deep knowledge of Salesforce architecture, including data models, automation, security, integration and application lifecycle management, with enough hands-on fluency in declarative and programmatic development to guide and review the work of developers.
- Proven experience managing and developing a team of technical professionals, and overseeing contractors, consultants or delivery partners.
- An understanding of how nonprofits or comparable organisations raise and manage income (such as individual and recurring giving, gift processing and donor data) and how a CRM supports that work.
- Experience overseeing platform operations, including incident, change and release management.
- Experience working with APIs, ETL processes, integration platforms and cross-system data flows.
- Excellent stakeholder management and communication skills, including the ability to explain technical options and risks to non-technical and senior audiences.
- Experience of Agile delivery, using tools such as Git-based source control and Jira.
- Strong analytical thinking, judgement, problem solving ability and customer service orientation.

**Preferred:**

- Hands-on experience with Nonprofit Success Pack and Nonprofit Cloud, ideally including an NPSP-to-Nonprofit Cloud evaluation or migration.
- Experience delivering technology for fundraising, marketing, advocacy or supporter engagement teams.
- Familiarity with Salesforce Account Engagement (Pardot), Data Cloud, Agentforce or comparable marketing, data and AI platforms.
- Experience working with enterprise architecture, DevOps, Business Intelligence, Data Warehousing or integration technologies.
- Experience working with an international nonprofit, humanitarian or mission-led organisation.
- Experience running a CRM across multiple countries and currencies, including under GDPR and other data protection regimes.
- Experience contributing to supplier management, procurement, licensing, budgeting and technology business cases.
- Hands-on development experience with Apex, SOQL and Lightning Web Components.

  
**Working Environment*****:***

A collegiate environment working collaboratively across External Relations and broader IRC. Strong sense of transparency and accountability to ensure we are doing right by our clients and donors, exemplifying the IRC Way.

- This is a fully remote role, with travel 3–5 times per year for in-person time with the team and for learning and development.

***This is a remote position open to internal candidates based in countries where IRC operates who have the right to work in their location. Successful candidates will be hired on a local employment contract and according to local salary scale.***

***This role is open to candidates located and with the right to work in United States of America, United Kingdom, and Kenya.***

**Compensation:** (US Pay Rate: $113,102-$120,000/yr; UK Pay Rate: £69,440-£84,058/yr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

title: Research Manager for Venezuela, based in Caracas
Research Manager for Nigeria, based in Abuja
body:
## **BACKGROUND ON IMPACT AND REACH**

IMPACT Initiatives is a humanitarian NGO, based in Geneva, Switzerland. The organisation manages several initiatives, including the PANDA Initiative. The IMPACT team comprises specialists in data collection, management and analysis and GIS. IMPACT operates through three Initiatives: REACH, PANDA, and AGORA. This recruitment opportunity pertains to the PANDA Initiative.

PANDA is IMPACT’s lever on humanitarian aid responses which focusing on improving outcomes for beneficiaries through direct engagement with partners and their activities. Where REACH works through soft power and partnerships to affect systemic change, PANDA is direct action that allows us to ensure that system and its participants are trustworthy and delivering the most effective, efficient and equitable response possible. PANDA is praxis – it is how IMPACT manifests our vision of acting as a catalyst of change within the aid community to work through focused or multidimensional analysis of projects, programmes and policies to identify their results, strengths and weaknesses, and how they can be improved, then proposes or implements a concrete plan for improvement.

**We are currently looking for a Research Manager to support our team in Nigeria.**

**Department**: PANDA

**Position**: Research Manager

**Contract duration**: 4 months

**Location**: Abuja, Nigeria (with occasional stays in Dakar, Senegal)

**Starting Date**: ASAP.

## **COUNTRY PROFILE**

Nigeria is among the world's most critical hunger hotspots, where protracted conflict, displacement, economic pressures, and climate shocks are driving rapidly worsening humanitarian needs. In the Northeast, more than 8.8 million people require urgent assistance, including 4.9 million children, sustained displacement, protection risks, severe funding shortfalls, a growing nutrition emergency, and a cholera outbreak. Food insecurity is expected to reach record levels, with an estimated 34.7 million people nationwide projected to face Crisis-level food insecurity or worse by August 2026. Meanwhile, the Northwest faces a different but equally severe crisis driven by chronic poverty, banditry, communal violence, and recurrent flooding, which have displaced hundreds of thousands of people (800,000 IOM DTM R18), damaged livelihoods and farmland, and contributed to sharp declines in agricultural production. Together, these overlapping shocks are undermining resilience, increasing humanitarian needs, and threatening both current food security and future harvests.

Against this backdrop, IMPACT Initiatives has developed a wide range of research cycles to provide an evidence-base for the humanitarian community. Historically, IMPACT Initiatives has been present in both the Northeast and Northwest of Nigeria. Thematically, across 2021 – 2023 IMPACT Initiatives fielded [Multi-Sectoral Needs Assessments](https://www.impact-repository.org/document/reach/7b6cde65/REACH_NGA_TOR_MSNA-Northwest_March-2022-1.pdf) (MSNAs), [Hard to Reach](https://www.impact-repository.org/document/reach/0f980ce2/NGA-1809_Situation_Overview_Q1_Feb_Mar_2022.pdf) (H2R) assessments, [Area Based Assessments](https://www.impact-repository.org/document/reach/7cddc3c2/REACH_NGA_TOR_Rapid_Area-Based_Assessments_in_Areas_of_Return_February_2021.pdf) (ABA), [Rapid Overviews of Areas of Return](https://www.impact-repository.org/document/reach/07db0c79/REACH_NGA_ToR_Rapid_Overview_Of_Areas_Of_Return_ROAR_-Feb-2022.pdf) (ROAR), [Thematic Assessments](https://www.impact-repository.org/document/reach/9fa6a7cf/REACH_NGA_Brief_assessment-of-H2R-Gujba-and-Tarmua-LGA_April-2022.pdf) (TA), [Rapid Assessments](https://www.impact-repository.org/document/reach/6b1d770d/REACH_NGA_Yobe_Floods_Brief.pdf) (RA), and [WASH Infrastructure Mapping](https://www.impact-repository.org/document/reach/afb497ac/REACH_NGA_Factsheet_WASH-Infrastructure-Maiduguri_May-2021.pdf), while also playing a key role in Famine Monitoring, Nutrition and Food Security Surveillance, and the Joint Market Monitoring Initiative (JMMI). Since 2026, IMPACT has reintroduced the MSNA, Acute Needs Analysis (ANA), JMMI and other thematic assessments in Nigeria in addition to the HARP TPM project which has been running since 2024.

## **PROJECT PRFILE**

The position is recruited for the Third-Party Monitoring (TPM) Project covering FCDOs Humanitarian and Resilience Programme (HARP) Facility. For this programme, IMPACT is in partnership with FACT Foundation. While in Nigeria, staff shall be hosted by FACT Foundation and for his or her mission, the Research Manager will fall under the direct responsibility and management of FACT and their delegates for all Administrative, Security, Logistics and Finance issues. S/he will therefore fully abide by FACT’s Security, HR, Administration, and Logistics rules and regulations, and in coordination with FACT, ensure that all IMPACT staff abide by them.

## **FUNCTIONS**

Under the management of the Country Representative, the Research Manager oversees the research activities and staff within the purview of the FCDO-funded Third Party Monitoring (TPM) Project. The Research Manager shall oversee and execute all research activities within the above-mentioned Project, meeting quarterly deliverables in a timely fashion while ensuring that the quality of research remains high. S/he will moreover liaise extensively with counterparts from Fact Foundation who are IMPACT’s partners in the Consortium for the Project, while supporting the Country Representative in stakeholder engagement with FCDO’s Implementing Partners.

## **RESPONSIBILITIES**

The Research Manager responsibilities include the following:

***Strategy development & implementation***

- With specific attention to the FCDO-funded TPM Project’s, and while supervised by the CR, the RM is to ensure that IMPACT has an up to date understanding of the country’s socio-economic situation, the impact of a crisis and the aid/humanitarian situation, as well as the humanitarian planning, coordination, response mechanism developments, and key humanitarian stakeholders.
- For the TPM Project, **develop and oversee the implementation of the project’s strategy**. Specifically, during the inception period, in conjunction with the CR, set out the project’s overall strategy, develop concomitant workplans for each staff member, and put in place the requisite structures for the staff members such that each individual has clarity as to how to work towards the common goal of completing deliverables in a timely manner and at a high standard, and ultimately supplying impact to FCDO and Implementing Partners at the outcome level.

## ***Research Planning***

- For the TPM Project, ensure that all the research is planned in line with the relevant project and programme objectives, as well as the Project and Country Strategy. This is to include:
- Ensure that all research complies with IMPACT’s HQ Research Department guidelines and standards.
- Ensure that al necessary Secondary Data Reviews are conducted and integrated into the research.
- Ensure that research ToRs are validated by HQ prior to the commencement of data collection.
- Ensure that research ToRs are understood by the team and updated accordingly.
- Keep track of progress and delays of all assigned assessments throughout the research cycle.
- Liaise with FACT Foundation, to include their two assessment and data staff in the research.
- Liaise with FACT Foundation to ensure that the portion of the research carried out by them is validated by IMPACT HQ.
- Where necessary, proactively support the team by conducting research (research design. ToRs, tool building, data management, data analysis, product drafting).
- While supported by the CR, conduct dissemination and stakeholder meetings with FCDO and Implementing Partners.

***Research Implementation***

- Liaise with FACT Foundation, to **ensure that the data is collected in the fashion and format that allows IMPACT to clean and analyse the data**.
- Ensure that all collected data is stored **in line with IMPACT’s Data Management Guidelines**, as well as with the data management plan Annex in the Research ToR.
- Ensure that data is revised and cleaned, **with all revisions recorded** as per IMPACT data management guidelines.
- **Oversee all the analyses of the collected data**, as stipulated in the Research ToRs.
- Ensure that data and its analysis **do not contain personal information** and are validated by IMPACT HQ, before sharing to external parties.
- Supervise and where necessary support the team with the analysis and drafting of the information products.
- **Review all products** before they are sent to the CR or IMPACT HQ for validation.
- Ensure that all written products are validated by IMPACT HQ **before release to FCDO and Implementing Partners**.

***Team Management and Leadership***

- Ensure that all staff members understand and are able to perform their roles and responsibilities, as well as their reporting and validation duties to HQ.
- Ensure that all staff members have **clear and regularly updated ToRs, Workplans, and Key performance Indicators (KPIs)** against which their performance will be appraised.
- **Promote team building, productivity, and staff welfare**.
- Mentor and support the team **to build capacities, improve efficiency and performance**.
- **Promote the growth and development of staff** within the organisation, actively linking with HQ to provide feedback and support retention and internal mobility. Identify capacity building opportunities for growth, proactively provide high-performing staff with opportunities to surge (a short-term deployment to another mission) and develop pathways for junior staff to grow and move into management or specialist positions.
- **Ensure communication and linkages with HQ** are made immediately in case of the occurrence of an HR-related problem.

***Internal Coordination and Communication***

- Facilitate clear and seamless communication within the IMPACT TPM team across Senegal and Nigeria, as well as the FACT Foundation team in Nigeria.
- Ensure regular reporting to the CR.

***INFLUENCING - External Engagement***

- With the support from the CR, on a quarterly basis, engage with FCDO and the Implementing Partners to share findings and hold analysis and lessons learned workshops.
- Under the supervision of the CR, and where necessary, engage with the humanitarian response beyond the remit of the TPM Project.
- In conjunction with FCDO and Implementing Partners, support the CR in the dissemination of selected research with key stakeholders and coordination forums.

## **REQUIREMENTS**

- **Academic** Excellent academic qualifications, including a master’s degree in a relevant discipline (International Relations, Political Sciences, Social Research, Economics, Development Studies, or similar)
- **Management experience** Previous experience in a management role in an INGO at field level. Proven track record in successful management of international and national teams in humanitarian contexts
- **Familiarity aid system** Familiarity with the aid system, and the research community.
- **Communication/reporting skills** Excellent communication and drafting skills for effective reporting, including proven experience in contributing to high level presentations/briefings.
- **Years of work experience** At least 3 years of relevant working experience or proven progression within IMPACT.
- **Research skills:** Excellent research and analytical skills an asset. Experience in assessments. M&E, field research, evaluations is an asset.
- **Software skills:** Proven knowledge of the Microsoft Office Suite, to include Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. Familiarity with R, SPSS and/or STATA or other statistical analysis software an asset.
- **Multi-tasking skills** Ability to multitask with tight deadlines, on numerous research cycles in complex environment.
- **Level of independence** A self-starter with a proven ability to work independently.
- **Cross-cultural work environment** Ability to operate in a cross-cultural environment requiring flexibility.
- **Experience in geographical region** Past experience in the \[relevant\] region is desirable.
- **Language skills** Fluency in English required.
- **Security environment** Ability to operate in a complex and challenging security environment.

## **COMPENSATION & BENEFITS**

- For this position, salary between 3’180 CHF and 3’240 CHF monthly (before income tax), etc as well as a monthly living allowance of 300 USD *NB - IMPACT salaries are strictly determined by our salary grid depending on the grade of the position and the level of education of staff. A location-dependent security and/or isolation adjustment is then applied as a recognition that some staff are required to work in difficult places where living and working conditions are much more difficult than elsewhere.*
- Accommodation and food provided in the guesthouse.
- Enrolment in Swiss private pension fund (Swisslife – approx. 9.975% of staff gross salary), health insurance, life insurance and repatriation assistance
- Flight tickets every 6 months & visa fees covered (in-country travel costs and professional expenses are fully covered)
- Contribution to the luggage transportation: between 20 and 100 kgs, depending on the length of the contract (+ luggage and personal property insurance)

title: Emergency Watsan Coordinator H/F
body:
Context

To fulfill its mission of assistance to victims of conflicts, epidemics or natural disasters, MSF-Switzerland has created an Emergency Pool, of which members are experienced individuals capable of evaluating a situation, opening and coordinating emergency projects.

The candidate is expected to

- work in all contexts set by the emergency cell
- have the flexibility to work in different positions depending on his/her profile
- work in emergency contexts with regular cells and fill gaps in regular projects if needed.

Duty Station

All countries where the emergency desk opens activities, which require an urgent response. On call, the Emergency Watsan technical Referent should be available within 48 hours for rapid and short interventions. He/she is part of a core group of medicals, para-medicals and support staff responsible for responding to:

- epidemic outbreaks
- nutritional crises
- displaced populations and/or refugees’ camps
- conflict contexts
- natural disasters
- exploratory missions
- Short gaps filling in the field on regular missions

Responsibilities

The main responsibilities of the Emergency Watsan Coordinator are structured in 4 main activities:

- Direct technical support to field operations (regular missions and emergencies)
- Contribution to missions' operational strategies
- Management and supervision of Watsan team
- Follow up of WASH specific supply and budget line in mission.

1. **Direct technical support to field operations**

- Promote and implement water & sanitation activities of the mission (implement or facilitate)
- Participate in:
- Exploratory missions
- Program support visits
- Assume the post of WATSAN Coordinator, where appropriate, in emergencies.

1. Contribution to missions’ operational strategies

- Share information with medical and logistic coordinators to identify potential Water, Hygiene and Sanitation related activities to develop
- Participate in the development of appropriate project strategies based on analysis of the situation
- Advise on Emergency preparedness capacity when appropriate

1. Management and supervision

- Contribute to the definition of Watsan team required in emergency
- Organize and prioritize the Watsan team members according to needs.
- In the field provides coaching to Watsan and logistic teams both local staff and expatriate

1. Follow up of WASH specific supply and budget line in mission.

- Compile orders coming from the team he/she supervises
- Validate orders according to the finance validation grid
- Follow up and ensure dispatch according to priorities
- validate local suppliers.
- Clean up stock and Eprep stocks

Your Profile

Field Experience

- 18 months of Watsan field experience with MSF with at least two missions in an emergency context with MSF.
- Or experience with other humanitarian organizations, with 24 months of field experience in emergency contexts in a Watsan role.
- Experience in at least 2 of the following emergencies: cholera, ebola, displacement (refugies/IDPs), and natural disasters.
- General knowledge of MSF in emergency management, Public Health, Rapid Water and Hygiene Assessment, and MSF standard Watsan protocols,
- Knowledge of basics in logistics to work as an Emergency filed logistician desirable

Technical, strategic and Interpersonal Skills

- Capacity to quickly evaluate an emergency on ground and to propose an appropriate Watsan strategy
- A demonstrable understanding of the need to integrate Medical and Public Health/WatSan activities,
- Proven hands-on experience of deploying and using MSF WatSan kits in the field
- Excellent knowledge of the necessary Infection, Prevention and Control (IPC) measures required in emergency medical facilities.
- Knowledge of surface water treatment, groundwater, water quality and water trucking management.
- Proven skills in negotiation, diplomacy and decision-making skills
- Strong people management skills.
- Strong coordination and organizational skills.
- Ability to work effectively in volatile and insecure environments, with strong resilience and stress management skills.
- Strong adaptability and flexibility to navigate changing priorities, dynamic operational environments, and evolving team dynamics.
- Responsible behavior that contributes to the safety and integrity of everyone - prevent, report, and refuse any abusive behavior and/or behavior that goes against MSF's values.
- Ability to thrive in a multicultural environment and demonstrate commitment and support for diversity, inclusive and non-discriminatory attitudes and behaviors.

**Language skills**

- Fluency in both French and English is highly desirable. Alternatively, candidates must demonstrate an excellent command of either language and at least B1 proficiency in the other.
- Knowledge of other mission languages is an advantage (Spanish, Portuguese, Arabic).

Terms of Employment

- Field-based contract. One year fixed-term contract, renewable based on operational needs and performance.
- Duration of field assignments: 4 weeks to 3 months (flexibility required according to needs).
- Accommodation and travel arrangements such as visa-related costs will be taken in charge by MSF.

We encourage applications from people of all genders, ages, sexual orientations, backgrounds, religions, beliefs, abilities, and all other characteristics of diversity.   
MSF does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, any kind of discrimination or harassment, including Sexual harassment.

All selected candidates will, therefore, undergo reference and criminal record checks.

title: Associate Research Manager for Syria, based in Damascus
body:
## **BACKGROUND ON IMPACT AND REACH**

IMPACT Initiatives is a humanitarian NGO, based in Geneva, Switzerland. The organisation manages several initiatives, including the REACH Initiative. The IMPACT team comprises specialists in data collection, management and analysis, GIS and remote sensing. IMPACT was launched at the initiative of ACTED, an international NGO with headquarters based in Paris and presence in thirty countries. The two organizations have a strong complementarity formalized in a global partnership, which allows IMPACT to benefit from ACTED’s operational support in its fields of intervention.

**We are currently looking for an Associate Research Manager to lead our Early Recovery, Markets, and Durable Solutions work in Syria.**

**Department**: IMPACT Syria mission

**Position**: Associate Research Manager Contract duration: 6 months

**Starting Date**: 1 December 2026

**Location**: Damascus, Syria.

## **COUNTRY PROFILE**

After more than a decade of conflict, economic collapse, and large-scale displacement, a regime change in December 2024 marked a new phase in Syria’s history. Conditions remain volatile, marked by regular armed clashes, prolonged socioeconomic and infrastructure challenges, and limited access to basic services such as healthcare, education, water, and electricity. While it is widely acknowledged that Syria needs large investments in development in order to recover from years of destruction and economic degradation, the humanitarian response also continues at scale due to high levels of need after fifteen years of conflict, exacerbated by the economic situation and poor basic services infrastructure.

Active in Syria since 2013, the IMPACT Syria mission has been producing key information products over the last decade to provide an evidence base for an informed humanitarian response. Activities have ranged from monthly humanitarian situation overviews and market monitoring, to displacement tracking, to supporting joint planning processes through the provision of multi-sectoral needs data, to providing evidence for durable solutions via area-based assessments.

## **POSITION PROFILE**

The Associate Research Manager will be responsible for leading research workstreams around Area-Based Assessments in support of Durable Solutions, market monitoring in support of economic analysis and recovery, and other related thematic assessments and analyses. Under the supervision of the Senior Research Manager (SRM), the ARM will lead on the development and timely implementation of the team’s strategy and research cycles.

This position requires a profile that can be both analytical and managerial, as the Associate Research Manager’s job can range from coordinating with external partners (whether data actor, sector stakeholder, or donor) to analytical oversight of research products, as well as support on data collection logistics, reporting, and financial planning.

## **RESPONSIBILITIES**

The Associate Research Manager’s responsibilities will include:

***STAFF MANAGEMENT***

- Under the guidance of the SRM, direct management of two team members, including recruitment, capacity building and staff career management, with potential for growing the team as funding allows.
- In coordination with the SRM, development and implementation of capacity training plans for team members.
- Day-to-day management of team members, including the development of work plans and performance indicators.

***PROJECT/RESEARCH CYCLE MANAGEMENT***

- Ensure all assessments and analysis are planned and implemented in a structured and coherent manner, in line with relevant project and strategic objectives, and with global REACH guidelines;
- Oversee all of the team’s research cycles, including reviewing ToRs, methodology notes, tools, products and dissemination strategies.
- Ensure the writing and production of timely, accurate and analytically rigorous outputs;
- Ensure relevant stakeholders and partners are engaged in assessment design and planning;
- Monitor output achievement and ensure timely completion of the project.
- Actively advocate for the improving of analysis within REACH products, and using common methodologies, tools and analysis frameworks across workstreams where relevant.

***GRANTS MANAGEMENT***

- Under the guidance of the SRM, manage grant components, including conceptualisation of new projects, drafting proposals, regular reporting, and M&E. Lead in identifying funding opportunities and strategic positioning for the team.
- Support the SRM / Country Representative in the financial management of all grants covering the team’s projects, including oversight of budget and expenditure with regards to data collection.
- Ensure that contractual obligations are met at a high-quality standard in terms of programs deliverables.

***EXTERNAL ENGAGEMENT***

- In coordination with the SRM and Country Representative and where relevant, represent REACH with donors, partners, and the wider response community in Syria, particularly with the Solutions Working Group, Data for Solutions Working Group, and Cash Working Group.

***STRATEGY DEVELOPMENT AND IMPLEMENTATION***

- Work with key sectors and partner organizations and working groups to understand the various relevant information gaps within Syria and identify how REACH can fill these gaps.
- Contribute to the development and implementation of the REACH Research Unit’s strategy, ensuring workstream research strategies are integrated within the wider strategy.
- In coordination with the SRM, develop and implement dissemination strategies to strengthen the impact of the team’s research cycles.
- Engagement with HQ on research and/or coordination and provide support to relevant IMPACT Global Community of Practices (CoPs).
- The Associate Research Manager will maintain the strictest confidentiality on all data collected and related processes. They will actively take measures to prevent the unauthorized sharing of any information and data belonging to IMPACT and its partners or collected during his/her assignment with IMPACT.

## **REQUIREMENTS**

- **Years of work experience** At least 3 years of relevant and progressive working experience in a humanitarian setting, such as program management, evaluation and assessments.
- **Research skills** Excellent quantitative and qualitative research design, data collection, and data analysis experience required. Solid understanding of IMPACT Research Quality Assurance standards also required.
- **Understanding of aid system** Good understanding of the response system and key actors, as well as of the research community. Prior experience with humanitarian coordination forums preferred.
- **Management experience** Demonstrated progressive staff management skills, including remote management and inspirational leadership.
- **Thematic experience** Prior experience with displacement, durable solutions, area-based and movement-related research highly desirable.
- **Experience in geographical region** Past experience in the region is desirable but not decisive.
- **Communication/reporting skills** Excellent communication and drafting skills for effective reporting and external engagement with donors and other high-level stakeholders.
- **Cross-cultural work environment** Ability to operate in a cross-cultural environment requiring flexibility and work independently;
- **Academic qualifications** Excellent academic qualifications, including a master’s degree in a relevant discipline.
- **Software skills** Proven knowledge of the Microsoft Office Suite, to include Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. Familiarity with R, SPSS and/or STATA or other statistical analysis software an asset.
- **Security environment** Ability to operate in a complex and challenging security environment.
- **Language skills** Fluency in English required, competency in Arabic is an asset.

## **COMPENSATION & BENEFITS**

- For this position, salary between 3’180 CHF and 3’240 CHF monthly (before income tax), etc as well as a monthly living allowance of 300 USD *NB - IMPACT salaries are strictly determined by our salary grid depending on the grade of the position and the level of education of staff. A location-dependent security and/or isolation adjustment is then applied as a recognition that some staff are required to work in difficult places where living and working conditions are much more difficult than elsewhere.*
- Accommodation provided in the guesthouse.
- Enrolment in Swiss private pension fund (Swisslife – approx. 9.975% of staff gross salary), health insurance, life insurance and repatriation assistance.
- Flight tickets every 6 months & visa fees covered (in-country travel costs and professional expenses are fully covered).
- Contribution to the luggage transportation: between 20 and 100 kgs, depending on the length of the contract (+ luggage and personal property insurance)
- Annual leave of 36 days per year. Public holidays of the country of assignment. Family/compassionate leave when applicable.
- Predeparture induction - 3 days at IMPACT Initiatives’s HQ in Geneva + one week pre-departure training in ACTED HQ in Paris, including a 4-days in situ security training;
- IMPACT prioritizes the psychological safety of its staff and the health insurance provided covers, among others, up to 1000 € per year of psychosocial counselling fees.

title: Senior Data Analyst for Ethiopia, based in Kampala
body:
**BACKGROUND ON IMPACT AND REACH**

REACH was born in 2010 as a joint initiative of two International NGOs ([IMPACT Initiatives](http://www.impact-initiatives.org/) and [ACTED](http://www.acted.org/)) and the United Nations Operational Satellite Applications Programme ([UNOSAT](http://www.unitar.org/unosat/)). REACH’s **purpose** is to promote and facilitate the development of information products that enhance the humanitarian community’s decision making and planning capacity for emergency, reconstruction and development contexts. REACH facilitates information management for aid actors through three complementary services: (a) need and situation assessments facilitated by REACH teams; (b) situation analysis using satellite imagery; (c) provision of related database and (web)-mapping facilities and expertise.

IMPACT Initiatives is a humanitarian NGO, based in Geneva, Switzerland. The organisation manages several initiatives, including the REACH Initiative. The IMPACT team comprises specialists in data collection, management and analysis and GIS. IMPACT was launched at the initiative of ACTED, an international NGO whose headquarter is based in Paris and is present in thirty countries. The two organizations have a strong complementarity formalized in a global partnership, enabling IMPACT to benefit from ACTED’s operational support on its fields of intervention.

**We are currently looking for a Senior Data Analyst or Data Specialist, depending on profile, to work with our team in Ethiopia.**

**Position:** Senior Data Analyst / Data Specialist (depending on profile)

**Contract duration**: 5 months

**Location**: Kampala, with possible travel to Addis Ababa

**Starting Date**: ASAP.

## **COUNTRY PROFILE**

Since 2018, Ethiopia has experienced escalating insecurity and unrest, including large-scale displacement, loss of life, and widespread destruction of property, following significant domestic political changes. These crises have compounded the effects of recurring climate-related shocks affecting large parts of the country. In November 2020, conflict erupted in the northern Tigray region, triggering significant displacement across Tigray, Amhara, and Afar regions. Since August 2023, renewed conflict in Amhara has further intensified humanitarian needs, leading to the declaration of a state of emergency and restrictions on movement across the region. Together, these crises have severely disrupted livelihoods, constrained access to essential goods and staple commodities, and increased the vulnerability of affected populations, placing additional pressure on humanitarian response capacities across the country.

## **JOB PROFILE**

The Senior Data Analyst / Data Specialist position is based in Kampala, with possible travel to Addis Ababa. The position is fully dedicated to the Ethiopia mission and will report directly to the Deputy Country Representative. The postholder will lead the mission’s data team, coordinating its work across the Sectoral, Intersectoral and PANDA units in close collaboration with Research Managers, the GIS Specialist and relevant HQ technical teams.

The postholder will provide technical leadership and backstopping throughout the research cycle, from methodology and sampling design to data collection, cleaning, analysis, validation and dissemination. The role is responsible for coordinating data officers and interns, agreeing priorities and resource needs with Research Managers, maintaining reusable analysis systems, and ensuring compliance with IMPACT research standards and data protection requirements. The appointment level will depend on the selected candidate’s experience and technical skills; both profiles will carry responsibility for leading the data team.

During the assignment, the Senior Data Analyst / Data Specialist will be hosted by Acted, IMPACT's global partner, and will be under the responsibility of its delegates for all administrative, security, logistics and financial matters. The postholder will fully comply with Acted and IMPACT rules and procedures, including those relating to data protection and information security.

## **RESPONSIBILITIES**

- **Planning and coordination:** Estimate deadlines and resource requirements for each research cycle across the Sectoral, Intersectoral and PANDA units. Coordinate team members’ workloads, agree data team priorities with Research Managers, and flag risks, capacity gaps and delays early, in writing, to the relevant Research Managers and direct manager.
- **Research design:** Support assessment teams in designing methodologies, sampling strategies (including sample size calculations and survey weighting), data analysis plans and data collection tools, in line with IMPACT research standards.
- **Data collection and cleaning:** Oversee the review, testing and deployment of XLSForms on IMPACT’s Kobo server, data checks during collection, and data cleaning in line with IMPACT’s Data Cleaning Minimum Standards. Where relevant, train enumerators and partner staff on data checks and cleaning.
- **Analysis systems:** Maintain and develop the mission’s R-based cleaning and analysis workflows, including IMPACT R packages, templates and Shiny applications, under version control and with up-to-date documentation so that they can be reused across research cycles.
- **Information products:** Review country-level information products and dissemination strategies to maximise the use of findings, in accordance with IMPACT research standards and in close coordination with the direct manager.
- **Data quality:** Improve data quality and monitoring at country level, including resolving discrepancies, keeping geospatial and administrative reference data up to date in coordination with GIS colleagues, and ensuring collected data is correctly georeferenced.
- **Data protection:** Ensure compliance with IMPACT’s data protection policy and SOP on personally identifiable information in all research cycles. This includes anonymisation and disclosure-risk checks before any dataset is shared, secure transfer, storage and deletion of data, and compliance with data-sharing or data processing agreements with partners.
- **Capacity building:** Lead the development and implementation of an ongoing capacity-building plan for country data officers and interns, with support from relevant technical colleagues and HQ teams. Provide training, mentoring and regular feedback on data cleaning, analysis and tools, and coordinate with Research Managers on staff development and performance.
- **Partner engagement:** At the request of the line manager, support partners on data processing, data sharing and the use of findings, and represent IMPACT on data matters in relevant coordination forums.

***DELIVERABLES***

- Lead weekly data team meetings, maintain a shared task tracker with clear responsibilities and agreed timelines, and follow up on progress and outstanding actions.
- Provide technical guidance to data officers and interns on cleaning, analysis and troubleshooting, implement and track the capacity-building plan, and provide input to their performance appraisals in coordination with Research Managers.
- Regularly liaise with project focal points and Research Managers to monitor deadlines and resource needs, anticipate delays, and communicate risks and agreed corrective actions in writing.
- Conduct internal technical validation of all research cycles, including review of sampling, data collection tools, cleaning and analysis outputs, to ensure alignment with IMPACT/HQ guidelines before submission to HQ for validation.
- Ensure regular maintenance of all mission dashboards, including Power BI and Shiny, and contribute to the design and development of new dashboards when required.
- Keep documentation, including READMEs, SOPs and decision logs, up to date for all workflows and dashboards maintained by the data team, with code under version control and clear maintenance responsibilities.
- For every dataset shared outside IMPACT, document the anonymisation applied, disclosure-risk checks and transfer, in line with the relevant agreement and applicable IMPACT procedures.

## **REQUIRED SKILLSET**

- At least 3 years of relevant professional experience in data management and analysis, preferably in humanitarian settings.
- A master’s degree in a relevant discipline, such as statistics, data science or social sciences, is preferred.
- Fluency in English is required.
- Excellent communication and data visualisation skills.
- Strong skills in R and in data cleaning and survey analysis workflows; familiarity with IMPACT’s R packages is an asset.
- Proven skills in Power BI and R Shiny.
- Experience with KoboToolbox or ODK and XLSForm design.
- Sound knowledge of sampling methods, sample size calculations and survey weighting.
- Experience with Git/GitHub; GIS skills in QGIS or ArcGIS are an asset.
- Knowledge of humanitarian data protection practice, including anonymisation of microdata and disclosure-risk assessment.
- Experience supervising or mentoring data staff, including remotely.
- Ability to manage multiple priorities across many research cycles, at times under tight deadlines.
- Strong ability to work independently in support of colleagues and partners.
- Ability to work in an intercultural environment.
- Previous experience in Ethiopia or the Horn of Africa is highly preferred.

## **COMPENSATION & BENEFITS**

- For this position, salary between 2’580 CHF and 2’640 CHF monthly (before income tax), etc as well as a monthly living allowance of 300 USD NB - IMPACT salaries are strictly determined by our salary grid depending on the grade of the position and the level of education of staff. A location-dependent security and/or isolation adjustment is then applied as a recognition that some staff are required to work in difficult places where living and working conditions are much more difficult than elsewhere.
- Accommodation and food provided in the guesthouse.
- Enrolment in Swiss private pension fund (Swisslife – approx. 9.975% of staff gross salary), health insurance, life insurance and repatriation assistance.
- Flight tickets every 6 months & visa fees covered (in-country travel costs and professional expenses are fully covered).
- Contribution to the luggage transportation: between 20 and 100 kgs, depending on the length of the contract (+ luggage and personal property insurance)
- Annual leave of 36 days per year. Public holidays of the country of assignment. Family/compassionate leave when applicable.
- Predeparture induction - 3 days at IMPACT Initiatives’s HQ in Geneva + one week pre-departure training in ACTED HQ in Paris, including a 4-days in situ security training;
- IMPACT prioritizes the psychological safety of its staff and the health insurance provided covers, among others, up to 1000 € per year of psychosocial counselling fees.

title: Youth Services Specialist
body:
**This position is open to candidates with existing work authorization in the location where the position is advertised.**

**Job Overview:** The Youth Services Specialist supports IRC's Refugee School Impact (RSI) program, helping ORR-eligible refugee students (ages 6-18) and their parents or guardians’ access and succeed in the U.S. education system. The Specialist helps families enroll their children in school, leads student and parent orientations, provides after-school tutoring and academic support during the school year, and runs a summer academic program. The Specialist also checks in regularly with students to track academic progress and coordinates with school staff, community partners, and the Education & Youth Services Manager to keep services aligned with program goals.

**Major Responsibilities:**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Assist newly arrived ORR-eligible families with school enrollment for children ages 6–18, including interpretation support as needed.
- Provide school orientation to enrolled students and lead Extended School Orientation workshops for parents and guardians, covering topics such as school choice, transportation, attendance, and how to support their child's education.
- Coordinate with Jefferson County Public Schools (JCPS) Office of Multilingual Learners and other school staff to identify enrollment issues early and keep teachers informed of students' academic progress.
- Support families choosing private schools, homeschools, or districts outside JCPS, including newly arrived refugee families served through the Program of Initial Resettlement.
- Deliver the after-school program twice a week during the school year, providing tutoring in reading and writing and other academic support, with the help of interns or volunteers.
- Conduct regular one-on-one check-ins with students at school to track grades, homework completion, and attendance, and coordinate with teachers to address concerns early.
- Refer students and families to IRC programs or other community resources when needs arise outside of school.
- Plan and lead the summer academic program, including academic reinforcement, enrichment activities, field trips, and transportation to and from students' homes.
- Maintain accurate and timely documentation of services, referrals, and orientations in ClientTrack.
- Assist in the recruitment, training, and supervision of interns or other youth program staff.
- Attend regular meetings with the Education & Youth Services Manager to discuss programming and any concerns.
- Support case closures, transition planning, and other closeout activities as the program year winds down.
- Other duties as assigned.

**Job Requirements:**

**Education:** Bachelor’s degree in social work, education, or a related field of study preferred.

**Work Experience:**

- Experience working with refugee, immigrant, or other multicultural youth and families, preferably in a school, resettlement, or case management setting.

**Demonstrated Skills & Competencies:**

- Demonstrated success working and communicating effectively in a multicultural environment.
- Self-starter with excellent problem-solving skills combined with the proven ability to prioritize and manage time effectively.
- Attention to detail and accuracy in work product.
- Fluent in English, both spoken and written; proficiency in language(s) spoken by client group is desired.
- Proficient in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Outlook); ability to use the internet and other digital tools for data entry, research, and problem-solving purposes.
- Familiarity with the U.S. education system, or willingness to learn local school district processes and requirements, is preferred. Experience with a client database system (such as ClientTrack) is a plus.
- Valid driver’s license and access to a personal, insured vehicle, with the ability to transport clients as needed.
- Required to drive clients for school enrollment, summer programs, and after school.
- First Aid and CPR certification preferred (or willingness to obtain before the start of the program).

**Working Environment:**

- A combination of standard office environment, remote work, and ‘field’ time within the service delivery area to perform the above-outlined responsibilities.
- Occasional domestic (non-local) travel required; up to 10%.
- May require occasional weekend and/or evening work.

***This position is expected to end on September 30, 2027.***

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $21-$23/hr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

title: ESOL Instructor
body:
This position is represented by the OPEIU union and subject to the terms and conditions of a collective bargaining agreement.

The ESOL Instructor is responsible for providing integrated English language instruction for non-native English speakers. The instructor must be able to successfully develop and tailor curriculum and materials to the needs of students enrolled into the program including the support of student recruitment, registration, attendance tracking, retention, progress, and assessment.

In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.
