title: Program Development and Awards Advisor, WACAR
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

***The IRC is seeking two (2) Program Development & Award Advisors. These positions are open to candidates in the West and Central Africa Region (WACAR), or other IRC locations in GMT and EAT time zones, who have significant experience working in West and Central Africa countries. Candidates based in these countries are encouraged to apply.***

**BACKGROUND**

Over the past 80 years, the International Rescue Committee (IRC) has developed unparalleled expertise in responding to emergencies and helping uprooted communities to rebuild. Founded in 1933 at the request of Albert Einstein, the IRC’s mission is to help people whose lives and livelihoods are shattered by conflict and disaster to survive, recover, and gain control of their future. The International Rescue Committee is on the ground in more than 40 countries, providing emergency relief and rebuilding lives in the wake of disaster. Through 28 regional offices in cities across the United States, the IRC also helps refugees resettle in the US and become self-sufficient. The IRC is committed to a culture of bold leadership, innovation in all aspects of our work, creative partnerships and, most crucially, accountability to those we serve. The IRC is a tireless advocate for the most vulnerable.

**Crisis Response, Recovery and Development Department (CRRD)**

The Crisis Response, Recovery and Development Department (CRRD) have a growing portfolio of humanitarian relief, post-crisis recovery, and development programs under their remit. This work focuses support in five key areas: ensuring safety from harm, improving health, increasing access to education, improving economic well-being and ensuring people have the power to influence decisions that affect their lives. In all these programs, there is a drive to address the unique needs of women and girls (who represent the majority of those displaced) – and the universal barriers they face.

**The Awards Management Unit (AMU)** is one of four pillars within CRRD**.** The unit is responsible for identifying, securing, and supporting the management of all funding from statutory/government donors. The AMU is a bridge between donors and country programs: providing expert technical advice to the country teams, while maintaining portfolio-level visibility to ensure consistency and compliance and manage risk. This pillar ensures that donor compliance policies and procedures are implemented consistently and supports all staff working across the award management cycle for all restricted funding from global government sources.

**West and Central Africa Regional Overview**

The West and Central Africa Region (WACAR) supports effective, efficient, and high-quality programming by strengthening capacity around client outcomes, program quality, strategic positioning, and business development. It addresses overlapping humanitarian and development challenges—conflict, weak governance, and environmental degradation—through integrated, impactful approaches.

WACAR prioritizes cross-learning, innovation, and harmonized technical strategies, especially in high-need areas. It ensures continuity of care and coordinated service delivery for clients on the move, while advancing strategic donor engagement through cohesive fundraising and regional collaboration.

The regional team responds swiftly to country program needs, filling critical gaps and navigating access constraints, emergencies, and security shifts. It amplifies client and frontline voices to inform global advocacy and fosters strong team cohesion to enhance program delivery. WACAR focuses on cost-efficient and adaptive approaches to the evolving humanitarian and donor landscape, with a clear focus on resourcing country programs.

WACAR comprises Burkina Faso, Burundi, Cameroon and CAR, Chad, Cote d’Ivoire, DRC, Mali, Niger, Nigeria.

**The Purpose of the Role**

As part of the Regional Program and Award Support (RPAS) team, the PDAAs oversee a diverse portfolio of awards across the humanitarian, recovery, and development sectors. PDAAs liaise with country programs, HQ departments and donor contacts to ensure high-quality guidance and support to country offices throughout the award lifecycle.

These roles will support country programs in the West and Central Africa region (WACAR) with donor compliance, award management, and producing high-quality donor deliverables. They will advise on IRC’s partnership system (PEERS), manage donor relationships including with HQ counterparts.

In addition, these roles will support WACAR country programs in securing funding for their programmes, through supporting and leading pursuit of new funding opportunities, in line with IRC’s Business Development Strategy. Support includes all phases of the business development process, from opportunity identification to contract signature, including pre-positioning, partnerships building, proposal development, and due diligence phases.

Successful candidates will have a strong track record of contributing to new humanitarian and development funding opportunities, deep knowledge of donor rules and regulations, and experience collaborating with local partner organizations.

**Scope and Authority**

These roles have no line management responsibilities.

**Key Working Relationships**

These positions will report jointly to the Senior Program and Awards Advisor (SPAA) and the Head of Business Development (HBD) for the WACAR region and work closely with RPAS team members, country program grants and partnership teams, and across all teams within the Awards Management Unit, Crisis Response Recovery and Development Department, Global Supply Chain, Finance, Office of General Counsel, Technical Excellence, and other key departments within IRC. PDAAs also serve as donor and partner points of contact as applicable per region.

KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES

***Awards Management and Compliance***

- Manage a portfolio of awards for the WACAR region as assigned.
- Provide timely support on narrative reporting and post-award deliverables, guiding country offices on amendments, modifications, and submissions while collaborating with technical and financial staff.
- Provide support on budget realignments, changes in scope, NCEs, and other amendments for project elements not captured at proposal stage or emerging needs.
- Serve as first point of contact for country program-based awards staff to problem solve, guide and advise them on compliance post-award issues within the mentioned portfolio and to act as a connecting point between country program and other AMU teams to facilitate the timely flow of key information between them.
- Manage donor relationships by maintaining communication on contractual issues, updates on program implementation and following up on compliance queries and securing changes and approvals as needed.
- With support from the Program & Awards Officer (PAO), guide and coach country offices on partner management policies and PEER system compliance, and review and process sub-grants/partnership agreements. Coordinate with the Sub-awards and Partnerships (S&P) team as needed.
- Provide support to and monitor projects to ensure compliance with donor guidelines and IRC internal requirements. Monitoring awards can take the shape of monitoring visits, project implementation meetings and targeted calls following specific donor internal guidelines and IRC established processes.
- In collaboration with other regional team members, monitor award spending and help problem-solve for under-/over-spending. Partner with country programs and regional team as needed, to address implementations challenges.
- Provide technical advice to country offices on ad-hoc queries on donor compliance issues in coordination with AMU’s Compliance and Policy team on non-routine and high-level compliance matters and escalate to leadership for support as needed.
- Take part in meetings and calls with country teams where required to provide support and collaborate closely on specific issues related to donor compliance, submissions and/or monitoring/award management.
- Ensure lessons learned from finalized projects are fed back into new Business Development.
- Advise and support country programs appropriately to enable them to successfully follow internal IRC policies and procedures and maintain the integrity of awards-related data (e.g. OTIS, PEERS).
- Stay informed about programmatic issues and security and political developments affecting implementation.
- Coordinate with other members of the Regional Program and Award Support (RPAS) Team and other AMU members for information sharing and establishing a coherent awards support.
- Ensure proper donor-related and contractual documentation to support compliance and audit readiness (including maintaining up-to-date, organized award files).
- Participate in the recruitment of and the onboarding of new CP Grants Coordinators/Heads of Grants teams.
- Contribute to the development of training materials, and deliver training to in-country staff, as required and in coordination with the Director, Awards Management (DAM) and Program and Award Support (PAS) team leaders. In coordination with the DAM and PAS leaders, develop and maintain work-processes and checklists for award implementation and report review, as well as record lessons learned.
- Onboard new country office Grants and Partnerships staff and new PAS team members to assigned donors, policies and/or IRC processes, as requested.
- Mentor and coach Grants and Partnerships staff on IRC systems and processes to ensure capacity is built at country level.
- Contribute to AMU and regional strategic priorities and initiatives.
- Other duties as assigned by supervisor.

***Business Development***

- undefined
- Help drive business development in the region by providing effective proposal support, ranging from direct proposal management to light quality assurance.
- Support country offices with donor engagement, intel sharing and positioning with prioritized donors in the PDAA portfolio; prepare for and participate in donor calls as needed.
- Represent IRC externally at country-specific meetings, with donors and stakeholder networks in donor capitals as needed.
- Coordinate proposal development, including sharing initial assessments of new opportunities, preparing timelines, ensuring the proposal team adheres to deadlines, supporting recruitment, assisting in budget development, ensuring document completion, organizing meetings and compiling notes, and drafting and proofreading proposal sections.
- Collaborate with regional technical leads and technical advisors, country offices, and other colleagues to support conceptualization of winning proposals and designs for new project activities and/or amendments to current projects.
- Provide quality assurance and quality compliance support on proposals. Ensure responsiveness to and compliance with solicitation documents and with IRC’s requirements, including the PEER system.
- Lead or support coordination, communication, and inputs from consortium partners in accordance with donor and IRC processes.
- Coordinate and support regional reviews and approvals of proposal packages depending on country and regional needs. This includes partners’ packages if applicable.
- Review agreements to ensure accurateness and highlight key compliance requirements, in coordination with compliance and country grants teams and support in award negotiation and hand-over as required.
- Work with RPAS to incorporate lessons learned from implementation at the proposal stage.
- Maintain complete and accurate electronic files, including final submission packages and internal trackers.
- Deploying offices to lead proposal development as available and needed.
- Facilitate internal post-submission debrief sessions with country teams, technical units, regional team and other relevant stakeholders to collect lessons learned.

**PERSON SPECIFICATION**

**Essential**

Skills, Knowledge and Qualifications:

- Degree, preferably in a subject related to IRC’s work (International Relations, Refugee or Migration Studies, Development Studies, Public Policy) or equivalent experience
- \*\*Fluency in English and French, both spoken and written
- \*\*Good understanding of humanitarian aid and development programming
- Ability to work collaboratively as part of a diverse team and handle a multifaceted workload
- Good financial management and budgeting skills
- Ability to analyze and synthesize information
- Proven organizational skills, detail-oriented, ability to prioritize tasks, and to learn quickly
- Excellent interpersonal and communication skills: the ability to successfully and effectively liaise with people within and across departments in a multi-cultural environment.
- Ability to work independently in a very fast paced environment
- A flexible and calm work attitude
- International work experience in the Global South is a plus
- Excellent IT skills (Word, Outlook, Excel)
- Ability to travel internationally, sometimes on short notice and to insecure areas (15%)

Experience:

- Experience with and a strong understanding of institutional donors’ compliance requirements, e.g. UN, World Bank, US government, and/or European government donors (experience with all is not required, but a good mix would be a strong asset)
- Working at a distance and supporting country-based staff
- Writing, reviewing and editing narrative and financial reports and excellent attention to detail
- Working on new funding opportunities in the humanitarian and international development sectors with a range of multilateral and bilateral donors (FCDO, EU and ECHO, GFFO, BMZ, Sida, SDC, World Bank, US Department of State, etc.), as well as experience collaborating with local partner organizations.
- Experience with strategies and proposal processes of key government/statutory donors – US, UK, EU, German, Scandinavian, etc.

**Compensation (UK):** (GBP 52,210 -GBP 58,000). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

title: Emergency Response Team Protection Coordinator
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**FLUENCY IN WRITTEN & SPOKEN FRENCH & ENGLISH REQUIRED.**

**Job Overview:**

Responding to the world’s worst humanitarian crises in a great variety of roles, the International Rescue Committee’s staff is a force for humanity and hope. If you are skilled and passionate, we would like to add your energy to ours. Through its Emergency Unit (EmU), the IRC is one of the world’s largest humanitarian agencies leading rapid emergency responses that provide life-saving assistance, early recovery, and stabilization support to people affected by conflict, displacement, natural disasters, and complex emergencies across multiple contexts worldwide. We are committed to innovation, agility, and strong partnerships to deliver timely and effective humanitarian action.

Active in public health, education in emergencies, livelihoods, women's empowerment, youth development, and protection and promotion of rights, we assist people from harm to home. The IRC recognizes that people affected by crisis and the actors closest to them are best placed, have the right, and should have the power and resources to respond and drive lasting change. We commit to increasing the share of funding channeled to local actors in emergencies, asking “Why not partner?’ whenever we plan programming, and partner as equals.

The Violence Prevention and Response in Emergencies (VPRIE) team sits jointly within IRC's Emergency Unit (EmU) and IRC’s Protection Unit. With few predictable, effective protection providers in emergencies, major gaps remain in delivering life-saving and life-sustaining VPR interventions at scale. VPRIE programming in acute emergencies spans integrated protection, Child Protection (CP), Women's Protection and Empowerment (WPE)/Gender-Based Violence (GBV), and Protection Rule of Law (PROL), focusing on four core service offerings: Social Work in Emergencies, Focused MHPSS Interventions, Responsive Information Services in Emergencies, and Community Risk Mitigation and Access. These complementary, mutually reinforcing interventions address the most urgent protection threats facing emergency-affected communities in all their diversity.

**Scope of Work**

The Emergency Response Team (ERT) is a specialized group within the Emergency Unit (EmU), deployed to support existing country programs in emergency response or to launch new programs in crisis zones. The team's core responsibility is to rapidly and effectively design, develop, and manage the IRC's on-site humanitarian response to meet the immediate needs of the affected population, while also transferring responsibilities and knowledge to long-term staff to ensure continuity of IRC programming and operations.

All ERT staff must be prepared to deploy to the site of an emergency within 72 hours of notification and should expect to spend up to 65% of their time in the field, in either an emergency or roving capacity.

The ERT Protection Coordinator (Child Protection) will be responsible for starting up and leading integrated protection and/or child protection programming in acute emergency responses. This may include rapid assessment, program start-up, strategy development, proposal development, technical oversight, staff recruitment and management, budget management, grants compliance and local partner relations. When not deployed, the ERT Protection Coordinator will contribute to IRC's strategic objectives and technical workstreams for CP and violence prevention and response in emergencies. A successful candidate will demonstrate a track record of working independently in fast-paced environments and applying creative, flexible design to protection programming in acute emergency contexts.

**Major Responsibilities:**

***Emergency Responses:***

**Context Evaluation**

- Following the onset of an emergency, identify areas with greatest impact, highest needs, and emerging safety protection risks for diverse populations (integrated protection, CP, WPE / GBV, PROL), including specific protection risks for young children, adolescents, and families, and care arrangements
- Conduct stakeholder analysis: continually review existing actor mapping with a view to identifying key actors and establishing partnerships with focused on the delivery of protection services
- Design and conduct multisector needs assessments

**Program design and management**

- Provide strategic direction, leadership and overall technical management of IRC’s protection response aligned to the response strategy and emergency safety outcomes, while ensuring high program quality and alignment with IRC’s standards and approaches
- Lead and directly contribute to the start-up, implementation and coordination of emergency protection programming, including (depending on the context): emergency case management; support to Unaccompanied and Separated Children (UASC), including Family Tracing and Reunification (FTR) and alternative care; cash for protection; rapid group MHPSS interventions; emergency safety and wellbeing sessions; two-way, responsive information services; community-based protection and risk mitigation; group cash transfers for community-led protection actions; and safe, inclusive programming and protection mainstreaming.
- In collaboration with partners, develop a VPRIE strategy to respond to identified protection risks and needs, outlining a problem statement, response modalities, activity sequencing, and required resources
- In collaboration with response leadership and technical coordinators, input into the design of an overall emergency response strategy, including partnerships so that the IRC is working in ways that are complementary to and in support of partners and child protection actors
- Participate in cross-departmental collaboration and coordination with other sector colleagues to ensure that linkages between programs are made and programs gain from protection best practice
- Ensure – through program design and practice, team capacity and behavior – that clients, including young children, adolescents, and caregivers, participate in the design and implementation of IRC programs, and that their access to services and programs is meaningful and safe
- Develop and/or adapt technical tools and approaches, and deliver creative solutions to mitigate challenges in the operating context, to facilitate response start-up and day to day implementation
- Support emergency protection staff to implement and monitor work plans ensuring that activities reflect the commitments IRC made to the donor and the community
- Oversee IRC’s relationship with partners, ensuring co-design, regular exchange, and project performance monitoring to achieve program objectives
- Design and implement appropriate monitoring and evaluation (M&E) systems ensuring consistent reporting and analysis of results to improve program effectiveness and quality
- Provide a comprehensive handover to successor, including ensuring transfer of all related documentation, program data and staff performance information

**Grant and financial management**

- Manage emergency grant/program implementation including recruitment and training, work plan development, procurement and inventory planning, budget management, and M&E plans
- Develop high quality technical proposals and reports with relevant program staff in line with IRC and donor requirements
- Collaborate with IRC grants and finance staff to finalize proposals and respond to any requests for additional information

**Staff management**

- Recruit, onboard, and supervise emergency protection staff, and provide ongoing training and targeted capacity building, including technical guidance, on the job coaching and supervision, and capacity development plans on technical and managerial skills
- Comply with and ensure that new protection staff understand the IRC Code of Conduct and policies related to Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse and Child Safeguarding. This includes ensuring that staff and communities have knowledge of and safe, confidential access to reporting mechanisms and support services
- Maintain open and professional relations with team members, promoting a strong team spirit and providing oversight and guidance to enable staff to successfully perform in their positions

**Coordination and representation**

- Actively develop and maintain effective working relationships with key actors, including donors, government actors, UN agencies, international and local NGOs, and other relevant actors
- Regularly attend emergency protection coordination and task force meetings, at appropriate levels to feed in IRC priorities from the field
- Ensure protection concerns and challenges are brought to relevant fora to advocate for standards and procedures that systematize how protection programming is implemented and coordinated at the field level

***Technical support and guidance***

When not deployed, the ERT Protection Coordinator (CP) will:

- Contribute to IRC’s strategic priorities for violence prevention and response in emergencies, and lead on CP-specific ambitions, including: refining emergency CP program models, toolkits, and technical guidance; supporting emergency preparedness and readiness; contributing to integrated and multi-sectoral program design, etc.
- Provide technical support, coaching, and backstopping to CP-centered emergency responses in countries with existing IRC programming, as needed
- Participate in cross-departmental collaboration and coordination with WPE, PROL, Education / ECD, and other sector colleagues to ensure that linkages between programs are made and programs gain from protection best practice
- Represent acute emergency approaches and priorities within IRC’s global CP team, including liaising and coordinating with CP TAs and Global Practice Lead, contributing to IRC’s global CP ambitions and representation as needed
- Contribute to delivery of IRC’s Emergency and Humanitarian Action strategic action plan and commitments to partnerships, safeguarding, and Diversity, Equality, and Inclusion (DEI)

**Job Requirements:**

- Post-graduate degree in social work, psychology, international humanitarian law, other related field, or equivalent work experience
- At least five years’ experience working in the field of Protection, Child Protection, or WPE / GBV programming at the Coordinator level or above required, with proven track record managing multi-donor portfolios in acute emergency response, program and project start-up
- Experience working with IRC and an understanding of IRC’s systems and processes is strongly preferred
- Familiarity with key donor regulations such as UNHCR, FCDO, BPRM and ECHO
- Experience in working with and coordinating with the UN, donors, INGOs and other humanitarian actors
- Demonstrated experience in staff supervision, capacity building, project design and budget management
- Proven leadership of multi-disciplinary, cross-cultural teams, with strong mentoring, coaching, motivational, and team-building skills.
- Demonstrated commitment to inclusion and fair treatment of staff, and ability to identify and address barriers to inclusion for marginalized groups in emergency response.

title: Career Development Specialist, NVPPA
body:
**This position is open to candidates with existing work authorization in the location where the position is advertised.**

**Program Background:**

The National Virtual Program for Professional Advancement (NVPPA) is a nationwide, fully virtual program through which the International Rescue Committee (IRC) serves newly arrived refugees under a cooperative agreement with the Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR). Participants receive career navigation, training, job placement support, and direct financial assistance to advance an individualized career goal. NVPPA operates alongside other federally funded programs, such as initial resettlement services and Matching Grant, and is designed to complement rather than replace or duplicate these programs.

**Job Overview**

The Career Development Specialist is the participant's primary point of contact in the program, working remotely with refugees across the country by phone, video, and online tools. From intake and eligibility verification through an approved Professional Advancement Plan (PAP), this position guides each participant toward their career goal, whether that means finding a training partner, completing credential evaluation and recertification, or moving forward with an approved vehicle purchase. The role coordinates closely with the Economic Empowerment Technical Unit, administrative and job development staff, and external resettlement partners to ensure participants move smoothly between services, while maintaining accurate case records and documentation in Efforts to Outcomes (ETO) in line with ORR reporting requirements and IRC financial controls.

**Major responsibilities:**

**Outreach and Intake**

- Conduct virtual outreach, intake, and enrollment for eligible participants, including verifying eligibility documentation.
- Coordinate with IRC offices, resettlement agencies, and local partners to identify and connect with eligible participants.

**Career Navigation**

- Complete a skills assessment with each participant and develop an individualized Professional Advancement Plan (PAP) that defines their career goal, pathway, and planned use of direct financial assistance.
- Review the PAP with each participant, provide feedback on the career goal, and confirm that proposed use of funds meets ORR eligible-use requirements.
- Provide ongoing navigation by phone and video to help participants access training, credential evaluation and recertification, and other approved supports.
- Research career advancement, certification, and vocational education opportunities across state and local labor markets.
- Connect participants to resources and services within IRC and in their local communities.
- Maintain working knowledge of credential evaluation services and state licensing requirements in high-demand fields, and carry a caseload of participants pursuing those pathways.

**Coordination**

- Work with the Economic Empowerment Technical Unit, Administrative Staff, and Job Development staff so participants move smoothly between navigation, training, and placement services, and to ensure financial assistance requests align with approved PAPs.
- Coordinate with other service providers, including PIR providers and Matching Grant employment specialists, to support co-enrollment and avoid duplication of services.

**Compliance**

- Maintain accurate, timely case files in Efforts to Outcomes (ETO), including documentation and the service and outcome data required for ORR reporting.
- Ensure documentation for each financial assistance request is complete before submission, consistent with IRC financial controls.

- Experience managing a high-volume caseload, with strong organization, prioritization, time management, and follow-through.
- Ability to build and maintain productive internal and external relationships.
- Ability to research and navigate workforce, education, and social service systems in unfamiliar local markets.
- Proficiency with Microsoft Office, video conferencing, and remote collaboration tools, and with tracking and reporting information in a database.
- Commitment to anti-racism, ongoing learning, and equitable service to all eligible clients.

title: Education and Child Protection Officer (Training Facilitator)
body:
The **International Rescue Committee (IRC)** responds to the world’s most pressing humanitarian crises and helps people whose lives and livelihoods have been shattered by conflict and disaster. In Poland, IRC is supporting refugees and host communities with economic recovery, livelihood programs, and social protection initiatives to foster resilience and self-reliance.

**JOB OVERVIEW:**

REAL Talk is a two-year, EU-funded project that prevents gender-based violence (GBV) and cyber GBV among adolescents aged 11–16 in Poland, Italy and Estonia. It works with adolescents and with the adults around them: caregivers, especially fathers and male caregivers, and school staff and educators. IRC Poland leads the project’s work with caregivers and delivers all activities in Poland, together with IRC Italia (coordinator), Una Casa per l’Uomo, the University of Tartu and the International Child Development Initiatives (ICDI).

The **Education and Child Protection Officer (Training Facilitator)** is IRC Poland’s facilitator for REAL Talk. Working in tandem with another facilitator, the post holder delivers sessions of the project’s Cross-Cultural Socio-Emotional and Relational Education Model: dedicated sessions for adolescent boys, the “Cycle of Aware Fatherhood” workshops for fathers and male caregivers, and training for teachers and educators. The post holder also takes part in the project’s mandatory transnational training for facilitators, which starts on 12 November 2026.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

**1. Facilitation and delivery**

- Facilitate sessions of the Model with adolescents aged 11–16 at the partner school: dedicated sessions for boys, and mixed-gender groups co-facilitated with the female facilitator. Groups have 10–15 adolescents and follow a series of 5–8 sessions of 100–120 minutes, reaching around 40 adolescents in Poland.
- Deliver the “Cycle of Aware Fatherhood”: a series of 4–6 workshops of 60–90 minutes for small groups of 3–8 fathers and male caregivers (around 15 in total), on masculinity, emotional literacy, non-violent role modelling and parenting in the digital age.
- Co-facilitate, with the female facilitator, mixed-gender information sessions for parents and caregivers on adolescent relationship violence, social media and online safety (around 80 caregivers).
- Co-deliver training for school staff (around 30 teachers, in groups of about 10) and online basic training sessions for educators across Poland (around 80 participants).
- Create a safe, trauma-informed and non-judgmental space in every session. Respond to disclosures following IRC procedures and refer participants to support services through the agreed referral pathways.

**2. Preparation and learning**

- Take part in, and prepare for, the mandatory transnational capacity-building sessions for facilitators (online, in English). The first session is on 12 November 2026, and further sessions follow through January 2027.
- Study the Model and adapt session plans and materials to the Polish context and to participants with migrant or refugee backgrounds, together with the female facilitator and the project lead.
- Prepare sessions, materials and logistics, and stay in contact with participants, especially fathers, in line with the project’s engagement and retention strategy for caregivers.
- In November 2026, support colleagues, where needed, in focus group discussions and key informant interviews for the project’s research on online masculinity norms.

**3. Partnerships and coordination**

- Coordinate with the partner school (leadership, teachers and school counsellors) on schedules, venues, consent procedures and the recruitment of participants.
- Plan, deliver and debrief sessions jointly with the female facilitator, and exchange practice with facilitators from the project’s partner organizations in Italy and Estonia.
- When requested, support other REAL Talk activities in Poland, such as consultations with adolescents and caregivers, the Champions workshop, the national webinar and the study visit to Poland.

**4. Monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning (MEAL), safeguarding and compliance**

- Administer pre- and post-session questionnaires and feedback tools, and collect signed attendance lists and consent forms, following MEAL guidance and data protection (GDPR) requirements.
- Record sex-disaggregated session data and write short session reports. Contribute lessons learned to the project’s deliverables and donor reports.
- Apply the IRC Child Safeguarding Policy, the IRC Poland Child Protection Response Procedure and the IRC Way standards at all times. Report any concern immediately to the Protection and Safeguarding Coordinator.
- Make sure session materials carry the EU funding acknowledgement required by the donor.
- Mainstream gender equality, inclusion and a Do No Harm approach in all activities.
- Carry out other duties assigned by the supervisor, within the scope of the project.

**WORKING CONDITIONS**

- **Working time:** part-time. The indicative workload is around 230 hours over the assignment; the exact working time is confirmed in the offer.
- **November 2026 – January 2027:** onboarding, five online transnational training sessions of about two hours each (the first on 12 November 2026) and, if needed, support to the research activities. The successful candidate must be able to start in time for the first session.
- **February – May 2027 (dates to be confirmed):** delivery of sessions with adolescents, fathers, parents, teachers and educators, as the partner school is confirmed and the school semester allows. The rest of the assignment covers follow-up and reporting.

**JOB REQUIREMENTS**

**Education**

- Bachelor’s degree (Master’s preferred) in education, pedagogy, psychology, social work, sociology, gender studies or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. Additional training in facilitation, child protection or trauma-informed practice is an asset.

**Experience**

- At least 2 years of experience facilitating group sessions or workshops with adolescents and/or adults (such as parents or teachers) in a school, NGO, youth or community setting.
- Experience addressing sensitive topics, such as relationships, consent, violence, masculinity or online risks, in a participatory and non-judgmental way.
- Experience in gender equality, GBV prevention, engaging men and boys, positive parenting or child protection is strongly preferred.
- Familiarity with approaches such as Engaging Men through Accountable Practice (EMAP), Engaging Adolescent Boys in Accountable Practice (EABAP) or My Safety, My Wellbeing is an asset.
- Experience working with refugee or migrant communities, or in EU- or donor-funded projects, is an asset.

**Skills and competencies**

- Strong facilitation skills: able to build trust quickly with adolescent boys, fathers and teachers, and to manage group dynamics.
- Commitment to gender equality, an anti-racist and Do No Harm approach, and to modelling respectful behaviour. Ability to work in close tandem with a co-facilitator and in an international team.
- Good planning and organizational skills, attention to detail and reliable record keeping.
- Good digital skills: Microsoft Office, Teams, Zoom or Google Meet, confidence delivering online sessions, and an understanding of social media and online safety.
- Languages: Polish (fluent or native) and English (upper-intermediate or higher, as the transnational training is delivered in English). Ukrainian and/or Russian is an asset.
- Willingness to travel within Poland, and to deliver some sessions in the late afternoon or evening.
- Right to work in Poland.

Appointment is subject to the safeguarding screening for work with minors required by Polish law and IRC policy, including a certificate from the National Criminal Register, a check in the Register of Sexual Offenders and, where applicable, certificates from other countries of residence.

*We encourage male candidates to apply as the sessions are to be delivered to adolescent boys.*

title: Mozambique - Head of Finance and Administrative department (M/F) - PEMBA
body:
## About us

**Desired start date: 03/01/2027**  
**Duration of the mission: 6 months**  
**Location: Pemba**

**SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL (SI)** is an international humanitarian aid association which, since more than 40 years, has been providing assistance to populations affected by armed conflicts and natural disasters by meeting their basic needs for food, water and shelter. Particularly committed to the fight against diseases linked to unsafe water, the leading cause of death in the world, SI's interventions provide expertise in the field of access to drinking water, sanitation and hygiene promotion, but also in the essential area of food security and livelihoods. Present in 26 countries, the SI teams – 3200 people in total, made up of expatriates, national staff, permanent staff at HQ, and a few volunteers - intervene with professionalism and commitment while respecting cultural norms.

## About the mission

Solidarités International (SI) has been providing life-saving assistance in northern Mozambique since March 2019, initially responding to Cyclone Idai. As the crisis in Cabo Delgado escalated, SI began operations in Mueda in July 2021 and progressively expanded to other northern districts including Nangade, Muidumbe, Palma and, more recently, Mocímboa da Praia. By 2022, SI had established a coordination office in Pemba and operational bases in Mueda and Palma.  
Following the closure of the Palma base, SI opened a new base in Mocímboa da Praia in July 2023 to support urgent returnee needs. Today, SI operates from Pemba, Mueda and Mocímboa da Praia, covering not only the northern districts (Mueda, Mocímboa da Praia, Nangade, Muidumbe and Palma) but also additional districts further south, such as Metuge, Chiúre, Mecúfi and Ancuabe.  
In 2024–2025, SI Mozambique has prioritized integrated, multisectoral programming focused on the Rapid Response Mechanism (RRM), WASH, Food Security and Livelihoods (FSL), and Shelter/NFI. At the beginning of 2025, however, major BHA funding cuts forced a significant restructuring, reducing the mission from approximately 140 to around 50 staff and prompting a reorganization of operations to maintain essential activities.  
This restructuring coincided with a deterioration of the security situation in Cabo Delgado, with renewed attacks, increased displacement, and unpredictable access since mid-2024, requiring continuous adaptation of SI’s strategies.  
In 2026, despite these challenges, SI continues to deliver principled, needs-based assistance across Cabo Delgado with the support of key donors such as ECHO, SDC, CDCS, OCHA, IFSAN and UNICEF while exploring emergency and nexus funding opportunities with other donors such as DG INTPA, adapting its WASH strategy and stenghtening its FSL expertise,

## About the job

**GENERAL OBJECTIVE:**

The administrative coordinator will direct and coordinate all administrative, accounting and financial services associated with the mission.  
He/she will take part in defining Solidarités International’s human resources policy and ensure that it is followed.  
As coordinator, he is responsible for the mission’s financial balance.  
He/she will monitor adherence to Solidarités administrative procedures and donor procedures as well as to the laws of the country in which intervention is taking place.  
He/she is the point of reference for the mission, and the link between headquarters and the mission for all administrative matters.

**THE MAIN CHALLENGES:**

• Complex and evolving Mozambican legal and administrative environment   
• Visa and work permit procedures for expatriates remain lengthy and restrictive  
• Young mission with a relatively new team requiring training, coaching, and mentoring  
• In 2025 and 2026, the mission went through rapid decline and growth of its budget which led to signfiicant delays in accounting closure, budget management and reporting.

**PRIORITIES FOR THE 2/3 FIRST MONTHS:**

• Stabilised the implementation of the shared costs policy

• Strengthen and build the capacities of the HR and Finance newly nationalised teams

• Ensure ongoing capacity building and follow-up with the local partner organizations.

• Support the development of new financial proposals, including budget preparation

• Implement SI's new financial software in Mozambique

• Streghten internal control, conduct internal audit and lead on the financial aspects of the external audits

**SECURITY CONSTRAINTS:**

Very limited security constraints in Pemba where the position is based ; with regular visits of one to two weeks visits in the different bases.  
Mueda and Chiure – more restrictions; movement and activities depend on local conditions and Security Department guidance.

## Your profile

**DIPLOMA AND EXPERIENCE:**

Diploma : Minimumum Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Business Administration,Social sciences , Organization Development or related HR discipline

Experience in the humanitarian sector : 3/4 years

Experience on a similar position : 3/4 years

**SKILLS:**

TECHNICAL SKILLS

1. In-depth technical knowledge of the principles and concepts in HR administration (workforce and organizational planning,recruitment & selection , compensation and benefits , performance management, Training and development, employee relations, staff health and safety, and employee engagement), HR-good-practices, HR information systems and databases; / Knowledgeand experience working with SI HR procedures and tools is a major plus
2. Mastery of budget and accounting management, shared costs requirement, donors' financial requirements, audit management
3. Experience in capacity building and setting frameworks for staff development
4. Experience leading workplace investigation and supporting resolution of employee relations / Knowledge of Mozambique labout law is a plus

TRANSVERSAL SKILLS

1. coordination and management skills
2. training and facilitation skills
3. Diplomacy

**LANGUAGE:**

1. English mandatory
2. Portuguese is desirable
3. Spanish a plus if no portuguese

## SI will offer you

**A salaried position:**  
**According to experience,** starting from EUR 2860 gross per month (2600 base salary + 10% annual leave allowance paid monthly) and a monthly Per Diem of USD 750.

SI also covers accommodation costs and travel expenses between the expatriate's country of origin and the place of assignment.

**Breaks:** During the assignment, a system of alternation between work and time off is implemented at the rate of 7 working days every three months (with a USD 850 break allowance, allocated by Sl). To these breaks periods, SI grants one (1) additional rest day per month worked.

**Insurance package:** Expatriates benefit from an insurance package which refunds all healthcare expenses (including medical and surgical expenses, dental care and ophthalmological expenses, repatriation) and a welfare system including war risks. Essential vaccination and antimalarial treatment costs are refunded.

**LIVING CONDITIONS:**

Pemba is a peaceful coastal city with beautiful beaches, seafood, and a wide range of restaurants and leisure activities. There is no curfew, and walking is allowed during the day for expatriates. Many international NGOs are present. The guesthouse offers comfortable living conditions for expatriates with stable water and electricity. Internet connectivity is reliable (4G). Both bases are reachable by UNHAS flight in less than one hour.

title: Deputy Director, Programs
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**JOB OVERVIEW**

The DDP leads, oversees, and ensures the compliance of IRC’s program portfolio, while ensuring alignment with organizational and donor guidelines. The DDP ensures internal and external coordination to develop high-quality proposals and deliver effective, timely programs. The DDP collaborates with all departments and partners, reports to the Country Director (CD), and is a member of the Senior Management Team (SMT). We are looking for a dynamic leader with strong cross-departmental collaboration skills, able to drive strategic success and support an inclusive, motivated team, in particular by empowering women to exercise leadership.

In coordination with the Country Director, the DDP establishes and maintains strong relationships with donors, as well as with DRC government entities and authorities.

The DDP directly supervises the senior program coordinators/managers responsible for proposal development, program quality, and implementation.

 The incumbent is expected to spend at least 40% of their time supporting programs and teams in the provinces and in the field.

 **MAIN RESPONSIBILITIES**

 **1. Program Implementation**

- Oversee and ensure that programs are implemented to high quality standards and within the required timelines, including by supporting Program Coordinators and Technical Coordinators in the use of structured and realistic project management tools (including work plans, procurement plans, and spending plans), in coordination with the Operations teams.
- Closely monitor budgets, expenditures, and program progress to ensure that grants are implemented within budget and closed on time, ensuring consistent Project Cycle Management (PCM) routines and taking prompt, structured corrective action when needed.
- Ensure clear accountability, well-defined roles and responsibilities, and highly effective communication and coordination channels between teams within the Programs Department.
- Provide the CD with accurate, up-to-date advice on developments and opportunities in programming and project implementation, accompanied by recommendations for action.
- Support the MEAL Coordinator in implementing the country office MEAL strategy, ensuring that information from MEAL systems and client feedback mechanisms, including donor reporting, informs every stage of the project cycle.
- Ensure that appropriate technical assistance is provided by IRC Technical Units, external consultants, or partner agencies, as needed.

 **2. Strategic Planning and Implementation**

- Lead the development, review, and implementation of the Strategy Action Plan (SAP) and the SAP-IP, fostering ownership of the strategy across all programmatic departments, ensuring delivery of strategic commitments, and applying IMPACT quality standards.
- Ensure that programming is aligned with the strategic priorities of the IRC DRC SAP and with Impact at Scale (I@S) priorities (where applicable), including program planning, project design, and staff communications.
- In coordination with the CD and other colleagues, update the country program and sector strategies annually, as part of the SAP process, so that they remain relevant and operationally effective in the face of changing contexts.
- Lead the development and rollout of strategic initiatives such as research and innovation, and ensure that cross-cutting issues (gender, climate change, and disaster risk reduction) are integrated into sector programming.

 **3. Grants, Partnerships, and Business Development**

- Foster a partnership-driven, equality-based culture and working environment that reflects partnership principles and values and celebrates partnership successes (including risk sharing with partners and holding leadership accountable for a safeguarding culture in safe partnership).
- Ensure that IRC’s role in the DRC focuses on how we can add the most value to government actors and systems at the central and local levels, as well as to civil society and the private sector, within the framework of the SAP and of program planning and implementation.
- Provide overall direction and leadership to the IRC DRC Grants and Program Development teams by ensuring that a robust business development strategy, processes, and systems are in place, and that adequate funding is secured to deliver the intended results for clients.
- Oversee sound program design and proposal strategy for each new funding opportunity, including needs- and evidence-based program design, strong technical and operational engagement in design processes, and rigorous, competitive budgeting.
- Ensure that the Program, Grants, and Finance teams produce high-quality financial and narrative reports for donors.
- Lead the implementation of the IRC DRC Partnership Strategy and sector partnership plans, advancing localization commitments while maintaining high-quality, efficient services for clients; conduct stakeholder analysis and develop long-term partnerships with local civil society, government authorities, and private sector actors to promote locally led decision-making.
- Lead the implementation of IRC’s PEERS framework, ensuring cross-departmental collaboration, effective management of partnership risks, and responsive feedback systems with partners, while strengthening internal capacity through structured training, recruitment, and performance management aligned with partnership principles.
- Lead engagement with consortium partners, including strategic direction and coordination of program design or implementation.
- Increase the impact of IRC programming by maintaining and strengthening the trust of donors, partners, and key collaborators, while proactively positioning IRC for new program development opportunities.

 **4. Human Resources and Staff Development**

- Recruitment and Performance: In coordination with the People & Culture team, ensure that the IRC DRC Program team is made up of high-quality staff who embody the organization’s values. Participate in recruitment and manage individual and collective performance, including development plans, performance standards, and evaluations, in line with organizational standards.
- Team Cohesion: Ensure that the Program team collaborates effectively, with clear mutual expectations and priority support for field teams.
- Foster collaboration, accountability, and staff well-being through quality management practices, performance monitoring systems, and leadership suited to the dynamics of remote work.

 **5. Liaison/Representation and Coordination**

- Maintain a solid understanding of IRC programs in order to represent the organization and its interests externally in a professional manner, including with donors and government authorities, to ensure the sustainability of programs across the portfolio.
- Encourage and support greater program cohesion through coordination initiatives and information sharing among key country program staff.
- Actively contribute to advocacy initiatives, platforms, and external coordination forums, providing data from IRC programs to strengthen the protection of beneficiaries’ rights
- Participate actively in the Senior Management Team and serve as acting CD when necessary.

 **KEY WORKING RELATIONSHIPS**

- **Position reports to:** Country Director and technical to Deputy Regional Director (Management in Partnership)
- **Positions under direct supervision:**

\- Technical sector program coordinators

 **-** Senior Grants and Business Development Coordinator

 **-** Partnership Coordinator

 **-** MEAL Coordinator

- **Indirect reporting:** N/A
- **Other internal and/or external contacts:** *E-SMT Members and different partners and leaders of other NGOs*

**JOB REQUIREMENTS**

**Education:** Bachelor’s degree in International Development, International Relations, a relevant social science, or equivalent experience in related fields

**Experience:** Experience in a refugee context or a complex humanitarian and development environment with:

- More than 10 years of experience, including at least 5 years at program management level
- Excellent budget management and experience managing a wide range of donor contracts, including large-scale programs with substantial budgets
- Experience leading programs through both a direct operational approach and partnerships with local NGOs

**Skills and Abilities:**

- Excellent leadership, people management, interpersonal and negotiation skills, with a proven ability to build gender-balanced, harmonious, high-performing teams
- Strategic thinking, prioritization and ability to meet deadlines in a demanding environment
- Flexibility to adapt to changing needs
- Ability to work effectively and efficiently within a culturally diverse team
- Strong diplomatic skills to establish and maintain good working relationships with partners, donors and peers in a sensitive environment
- Excellent command of English and French, written and spoken
- Commitment to IRC’s core values: Integrity, Equality, Accountability and Service

**Working environment:**

**Location:** Goma

**Security:** The DDP will be based in Goma and will be required to travel regularly to the provinces of South Kivu, North Kivu, Ituri, Haut-Katanga, and Tanganyika. Goma is the capital of North Kivu and has a population of approximately one million. The city is rated Orange 4 on the MONUSCO security scale. As in any large city in the world, it is advisable to take precautions to prevent crime and theft.

**Accommodation:** This is an unaccompanied position, and the DDP will be housed in individual accommodation.

**Version française**  
  
**APERÇU DU POSTE**

Le DDP dirige, supervise et assure la conformité du portefeuille de programmes de l’IRC, tout en veillant à son alignement avec les directives de l’organisation et des bailleurs. Le DDP assure la coordination interne et externe afin d’élaborer des propositions de haute qualité et de mettre en œuvre des programmes efficaces et dans les délais. Le DDP collabore avec l’ensemble des départements et des partenaires, relève de la Directrice Pays et est membre de l’Équipe de Direction Senior (SMT). Nous recherchons un leader dynamique, doté de solides compétences de collaboration transversale, capable de piloter la réussite stratégique et de soutenir une équipe inclusive et motivée, notamment en donnant aux femmes les moyens d’exercer un leadership.

En coordination avec le Directeur Pays, le DDP établit et entretient des relations solides avec les bailleurs, ainsi qu’avec les entités et autorités gouvernementales de la RDC.

Le DDP supervise directement les coordinateurs/responsables seniors de programmes chargés de l’élaboration des propositions, de la qualité des programmes et de leur mise en œuvre.

Le titulaire du poste devra consacrer au moins 40 % de son temps à l’appui aux programmes et aux équipes dans les provinces et sur le terrain.

**PRINCIPALES RESPONSABILITÉS**

**1. Mise en œuvre des programmes**

- Superviser et veiller à ce que les programmes soient mis en œuvre selon des normes de qualité élevées et dans les délais requis, notamment en appuyant les Coordinateurs de Programmes et les Coordinateurs Techniques dans l’utilisation d’outils de gestion de projet structurés et réalistes (y compris les plans de travail, les plans de passation de marchés et les plans de dépenses), en coordination avec les équipes Opérations.
- Suivre de près les budgets, les dépenses et l’avancement des programmes afin de garantir que les subventions sont mises en œuvre dans les limites du budget et clôturées à temps, en assurant des routines cohérentes de gestion du cycle de projet (PCM) et en prenant rapidement des mesures correctives structurées en cas de besoin.
- Garantir une redevabilité claire, des rôles et responsabilités bien définis, ainsi que des canaux de communication et de coordination très efficaces entre les équipes du Département des Programmes.
- Fournir au DP des conseils précis et à jour sur les évolutions et les opportunités en matière de programmation et de mise en œuvre des projets, accompagnés de recommandations d’action.
- Appuyer le Coordinateur MEAL dans la mise en œuvre de la stratégie MEAL du bureau pays, en veillant à ce que les informations issues des systèmes MEAL et des mécanismes de retour d’information des clients, y compris les rapports aux bailleurs, alimentent chaque étape du cycle de projet.
- Veiller à ce qu’une assistance technique appropriée soit fournie par les Unités Techniques de l’IRC, des consultants externes ou des agences partenaires, selon les besoins.

**2. Planification et mise en œuvre stratégiques**

- Diriger l’élaboration, la révision et la mise en œuvre du Plan d’Action Stratégique (SAP) et du SAP-IP, en favorisant l’appropriation de la stratégie par l’ensemble des départements programmatiques, en assurant la réalisation des engagements stratégiques et en appliquant les normes de qualité IMPACT.
- Veiller à ce que la programmation soit alignée sur les priorités stratégiques du SAP de l’IRC RDC et sur les priorités d’Impact at Scale (I@S) (le cas échéant), y compris la planification des programmes, la conception des projets et la communication avec le personnel.
- En coordination avec le DP et d’autres collègues, mettre à jour chaque année les stratégies du programme pays et des secteurs, dans le cadre du processus SAP, afin qu’elles restent pertinentes et efficaces sur le plan opérationnel face à l’évolution des contextes.
- Diriger l’élaboration et le déploiement d’initiatives stratégiques telles que la recherche et l’innovation, et veiller à ce que les questions transversales (genre, changement climatique et réduction des risques de catastrophe) soient intégrées dans la programmation sectorielle.

**3. Subventions, partenariats et développement des affaires**

- Promouvoir une culture et un environnement de travail axés sur le partenariat et fondés sur l’égalité, qui reflètent les principes et valeurs du partenariat et célèbrent les réussites en la matière (y compris le partage des risques avec les partenaires et la redevabilité de la direction quant à une culture de sauvegarde dans le cadre d’un partenariat sûr).
- Veiller à ce que le rôle de l’IRC en RDC se concentre sur la manière dont nous pouvons apporter le plus de valeur aux acteurs et systèmes gouvernementaux aux niveaux central et local, ainsi qu’à la société civile et au secteur privé, dans le cadre du SAP et de la planification et de la mise en œuvre des programmes.
- Assurer l’orientation et le leadership d’ensemble des équipes Subventions et Développement de Programmes de l’IRC RDC, en veillant à ce qu’une stratégie, des processus et des systèmes robustes de développement des affaires soient en place et à ce que des financements adéquats soient mobilisés pour obtenir les résultats escomptés pour les clients.
- Superviser la qualité de la conception des programmes et de la stratégie de proposition pour chaque nouvelle opportunité de financement, y compris une conception de programme fondée sur les besoins et les données probantes, un engagement technique et opérationnel fort dans les processus de conception, et une budgétisation rigoureuse et compétitive.
- Veiller à ce que les équipes Programmes, Subventions et Finance produisent des rapports financiers et narratifs de haute qualité à l’intention des bailleurs.
- Diriger la mise en œuvre de la Stratégie de Partenariat de l’IRC RDC et des plans de partenariat sectoriels, en faisant progresser les engagements en matière de localisation tout en maintenant des services efficaces et de haute qualité pour les clients ; mener une analyse des parties prenantes et développer des partenariats à long terme avec la société civile locale, les autorités gouvernementales et les acteurs du secteur privé afin de promouvoir une prise de décision pilotée localement.
- Diriger la mise en œuvre du cadre PEERS de l’IRC, en assurant la collaboration interdépartementale, une gestion efficace des risques liés aux partenariats et des systèmes de retour d’information réactifs avec les partenaires, tout en renforçant les capacités internes par la formation structurée, le recrutement et la gestion de la performance, en cohérence avec les principes du partenariat.
- Diriger l’engagement auprès des partenaires de consortium, y compris l’orientation stratégique et la coordination de la conception ou de la mise en œuvre des programmes.
- Accroître l’impact de la programmation de l’IRC en maintenant et en renforçant la confiance des bailleurs, des partenaires et des acteurs clés, tout en positionnant de manière proactive l’IRC pour de nouvelles opportunités de développement de programmes.

**4. Ressources humaines et développement du personnel**

- Recrutement et performance : En coordination avec l’équipe Personnes & Culture (People & Culture), veiller à ce que l’équipe Programmes de l’IRC RDC soit composée de personnel de grande qualité qui incarne les valeurs de l’organisation. Participer au recrutement et gérer la performance individuelle et collective, y compris les plans de développement, les normes de performance et les évaluations, conformément aux normes de l’organisation.
- Cohésion d’équipe : Veiller à ce que l’équipe Programmes collabore efficacement, avec des attentes mutuelles claires et un appui prioritaire aux équipes de terrain.
- Favoriser la collaboration, la redevabilité et le bien-être du personnel par des pratiques de gestion de qualité, des systèmes de suivi de la performance et un leadership adapté à la dynamique du travail à distance.

**5. Liaison/Représentation et coordination**

- Maintenir une solide compréhension des programmes de l’IRC afin de représenter l’organisation et ses intérêts de manière professionnelle à l’extérieur, y compris auprès des bailleurs et des autorités gouvernementales, afin d’assurer la pérennité des programmes sur l’ensemble du portefeuille.
- Encourager et soutenir une plus grande cohésion des programmes par des initiatives de coordination et le partage d’informations entre les principaux membres du personnel du programme pays.
- Contribuer activement aux initiatives et plateformes de plaidoyer ainsi qu’aux forums externes de coordination, en fournissant des données issues des programmes de l’IRC afin de renforcer la protection des droits des clients.
- Participer activement à l’Équipe de Direction Senior et assurer l’intérim du DP en cas de besoin.

**PRINCIPALES RELATIONS DE TRAVAIL**

- **Le poste est rattaché au :** Directeur Pays et, sur le plan technique, au Directeur Régional Adjoint (Management en Partenariat)
- **Postes sous supervision directe :**

  **-** Coordinateurs techniques des programmes sectoriels

  **-** Coordinateur Senior Subventions et Développement des Affaires

  **-** Coordinateur Partenariats

 **-** Coordinateur MEAL

- **Rattachement indirect :** N/A
- **Autres contacts internes et/ou externes :** *Membres de l’E-SMT et différents partenaires et dirigeants d’autres ONG*

**EXIGENCES DU POSTE**

**Formation :** Licence (Bachelor) en développement international, relations internationales, sciences sociales pertinentes, ou expérience équivalente dans des domaines connexes

**Expérience :** Expérience dans un contexte de réfugiés ou dans un environnement humanitaire et de développement complexe, avec :

- Plus de 10 ans d’expérience, dont au moins 5 ans à un niveau de gestion de programme
- Excellente maîtrise de la gestion budgétaire et expérience de la gestion d’un large éventail de contrats de bailleurs, y compris de programmes de grande envergure dotés de budgets importants
- Expérience de la direction de programmes à la fois selon une approche opérationnelle directe et à travers des partenariats avec des ONG locales

**Compétences et aptitudes :**

- Excellentes compétences en leadership, en gestion d’équipes, en relations interpersonnelles et en négociation, avec une capacité avérée à constituer des équipes équilibrées en termes de genre, harmonieuses et très performantes
- Pensée stratégique, sens des priorités et capacité à respecter les délais dans un environnement exigeant
- Flexibilité pour s’adapter à l’évolution des besoins
- Capacité à travailler de manière efficace et efficiente au sein d’une équipe culturellement diverse
- Solides compétences diplomatiques pour établir et entretenir de bonnes relations de travail avec les partenaires, les bailleurs et les pairs dans un environnement sensible
- Excellente maîtrise de l’anglais et du français, à l’écrit comme à l’oral
- Engagement envers les valeurs fondamentales de l’IRC : Intégrité, , Egalité, Responsabilité et Service

**Environnement de travail :**

**Lieu** : Goma

**Sécurité :** Le DDP sera basé à Goma et devra se déplacer régulièrement dans les provinces du Sud-Kivu, du Nord-Kivu, de l’Ituri, du Haut-Katanga et du Tanganyika. Goma est la capitale du Nord-Kivu et compte environ un million d’habitants. La ville est classée Orange 4 sur l’échelle de sécurité de la MONUSCO. Comme dans toute grande ville du monde, il est conseillé de prendre des précautions pour prévenir la criminalité et les vols.

**Hébergement :** Il s’agit d’un poste non accompagné, et le DDP sera hébergé dans un logement individuel.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

title: Caseworker
body:
**This position is open to candidates with existing work authorization in the location where the position is advertised.**

**Job Overview:** The Caseworker provides trauma-informed services to refugees and other ORR qualified immigrants to support a positive integration experience and the achievement of client self-sufficiency. The Caseworker works closely with clients, colleagues, and external parties to develop service and/or self-sufficiency plans to meet individual client needs and preferences utilizing a broad range of financial, medical, social, vocational, and other services and resources in accordance with client eligibility and program requirements.

**Major Responsibilities:**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Provide comprehensive case management services enrolled clients.
- Conduct intake services with clients to assess needs. Develop self-sufficiency plans and timelines in partnership with each client. Provide individualized support through direct services, referrals, and advocacy.
- Receive referrals for case management for ORR-eligible and TANF-eligible clients and participate in any needed case conference meetings to assure continuity of care.
- Assess client needs, creates Family Self-Sufficiency Plans (FSSPs) and Individual Employability Plans (IEPs), focusing on removing employment barriers, stabilizing, and obtaining and retaining employment.
- Assess and monitor client progress to support their attainment of established goals, address challenges, and to ensure that available resources are utilized.
- Detail each client interaction in accordance with program requirements. Input client information in database(s) and assist with tracking and reporting as needed.
- Collaborate effectively with coworkers and partner organizations. Build and maintain relationships with area service providers for the benefit of clients.
- Use personal, insured vehicle and/or public transportation (where available) to travel and transport clients and materials as needed throughout the service delivery area.
- May train and lead the activities of volunteers and interns.
- Conduct outreach to case management staff, refugee-serving agencies, ethnic community-based organizations, and others to inform service providers and refugees of programs and services.
- Complete eligibility screenings for all referral and enrollment paperwork for all eligible Program participants.
- Provide comprehensive case management services, including assisting with benefits applications as appropriate.
- Guide/assist participants to establish contact and receive support services in the community based on their service plan.
- Ensure all services are linguistically appropriate and help advocate with mainstream service providers for linguistically appropriate services.
- Complete case notes in a detailed and timely fashion.
- Ensure all family data is entered into data management system in a timely manner.
- Assist with the preparation of donor funding reports and new funding proposals.
- Participate in all program meetings, staff development activities, and fully engages as a member of the team.
- Follow all IRC policies, procedures and protocols including adherence to the IRC Way and Child Safeguarding.
- Other related duties as assigned.

**Key Working Relationships:**

**Position Reports to:** Casework Supervisor

**Indirect Reporting:** Interns/Volunteers

**Job Requirements:**

***Education:***

- Undergraduate degree Social Work or similar field strongly preferred; comparable related work experience may be substituted.

***Work Experience:***

- 2+ years of case management experience in a social services environment.
- Experience working with vulnerable or under served populations preferred

***Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:***

- Computer proficiency with an emphasis on Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Teams, Outlook).
- Strong organizational skills and detail-oriented
- Public Speaking and/or presentation experience preferred
- Ability to effectively communicate and work as a team member with collaborative partners, the community, and clients in a cross-cultural, multi-disciplinary environment.
- Ability and willingness to drive 15 passenger van.
- Strong attention to detail with the ability to prioritize and manage time effectively.
- Problem solver capable of working well independently and as a part of a team.

***Language Skills:***

- Proficiency in written and spoken English, bilingual ability preferred in Spanish, Dari, Swahili, Kinyarwanda, Arabic, French or other refugee/immigrant language used in Arizona. Cross-cultural understanding and strong communication skills, both written and verbal.

***Certificates or Licenses:***

- Must have a valid driver’s license, active insurance policy, access to reliable transportation and the ability to travel regularly throughout the service delivery area.
- In accordance with Arizona State Law, must possess or be eligible to receive a fingerprint clearance card.

**Working Environment**\*\*\*:\*\*\*

- A combination of standard office environment, remote work, and ‘field’ time within the service delivery area to perform the above outlined responsibilities.
- May require occasional weekend and/or evening work.
- Must be able to lift 35 to 50 pounds (furniture, household supplies, and food boxes).

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $20.97/hr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

title: Request for proposals : provision of WIBA plus and group personal accident insurance policy & employer’s liability insurance
body:
**Background**

Tdh is present in Kenya since 2011. Currently Tdh is providing protection services for children and families affected by migration, natural crises and poverty in Dadaab, Kakuma refugee camps, in Garissa and Turkana County respectively, and in Kiambu for child’s rights business in Kiambu County

## The Need/Purpose

TDH provides WIBA Plus & GPA insurance & Employer’s Liability coverage for its employees across the country. TDH is now soliciting detailed proposals from eligible insurance firms to provide WIBA Plus & GPA Insurance for its staff. **The staff number will be subject to change due to staff leaving and staff being hired**.

## Salaries and number of Staff

Details for number of staff as at October 2026 of staff is 52 at an accumulative gross salary of 11,029,041.22 broken down into below categories.

- **Category 1.** 48 Office Workers

Gross Salary Kshs 10,756,899.47

- **Category 2**. 4 Drivers

Gross Salary Kshs. 272,141.75

## Scope of Work/ Service Outcomes

TDH requires extensions provided to cover the following cases/incidents; and all proposals should provide limits on but not limited to the items below.

**GROUP LIFE**

- Accidental Death Benefit – 3 Times annual salary
- Permanent Total Disability - 3 Times annual salary
- Critical illness – 30% of sum Assured to a maximum of 10,000,000.00.
- Last Expense
    - Last expense Main Member – Kshs.300,000.00
    - Coffin and Hearse – Kshs.100,000.00
    - Dependent’s last expense - Kshs.100,000.00
    - Free Cover Limit Kshs 25,000,000.00

**WIBA/GPA**

- Accidental Death Benefit – 8 Times annual Gross salary
